Operations over `Result`.

The type is wired in; Base includes this module, so these are in unqualified scope everywhere.
modules.source:
-- | Operations over `Result`.
--
-- The type is wired in; Base includes this module, so these are in
-- unqualified scope everywhere.

-- | True when the result is `Ok`.
--
-- ```prism
-- is_ok(Ok(5))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- true
-- ```
pub fn is_ok(r) =
  match r of
    Ok(_x) => true
    Err(_e) => false

-- | True when the result is `Err`.
pub fn is_err(r) =
  match r of
    Ok(_x) => false
    Err(_e) => true

-- | Apply `f` to the `Ok` value, leaving an `Err` untouched.
--
-- ```prism
-- map_result(\(x) -> x * 2, Ok(21))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- Ok(42)
-- ```
pub fn map_result(f, r) =
  match r of
    Ok(x) => Ok(f(x))
    Err(e) => Err(e)

-- | Apply `f` to the `Err` value, leaving an `Ok` untouched (the error-side
-- counterpart of `map_result`).
pub fn map_err(f, r) =
  match r of
    Ok(x) => Ok(x)
    Err(e) => Err(f(e))

-- | Chain a result-returning function, short-circuiting on `Err` (monadic bind
-- for `Result`).
--
-- ```prism
-- and_then_result(\(x) -> if x > 0 then Ok(x) else Err("neg"), Ok(5))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- Ok(5)
-- ```
pub fn and_then_result(f, r) =
  match r of
    Ok(x) => f(x)
    Err(e) => Err(e)

-- | The `Ok` value, or the default `d` when the result is `Err`.
--
-- ```prism
-- result_or(0, Err("boom"))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 0
-- ```
pub fn result_or(d, r) =
  match r of
    Ok(x) => x
    Err(_e) => d

-- | Convert an `Option` to a `Result`, using `err` in place of `None`.
--
-- ```prism
-- ok_of_option("missing", None)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- Err(missing)
-- ```
pub fn ok_of_option(err, o) =
  match o of
    None => Err(err)
    Some(x) => Ok(x)

-- | Convert a `Result` to an `Option`, discarding the error.
--
-- ```prism
-- option_of_result(Ok(5))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- Some(5)
-- ```
pub fn option_of_result(r) =
  match r of
    Ok(x) => Some(x)
    Err(_e) => None

modules.doc:
Lexical scope resolution over branded names: a spelling-to-binder stack.

While resolving syntax, a scope maps each source spelling to the stack of `Data.Name` binders currently in force for it. Entering a binding pushes; leaving pops; a reference resolves to the innermost binder. Shadowing is a push that changes what the spelling means without disturbing the identity underneath, so alpha-renaming a source program never changes which identities the resolved output carries, only their hints.

Failure is explicit and named: resolving an unknown spelling and popping a spelling with no active binder are `ScopeError` values, never silent fallbacks. The scope is an ordinary persistent value, so a resolver may thread it through `State`, pass it as an argument, or keep sub-scopes by simply keeping the old value. Opt-in: not in Base.
modules.source:
-- | Lexical scope resolution over branded names: a spelling-to-binder stack.
--
-- While resolving syntax, a scope maps each source spelling to the stack of
-- `Data.Name` binders currently in force for it. Entering a binding pushes;
-- leaving pops; a reference resolves to the innermost binder. Shadowing is a
-- push that changes what the spelling means without disturbing the identity
-- underneath, so alpha-renaming a source program never changes which
-- identities the resolved output carries, only their hints.
--
-- Failure is explicit and named: resolving an unknown spelling and popping a
-- spelling with no active binder are `ScopeError` values, never silent
-- fallbacks. The scope is an ordinary persistent value, so a resolver may
-- thread it through `State`, pass it as an argument, or keep sub-scopes by
-- simply keeping the old value. Opt-in: not in Base.

import Data.Map (map_empty, map_lookup, map_insert)

import Data.Name (Binder)

-- | A resolution scope for one namespace: each spelling maps to its stack of
-- active binders, innermost first.
pub type Scope(space) = Scope { spellings: Map(String, List(Binder(space))) }

-- | Why a scope operation refused.
pub type ScopeError
  = ScopeUnknown(String)
  | ScopeUnderflow(String)
  deriving (Eq, Show)

-- | The empty scope: no spelling resolves.
pub let scope_empty : Scope(space) = Scope { spellings = map_empty }

-- The active stack for a spelling; absent means empty.
fn stack_of(sc : Scope(space), spelling : String) : List(Binder(space)) =
  match map_lookup(spelling, sc.spellings) of
    None => Nil
    Some(bs) => bs

-- | Bring `binder` into force for its own hint spelling, shadowing any binder
-- already in force for it.
pub fn scope_push(sc : Scope(space), binder : Binder(space)) : Scope(space) =
  Scope {
    spellings = map_insert(
        binder.hint,
        Cons(binder, stack_of(sc, binder.hint)),
        sc.spellings,
      )
  }

-- | The innermost binder in force for `spelling`, or `ScopeUnknown`.
pub fn scope_lookup(
  sc : Scope(space),
  spelling : String
) : Result(Binder(space), ScopeError) =
  match stack_of(sc, spelling) of
    Nil => Err(ScopeUnknown(spelling))
    Cons(b, _rest) => Ok(b)

-- | Leave the innermost binding for `spelling`, restoring whatever it
-- shadowed; popping a spelling with no active binder is `ScopeUnderflow`.
pub fn scope_pop(
  sc : Scope(space),
  spelling : String
) : Result(Scope(space), ScopeError) =
  match stack_of(sc, spelling) of
    Nil => Err(ScopeUnderflow(spelling))
    Cons(_b, rest) =>
      Ok(Scope { spellings = map_insert(spelling, rest, sc.spellings) })

-- | How many binders are in force for `spelling`; zero for an unknown one.
pub fn scope_depth(sc : Scope(space), spelling : String) : Int =
  depth_go(stack_of(sc, spelling), 0)

fn depth_go(bs : List(Binder(space)), n : Int) : Int =
  match bs of
    Nil => n
    Cons(_b, rest) => depth_go(rest, n + 1)

Ordered sets, reusing the balanced-tree map.

There is no `Set` type. A set is exactly a `Map(k, Unit)`, which is what the signatures below say and what the reference documents: the module is a naming layer over `Data.Map`, not an abstraction over it. So a set is also a map wherever one is expected, `map_size` and `map_keys` read it directly (which is how `set_size` and `set_to_list` are defined), and only the `Unit` value discipline of these functions keeps its values uniform.

Set algebra stays O(n log n) and preserves iteration order. Base includes this module.

Like `Map`, a set's representation depends on the canonical `Ord` instance used to build it. The compiler classifies `Ord` and `Hash` as representation-affecting in `store::coherence::is_representation_affecting`. Set identity does not currently encode that instance, so programs exchanging a set across an assembly boundary must agree on its canonical ordering.

-- | Ordered sets, reusing the balanced-tree map.
--
-- There is no `Set` type. A set is exactly a `Map(k, Unit)`, which is what the
-- signatures below say and what the reference documents: the module is a naming
-- layer over `Data.Map`, not an abstraction over it. So a set is also a map
-- wherever one is expected, `map_size` and `map_keys` read it directly (which
-- is how `set_size` and `set_to_list` are defined), and only the `Unit` value
-- discipline of these functions keeps its values uniform.
--
-- Set algebra stays O(n log n) and preserves iteration order. Base includes
-- this module.
--
-- Like `Map`, a set's representation depends on the canonical `Ord` instance
-- used to build it. The compiler classifies `Ord` and `Hash` as
-- representation-affecting in `store::coherence::is_representation_affecting`.
-- Set identity does not currently encode that instance, so programs exchanging a
-- set across an assembly boundary must agree on its canonical ordering.

import Data.Map (map_empty, map_insert, map_member, map_delete, map_size, map_keys)

import Data.List (foldl, filter)

-- | The empty set.
pub let set_empty : Map(k, Unit) = map_empty

-- | Add `x` to the set (a no-op if already present).
--
-- ```prism
-- set_to_list(set_insert(2, set_insert(1, set_empty)))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [1, 2]
-- ```
pub fn set_insert(x : k, s : Map(k, Unit)) : Map(k, Unit) given Ord(k) =
  map_insert(x, (), s)

-- | True when `x` is a member of the set.
--
-- ```prism
-- set_member(2, set_from_list([1, 2, 3]))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- true
-- ```
pub fn set_member(x : k, s : Map(k, Unit)) : Bool given Ord(k) = map_member(x, s)

-- | Remove `x` from the set (a no-op if absent).
--
-- ```prism
-- set_to_list(set_delete(2, set_from_list([1, 2, 3])))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [1, 3]
-- ```
pub fn set_delete(x : k, s : Map(k, Unit)) : Map(k, Unit) given Ord(k) =
  map_delete(x, s)

-- | The number of elements.
--
-- ```prism
-- set_size(set_from_list([1, 2, 2, 3]))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 3
-- ```
pub fn set_size(s) = map_size(s)

-- | The elements in ascending order.
--
-- ```prism
-- set_to_list(set_from_list([3, 1, 2, 1]))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [1, 2, 3]
-- ```
pub fn set_to_list(s) = map_keys(s)

-- | Build a set from a list, dropping duplicates.
--
-- ```prism
-- set_to_list(set_from_list([3, 1, 2, 1]))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [1, 2, 3]
-- ```
pub fn set_from_list(xs : List(k)) : Map(k, Unit) given Ord(k) =
  foldl(\(acc, x) -> set_insert(x, acc), set_empty, xs)

-- | Every element in either set.
--
-- ```prism
-- set_to_list(set_union(set_from_list([1, 2]), set_from_list([2, 3])))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [1, 2, 3]
-- ```
pub fn set_union(s1 : Map(k, Unit), s2 : Map(k, Unit)) : Map(k, Unit) given Ord(k) =
  foldl(\(acc, x) -> set_insert(x, acc), s1, set_to_list(s2))

-- | The elements in both sets.
--
-- ```prism
-- set_to_list(set_intersection(set_from_list([1, 2, 3]), set_from_list([2, 3, 4])))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [2, 3]
-- ```
pub fn set_intersection(
  s1 : Map(k, Unit),
  s2 : Map(k, Unit)
) : Map(k, Unit) given Ord(k) =
  set_from_list(filter(\(x) -> set_member(x, s2), set_to_list(s1)))

-- | The elements of `s1` that are not in `s2`.
--
-- ```prism
-- set_to_list(set_difference(set_from_list([1, 2, 3]), set_from_list([2, 3])))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [1]
-- ```
pub fn set_difference(
  s1 : Map(k, Unit),
  s2 : Map(k, Unit)
) : Map(k, Unit) given Ord(k) =
  set_from_list(filter(\(x) -> not(set_member(x, s2)), set_to_list(s1)))

String operations, byte-oriented and ASCII-accurate.

Built over the primitive UTF-8 string operations. Base includes this module.
modules.source:
-- | String operations, byte-oriented and ASCII-accurate.
--
-- Built over the primitive UTF-8 string operations. Base includes this
-- module.

import Data.Char (is_space, to_upper_c, to_lower_c)

-- | Join a list of strings, placing `sep` between adjacent elements.
--
-- ```prism
-- str_join(", ", ["a", "b", "c"])
-- ```
-- ```output
-- a, b, c
-- ```
pub fn str_join(sep, xs) =
  match xs of
    Nil => ""
    Cons(x, Nil) => x
    Cons(x, rest) => concat(x, concat(sep, str_join(sep, rest)))

-- | `s` repeated `n` times (the empty string when `n <= 0`).
--
-- ```prism
-- str_repeat("ab", 3)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- ababab
-- ```
pub fn str_repeat(s, n) =
  if n <= 0 then
    ""
  else
    concat(s, str_repeat(s, n - 1))

-- | Right-align `s` to width `w` by prepending spaces (unchanged if already wider).
--
-- ```prism
-- pad_left("42", 5)
-- ```
-- ```output
--    42
-- ```
pub fn pad_left(s, w) =
  let pad = w - str_len(s)
  if pad <= 0 then
    s
  else
    concat(str_repeat(" ", pad), s)

-- | Left-align `s` to width `w` by appending spaces (unchanged if already wider).
--
-- ```prism
-- pad_right("42", 5)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 42
-- ```
pub fn pad_right(s, w) =
  let pad = w - str_len(s)
  if pad <= 0 then
    s
  else
    concat(s, str_repeat(" ", pad))

-- | Join a list of strings with newlines between them.
--
-- ```prism
-- lines_of(["one", "two"])
-- ```
-- ```output
-- one
-- two
-- ```
pub fn lines_of(xs) = str_join("\n", xs)

-- | Helper for the substring queries: whether `needle` sits at byte offset `j`
-- in `s`, comparing from position `k`.
pub fn occurs_at(needle, s, j, k) =
  if k >= byte_len(needle) then
    true
  elif j + k >= byte_len(s) then
    false
  elif byte_at(needle, k) == byte_at(s, j + k) then
    occurs_at(needle, s, j, k + 1)
  else
    false

-- | True when `s` begins with `prefix`.
--
-- ```prism
-- starts_with("foo", "foobar")
-- ```
-- ```output
-- true
-- ```
pub fn starts_with(prefix : String, s : String) : Bool = occurs_at(prefix, s, 0, 0)

-- | True when `s` ends with `suffix`.
--
-- ```prism
-- ends_with("bar", "foobar")
-- ```
-- ```output
-- true
-- ```
pub fn ends_with(suffix : String, s : String) : Bool =
  let d = byte_len(s) - byte_len(suffix)
  if d < 0 then
    false
  else
    occurs_at(suffix, s, d, 0)

-- | Helper for `index_of`: search for `needle` in `s` from byte offset `j`.
pub fn index_of_go(needle, s, j) =
  if j + byte_len(needle) > byte_len(s) then
    -1
  elif occurs_at(needle, s, j, 0) then
    j
  else
    index_of_go(needle, s, j + 1)

-- | The byte offset of the first occurrence of `needle` in `s`, or `-1` if absent.
--
-- ```prism
-- index_of("bar", "foobar")
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 3
-- ```
pub fn index_of(needle : String, s : String) : Int = index_of_go(needle, s, 0)

-- | True when `needle` occurs anywhere in `s`.
--
-- ```prism
-- contains("oob", "foobar")
-- ```
-- ```output
-- true
-- ```
pub fn contains(needle : String, s : String) : Bool = index_of(needle, s) >= 0

-- | Helper for `to_upper`/`to_lower`: fold ASCII case mapping over `s` into a
-- byte buffer (`up` selects upper- vs lower-casing).
pub fn map_case(s, i, buf, up) =
  if i >= byte_len(s) then
    buf
  else
    let c = byte_at(s, i)
    map_case(
        s,
        i + 1,
        buf_push(buf, if up then to_upper_c(c) else to_lower_c(c)),
        up,
      )

-- | ASCII upper-case of `s` (non-letters unchanged).
--
-- ```prism
-- to_upper("Hello")
-- ```
-- ```output
-- HELLO
-- ```
pub fn to_upper(s : String) : String =
  string_of_buf(map_case(s, 0, buf_empty(), true))

-- | ASCII lower-case of `s` (non-letters unchanged).
--
-- ```prism
-- to_lower("Hello")
-- ```
-- ```output
-- hello
-- ```
pub fn to_lower(s : String) : String =
  string_of_buf(map_case(s, 0, buf_empty(), false))

-- | Helper for `trim`: the first non-whitespace byte index at or after `i`.
pub fn ltrim_idx(s, i) =
  if i < byte_len(s) && is_space(byte_at(s, i)) then
    ltrim_idx(s, i + 1)
  else
    i

-- | Helper for `trim`: the index just past the last non-whitespace byte before `i`.
pub fn rtrim_idx(s, i) =
  if i > 0 && is_space(byte_at(s, i - 1)) then
    rtrim_idx(s, i - 1)
  else
    i

-- | Helper for `trim`: collect the bytes of `s` in `[lo, hi)` into `buf`.
pub fn slice_bytes(s, lo, hi, buf) =
  if lo >= hi then
    buf
  else
    slice_bytes(s, lo + 1, hi, buf_push(buf, byte_at(s, lo)))

-- | Strip leading and trailing ASCII whitespace.
--
-- ```prism
-- trim("  hi  ")
-- ```
-- ```output
-- hi
-- ```
pub fn trim(s : String) : String =
  let lo = ltrim_idx(s, 0)
  let hi = rtrim_idx(s, byte_len(s))
  if lo >= hi then
    ""
  else
    string_of_buf(slice_bytes(s, lo, hi, buf_empty()))

-- | The index of character `c` in `s` at or after position `i`, or `-1` if absent.
pub fn index_of_from(c, s, i) =
  if i >= str_len(s) then
    -1
  elif char_at(s, i) == c then
    i
  else
    index_of_from(c, s, i + 1)

-- | Helper for `split`: split `s` on `c`, starting from position `i`.
pub fn split_from(c, s, i) =
  let j = index_of_from(c, s, i)
  if j < 0 then
    Cons(substring(s, i, str_len(s) - i), Nil)
  else
    Cons(substring(s, i, j - i), split_from(c, s, j + 1))

-- | Split `s` into the pieces between each occurrence of character `c`.
--
-- ```prism
-- split(char_at(",", 0), "a,b,c")
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [a, b, c]
-- ```
pub fn split(c, s) = split_from(c, s, 0)

-- | The single-character string containing `c`.
--
-- ```prism
-- str_of_char(chr(65))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- A
-- ```
pub fn str_of_char(c) = show_char(c)

-- | Helper for `chars`: the characters of `s` from position `i` onward.
pub fn chars_from(s : String, i : Int) : List(Char) =
  if i >= str_len(s) then
    Nil
  else
    Cons(chr(char_at(s, i)), chars_from(s, i + 1))

-- | The list of characters in `s`.
--
-- ```prism
-- chars("hi")
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [104, 105]
-- ```
pub fn chars(s : String) : List(Char) = chars_from(s, 0)

modules.doc:
Dense multi-dimensional tensors over a flat `FloatBuf`.

A `Tensor` is a flat buffer of `f64` words plus three lists, one entry per axis: the axis `shape` (its extent), its `strides` (the flat-offset step for a unit step along that axis), and its `axes` (a name). Reading `t[i, j]` is a strided lookup: `offset = sum_k idx[k] * strides[k]`, then a single `tbuf_get`. Because the layout lives entirely in the stride list, transposing by name is a permutation of the three lists with no data movement, and the underlying buffer is shared until a write forces a copy (the buffer's own rc==1 in-place / shared-copy discipline).

The surface covers construction, indexing, transpose-by-name, a contiguity-checked reshape, elementwise math (`map_tensor`, `zip_with_tensor`, `add`/`sub`/`mul`/`div`, `scale`), full reductions (`sum_all`, `prod_all`, `mean`), and `matmul`. Every reduction and contraction sums in row-major source-loop order, so results are bit-identical across backends. Broadcasting is deliberately absent, and the math functions require contiguous operands (a transposed view must be materialised first).

`t[i, j]` and `t[i, j] := v` are surface sugar for `at_tensor` / `tensor_set`.
modules.source:
-- | Dense multi-dimensional tensors over a flat `FloatBuf`.
--
-- A `Tensor` is a flat buffer of `f64` words plus three lists, one entry per
-- axis: the axis `shape` (its extent), its `strides` (the flat-offset step for a
-- unit step along that axis), and its `axes` (a name). Reading `t[i, j]` is a
-- strided lookup: `offset = sum_k idx[k] * strides[k]`, then a single
-- `tbuf_get`. Because the layout lives entirely in the stride list, transposing
-- by name is a permutation of the three lists with no data movement, and the
-- underlying buffer is shared until a write forces a copy (the buffer's own
-- rc==1 in-place / shared-copy discipline).
--
-- The surface covers construction, indexing, transpose-by-name, a
-- contiguity-checked reshape, elementwise math (`map_tensor`, `zip_with_tensor`,
-- `add`/`sub`/`mul`/`div`, `scale`), full reductions (`sum_all`, `prod_all`,
-- `mean`), and `matmul`. Every reduction and contraction sums in row-major
-- source-loop order, so results are bit-identical across backends. Broadcasting
-- is deliberately absent, and the math functions require contiguous operands (a
-- transposed view must be materialised first).
--
-- `t[i, j]` and `t[i, j] := v` are surface sugar for `at_tensor` / `tensor_set`.

import Data.List (..)

import Data.Maybe (..)

import Data.Foldable (..)

-- | A dense tensor: flat storage plus per-axis shape, strides, and names.
pub type Tensor = MkTensor(FloatBuf, List(Int), List(Int), List(String))

-- | The flat backing buffer.
pub fn buf(t : Tensor) : FloatBuf =
  match t of
    MkTensor(b, _, _, _) => b

-- | The extent of each axis, outermost first.
--
-- ```prism
-- shape(new([2, 3], 0.0))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [2, 3]
-- ```
pub fn shape(t : Tensor) : List(Int) =
  match t of
    MkTensor(_, s, _, _) => s

-- | The flat-offset stride of each axis.
--
-- ```prism
-- strides(new([2, 3], 0.0))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [3, 1]
-- ```
pub fn strides(t : Tensor) : List(Int) =
  match t of
    MkTensor(_, _, st, _) => st

-- | The name of each axis.
--
-- ```prism
-- axes(new([2, 3], 0.0))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [0, 1]
-- ```
pub fn axes(t : Tensor) : List(String) =
  match t of
    MkTensor(_, _, _, ax) => ax

-- | The number of axes.
--
-- ```prism
-- rank(new([2, 3], 0.0))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 2
-- ```
pub fn rank(t : Tensor) : Int = length(shape(t))

-- | The total number of elements: the product of the shape.
--
-- ```prism
-- size(new([2, 3], 0.0))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 6
-- ```
pub fn size(t : Tensor) : Int = prod(shape(t))

-- The product of a list of extents (the flat length a shape needs).
fn prod(xs : List(Int)) : Int = foldl(\(acc, x) -> acc * x, 1, xs)

-- The sum of a list.
fn sum(xs : List(Int)) : Int = foldl(\(acc, x) -> acc + x, 0, xs)

-- Row-major (C-order) strides for a shape: the stride of an axis is the product
-- of every extent to its right, so the last axis has stride 1.
fn rm_strides_go(k : Int, n : Int, shape : List(Int)) : List(Int) =
  if k >= n then
    Nil
  else
    Cons(prod(drop(k + 1, shape)), rm_strides_go(k + 1, n, shape))

fn rm_strides(shape : List(Int)) : List(Int) =
  rm_strides_go(0, length(shape), shape)

-- Default axis names "0", "1", ... for a rank.
fn default_axes(n : Int) : List(String) = map(\(i) -> show_int(i), range(0, n))

-- The flat offset of a multi-index under a stride list: the dot product of the
-- index and the strides.
fn offset(idx : List(Int), st : List(Int)) : Int =
  sum(zip_with(\(i, s) -> i * s, idx, st))

-- | A tensor of the given shape with every element set to `fill`, row-major.
--
-- ```prism
-- let t = new([2, 2], 7.0)
-- t[1, 1]
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 7
-- ```
pub fn new(shape : List(Int), fill : Float) : Tensor =
  MkTensor(
      tbuf_new(prod(shape), fill),
      shape,
      rm_strides(shape),
      default_axes(length(shape)),
    )

-- Write a list of values into a buffer starting at index `i`.
fn fill_from(b : FloatBuf, i : Int, xs : List(Float)) : FloatBuf =
  match xs of
    Nil => b
    Cons(x, rest) => fill_from(tbuf_set(b, i, x), i + 1, rest)

-- | A row-major tensor of the given shape filled from a flat list of values.
-- Extra list elements past the shape's size are ignored; missing ones stay 0.
--
-- ```prism
-- let t = from_list([2, 2], [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0])
-- t[1, 0]
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 3
-- ```
pub fn from_list(shape : List(Int), xs : List(Float)) : Tensor =
  MkTensor(
      fill_from(tbuf_new(prod(shape), 0.0), 0, xs),
      shape,
      rm_strides(shape),
      default_axes(length(shape)),
    )

-- | The element at a multi-index, or `fail()` if the offset is out of range.
-- Backs `t[i, j]`.
--
-- ```prism
-- at_tensor(from_list([2, 2], [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0]), [0, 1])
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 2
-- ```
pub fn at_tensor(t : Tensor, idx : List(Int)) : Float =
  match t of
    MkTensor(b, _, st, _) =>
      let off = offset(idx, st)
      if off >= 0 && off < tbuf_len(b) then
        tbuf_get(b, off)
      else
        fail()

-- | A tensor equal to `t` but with the element at a multi-index set to `v`, or
-- `fail()` if out of range. Backs `t[i, j] := v`.
--
-- ```prism
-- let t = tensor_set(new([2, 2], 0.0), [0, 1], 5.0)
-- t[0, 1]
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 5
-- ```
pub fn tensor_set(t : Tensor, idx : List(Int), v : Float) : Tensor =
  match t of
    MkTensor(b, sh, st, ax) =>
      let off = offset(idx, st)
      if off >= 0 && off < tbuf_len(b) then
        MkTensor(tbuf_set(b, off, v), sh, st, ax)
      else
        fail()

-- The position of a name in a list, or `fail()` if absent.
fn index_of_go(k : Int, x : String, xs : List(String)) : Int =
  match xs of
    Nil => fail()
    Cons(y, rest) =>
      if y == x then
        k
      else
        index_of_go(k + 1, x, rest)

fn index_of(x : String, xs : List(String)) : Int = index_of_go(0, x, xs)

-- Swap the elements at two positions of a list.
fn swap_at(i : Int, j : Int, xs : List(a)) : List(a) =
  match nth(i, xs) of
    None => fail()
    Some(vi) =>
      match nth(j, xs) of
        None => fail()
        Some(vj) => list_set(list_set(xs, i, vj), j, vi)

-- | Transpose two named axes: a permutation of the shape, strides, and names
-- with no data movement (the buffer is shared). Reading a transposed tensor
-- walks the same buffer in the permuted stride order.
--
-- ```prism
-- let t = transpose(from_list([2, 2], [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0]), "0", "1")
-- t[0, 1]
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 3
-- ```
pub fn transpose(t : Tensor, a : String, b : String) : Tensor =
  match t of
    MkTensor(b0, sh, st, ax) =>
      let i = index_of(a, ax)
      let j = index_of(b, ax)
      MkTensor(b0, swap_at(i, j, sh), swap_at(i, j, st), swap_at(i, j, ax))

-- | Reinterpret the elements under a new shape of the same size. Requires the
-- tensor to be contiguous (row-major strides); a transposed view must be copied
-- first, so reshaping one is a `fail()`. The new axes get default names.
--
-- ```prism
-- shape(reshape(from_list([2, 2], [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0]), [4]))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [4]
-- ```
pub fn reshape(t : Tensor, new_shape : List(Int)) : Tensor =
  match t of
    MkTensor(b, sh, st, _) =>
      if st == rm_strides(sh) && prod(sh) == prod(new_shape) then
        MkTensor(
            b,
            new_shape,
            rm_strides(new_shape),
            default_axes(length(new_shape)),
          )
      else
        fail()

-- Whether a tensor is contiguous: its strides are the row-major strides of its
-- shape, so the flat buffer is exactly the row-major element sequence and can be
-- read and written by flat position. `new`, `from_list`, and the math below all
-- produce contiguous tensors; a `transpose` view is not contiguous and must be
-- copied (e.g. through `reshape` after a materialising op) before the elementwise
-- and matmul functions accept it.
fn is_contig(t : Tensor) : Bool =
  match t of
    MkTensor(_, sh, st, _) => st == rm_strides(sh)

-- Wrap a freshly filled row-major buffer as a contiguous tensor of `sh`.
fn contig_tensor(sh : List(Int), b : FloatBuf) : Tensor =
  MkTensor(b, sh, rm_strides(sh), default_axes(length(sh)))

-- Apply `f` to each element of `bi`, writing into `out` at the same flat
-- position, over `[p, n)`. Pure: raw buffer reads and writes, and `f` is a plain
-- `Float -> Float`. Tail-recursive, so constant stack over any size.
fn map_fill(f, bi : FloatBuf, out : FloatBuf, p : Int, n : Int) : FloatBuf =
  if p >= n then
    out
  else
    map_fill(f, bi, tbuf_set(out, p, f(tbuf_get(bi, p))), p + 1, n)

-- | A tensor of the same shape with `f` applied to every element. Requires a
-- contiguous input; the result is contiguous.
--
-- ```prism
-- sum_all(map_tensor(\(x) -> x + 1.0, from_list([2], [10.0, 20.0])))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 32
-- ```
pub fn map_tensor(f, t : Tensor) : Tensor ! {Fail} =
  if is_contig(t) then
    let sh = shape(t)
    contig_tensor(sh, map_fill(f, buf(t), tbuf_new(prod(sh), 0.0), 0, prod(sh)))
  else
    fail()

-- Combine the pth elements of `ba` and `bb` with `f` into `out`, over `[p, n)`.
fn zip_fill(
  f,
  ba : FloatBuf,
  bb : FloatBuf,
  out : FloatBuf,
  p : Int,
  n : Int
) : FloatBuf =
  if p >= n then
    out
  else
    zip_fill(
        f,
        ba,
        bb,
        tbuf_set(out, p, f(tbuf_get(ba, p), tbuf_get(bb, p))),
        p + 1,
        n,
      )

-- | Combine two identically-shaped contiguous tensors elementwise with `f`, or
-- `fail()` if the shapes differ or either is not contiguous. No broadcasting.
--
-- ```prism
-- sum_all(zip_with_tensor(\(x, y) -> x + y, from_list([2], [1.0, 2.0]), from_list([2], [3.0, 4.0])))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 10
-- ```
pub fn zip_with_tensor(f, a : Tensor, b : Tensor) : Tensor ! {Fail} =
  let sh = shape(a)
  if sh == shape(b) && is_contig(a) && is_contig(b) then
    contig_tensor(
        sh,
        zip_fill(f, buf(a), buf(b), tbuf_new(prod(sh), 0.0), 0, prod(sh)),
      )
  else
    fail()

-- | Elementwise sum of two identically-shaped tensors.
--
-- ```prism
-- sum_all(add(from_list([2], [1.0, 2.0]), from_list([2], [3.0, 4.0])))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 10
-- ```
pub fn add(a : Tensor, b : Tensor) : Tensor ! {Fail} =
  zip_with_tensor(\(x, y) -> x + y, a, b)

-- | Elementwise difference.
pub fn sub(a : Tensor, b : Tensor) : Tensor ! {Fail} =
  zip_with_tensor(\(x, y) -> x - y, a, b)

-- | Elementwise (Hadamard) product, not matrix multiplication.
--
-- ```prism
-- sum_all(mul(from_list([2], [2.0, 3.0]), from_list([2], [4.0, 5.0])))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 23
-- ```
pub fn mul(a : Tensor, b : Tensor) : Tensor ! {Fail} =
  zip_with_tensor(\(x, y) -> x * y, a, b)

-- | Elementwise quotient.
pub fn div(a : Tensor, b : Tensor) : Tensor ! {Fail} =
  zip_with_tensor(\(x, y) -> x / y, a, b)

-- | Every element multiplied by a scalar.
--
-- ```prism
-- sum_all(scale(2.0, from_list([2], [1.0, 2.0])))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 6
-- ```
pub fn scale(s : Float, t : Tensor) : Tensor ! {Fail} = map_tensor(\(x) -> x * s, t)

-- Fold `op` over the buffer in flat (row-major) order from `acc`, over `[p, n)`.
-- The fixed order is what makes the reductions bit-identical across backends.
fn reduce_fill(op, b : FloatBuf, acc : Float, p : Int, n : Int) : Float =
  if p >= n then
    acc
  else
    reduce_fill(op, b, op(acc, tbuf_get(b, p)), p + 1, n)

-- | The sum of every element, added in row-major order. Requires a contiguous
-- tensor (so the summation order is well defined).
--
-- ```prism
-- sum_all(from_list([2, 2], [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0]))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 10
-- ```
pub fn sum_all(t : Tensor) : Float ! {Fail} =
  if is_contig(t) then
    reduce_fill(\(a, x) -> a + x, buf(t), 0.0, 0, size(t))
  else
    fail()

-- | The product of every element, in row-major order.
--
-- ```prism
-- prod_all(from_list([2], [3.0, 4.0]))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 12
-- ```
pub fn prod_all(t : Tensor) : Float ! {Fail} =
  if is_contig(t) then
    reduce_fill(\(a, x) -> a * x, buf(t), 1.0, 0, size(t))
  else
    fail()

-- | The arithmetic mean of every element.
--
-- ```prism
-- mean(from_list([2, 2], [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0]))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 2.5
-- ```
pub fn mean(t : Tensor) : Float ! {Fail} = sum_all(t) / to_float(size(t))

-- The element at position `i` of a list, or `fail()` if out of range.
fn at_or_fail(i : Int, xs : List(Int)) : Int =
  match nth(i, xs) of
    None => fail()
    Some(v) => v

-- The list with the element at position `i` removed.
fn drop_at(i : Int, xs : List(a)) : List(a) =
  append(take(i, xs), drop(i + 1, xs))

-- Sum `extent` elements of `b` starting at flat `base`, stepping by `sa` (the
-- stride of the contracted axis), in index order `0..extent`. The fixed order is
-- what makes the axis reduction bit-identical across backends.
fn contract_sum(
  b : FloatBuf,
  base : Int,
  sa : Int,
  e : Int,
  extent : Int,
  acc : Float
) : Float =
  if e >= extent then
    acc
  else
    contract_sum(b, base, sa, e + 1, extent, acc + tbuf_get(b, base + e * sa))

-- Fill output flat position `q` with the sum over the contracted axis of the
-- input elements sharing `q`'s index on every remaining axis, over `[q, total)`.
-- `out_idx` unravels `q` against the output shape; its dot with the kept input
-- strides `ks` is the flat base of the contracted fibre.
fn sum_axis_fill(
  b : FloatBuf,
  out : FloatBuf,
  ostrides : List(Int),
  osh : List(Int),
  ks : List(Int),
  sa : Int,
  extent : Int,
  q : Int,
  total : Int
) : FloatBuf =
  if q >= total then
    out
  else
    let out_idx = zip_with(\(s, n) -> q / s % n, ostrides, osh)
    let base = offset(out_idx, ks)
    sum_axis_fill(
        b,
        tbuf_set(out, q, contract_sum(b, base, sa, 0, extent, 0.0)),
        ostrides,
        osh,
        ks,
        sa,
        extent,
        q + 1,
        total,
      )

-- | Reduce over one named axis by summing, removing that axis (rank `r` becomes
-- `r - 1`); the remaining axes keep their names. The contracted axis is summed in
-- index order `0..extent` (source loop order), so the result is bit-identical
-- across backends. `fail()` on a missing axis or a non-contiguous input.
--
-- ```prism
-- let s = sum_axis(from_list([2, 2], [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0]), "0")
-- (at_tensor(s, [0]), at_tensor(s, [1]))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- (4, 6)
-- ```
pub fn sum_axis(t : Tensor, axis_name : String) : Tensor ! {Fail} =
  if is_contig(t) then
    let sh = shape(t)
    let st = strides(t)
    let ax = axes(t)
    let a = index_of(axis_name, ax)
    let extent = at_or_fail(a, sh)
    let sa = at_or_fail(a, st)
    let osh = drop_at(a, sh)
    let oax = drop_at(a, ax)
    let ks = drop_at(a, st)
    let ostrides = rm_strides(osh)
    let total = prod(osh)
    MkTensor(
        sum_axis_fill(
            buf(t),
            tbuf_new(total, 0.0),
            ostrides,
            osh,
            ks,
            sa,
            extent,
            0,
            total,
          ),
        osh,
        ostrides,
        oax,
      )
  else
    fail()

-- | Reduce over one named axis by averaging: the sum over that axis divided by
-- its extent, removing the axis. Same source-loop order and contiguity
-- requirement as `sum_axis`.
--
-- ```prism
-- let m = mean_axis(from_list([2, 2], [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0]), "1")
-- (at_tensor(m, [0]), at_tensor(m, [1]))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- (1.5, 3.5)
-- ```
pub fn mean_axis(t : Tensor, axis_name : String) : Tensor ! {Fail} =
  let extent = at_or_fail(index_of(axis_name, axes(t)), shape(t))
  scale(1.0 / to_float(extent), sum_axis(t, axis_name))

-- The dot product of row `i` of `a` (flat base `i * k`) and column `j` of `b`
-- (flat stride `n`), contracted over `0..k` in order. The fixed summation order
-- makes `matmul` deterministic across backends and optimization levels.
fn mm_dot(
  ba : FloatBuf,
  bb : FloatBuf,
  i : Int,
  j : Int,
  k : Int,
  n : Int,
  p : Int,
  acc : Float
) : Float =
  if p >= k then
    acc
  else
    mm_dot(
        ba,
        bb,
        i,
        j,
        k,
        n,
        p + 1,
        acc + tbuf_get(ba, i * k + p) * tbuf_get(bb, p * n + j),
      )

-- Fill output flat position `q` (row `q / n`, column `q % n`) with its dot
-- product, over `[q, total)`.
fn mm_fill(
  ba : FloatBuf,
  bb : FloatBuf,
  out : FloatBuf,
  k : Int,
  n : Int,
  q : Int,
  total : Int
) : FloatBuf =
  if q >= total then
    out
  else
    mm_fill(
        ba,
        bb,
        tbuf_set(out, q, mm_dot(ba, bb, q / n, q % n, k, n, 0, 0.0)),
        k,
        n,
        q + 1,
        total,
      )

-- | Matrix product of a rank-2 `[m, k]` tensor with a rank-2 `[k, n]` tensor,
-- giving `[m, n]`. The contraction sums in source loop order, so the result is
-- bit-identical across backends. `fail()` unless both operands are contiguous,
-- rank 2, with matching inner extents.
--
-- ```prism
-- let c = matmul(from_list([2, 2], [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0]), from_list([2, 2], [1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0]))
-- (c[0, 0], c[1, 1])
-- ```
-- ```output
-- (1, 4)
-- ```
pub fn matmul(a : Tensor, b : Tensor) : Tensor ! {Fail} =
  match shape(a) of
    Cons(m, Cons(k, Nil)) =>
      match shape(b) of
        Cons(k2, Cons(n, Nil)) =>
          if k == k2 && is_contig(a) && is_contig(b) then
            contig_tensor(
                Cons(m, Cons(n, Nil)),
                mm_fill(buf(a), buf(b), tbuf_new(m * n, 0.0), k, n, 0, m * n),
              )
          else
            fail()
        _ => fail()
    _ => fail()

A persistent union-find (disjoint-set) over an ordered key type.

A set is named by its canonical root, and `uf_union` always keeps the smaller key (by `Ord`) as the root, so a set's representative is a pure function of its members, never of the order unions ran in. There is no path compression (that needs mutation); `uf_find` walks parent links to the root on each call. A key absent from the map is its own singleton root, so `uf_empty` needs no pre-population. The occurs check an HM unifier layers on top is type-specific and lives with the unifier, not here. Opt-in: not in Base.
modules.source:
-- | A persistent union-find (disjoint-set) over an ordered key type.
--
-- A set is named by its canonical root, and `uf_union` always keeps the smaller
-- key (by `Ord`) as the root, so a set's representative is a pure function of its
-- members, never of the order unions ran in. There is no path compression (that
-- needs mutation); `uf_find` walks parent links to the root on each call. A key
-- absent from the map is its own singleton root, so `uf_empty` needs no
-- pre-population. The occurs check an HM unifier layers on top is type-specific
-- and lives with the unifier, not here. Opt-in: not in Base.

import Data.Map (map_empty, map_lookup, map_insert)

-- | The empty forest: every key is its own singleton root.
pub let uf_empty : Map(k, k) = map_empty

-- | The canonical root of `x`'s set.
--
-- ```prism
-- uf_find(uf_union(uf_union(uf_empty, 3, 2), 2, 1), 3)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 1
-- ```
pub fn uf_find(uf : Map(k, k), x : k) : k given Ord(k) =
  match map_lookup(x, uf) of
    None => x
    Some(p) =>
      if cmp(p, x) == 0 then
        x
      else
        uf_find(uf, p)

-- | Merge the sets of `x` and `y`, keeping the smaller root; a no-op when they
-- are already joined.
--
-- ```prism
-- uf_equiv(uf_union(uf_union(uf_empty, 1, 2), 2, 3), 1, 3)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- true
-- ```
pub fn uf_union(uf : Map(k, k), x : k, y : k) : Map(k, k) given Ord(k) =
  let rx = uf_find(uf, x)
  let ry = uf_find(uf, y)
  let c = cmp(rx, ry)
  if c == 0 then
    uf
  elif c < 0 then
    map_insert(ry, rx, uf)
  else
    map_insert(rx, ry, uf)

-- | True when `x` and `y` belong to the same set.
pub fn uf_equiv(uf : Map(k, k), x : k, y : k) : Bool given Ord(k) =
  cmp(uf_find(uf, x), uf_find(uf, y)) == 0

modules.doc:
A persistent union-find whose canonical roots carry a descriptor payload.

The payload-free forest in `Data.UnionFind` answers only equivalence; this module is the opt-in layer for solvers that also attach a fact to each class (a metavariable's solution, a binding level, a rank). One descriptor lives at each canonical root, and `ufp_union_with` combines exactly the two descriptors whose classes are joined, exactly once per join.

Absence is explicit where the payload-free forest is implicit: a key that was never inserted has no descriptor, so it is not a silent singleton; `ufp_find` answers `None` and the writing operations answer `UfAbsent`. Duplicate insertion is `UfDuplicate`, never a silent overwrite.

Determinism is part of the public contract, not a courtesy: `ufp_union_with` keeps the smaller root by `Ord`, passes the kept root's descriptor to `combine` first and the absorbed root's second, and deletes the losing descriptor, so a class's representative and payload are a pure function of the insertions and unions performed, never of the order finds ran in. The representation (parent links) is private; render a forest through `ufp_roots`, which describes the logical partition. There is no path compression: a query-history-dependent representation would leak into any structural comparison, the wrong trade before a serialization boundary is pinned. Opt-in: not in Base.

-- | A persistent union-find whose canonical roots carry a descriptor payload.
--
-- The payload-free forest in `Data.UnionFind` answers only equivalence; this
-- module is the opt-in layer for solvers that also attach a fact to each
-- class (a metavariable's solution, a binding level, a rank). One descriptor
-- lives at each canonical root, and `ufp_union_with` combines exactly the two
-- descriptors whose classes are joined, exactly once per join.
--
-- Absence is explicit where the payload-free forest is implicit: a key that
-- was never inserted has no descriptor, so it is not a silent singleton;
-- `ufp_find` answers `None` and the writing operations answer `UfAbsent`.
-- Duplicate insertion is `UfDuplicate`, never a silent overwrite.
--
-- Determinism is part of the public contract, not a courtesy: `ufp_union_with`
-- keeps the smaller root by `Ord`, passes the kept root's descriptor to
-- `combine` first and the absorbed root's second, and deletes the losing
-- descriptor, so a class's representative and payload are a pure function of
-- the insertions and unions performed, never of the order finds ran in. The
-- representation (parent links) is private; render a forest through
-- `ufp_roots`, which describes the logical partition. There is no path
-- compression: a query-history-dependent representation would leak into any
-- structural comparison, the wrong trade before a serialization boundary is
-- pinned. Opt-in: not in Base.

import Data.Map (map_empty, map_lookup, map_insert, map_delete, map_to_list)

import Data.Result (result_or)

-- | A payload-carrying forest over ordered keys. The constructor is the
-- module's private representation; go through the `ufp_` functions.
pub type UnionFind(k, a) = Ufp { parents: Map(k, k), payloads: Map(k, a) }

-- | Why a forest operation refused.
pub type UfError = UfDuplicate | UfAbsent deriving (Eq, Show)

-- | The empty forest: no keys, no classes.
pub let ufp_empty : UnionFind(k, a) =
  Ufp { parents = map_empty, payloads = map_empty }

-- The canonical root of `x`, which must be a member. Walks parent links; the
-- chain is as long as the joins that built it, never compressed.
fn root_of(uf : UnionFind(k, a), x : k) : k given Ord(k) =
  match map_lookup(x, uf.parents) of
    None => x
    Some(p) => root_of(uf, p)

-- Whether `x` was ever inserted: members are exactly the keys that either
-- carry a descriptor (roots) or a parent link (absorbed members).
fn member(uf : UnionFind(k, a), x : k) : Bool given Ord(k) =
  match map_lookup(x, uf.payloads) of
    Some(_a) => true
    None =>
      match map_lookup(x, uf.parents) of
        Some(_p) => true
        None => false

-- | Insert `x` as a fresh singleton class with descriptor `a`. Inserting a
-- key that is already a member (root or not) is `UfDuplicate`.
--
-- ```prism
-- ufp_find(result_or(ufp_empty, ufp_insert(ufp_empty, 1, "one")), 1)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- Some((1, one))
-- ```
pub fn ufp_insert(
  uf : UnionFind(k, a),
  x : k,
  a : a
) : Result(UnionFind(k, a), UfError) given Ord(k) =
  if member(uf, x) then
    Err(UfDuplicate)
  else
    Ok(Ufp { ..uf, payloads = map_insert(x, a, uf.payloads) })

-- | The canonical root of `x`'s class and the class descriptor, or `None`
-- when `x` was never inserted.
--
-- ```prism
-- ufp_find(result_or(ufp_empty, ufp_insert(ufp_empty, 1, "one")), 9)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- None
-- ```
pub fn ufp_find(uf : UnionFind(k, a), x : k) : Option((k, a)) given Ord(k) =
  if member(uf, x) then
    let r = root_of(uf, x)
    match map_lookup(r, uf.payloads) of
      Some(a) => Some((r, a))
      None => None
  else
    None

-- | Replace the descriptor of `x`'s class, or `UfAbsent` when `x` was never
-- inserted. The class and its root are unchanged.
pub fn ufp_set(
  uf : UnionFind(k, a),
  x : k,
  a : a
) : Result(UnionFind(k, a), UfError) given Ord(k) =
  if member(uf, x) then
    let r = root_of(uf, x)
    Ok(Ufp { ..uf, payloads = map_insert(r, a, uf.payloads) })
  else
    Err(UfAbsent)

-- | Join the classes of `x` and `y`. The smaller root by `Ord` stays the
-- root; `combine` receives the kept root's descriptor first and the absorbed
-- root's second, runs exactly once per join that changes the partition, and
-- its result becomes the joined class's descriptor. Joining a class with
-- itself is a no-op that never calls `combine`; either key absent is
-- `UfAbsent`.
--
-- ```prism
-- let uf1 = result_or(ufp_empty, ufp_insert(ufp_empty, 2, "b"))
-- let uf2 = result_or(ufp_empty, ufp_insert(uf1, 1, "a"))
-- ufp_find(result_or(ufp_empty, ufp_union_with(concat, uf2, 2, 1)), 2)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- Some((1, ab))
-- ```
pub fn ufp_union_with(
  combine : (a, a) -> a ! {| e},
  uf : UnionFind(k, a),
  x : k,
  y : k
) : Result(UnionFind(k, a), UfError) ! { | e} given Ord(k) =
  if not(member(uf, x)) || not(member(uf, y)) then
    Err(UfAbsent)
  else
    let rx = root_of(uf, x)
    let ry = root_of(uf, y)
    let c = cmp(rx, ry)
    if c == 0 then
      Ok(uf)
    else
      let kept =
        if c < 0 then
          rx
        else
          ry
      let lost =
        if c < 0 then
          ry
        else
          rx
      match ((map_lookup(kept, uf.payloads), map_lookup(lost, uf.payloads))) of
        (Some(ka), Some(la)) =>
          let joined = combine(ka, la)
          Ok(
              Ufp {
                parents = map_insert(lost, kept, uf.parents),
                payloads = map_insert(kept, joined, map_delete(lost, uf.payloads))
              },
            )
        _ => Err(UfAbsent)

-- | The logical partition: every canonical root paired with its class
-- descriptor, in ascending key order. This is the rendering to compare or
-- serialize; it is independent of the parent paths any sequence of joins
-- happened to build.
--
-- ```prism
-- let uf1 = result_or(ufp_empty, ufp_insert(ufp_empty, 2, "b"))
-- let uf2 = result_or(ufp_empty, ufp_insert(uf1, 1, "a"))
-- ufp_roots(result_or(ufp_empty, ufp_union_with(concat, uf2, 1, 2)))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [(1, ab)]
-- ```
pub fn ufp_roots(uf : UnionFind(k, a)) : List((k, a)) given Ord(k) =
  map_to_list(uf.payloads)

-- | Whether `x` and `y` are members of the same class; `None` when either was
-- never inserted.
pub fn ufp_equiv(uf : UnionFind(k, a), x : k, y : k) : Option(Bool) given Ord(k) =
  if member(uf, x) && member(uf, y) then
    Some(cmp(root_of(uf, x), root_of(uf, y)) == 0)
  else
    None

`Validation`, the error-accumulating sibling of `Result`.

Where `Result` short-circuits on the first `Err`, `Validation` collects every error, so checking several independent fields reports all their failures at once instead of only the first. Combine independent validations with `validate2` or `validation_ap`; both concatenate the error lists of whatever failed. Opt-in: not in Base.
modules.source:
-- | `Validation`, the error-accumulating sibling of `Result`.
--
-- Where `Result` short-circuits on the first `Err`, `Validation` collects every
-- error, so checking several independent fields reports all their failures at
-- once instead of only the first. Combine independent validations with
-- `validate2` or `validation_ap`; both concatenate the error lists of whatever
-- failed. Opt-in: not in Base.

import Data.List (append, foldr)

-- | A validated `a`, or the list of accumulated errors `e`.
pub type Validation(e, a) = Valid(a) | Invalid(List(e)) deriving (Eq, Show)

-- | True when the value validated.
pub fn is_valid(v) =
  match v of
    Valid(_x) => true
    Invalid(_es) => false

-- | True when there were errors.
pub fn is_invalid(v) = not(is_valid(v))

-- | Apply `f` to a `Valid` value, leaving accumulated errors untouched.
pub fn map_valid(f, v) =
  match v of
    Valid(x) => Valid(f(x))
    Invalid(es) => Invalid(es)

-- | Applicative apply: when both sides validate, apply the function; otherwise
-- keep every error from both sides, in order. This is the accumulation.
--
-- ```prism
-- validation_ap(Invalid(["bad function"]), Invalid(["bad argument"]))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- Data.Validation.Invalid([bad function, bad argument])
-- ```
pub fn validation_ap(vf, va) =
  match vf of
    Valid(f) =>
      match va of
        Valid(x) => Valid(f(x))
        Invalid(es) => Invalid(es)
    Invalid(es1) =>
      match va of
        Valid(_x) => Invalid(es1)
        Invalid(es2) => Invalid(append(es1, es2))

-- | Combine two validations with the two-argument `f`, accumulating the errors
-- of whichever failed.
--
-- ```prism
-- validate2(\(a, b) -> a + b, Valid(1), Invalid(["oops"]))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- Data.Validation.Invalid([oops])
-- ```
pub fn validate2(f, va, vb) =
  match va of
    Valid(a) =>
      match vb of
        Valid(b) => Valid(f(a, b))
        Invalid(es) => Invalid(es)
    Invalid(es1) =>
      match vb of
        Valid(_b) => Invalid(es1)
        Invalid(es2) => Invalid(append(es1, es2))

-- | The `Valid` value, or `d` when there were errors.
--
-- ```prism
-- (validation_or(0, Valid(7)), validation_or(0, Invalid(["bad"])))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- (7, 0)
-- ```
pub fn validation_or(d, v) =
  match v of
    Valid(x) => x
    Invalid(_es) => d

-- | Turn a `Result` into a single-error `Validation`.
pub fn validation_of_result(r) =
  match r of
    Ok(x) => Valid(x)
    Err(e) => Invalid([e])

-- | Turn a `Validation` back into a `Result`, keeping the whole error list on
-- the `Err` side.
pub fn result_of_validation(v) =
  match v of
    Valid(x) => Ok(x)
    Invalid(es) => Err(es)

-- Fold step for `sequence_validation`: cons a `Valid` head onto a `Valid` tail,
-- otherwise accumulate whatever errors either side carries. A top-level helper
-- (not an inline lambda) so the nested match parses.
fn cons_validation(v, acc) =
  match v of
    Valid(x) =>
      match acc of
        Valid(xs) => Valid(Cons(x, xs))
        Invalid(es) => Invalid(es)
    Invalid(es1) =>
      match acc of
        Valid(_xs) => Invalid(es1)
        Invalid(es2) => Invalid(append(es1, es2))

-- | Collapse a list of validations into a validation of the list, accumulating
-- every error across all of them.
--
-- ```prism
-- sequence_validation([Valid(1), Invalid(["first"]), Invalid(["second"])])
-- ```
-- ```output
-- Data.Validation.Invalid([first, second])
-- ```
pub fn sequence_validation(vs) = foldr(cons_validation, Valid(Nil), vs)

Fixed-length vectors indexed by a `Nat` dimension.

`Vec(a, n)` is a list of `a` whose length `n` is a type-level natural. The `Nat` kind unifies dimensions by equality of literals and variables only: there is no successor structure and no arithmetic, and `n + m` in a dimension position is declined at the parser. This module therefore ships exactly the operations that equality-only indexing can type honestly:

- `vempty` and `vsingle` pin a literal length (`0`, `1`). - `vmap` preserves the length (`n` appears on both sides). - `vzip` requires equal lengths (both `n`); a length clash is a compile error that names both lengths.

Two operations are deliberately absent because their result length is not expressible under equality-only unification: a length-changing `vcons : (a, Vec(a, n)) -> Vec(a, n + 1)` and an append `(Vec(a, n), Vec(a, m)) -> Vec(a, n + m)`. That is the declined line; writing either `n + 1` produces a pointed rejection rather than a bare parse error.

`vhead` accepts any length, so it cannot statically forbid the empty vector (ruling it out needs `n = m + 1`, again arithmetic). On an empty vector it raises `Fail` rather than guarding with an `Option`; this is the head-on-empty consequence of the declined line.

-- | Fixed-length vectors indexed by a `Nat` dimension.
--
-- `Vec(a, n)` is a list of `a` whose length `n` is a type-level natural. The
-- `Nat` kind unifies dimensions by equality of literals and variables only:
-- there is no successor structure and no arithmetic, and `n + m` in a dimension
-- position is declined at the parser. This module therefore ships exactly the
-- operations that equality-only indexing can type honestly:
--
--   - `vempty` and `vsingle` pin a literal length (`0`, `1`).
--   - `vmap` preserves the length (`n` appears on both sides).
--   - `vzip` requires equal lengths (both `n`); a length clash is a compile
--     error that names both lengths.
--
-- Two operations are deliberately absent because their result length is not
-- expressible under equality-only unification: a length-changing
-- `vcons : (a, Vec(a, n)) -> Vec(a, n + 1)` and an append
-- `(Vec(a, n), Vec(a, m)) -> Vec(a, n + m)`. That is the declined line; writing
-- either `n + 1` produces a pointed rejection rather than a bare parse error.
--
-- `vhead` accepts any length, so it cannot statically forbid the empty vector
-- (ruling it out needs `n = m + 1`, again arithmetic). On an empty vector it
-- raises `Fail` rather than guarding with an `Option`; this is the head-on-empty
-- consequence of the declined line.

import Data.List (..)

-- | A vector of `a` with a type-level length `n`.
pub type Vec(a, n : Nat) = MkVec(List(a))

-- | The empty vector, length `0`.
pub fn vempty() : Vec(a, 0) = MkVec([])

-- | The one-element vector, length `1`.
--
-- ```prism
-- vto_list(vsingle(42))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [42]
-- ```
pub fn vsingle(x : a) : Vec(a, 1) = MkVec([x])

-- | The underlying list, forgetting the static length.
--
-- ```prism
-- vto_list(vsingle(7))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [7]
-- ```
pub fn vto_list(v : Vec(a, n)) : List(a) =
  match v of
    MkVec(xs) => xs

-- | Apply `f` to every element, preserving the length.
--
-- ```prism
-- vto_list(vmap(\(x) -> x * 2, vsingle(21)))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [42]
-- ```
pub fn vmap(f : (a) -> b, v : Vec(a, n)) : Vec(b, n) =
  match v of
    MkVec(xs) => MkVec(map(f, xs))

-- | Zip two vectors of the SAME length into a vector of pairs. The shared `n`
-- forces equal lengths; a mismatch is rejected at compile time, naming both.
--
-- ```prism
-- vto_list(vzip(vsingle(1), vsingle(2)))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [(1, 2)]
-- ```
--
-- A length mismatch is a compile error:
--
-- ```prism,compile_fail
-- vzip(vsingle(1), vempty())
-- ```
pub fn vzip(u : Vec(a, n), v : Vec(b, n)) : Vec((a, b), n) =
  match u of
    MkVec(xs) =>
      match v of
        MkVec(ys) => MkVec(zip(xs, ys))

-- | The first element. `n` is unconstrained, so the empty vector is not ruled
-- out statically; on an empty vector this raises `Fail`.
--
-- ```prism
-- vhead(vsingle(42))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 42
-- ```
pub fn vhead(v : Vec(a, n)) : a =
  match v of
    MkVec(xs) =>
      match xs of
        Cons(x, _) => x
        Nil => fail()

Analysis walks over the surface syntax tree.

Every function here is a few lines over `Control.Layer`'s generic queries at `expr_layer()`, and that is the point: a pass asks for "every variable occurrence" or "every call site" instead of writing its own recursion, and the answer comes back in source order every time. Nothing here decides what a name means; that is the resolver's job and `Syntax.Rename` queries it.
modules.source:
-- | Analysis walks over the surface syntax tree.
--
-- Every function here is a few lines over `Control.Layer`'s generic queries at
-- `expr_layer()`, and that is the point: a pass asks for "every variable
-- occurrence" or "every call site" instead of writing its own recursion, and
-- the answer comes back in source order every time. Nothing here decides what a
-- name means; that is the resolver's job and `Syntax.Rename` queries it.

import Control.Layer (..)

import Data.Foldable (elem, length)

import Data.List (concat_map, filter, map)

import Syntax.Ast (..)

import Syntax.Source (..)

import Syntax.Walk (..)

-- | Every node of an expression, root first, in source order.
pub fn an_nodes(e : Sp(Expr)) : List(Sp(Expr)) = lay_universe(expr_layer(), e)

-- | Every node satisfying a predicate, in source order.
pub fn an_where(
  q : (Sp(Expr)) -> Bool ! {| f},
  e : Sp(Expr)
) : List(Sp(Expr)) ! { | f} =
  lay_collect(expr_layer(), q, e)

-- | The number of nodes in an expression.
pub fn an_size(e : Sp(Expr)) : Int = lay_size(expr_layer(), e)

-- | The height of an expression: `1` at a leaf.
pub fn an_depth(e : Sp(Expr)) : Int = lay_depth(expr_layer(), e)

-- | The span of every node, root first, in source order.
pub fn an_spans(e : Sp(Expr)) : List(Span) = map(span_of, an_nodes(e))

-- | Every variable occurrence: the identifier and the exact span it covers.
-- This is the occurrence table an editor tool wants, and the one place a
-- purely syntactic tool should stop: it says where a name is written, never
-- what it refers to.
pub fn an_var_uses(e : Sp(Expr)) : List((String, Span)) =
  concat_map(an_var_use, an_nodes(e))

fn an_var_use(n : Sp(Expr)) : List((String, Span)) =
  match node_of(n) of
    EVar(name) => [(name, span_of(n))]
    _ => []

-- | Every name written as a variable, in first-occurrence order and without
-- repeats.
pub fn an_var_names(e : Sp(Expr)) : List(String) =
  an_dedup(map(an_use_name, an_var_uses(e)), Nil)

fn an_use_name(u : (String, Span)) : String =
  match u of
    (name, _) => name

-- | How many times a name is written as a variable.
pub fn an_uses_of(name : String, e : Sp(Expr)) : Int =
  length(filter(\(u) -> an_use_name(u) == name, an_var_uses(e)))

-- | Every call site, in source order.
pub fn an_calls(e : Sp(Expr)) : List(Sp(Expr)) = filter(an_is_call, an_nodes(e))

-- | Whether a node is an application. The predicate `an_calls` filters on, made
-- public so a rewrite can scope a rule to call sites without restating it.
pub fn an_is_call(n : Sp(Expr)) : Bool =
  match node_of(n) of
    ECall(_, _) => true
    _ => false

-- | The name of every directly called function, in source order. A call whose
-- head is not a plain variable (a field access, a lambda, a computed callee)
-- contributes nothing rather than a guess.
pub fn an_call_targets(e : Sp(Expr)) : List(String) =
  concat_map(an_call_target, an_nodes(e))

fn an_call_target(n : Sp(Expr)) : List(String) =
  match node_of(n) of
    ECall(f, _) =>
      match node_of(f) of
        EVar(name) => [name]
        _ => []
    _ => []

-- | The span of every typed hole, in source order: what a completion tool asks
-- for first.
pub fn an_holes(e : Sp(Expr)) : List(Span) = concat_map(an_hole, an_nodes(e))

fn an_hole(n : Sp(Expr)) : List(Span) =
  match node_of(n) of
    EHole(_) => [span_of(n)]
    _ => []

-- | Whether any node satisfies the predicate, short-circuiting on the first
-- hit.
pub fn an_any(q : (Sp(Expr)) -> Bool ! {| f}, e : Sp(Expr)) : Bool ! { | f} =
  lay_any(expr_layer(), q, e)

-- | A shape census of one expression: the counts a size heuristic, a lint
-- threshold, or a complexity report is built from. `nodes` is every node,
-- `vars` every variable occurrence, `calls` every application, `holes` every
-- typed hole, and `binds` every form that introduces a name (a let, a mutable
-- declaration, a lambda, a match, a for loop, a comprehension), counted once per
-- form rather than once per name it binds.
pub type ExprCensus = ExprCensus {
  nodes: Int,
  vars: Int,
  calls: Int,
  binds: Int,
  holes: Int
}

-- | Count every shape in one walk. The combining operation is field-wise
-- addition, which is what `lay_summarize` was shaped for: one pass, one
-- caller-supplied monoid, no repeated traversals.
pub fn an_census(e : Sp(Expr)) : ExprCensus =
  lay_summarize(expr_layer(), an_measure, an_add, an_zero(), e)

fn an_zero() : ExprCensus =
  ExprCensus {
    nodes = 0,
    vars = 0,
    calls = 0,
    binds = 0,
    holes = 0
  }

fn an_one(vars : Int, calls : Int, binds : Int, holes : Int) : ExprCensus =
  ExprCensus {
    nodes = 1,
    vars = vars,
    calls = calls,
    binds = binds,
    holes = holes
  }

fn an_measure(n : Sp(Expr)) : ExprCensus =
  match node_of(n) of
    EVar(_) => an_one(1, 0, 0, 0)
    ECall(_, _) => an_one(0, 1, 0, 0)
    EHole(_) => an_one(0, 0, 0, 1)
    ELet(_, _, _) => an_one(0, 0, 1, 0)
    EVarDecl(_, _, _) => an_one(0, 0, 1, 0)
    ELam(_, _) => an_one(0, 0, 1, 0)
    EMatch(_, _) => an_one(0, 0, 1, 0)
    EFor(_, _, _, _) => an_one(0, 0, 1, 0)
    EComp(_, _, _, _) => an_one(0, 0, 1, 0)
    _ => an_one(0, 0, 0, 0)

fn an_add(a : ExprCensus, b : ExprCensus) : ExprCensus =
  ExprCensus {
    nodes = a.nodes + b.nodes,
    vars = a.vars + b.vars,
    calls = a.calls + b.calls,
    binds = a.binds + b.binds,
    holes = a.holes + b.holes
  }

fn an_dedup(xs : List(String), seen : List(String)) : List(String) =
  match xs of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(x, rest) =>
      if elem(x, seen) then
        an_dedup(rest, seen)
      else
        Cons(x, an_dedup(rest, Cons(x, seen)))

The typed surface syntax that the `prism-surface-syntax-v1` artifact decodes into.

Constructor prefixes name the family (`I` items, `E` expressions, `P` patterns, `Ty` types), and spanned nodes wrap in `Sp`. The shapes mirror the compiler's exporter exactly, so a decoded document re-encodes to identical bytes.
modules.source:
-- | The typed surface syntax that the `prism-surface-syntax-v1` artifact
-- decodes into.
--
-- Constructor prefixes name the family (`I` items, `E` expressions, `P`
-- patterns, `Ty` types), and spanned nodes wrap in `Sp`. The shapes mirror the
-- compiler's exporter exactly, so a decoded document re-encodes to identical
-- bytes.

import Syntax.Source (..)

-- | A parsed node with its byte span and the parse-sugar bit. Expressions and
-- patterns are spanned; `synth` is set when the parser rewrote surface sugar
-- into this node rather than reading it verbatim.
pub type Sp(a) = Sp { node: a, span: Span, synth: Bool }

-- | An integer literal's optional width suffix: `i64`, `u64`, or none.
pub type Suffix = SufNone | SufI64 | SufU64

-- | A kind: the classifier of a type parameter. Ground kinds classify types,
-- rows, and type-level naturals; `KFun` is the kind of a type constructor.
pub type Kind
  = KType
  | KRow
  | KNat
  | KFun(Kind, Kind)

-- | One effect label: an effect name applied to zero or more type arguments,
-- as it appears in an effect row or an effect alias.
pub type EffLabel = EffLabel { name: String, args: List(Ty) }

-- | An effect row: the labels present plus an optional row-variable tail. The
-- empty row and a tail-less label list share this one shape.
pub type Row = Row { labels: List(EffLabel), tail: Option(String) }

-- | A surface type. Ground types, type variables, applications, function types
-- with an effect row, saturated constructors, tuples, unboxed aggregates, row
-- literals, type-level naturals, and usage-qualified types.
pub type Ty
  = TyInt
  | TyI64
  | TyU64
  | TyBool
  | TyUnit
  | TyFloat
  | TyChar
  | TyStr
  | TyVar(String)
  | TyApp(String, List(Ty))
  | TyState(Int)
  | TyForall(List(String), Ty)
  | TyFun(List(Ty), Row, Ty)
  | TyCon(String, List(Ty))
  | TyTuple(List(Ty))
  | TyUnboxedTuple(List(Ty))
  | TyUnboxedRecord(List(CField))
  | TyRowLit(Row)
  | TyNat(Int)
  | TyUsage(Ty, List(String))

-- | A named field carrying a type: a record constructor field or an unboxed
-- record field.
pub type CField = CField { name: String, ty: Ty }

-- | A named field carrying an expression: a record literal field, a record
-- update field, a where binding, or a converter override.
pub type NamedExpr = NamedExpr { name: String, value: Sp(Expr) }

-- | A surface expression. One constructor per node kind the exporter emits,
-- including the desugarable surface forms (loops, comprehensions, throw and
-- try-catch, path reads and updates) that the parser records before lowering.
pub type Expr
  = EInt(String, Suffix)
  | EFloat(String)
  | EChar(String)
  | EBool(Bool)
  | EUnit
  | EStr(String)
  | EVar(String)
  | EHole(String)
  | EBin(String, Sp(Expr), Sp(Expr))
  | ENeg(Sp(Expr))
  | EIf(Sp(Expr), Sp(Expr), Sp(Expr))
  | ELet(String, Sp(Expr), Sp(Expr))
  | ELam(List(Param), Sp(Expr))
  | ECall(Sp(Expr), List(Sp(Expr)))
  | EPipe(Sp(Expr), Sp(Expr))
  | EMatch(Sp(Expr), List(Arm))
  | EList(List(Sp(Expr)))
  | ETuple(List(Sp(Expr)))
  | EField(Sp(Expr), String)
  | EUnboxedTuple(List(Sp(Expr)))
  | EUnboxedRecord(List(NamedExpr))
  | EUnboxedField(Sp(Expr), String)
  | ERecord(String, List(NamedExpr))
  | ERecordUpdate(Sp(Expr), String, List(NamedExpr))
  | EPathUpdate(Sp(Expr), List(PathUpdate))
  | EHandle(Sp(Expr), List(HandlerArm), Bool)
  | EMask(String, Sp(Expr))
  | EInst(Sp(Expr), List(String))
  | EIndex(Sp(Expr), Sp(Expr))
  | EIndexSet(Sp(Expr), Sp(Expr), Sp(Expr))
  | EAnn(Sp(Expr), Ty)
  | EMarker(String)
  | ENamedHandle(String, Sp(Expr), List(HandlerArm))
  | EVarDecl(String, Sp(Expr), Sp(Expr))
  | EAssign(String, Sp(Expr))
  | EIndexAssign(Sp(Expr), Sp(Expr), Sp(Expr))
  | EThrow(String, List(Sp(Expr)))
  | ETryCatch(Sp(Expr), List(CatchArm))
  | EFor(String, Sp(Expr), List(Qual), Sp(Expr))
  | EWhile(Sp(Expr), Sp(Expr))
  | ELoop(Sp(Expr))
  | EBreak
  | EContinue
  | EReturn(Sp(Expr))
  | EComp(Sp(Expr), String, Sp(Expr), List(Qual))
  | EDefault(Sp(Expr), Sp(Expr))
  | ETransact(Sp(Expr), Sp(Expr))
  | EProbe(String, Sp(Expr))
  | EReflect(String, String)
  | EOptChain(Sp(Expr), String)
  | ERange(List(Sp(Expr)), Sp(Expr))
  | ECompose(String, Sp(Expr), Sp(Expr))
  | EReadPath(Sp(Expr), List(PathStep))

-- | One match arm: a spanned pattern, an optional boolean guard, and the body
-- taken when the pattern matches and the guard holds.
pub type Arm = Arm { pat: Sp(Pat), guard: Option(Sp(Expr)), body: Sp(Expr) }

-- | One arm of an effect handler: the return clause, a full operation clause
-- binding the resumption, or the `once`, `val`, and `never` sugars.
pub type HandlerArm
  = HReturn(String, Sp(Expr))
  | HOp(String, List(String), String, Sp(Expr))
  | HOnce(String, List(String), Sp(Expr))
  | HVal(String, Sp(Expr))
  | HNever(String, List(String), Sp(Expr))

-- | One catch arm of a try-catch: the error name, the binders for its payload,
-- and the handler body.
pub type CatchArm = CatchArm {
  name: String,
  binders: List(String),
  body: Sp(Expr),
  span: Span
}

-- | One qualifier of a for-loop or comprehension: a boolean guard or a binding
-- generator.
pub type Qual = QGuard(Sp(Expr)) | QBind(String, Sp(Expr))

-- | One step of an optic path: a field, every element, a case selection, an
-- index, or a where filter.
pub type PathStep
  = PSField(String)
  | PSEach
  | PSCase(String)
  | PSIndex(Sp(Expr))
  | PSWhere(Sp(Expr))

-- | The write at the end of an optic path: set to a value or modify by a
-- function.
pub type PathOp = POSet(Sp(Expr)) | POModify(Sp(Expr))

-- | One update in a path-update expression: the path walked and the write
-- performed at its end.
pub type PathUpdate = PathUpdate { path: List(PathStep), op: PathOp }

-- | A surface pattern: wildcards, variables, literals, constructor and tuple
-- patterns, record patterns with an optional rest, and alternations. An
-- alternation is expanded into one match arm per alternative before the
-- checker, so it appears only in the surface seam.
pub type Pat
  = PWild
  | PVar(String)
  | PInt(String, Suffix)
  | PFloat(String)
  | PChar(String)
  | PBool(Bool)
  | PCtor(String, List(Sp(Pat)))
  | PTuple(List(Sp(Pat)))
  | PRecord(String, List(PatField), Bool)
  | POr(List(Sp(Pat)))

-- | One field of a record pattern: the field name and the pattern bound to it.
pub type PatField = PatField { name: String, pat: Sp(Pat) }

-- | A function parameter: its name, the pattern it was written as if it was
-- written as one rather than named, an optional type annotation, whether it is
-- taken by borrow, and an optional default expression. A pattern parameter's
-- name is synthesized from its position, so the pattern is the half of it the
-- source wrote.
pub type Param = Param {
  name: String,
  pat: Option(Sp(Pat)),
  ty: Option(Ty),
  is_borrow: Bool,
  dflt: Option(Sp(Expr))
}

-- | A class constraint on a type: the class name, the constrained type, and its
-- span.
pub type Constraint = Constraint { cls: String, ty: Ty, span: Span }

-- | A function, constant, or logic-function declaration, with every optional
-- clause the parser can attach: effect row, constraints, where bindings,
-- requires and ensures, a decreases measure, and the totality and resource
-- modifiers.
pub type Decl = Decl {
  name: String,
  params: List(Param),
  ret: Option(Ty),
  eff: Option(Row),
  constraints: List(Constraint),
  body: Sp(Expr),
  wheres: List(NamedExpr),
  reqs: List(Sp(Expr)),
  enss: List(Ensure),
  measure: Option(Sp(Expr)),
  is_test: Bool,
  totality: Option(String),
  fip_word: Option(String),
  is_replayable: Bool,
  is_no_alloc: Bool,
  span: Span
}

-- | One ensures clause: the binder for the result and the postcondition
-- expression over it.
pub type Ensure = Ensure { binder: String, expr: Sp(Expr) }

-- | The shape of a data constructor: a positional argument list or a named
-- field list.
pub type CtorShape = CPositional(List(Ty)) | CRecord(List(CField))

-- | One data constructor: its name and its argument shape.
pub type Ctor = Ctor { name: String, shape: CtorShape }

-- | One derived class on a data declaration: the class name and its span.
pub type Deriving = Deriving { name: String, span: Span }

-- | One class method signature: the method name and its declared type.
pub type Method = Method { name: String, ty: Ty }

-- | One operation of an effect declaration: its name, parameter types, result
-- type, and optional resumption grade.
pub type EffOp = EffOp {
  name: String,
  params: List(Ty),
  ret: Ty,
  grade: Option(String)
}

-- | One rung of a stable type: the version name, an optional base to inherit
-- from, its fields, and an optional frozen marker.
pub type Rung = Rung {
  name: String,
  base: Option(String),
  fields: List(RungField),
  frozen: Option(String),
  span: Span
}

-- | One field of a stable rung: the field name, its type, and an optional
-- default expression.
pub type RungField = RungField { name: String, ty: Ty, dflt: Option(Sp(Expr)) }

-- | One converter between stable rungs: the direction, the from and to rung
-- names, the base expression, overriding field bindings, and dropped fields.
pub type Converter = Converter {
  dir: String,
  from: String,
  to: String,
  base: Sp(Expr),
  overrides: List(NamedExpr),
  drop_loss: List(String),
  span: Span
}

-- | The route of a stable migration: automatic, or an explicit upgrade and
-- downgrade pair.
pub type MigrationRoute = MAuto | MVersion(MigrationDir, MigrationDir)

-- | One direction of an explicit migration: automatic or a given expression.
pub type MigrationDir = DAuto | DExpr(Sp(Expr))

-- | One migration of a stable type: the from and to rung names and its route.
pub type Migration = Migration {
  from: String,
  to: String,
  route: MigrationRoute,
  span: Span
}

-- | A top-level item of a source file, tagged by its declaration family.
-- Named items carry an optional visibility (`pub` or `opaque`) and an optional
-- deprecation message; imports, instances, and canonical bindings do not.
pub type Item
  = IImport { path: List(String), mod_alias: Option(String), names: Option(List(String)), glob: Bool, reexport: Bool, span: Span }
  | IData { nt: Bool, name: String, params: List(String), param_kinds: List(Kind), ctors: List(Ctor), derivs: List(Deriving), span: Span, vis: Option(String), dep: Option(String) }
  | IEffect { name: String, params: List(String), ops: List(EffOp), span: Span, vis: Option(String), dep: Option(String) }
  | IError { name: String, arg_types: List(Ty), span: Span, vis: Option(String), dep: Option(String) }
  | IEffAlias { name: String, labels: List(EffLabel), span: Span, vis: Option(String), dep: Option(String) }
  | ISynonym { name: String, params: List(String), ty: Ty, span: Span, vis: Option(String), dep: Option(String) }
  | IClass { name: String, param: String, supers: List(String), methods: List(Method), span: Span, vis: Option(String), dep: Option(String) }
  | IInstance { name: String, cls: String, head: Ty, context: List(Constraint), decls: List(Decl), span: Span }
  | ICanonical { cls: String, head: Ty, name: String, span: Span }
  | IPattern { name: String, params: List(String), forty: String, viewfn: Sp(Expr), makefn: Option(Sp(Expr)), span: Span, vis: Option(String), dep: Option(String) }
  | IStable { name: String, rungs: List(Rung), converters: List(Converter), migrations: List(Migration), span: Span, vis: Option(String), dep: Option(String) }
  | IDecl { decl: Decl, declkind: String, vis: Option(String), dep: Option(String) }

-- | The wrapped node, without its location.
pub fn node_of(sp : Sp(a)) : a = sp.node

-- | The node's byte span.
pub fn span_of(sp : Sp(a)) : Span = sp.span

-- | Whether the parser synthesized this node from surface sugar rather than
-- reading it verbatim from the source.
pub fn is_synth(sp : Sp(a)) : Bool = sp.synth

The printer here matches the compiler's export format precisely: two-space indent, one element per line, a space after each key's colon, `[]` and `{}` for empty collections, insertion-order object keys, and the shared escape discipline (named escapes plus lowercase `\u00xx` for other control characters).
