A Prism-language reimplementation of the compiler's raw token layer: exact UTF-8 tokenization, literal payload decoding, and interpolation splitting.

The whole layer is ordinary Prism. The Rust `lex_raw` pipeline remains the authoritative oracle; this module produces the same raw token stream (kind, byte span, and decoded value) and the same interleaved trivia (line comments and blank-line runs) so the two can be diffed. It is compared and reported, never used as a silent fallback.

Scope of this layer: the fixed-token vocabulary, identifiers, uppercase names, qualified paths, numbers, char and string literals, line comments, and blank-line trivia; the decoded value each token carries (identifier text, separator-stripped integers, normalized floats, unescaped chars and strings); and the interpolation split of a `"a {x} b"` literal into `istart`/`imid`/ `iend` segment tokens with the hole expressions re-lexed at their absolute source offsets. A nested string literal inside a hole is scanned with a brace-depth stack, so its own quotes and braces never end the outer token early. Bracket tracking and the offside layout virtuals are later layers; no layout virtual is synthesized here.
modules.source:
-- | A Prism-language reimplementation of the compiler's raw token layer: exact
-- UTF-8 tokenization, literal payload decoding, and interpolation splitting.
--
-- The whole layer is ordinary Prism. The Rust `lex_raw` pipeline remains the
-- authoritative oracle; this module produces the same raw token stream (kind,
-- byte span, and decoded value) and the same interleaved trivia (line comments
-- and blank-line runs) so the two can be diffed. It is compared and reported,
-- never used as a silent fallback.
--
-- Scope of this layer: the fixed-token vocabulary, identifiers, uppercase names,
-- qualified paths, numbers, char and string literals, line comments, and
-- blank-line trivia; the decoded value each token carries (identifier text,
-- separator-stripped integers, normalized floats, unescaped chars and strings);
-- and the interpolation split of a `"a {x} b"` literal into `istart`/`imid`/
-- `iend` segment tokens with the hole expressions re-lexed at their absolute
-- source offsets. A nested string literal inside a hole is scanned with a
-- brace-depth stack, so its own quotes and braces never end the outer token
-- early. Bracket tracking and the offside layout virtuals are later layers; no
-- layout virtual is synthesized here.

import Data.List (..)

import Data.Maybe (..)

import Data.Result (..)

import Data.Char (..)

import Syntax.Source (..)

import Syntax.Token (..)

-- | The raw token layer: the semantic token stream and the trivia interleaved
-- between them, each keyed by absolute byte span into the lexed text.
pub type LexRaw = LexRaw { tokens: List(Token), trivia: List(Trivia) }

-- | A lexing failure, mirroring the compiler's five `LexError` variants one for
-- one: an invalid token, an empty interpolation hole, an unterminated hole, an
-- unterminated string, and a misplaced numeric separator. Each carries the byte
-- offset where scanning stuck. The variant, its stable code, and its rendered
-- message travel as data (see `lex_offset`/`lex_code`/`lex_message`), never
-- encoded into a message string.
pub type LexError
  = LxInvalid(Int)
  | LxEmptyHole(Int)
  | LxUntermHole(Int)
  | LxUntermStr(Int)
  | LxNumberSep(Int)
  deriving (Eq, Show)

-- | The byte offset where a lexing failure stuck.
pub fn lex_offset(e : LexError) : Int =
  match e of
    LxInvalid(o) => o
    LxEmptyHole(o) => o
    LxUntermHole(o) => o
    LxUntermStr(o) => o
    LxNumberSep(o) => o

-- | The stable, append-only diagnostic code a lexing failure carries, matching
-- the compiler's `LexError::code` (E7000 through E7004).
pub fn lex_code(e : LexError) : String =
  match e of
    LxInvalid(_) => "E7000"
    LxEmptyHole(_) => "E7001"
    LxUntermHole(_) => "E7002"
    LxUntermStr(_) => "E7003"
    LxNumberSep(_) => "E7004"

-- | The rendered message, matching the compiler's `LexError` `Display` strings
-- byte for byte so a decoded diagnostic compares equal.
pub fn lex_message(e : LexError) : String =
  match e of
    LxInvalid(_) => "unexpected token"
    LxEmptyHole(_) => "empty interpolation hole `\{\}`"
    LxUntermHole(_) => "unterminated interpolation hole"
    LxUntermStr(_) => "unterminated string literal"
    LxNumberSep(_) =>
      "malformed numeric literal: `_` separators must sit between two digits"

-- One classification step: a comment ending at the given offset, a real token of
-- a kind ending at the given offset, or a hard error.
type LxStep = LxComment(Int) | LxTok(TokenKind, Int) | LxErr(LexError)

-- The sentinel returned by `lx_at` past end of input: outside the 0..255 byte
-- range so every byte comparison against it is false.
fn lx_eof() : Int = 256

-- Byte at `i`, or the end sentinel when `i` is at or past the end.
fn lx_at(text : String, i : Int) : Int =
  if i < byte_len(text) then
    byte_at(text, i)
  else
    lx_eof()

-- The single byte of a one-byte ASCII string, for naming punctuation.
fn lx_b(s : String) : Int = byte_at(s, 0)

-- Whitespace bytes logos skips between tokens: space, tab, form feed, CR, LF.
-- Form feed (12) matters here because logos skips it but `Data.Char.is_space`
-- omits it.
fn lx_ws(c : Int) : Bool = c == 32 || c == 9 || c == 12 || c == 13 || c == 10

-- A word-continuation byte: [A-Za-z0-9_].
fn lx_word(c : Int) : Bool = is_alnum(c) || c == lx_b("_")

-- A segment-start byte for a qualified path component: [A-Za-z_].
fn lx_seg_start(c : Int) : Bool = is_alpha(c) || c == lx_b("_")

-- A digit-or-separator byte inside a number run: [0-9_].
fn lx_digit_us(c : Int) : Bool = is_digit(c) || c == lx_b("_")

-- Skip a run of whitespace from `i`, returning the first non-whitespace offset.
fn lx_skip_ws(text : String, i : Int, n : Int) : Int =
  var j := i
  while j < n && lx_ws(byte_at(text, j)) do
    j += 1
  j

-- Scan a [A-Za-z0-9_]* run from `i`, returning the offset just past it.
fn lx_scan_word(text : String, i : Int, n : Int) : Int =
  var j := i
  while j < n && lx_word(byte_at(text, j)) do
    j += 1
  j

-- Scan a [0-9_]* run from `i`, returning the offset just past it.
fn lx_scan_digits(text : String, i : Int, n : Int) : Int =
  var j := i
  while j < n && lx_digit_us(byte_at(text, j)) do
    j += 1
  j

-- Scan a line comment body from `i` (at the `--`), returning the offset of the
-- terminating newline or end of input. The span is [i, result).
fn lx_scan_comment(text : String, i : Int, n : Int) : Int =
  var j := i
  while j < n && byte_at(text, j) /= 10 do
    j += 1
  j

-- Scan an optional exponent `[eE][+-]?[0-9_]+` starting at `k`. Returns the
-- offset past a well-formed exponent, or `k` unchanged when there is none.
fn lx_scan_exp(text : String, k : Int, n : Int) : Int =
  let c = lx_at(text, k)
  if c == lx_b("e") || c == lx_b("E") then
    let m0 = k + 1
    let s = lx_at(text, m0)
    let m1 =
      if s == lx_b("+") || s == lx_b("-") then
        m0 + 1
      else
        m0
    if lx_digit_us(lx_at(text, m1)) then
      lx_scan_digits(text, m1, n)
    else
      k
  else
    k

-- Scan a qualified-path tail `(\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)+` starting at `j` (a
-- `.` whose next byte is a segment start), returning the offset past the path.
fn lx_scan_qual(text : String, j : Int, n : Int) : Int =
  var k := j
  while (lx_at(text, k) == lx_b(".") && lx_seg_start(lx_at(text, k + 1))) do
    k := k + 2
    while k < n && lx_word(byte_at(text, k)) do
      k += 1
  k

-- The byte length of the UTF-8 codepoint led by byte `b`.
fn lx_cp_len(b : Int) : Int =
  if b < 128 then
    1
  elif b >= 240 then
    4
  elif b >= 224 then
    3
  elif b >= 192 then
    2
  else
    1

-- Skip one UTF-8 codepoint starting at `p`, returning the offset past it.
fn lx_skip_cp(text : String, p : Int, n : Int) : Int =
  let b = lx_at(text, p)
  if b == lx_eof() then
    p
  else
    p + lx_cp_len(b)

-- Whether text[i ..] begins with the exact bytes of `s`.
fn lx_matches(text : String, i : Int, s : String) : Bool =
  lx_matches_go(text, i, s, 0, byte_len(s))

fn lx_matches_go(text : String, i : Int, s : String, k : Int, m : Int) : Bool =
  if k >= m then
    true
  elif lx_at(text, i + k) == byte_at(s, k) then
    lx_matches_go(text, i, s, k + 1, m)
  else
    false

-- Whether the run [lo, hi) equals `s` exactly (same length, same bytes).
fn lx_run_eq(text : String, lo : Int, hi : Int, s : String) : Bool =
  hi - lo == byte_len(s) && lx_matches(text, lo, s)

-- The fixed spelling tables, built once per lex and threaded down the token
-- path. Each table below is a list literal, and evaluating one allocates every
-- string in it, so a table rebuilt per token costs more than the comparison it
-- feeds. Each is held bucketed by first byte rather than flat, so a token
-- compares itself only against the spellings that could possibly match it: an
-- identifier beginning with a letter that starts no keyword meets an empty
-- bucket instead of walking the whole table.
type LxTabs = LxTabs {
  lower: Array(List(String)),
  upper: Array(List(String)),
  ops: Array(List(String))
}

fn lx_tabs() : LxTabs =
  LxTabs {
    lower = lx_by_first(lx_lower_keywords()),
    upper = lx_by_first(lx_upper_keywords()),
    ops = lx_by_first(lx_operators())
  }

-- The number of distinct byte values, and so the width of a first-byte index.
-- Every byte the classifier can hand to a lookup is a real byte of the input
-- (`byte_at` only returns -1 past the end, and no classifier branch is reached
-- there), so an index this wide is always in bounds.
fn lx_byte_span() : Int = 256

-- A spelling table indexed by its entries' first byte. Buckets are derived from
-- the table rather than written out beside it, so the table above stays the one
-- place a spelling is named, and each bucket keeps the table's own order, so
-- maximal munch still reaches the longer spelling before its prefix.
fn lx_by_first(tbl : List(String)) : Array(List(String)) =
  lx_by_first_go(reverse(tbl), array_new(lx_byte_span(), Nil))

-- Entries are consumed back to front and pushed onto their bucket, which
-- restores the table's order within each bucket.
fn lx_by_first_go(
  xs : List(String),
  acc : Array(List(String))
) : Array(List(String)) =
  match xs of
    Nil => acc
    Cons(s, rest) =>
      let b = byte_at(s, 0)
      lx_by_first_go(rest, array_set(acc, b, Cons(s, array_get(acc, b))))

-- The first keyword spelling whose bytes equal the run [lo, hi), if any.
fn lx_find_kw(
  text : String,
  lo : Int,
  hi : Int,
  kws : List(String)
) : Option(String) =
  match kws of
    Nil => None
    Cons(k, rest) =>
      if lx_run_eq(text, lo, hi, k) then
        Some(k)
      else
        lx_find_kw(text, lo, hi, rest)

-- The lowercase-led keyword spellings, matching the compiler's fixed-token set.
fn lx_lower_keywords() : List(String) =
  [
      "fn",
      "fip",
      "fbip",
      "replayable",
      "logic",
      "requires",
      "ensures",
      "pub",
      "import",
      "as",
      "type",
      "newtype",
      "stable",
      "opaque",
      "effect",
      "error",
      "throw",
      "try",
      "catch",
      "transact",
      "probe",
      "alias",
      "class",
      "instance",
      "canonical",
      "pattern",
      "deriving",
      "where",
      "given",
      "handle",
      "with",
      "handler",
      "mask",
      "val",
      "return",
      "let",
      "var",
      "borrow",
      "in",
      "for",
      "while",
      "loop",
      "break",
      "continue",
      "do",
      "if",
      "then",
      "else",
      "elif",
      "match",
      "of",
      "each",
      "forall",
      "true",
      "false",
      "using",
    ]

-- The uppercase-led type keywords, matching the compiler's fixed-token set.
fn lx_upper_keywords() : List(String) =
  ["Int", "Bool", "Unit", "Float", "Char", "String", "I64", "U64"]

-- The operator and punctuation spellings, longest first so maximal munch tries
-- the three-byte forms before their two-byte prefixes and those before their
-- one-byte prefixes.
fn lx_operators() : List(String) =
  [
      "==.",
      "/=.",
      "<=.",
      ">=.",
      "->",
      "<-",
      "=>",
      "<.",
      ">.",
      "==",
      "/=",
      "<=",
      ">=",
      "&&",
      "||",
      "|>",
      ">>",
      "<<",
      "+.",
      "-.",
      "+=",
      "-=",
      "*=",
      "%=",
      "*.",
      "/.",
      ":=",
      "..",
      "??",
      "?.",
      "<",
      ">",
      "=",
      "|",
      "\\",
      "+",
      "-",
      "*",
      "/",
      "%",
      "^",
      "~",
      "(",
      ")",
      "\{",
      "\}",
      "[",
      "]",
      ",",
      ":",
      "!",
      "@",
      "#",
      ".",
      "?",
    ]

-- Classify a lowercase-led word run as a keyword token or an identifier, given
-- the keyword bucket for the byte the run starts with.
fn lx_lower(text : String, i : Int, n : Int, kws : List(String)) : LxStep =
  let j = lx_scan_word(text, i, n)
  match lx_find_kw(text, i, j, kws) of
    Some(kw) => LxTok(TFixed(kw), j)
    None => LxTok(TIdent, j)

-- Classify an uppercase-led run: a qualified path if a dotted segment follows,
-- else a type keyword, else an uppercase identifier.
fn lx_upper(text : String, i : Int, n : Int, kws : List(String)) : LxStep =
  let j = lx_scan_word(text, i, n)
  if (lx_at(text, j) == lx_b(".") && lx_seg_start(lx_at(text, j + 1))) then
    LxTok(TQual, lx_scan_qual(text, j, n))
  else
    match lx_find_kw(text, i, j, kws) of
      Some(kw) => LxTok(TFixed(kw), j)
      None => LxTok(TUid, j)

-- An integer token, consuming an optional `i64` or `u64` suffix.
fn lx_int_suffix(text : String, j : Int) : LxStep =
  if lx_matches(text, j, "i64") || lx_matches(text, j, "u64") then
    LxTok(TInt, j + 3)
  else
    LxTok(TInt, j)

-- The byte offset of the first misplaced `_` in the numeric run text[lo, hi), or
-- None when every separator sits between two digits. Mirrors the compiler's
-- `bad_separator`: a `_` is admissible only flanked by an ASCII digit on each
-- side, catching the leading, trailing, doubled, and adjacent-to-`.`/`e`/sign
-- cases in one rule. The `i64`/`u64` suffix holds no `_`, so scanning the whole
-- run rather than the digits-only slice reports the same first offset.
fn lx_bad_sep(text : String, lo : Int, hi : Int) : Option(Int) =
  lx_bad_sep_go(text, lo, lo, hi)

-- Whether the `_` at `k` is flanked by an ASCII digit on each side within
-- [lo, hi): the sole admissibility rule for a separator.
fn lx_sep_flanked(text : String, k : Int, lo : Int, hi : Int) : Bool =
  let left = k > lo && is_digit(byte_at(text, k - 1))
  let right = k + 1 < hi && is_digit(byte_at(text, k + 1))
  left && right

fn lx_bad_sep_go(text : String, k : Int, lo : Int, hi : Int) : Option(Int) =
  if k >= hi then
    None
  elif byte_at(text, k) == lx_b("_") then
    if lx_sep_flanked(text, k, lo, hi) then
      lx_bad_sep_go(text, k + 1, lo, hi)
    else
      Some(k)
  else
    lx_bad_sep_go(text, k + 1, lo, hi)

-- Classify a number: a float when a `.[0-9_]+` fraction or a bare exponent
-- follows the integer part, otherwise an integer. A separator out of place is a
-- hard error at its offset, validated over the whole run once the extent is
-- known.
fn lx_number(text : String, i : Int, n : Int) : LxStep =
  match lx_number_raw(text, i, n) of
    LxTok(k, end) =>
      match lx_bad_sep(text, i, end) of
        Some(off) => LxErr(LxNumberSep(off))
        None => LxTok(k, end)
    other => other

fn lx_number_raw(text : String, i : Int, n : Int) : LxStep =
  let j = lx_scan_digits(text, i, n)
  if lx_at(text, j) == lx_b(".") && lx_digit_us(lx_at(text, j + 1)) then
    let k = lx_scan_digits(text, j + 1, n)
    LxTok(TFloat, lx_scan_exp(text, k, n))
  else
    let e = lx_scan_exp(text, j, n)
    if e > j then
      LxTok(TFloat, e)
    else
      lx_int_suffix(text, j)

-- A char literal: `'` then one escaped or plain codepoint then `'`.
fn lx_char(text : String, i : Int, n : Int) : LxStep =
  let p = i + 1
  let c = lx_at(text, p)
  if c == lx_eof() then
    LxErr(LxInvalid(i))
  else
    let e =
      if c == lx_b("\\") then
        lx_skip_cp(text, p + 1, n)
      else
        lx_skip_cp(text, p, n)
    if lx_at(text, e) == lx_b("'") then
      LxTok(TChar, e + 1)
    else
      LxErr(LxInvalid(i))

-- Copy the raw bytes of [p, e) onto `buf`, byte for byte. Since token spans and
-- codepoint boundaries always agree, the copied run is well-formed UTF-8.
fn lx_push_bytes(text : String, p : Int, e : Int, buf : Buf) : Buf =
  if p >= e then
    buf
  else
    lx_push_bytes(text, p + 1, e, buf_push(buf, byte_at(text, p)))

-- Push the single UTF-8 codepoint at `p` onto `buf`, advancing past all its
-- bytes.
fn lx_push_cp(text : String, p : Int, buf : Buf) : Buf =
  lx_push_bytes(text, p, p + lx_cp_len(byte_at(text, p)), buf)

-- The byte-exact slice text[lo, hi) as a string. Byte-based rather than
-- codepoint-based so the offsets match the compiler's byte spans directly.
fn lx_slice(text : String, lo : Int, hi : Int) : String =
  string_of_buf(lx_push_bytes(text, lo, hi, buf_empty()))

-- A space or a tab: the two bytes a line's indentation is made of. A newline is
-- not one, since it is the separator the lines are counted from.
fn lx_hspace(c : Int) : Bool = c == 32 || c == 9

-- Whether the raw-string delimiter `"""` stands at `p`.
fn lx_quote3(text : String, p : Int, n : Int) : Bool =
  p + 3 <= n
    && byte_at(text, p) == lx_b("\"")
    && byte_at(text, p + 1) == lx_b("\"")
    && byte_at(text, p + 2) == lx_b("\"")

-- Whether a raw multiline string opens at `i`, with `r"""`.
fn lx_raw_opens(text : String, i : Int, n : Int) : Bool =
  i + 4 <= n && byte_at(text, i) == lx_b("r") && lx_quote3(text, i + 1, n)

-- The offset of the delimiter closing a raw literal, the first `"""` at or
-- after `p`. A raw body has no escape, so nothing inside it can be skipped.
fn lx_raw_end(text : String, p : Int, n : Int) : Option(Int) =
  if p + 3 > n then
    None
  elif lx_quote3(text, p, n) then
    Some(p)
  else
    lx_raw_end(text, p + 1, n)

-- The first offset in [p, e) holding neither a space nor a tab.
fn lx_skip_h(text : String, p : Int, e : Int) : Int =
  if p < e && lx_hspace(byte_at(text, p)) then
    lx_skip_h(text, p + 1, e)
  else
    p

-- The end of [p, e) with its trailing run of spaces and tabs dropped.
fn lx_trim_h(text : String, p : Int, e : Int) : Int =
  if e > p && lx_hspace(byte_at(text, e - 1)) then
    lx_trim_h(text, p, e - 1)
  else
    e

-- Where a raw body starts: past the newline the opening delimiter sits against,
-- which belongs to the delimiter rather than to the text. A run of spaces or
-- tabs may stand between the two; a body with no newline there starts at its
-- first byte and keeps it.
fn lx_raw_from(text : String, lo : Int, hi : Int) : Int =
  let p = lx_skip_h(text, lo, hi)
  if p < hi && byte_at(text, p) == 10 then
    p + 1
  else
    lo

-- Where a raw body ends, by the same rule read backwards.
fn lx_raw_upto(text : String, lo : Int, hi : Int) : Int =
  let e = lx_trim_h(text, lo, hi)
  if e > lo && byte_at(text, e - 1) == 10 then
    e - 1
  else
    hi

-- The end of the line starting at `p`, which is the next newline or `e`.
fn lx_line_end(text : String, p : Int, e : Int) : Int =
  if p < e && byte_at(text, p) /= 10 then
    lx_line_end(text, p + 1, e)
  else
    p

-- Whether [p, q) holds nothing but whitespace, so it contributes no margin of
-- its own and comes back from the dedent empty.
fn lx_blank(text : String, p : Int, q : Int) : Bool =
  if p >= q then
    true
  elif lx_ws(byte_at(text, p)) then
    lx_blank(text, p + 1, q)
  else
    false

-- How many leading bytes the indents at `a` and `b` share, so a body mixing
-- spaces and tabs is stripped only as far as the two agree rather than by a
-- count that would cut one line's tab off against another's space.
fn lx_common(text : String, a : Int, b : Int, k : Int, lim : Int) : Int =
  if k < lim && byte_at(text, a + k) == byte_at(text, b + k) then
    lx_common(text, a, b, k + 1, lim)
  else
    k

-- The indentation every nonblank line of [p, e) shares, carried as the offset
-- of one such indent and its length. A body with no nonblank line has none.
fn lx_margin(
  text : String,
  p : Int,
  e : Int,
  m : Option((Int, Int))
) : Option((Int, Int)) =
  let q = lx_line_end(text, p, e)
  let m2 =
    if lx_blank(text, p, q) then
      m
    else
      let ind = lx_skip_h(text, p, q) - p
      match m of
        None => Some((p, ind))
        Some(prev) =>
          let (mo, ml) = prev
          Some((mo, lx_common(text, mo, p, 0, if ml < ind then ml else ind)))
  if q >= e then
    m2
  else
    lx_margin(text, q + 1, e, m2)

-- The lines of [p, e) with `ml` bytes of shared indentation removed from each,
-- rejoined by the newlines that separated them.
fn lx_raw_lines(
  text : String,
  p : Int,
  e : Int,
  ml : Int,
  first : Bool,
  buf : Buf
) : Buf =
  let q = lx_line_end(text, p, e)
  let sep =
    if first then
      buf
    else
      buf_push(buf, 10)
  let out =
    if lx_blank(text, p, q) then
      sep
    else
      lx_push_bytes(text, p + ml, q, sep)
  if q >= e then
    out
  else
    lx_raw_lines(text, q + 1, e, ml, false, out)

-- The value of a raw literal whose body is [lo, hi): those bytes verbatim,
-- less the newline each delimiter sits against and the indentation the block
-- shares with the code around it. No escape is decoded and no brace opens a
-- hole, so what the author typed is what the string holds.
fn lx_raw_cook(text : String, lo : Int, hi : Int) : String =
  let from = lx_raw_from(text, lo, hi)
  let upto = lx_raw_upto(text, from, hi)
  let ml =
    match lx_margin(text, from, upto, None) of
      None => 0
      Some(m) =>
        let (_, k) = m
        k
  string_of_buf(lx_raw_lines(text, from, upto, ml, true, buf_empty()))

-- The decoded byte of a backslash escape, matching the compiler's fixed escape
-- set: `n t r " \ { }`. Numeric and unicode escapes are deliberately absent, so
-- the map stays one-to-one and the formatter round-trips. Any other escape is a
-- lexing error.
fn lx_esc_byte(e : Int) : Option(Int) =
  if e == lx_b("n") then
    Some(10)
  elif e == lx_b("t") then
    Some(9)
  elif e == lx_b("r") then
    Some(13)
  elif e == lx_b("\"") then
    Some(34)
  elif e == lx_b("\\") then
    Some(92)
  elif e == lx_b("\{") then
    Some(123)
  elif e == lx_b("\}") then
    Some(125)
  else
    None

-- The head of an `Int` stack, or 0 for the empty stack (the scanners keep the
-- stack non-empty for the whole scan, so this only degrades on malformed
-- re-entry).
fn lx_head0(xs : List(Int)) : Int =
  match xs of
    Nil => 0
    Cons(h, _) => h

-- The tail of an `Int` stack.
fn lx_tail(xs : List(Int)) : List(Int) =
  match xs of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(_, t) => t

-- Whether the stack is exactly the singleton [0]: the closing condition for a
-- hole scan (the hole's own brace depth returned to zero, no nested string
-- frames open).
fn lx_zero_one(xs : List(Int)) : Bool =
  match xs of
    Nil => false
    Cons(h, t) =>
      match t of
        Nil => h == 0
        Cons(_, _) => false

-- Find the end of a string literal opened at `oq`, returning the offset just
-- past the closing quote. A `{` opens a hole and a nested `"` inside it opens
-- another string frame, tracked with a stack of brace depths (one per string
-- nesting level), so an inner literal's quotes and braces never end the outer
-- token early. The outer quote closes only when the base frame is reached again.
fn lx_str_end(text : String, oq : Int, n : Int) : Result(Int, LexError) =
  lx_scan_str(text, oq + 1, n, Cons(0, Nil), Cons(oq, Nil), Nil, false)

-- Classify an unterminated string or hole exactly as the compiler's
-- `Scanner::unterminated`: an open brace depth points at the innermost `{` (an
-- unterminated hole), otherwise the innermost open `"` (an unterminated string),
-- each falling back to the other marker stack and finally offset 0 so a
-- malformed re-entry still yields a diagnostic rather than diverging.
fn lx_unterminated(
  depth : List(Int),
  quotes : List(Int),
  braces : List(Int)
) : LexError =
  if lx_head0(depth) > 0 then
    match braces of
      Cons(bo, _) => LxUntermHole(bo)
      Nil => LxUntermStr(lx_head0(quotes))
  else
    match quotes of
      Cons(qo, _) => LxUntermStr(qo)
      Nil => LxUntermHole(lx_head0(braces))

fn lx_scan_str(
  text : String,
  p : Int,
  n : Int,
  depth : List(Int),
  quotes : List(Int),
  braces : List(Int),
  esc : Bool
) : Result(Int, LexError) =
  if p >= n then
    Err(lx_unterminated(depth, quotes, braces))
  elif esc then
    lx_scan_str(
        text,
        p + lx_cp_len(byte_at(text, p)),
        n,
        depth,
        quotes,
        braces,
        false,
      )
  else
    let b = byte_at(text, p)
    let top = lx_head0(depth)
    if b == lx_b("\\") then
      lx_scan_str(text, p + 1, n, depth, quotes, braces, true)
    elif b == lx_b("\"") && top == 0 then
      let d2 = lx_tail(depth)
      let q2 = lx_tail(quotes)
      match d2 of
        Nil => Ok(p + 1)
        Cons(_, _) => lx_scan_str(text, p + 1, n, d2, q2, braces, false)
    elif b == lx_b("\"") then
      lx_scan_str(
          text,
          p + 1,
          n,
          Cons(0, depth),
          Cons(p, quotes),
          braces,
          false,
        )
    elif b == lx_b("\{") then
      lx_scan_str(
          text,
          p + 1,
          n,
          Cons(top + 1, lx_tail(depth)),
          quotes,
          Cons(p, braces),
          false,
        )
    elif b == lx_b("\}") && top > 0 then
      lx_scan_str(
          text,
          p + 1,
          n,
          Cons(top - 1, lx_tail(depth)),
          quotes,
          lx_tail(braces),
          false,
        )
    else
      lx_scan_str(text, p + lx_cp_len(b), n, depth, quotes, braces, false)

-- Find the `}` that closes a hole whose text starts at `from`, returning its
-- byte offset. Drives the same brace-depth stack as `lx_scan_str` but in hole
-- mode: the scan starts one brace deep and closes when that depth returns to
-- zero with no nested string frame open. None when the hole never closes.
fn lx_scan_hole(text : String, from : Int, n : Int) : Option(Int) =
  lx_hole_go(text, from, n, Cons(1, Nil), false)

fn lx_hole_go(
  text : String,
  p : Int,
  n : Int,
  depth : List(Int),
  esc : Bool
) : Option(Int) =
  if p >= n then
    None
  elif esc then
    lx_hole_go(text, p + lx_cp_len(byte_at(text, p)), n, depth, false)
  else
    let b = byte_at(text, p)
    let top = lx_head0(depth)
    if b == lx_b("\\") then
      lx_hole_go(text, p + 1, n, depth, true)
    elif b == lx_b("\"") && top == 0 then
      lx_hole_go(text, p + 1, n, lx_tail(depth), false)
    elif b == lx_b("\"") then
      lx_hole_go(text, p + 1, n, Cons(0, depth), false)
    elif b == lx_b("\{") then
      lx_hole_go(text, p + 1, n, Cons(top + 1, lx_tail(depth)), false)
    elif b == lx_b("\}") && top > 0 then
      let d2 = Cons(top - 1, lx_tail(depth))
      if lx_zero_one(d2) then
        Some(p)
      else
        lx_hole_go(text, p + 1, n, d2, false)
    else
      lx_hole_go(text, p + lx_cp_len(b), n, depth, false)

-- Whether text[lo, hi) has an unescaped `{`, marking an interpolated literal.
-- Escapes are skipped so a `\{` alone is a plain (cookable) string.
fn lx_has_hole(text : String, lo : Int, hi : Int) : Bool =
  if lo >= hi then
    false
  else
    let b = byte_at(text, lo)
    if b == lx_b("\\") then
      lx_has_hole(text, lo + 1 + lx_cp_len(lx_at(text, lo + 1)), hi)
    elif b == lx_b("\{") then
      true
    else
      lx_has_hole(text, lo + lx_cp_len(b), hi)

-- Cook a hole-free string body text[lo, hi): resolve every backslash escape and
-- copy the rest verbatim. A trailing lone backslash or an unknown escape is an
-- invalid token; the compiler's `cook` reports no inner offset, so the fault
-- lifts to the opening quote `oq`.
fn lx_cook(
  text : String,
  oq : Int,
  lo : Int,
  hi : Int
) : Result(String, LexError) =
  lx_cook_go(text, oq, lo, hi, buf_empty())

fn lx_cook_go(
  text : String,
  oq : Int,
  p : Int,
  hi : Int,
  buf : Buf
) : Result(String, LexError) =
  if p >= hi then
    Ok(string_of_buf(buf))
  else
    let b = byte_at(text, p)
    if b == lx_b("\\") then
      if p + 1 >= hi then
        Err(LxInvalid(oq))
      else
        match lx_esc_byte(byte_at(text, p + 1)) of
          Some(db) => lx_cook_go(text, oq, p + 2, hi, buf_push(buf, db))
          None => Err(LxInvalid(oq))
    else
      lx_cook_go(text, oq, p + lx_cp_len(b), hi, lx_push_cp(text, p, buf))

-- Whether text[lo, hi) is empty or entirely whitespace: an interpolation hole
-- with no expression is an error.
fn lx_blank_range(text : String, lo : Int, hi : Int) : Bool =
  if lo >= hi then
    true
  elif lx_ws(byte_at(text, lo)) then
    lx_blank_range(text, lo + 1, hi)
  else
    false

-- An operator or punctuation token by maximal munch over the bucket for the
-- byte it starts with, which is still longest first; a byte whose bucket holds
-- no match, including any byte that starts no operator at all, is a hard error.
fn lx_op(text : String, i : Int, ops : List(String)) : LxStep =
  match ops of
    Nil => LxErr(LxInvalid(i))
    Cons(s, rest) =>
      if lx_matches(text, i, s) then
        LxTok(TFixed(s), i + byte_len(s))
      else
        lx_op(text, i, rest)

-- Classify the token starting at `i` (guaranteed non-whitespace, i < n). The
-- leading byte both selects the branch and indexes that branch's table, so the
-- one `byte_at` here is the whole cost of narrowing the spellings to try.
fn lx_classify(text : String, i : Int, n : Int, tb : LxTabs) : LxStep =
  let c = byte_at(text, i)
  if c == lx_b("-") && lx_at(text, i + 1) == lx_b("-") then
    LxComment(lx_scan_comment(text, i, n))
  elif is_lower(c) || c == lx_b("_") then
    lx_lower(text, i, n, array_get(tb.lower, c))
  elif is_upper(c) then
    lx_upper(text, i, n, array_get(tb.upper, c))
  elif is_digit(c) then
    lx_number(text, i, n)
  elif c == lx_b("'") then
    lx_char(text, i, n)
  else
    lx_op(text, i, array_get(tb.ops, c))

-- Whether the gap [lo, hi) holds a blank line: two or more newlines. Bounded by
-- an early exit at the second newline.
fn lx_has_blank(text : String, lo : Int, hi : Int) : Bool =
  var i := lo
  var seen := 0
  while i < hi && seen < 2 do
    if byte_at(text, i) == 10 then
      seen += 1
    i += 1
  seen >= 2

-- Prepend a blank-line trivium spanning [cursor, lo) when that gap is blank.
fn lx_add_blank(
  trivs : List(Trivia),
  text : String,
  cursor : Int,
  lo : Int
) : List(Trivia) =
  if lx_has_blank(text, cursor, lo) then
    Cons(TBlank(Span { lo = cursor, hi = lo }), trivs)
  else
    trivs

-- Push the non-separator bytes of text[lo, hi) onto `buf`, dropping the `_`
-- digit separators so a numeric run parses. Suffix bytes (`i64`/`u64`) hold no
-- separators, so this leaves them intact.
fn lx_push_nonus(text : String, p : Int, hi : Int, buf : Buf) : Buf =
  if p >= hi then
    buf
  else
    let b = byte_at(text, p)
    if b == lx_b("_") then
      lx_push_nonus(text, p + 1, hi, buf)
    else
      lx_push_nonus(text, p + 1, hi, buf_push(buf, b))

-- The decoded value of an integer literal: its digits with separators removed,
-- keeping any `i64`/`u64` suffix, matching the compiler's `IntLit` rendering.
fn lx_int_value(text : String, lo : Int, hi : Int) : String =
  string_of_buf(lx_push_nonus(text, lo, hi, buf_empty()))

-- The decoded value of a float literal: separators stripped, then normalized
-- through the runtime's own parse and show so the byte spelling is canonical.
-- The differential gate compares floats numerically, not by spelling.
fn lx_float_value(text : String, lo : Int, hi : Int) : String =
  show_float(
      parse_float(string_of_buf(lx_push_nonus(text, lo, hi, buf_empty()))),
    )

-- The decoded value of a char literal text[lo, hi): the single inner codepoint,
-- or the resolved escape. A char admits one escape a string does not, `\'`.
fn lx_char_value(text : String, lo : Int, hi : Int) : String =
  let p = lo + 1
  let b = byte_at(text, p)
  if b == lx_b("\\") then
    let e = byte_at(text, p + 1)
    if e == lx_b("'") then
      string_of_buf(buf_push(buf_empty(), 39))
    else
      match lx_esc_byte(e) of
        Some(db) => string_of_buf(buf_push(buf_empty(), db))
        None => lx_slice(text, p, p + lx_cp_len(b))
  else
    lx_slice(text, p, p + lx_cp_len(b))

-- The decoded value a token of kind `k` carries over span [lo, hi), or None for
-- a value-free kind (fixed tokens and layout virtuals). Strings are decoded on
-- the string path in `lx_loop`, not here.
fn lx_value(text : String, k : TokenKind, lo : Int, hi : Int) : Option(String) =
  match k of
    TIdent => Some(lx_slice(text, lo, hi))
    TUid => Some(lx_slice(text, lo, hi))
    TQual => Some(lx_slice(text, lo, hi))
    TInt => Some(lx_int_value(text, lo, hi))
    TFloat => Some(lx_float_value(text, lo, hi))
    TChar => Some(lx_char_value(text, lo, hi))
    _ => None

-- Reverse `xs` onto `acc`: append the reversed list, used to splice a
-- forward-order token run onto the reversed accumulator.
fn lx_rev_append(xs : List(Token), acc : List(Token)) : List(Token) =
  match xs of
    Nil => acc
    Cons(x, rest) => lx_rev_append(rest, Cons(x, acc))

-- Re-lex the hole expression text[lo, hi) at its absolute source offsets. The
-- range is bounded at `hi`, so lookahead never reads past the closing brace; a
-- nested interpolated string inside recurses through the same driver.
fn lx_hole_tokens(
  text : String,
  lo : Int,
  hi : Int
) : Result(List(Token), LexError) =
  match lx_loop(text, hi, lo, lo, Nil, Nil, lx_tabs()) of
    Err(e) => Err(e)
    Ok(r) => Ok(r.tokens)

-- Split an interpolated literal opened at `oq` and closed just before `endq`
-- into segment and hole tokens: `istart`/`imid`/`iend` carry the recooked
-- literal segments and each hole's expression is re-lexed between them. Segment
-- spans run delimiter to delimiter (quote or brace); hole spans point at real
-- source. Mirrors the compiler's `split_interp`.
fn lx_interp(
  text : String,
  oq : Int,
  endq : Int
) : Result(List(Token), LexError) =
  lx_interp_go(text, oq + 1, endq - 1, endq, buf_empty(), oq, true, Nil)

fn lx_interp_go(
  text : String,
  p : Int,
  hi : Int,
  endq : Int,
  seg : Buf,
  seg_from : Int,
  first : Bool,
  acc : List(Token)
) : Result(List(Token), LexError) =
  if p >= hi then
    let iend =
      Token {
        kind = TIEnd,
        span = Span { lo = seg_from, hi = endq },
        value = Some(string_of_buf(seg))
      }
    Ok(reverse(Cons(iend, acc)))
  else
    let b = byte_at(text, p)
    if b == lx_b("\\") then
      if p + 1 >= hi then
        Err(LxInvalid(p))
      else
        match lx_esc_byte(byte_at(text, p + 1)) of
          Some(db) =>
            lx_interp_go(
                text,
                p + 2,
                hi,
                endq,
                buf_push(seg, db),
                seg_from,
                first,
                acc,
              )
          None => Err(LxInvalid(p + 1))
    elif b == lx_b("\{") then
      match lx_scan_hole(text, p + 1, hi) of
        None => Err(LxUntermHole(p))
        Some(close) =>
          if lx_blank_range(text, p + 1, close) then
            Err(LxEmptyHole(p))
          else
            let sk =
              if first then
                TIStart
              else
                TIMid
            let segtok =
              Token {
                kind = sk,
                span = Span { lo = seg_from, hi = p + 1 },
                value = Some(string_of_buf(seg))
              }
            match lx_hole_tokens(text, p + 1, close) of
              Err(e) => Err(e)
              Ok(htoks) =>
                let acc2 = lx_rev_append(htoks, Cons(segtok, acc))
                lx_interp_go(
                    text,
                    close + 1,
                    hi,
                    endq,
                    buf_empty(),
                    close,
                    false,
                    acc2,
                  )
    else
      lx_interp_go(
          text,
          p + lx_cp_len(b),
          hi,
          endq,
          lx_push_cp(text, p, seg),
          seg_from,
          first,
          acc,
        )

-- | Tokenize `text` into the raw token stream and its interleaved trivia,
-- reproducing the compiler's `lex_raw` layer: kinds, byte spans, decoded values,
-- interpolation splitting, comments, and blank-line runs. No layout virtuals.
pub fn lex_raw(text : String) : Result(LexRaw, LexError) =
  lx_loop(text, byte_len(text), 0, 0, Nil, Nil, lx_tabs())

-- | Whether `text` fails to lex only because a string literal or interpolation
-- hole runs off the end: the lexer-observable half of the compiler's
-- `incomplete` classification, telling an interactive reader to keep reading
-- rather than to reject. Any other lexing failure, or a clean lex, is complete.
pub fn lex_incomplete(text : String) : Bool =
  match lex_raw(text) of
    Err(LxUntermStr(_)) => true
    Err(LxUntermHole(_)) => true
    Err(_) => false
    Ok(_) => false

-- The driver, threading the scan offset `i`, the trivia cursor (the previous
-- token or comment's end), and the reversed token and trivia accumulators. A
-- string is handled here rather than in `lx_classify`: its extent is found with
-- the brace-aware scanner and, when interpolated, it expands to several tokens.
fn lx_loop(
  text : String,
  n : Int,
  i : Int,
  cursor : Int,
  toks : List(Token),
  trivs : List(Trivia),
  tb : LxTabs
) : Result(LexRaw, LexError) =
  if i >= n then
    Ok(LexRaw { tokens = reverse(toks), trivia = reverse(trivs) })
  else
    let c = byte_at(text, i)
    if lx_ws(c) then
      lx_loop(text, n, lx_skip_ws(text, i, n), cursor, toks, trivs, tb)
    elif lx_raw_opens(text, i, n) then
      match lx_raw_end(text, i + 4, n) of
        None => Err(LxUntermStr(i))
        Some(q) =>
          let endq = q + 3
          let tok =
            Token {
              kind = TStr,
              span = Span { lo = i, hi = endq },
              value = Some(lx_raw_cook(text, i + 4, q))
            }
          lx_loop(
              text,
              n,
              endq,
              endq,
              Cons(tok, toks),
              lx_add_blank(trivs, text, cursor, i),
              tb,
            )
    elif c == lx_b("\"") then
      match lx_str_end(text, i, n) of
        Err(e) => Err(e)
        Ok(endq) =>
          let trivs2 = lx_add_blank(trivs, text, cursor, i)
          if lx_has_hole(text, i + 1, endq - 1) then
            match lx_interp(text, i, endq) of
              Err(e) => Err(e)
              Ok(itoks) =>
                lx_loop(
                    text,
                    n,
                    endq,
                    endq,
                    lx_rev_append(itoks, toks),
                    trivs2,
                    tb,
                  )
          else
            match lx_cook(text, i, i + 1, endq - 1) of
              Err(e) => Err(e)
              Ok(v) =>
                let tok =
                  Token {
                    kind = TStr,
                    span = Span { lo = i, hi = endq },
                    value = Some(v)
                  }
                lx_loop(text, n, endq, endq, Cons(tok, toks), trivs2, tb)
    else
      match lx_classify(text, i, n, tb) of
        LxErr(e) => Err(e)
        LxComment(j) =>
          let trivs2 = Cons(
              TComment(Span { lo = i, hi = j }),
              lx_add_blank(trivs, text, cursor, i),
            )
          lx_loop(text, n, j, j, toks, trivs2, tb)
        LxTok(k, j) =>
          let tok =
            Token {
              kind = k,
              span = Span { lo = i, hi = j },
              value = lx_value(text, k, i, j)
            }
          let trivs2 = lx_add_blank(trivs, text, cursor, i)
          lx_loop(text, n, j, j, Cons(tok, toks), trivs2, tb)

-- | The public Prism-owned parser.
--
-- The compiler remains the bootstrap oracle, but this module is a complete
-- value-passing entry seam: source text is lexed and laid out by the Prism
-- frontend, then declarations and expressions consume that exact post-layout
-- token stream without calling back into Rust.

import Syntax.Source (..)

import Syntax.Token (..)

import Syntax.Lex (..)

import Syntax.Layout (..)

import Syntax.Ast (..)

import Syntax.Diagnostic (..)

import Syntax.Cursor (..)

import Syntax.Parse.Support (..)

import Syntax.Parse.Expr (..)

import Syntax.Parse.Decl (..)

-- | A source-level parse failure, preserving whether lexing or parsing refused
-- the input.
pub type ParseFailure = ParseLex(LexError) | ParseSyntax(Diagnostic)

-- | Parse an already-laid-out whole-program token stream.
pub fn parse_program_tokens(
  tokens : List(Token),
  stop : Int
) : Result(List(Item), Diagnostic) =
  match parse_program(cursor_of(tokens, stop), depth_budget()) of
    PTook(items, _) => Ok(items)
    PStuck(c) => Err(cursor_diagnostic(c))
    PFault(d) => Err(d)

-- | Lex, lay out, and parse one complete Prism source file.
pub fn parse_source(text : String) : Result(List(Item), ParseFailure) =
  parse_source_budgeted(depth_budget(), text)

-- | `parse_source` under an explicit recursion budget. The default budget is
-- deep enough that no realistic program meets it; a harness probing the depth
-- contract (acceptance below the budget, the structured refusal beyond it)
-- passes a small budget here instead of paying for thousands of nesting
-- levels. The refusal machinery exercised is identical at every budget.
pub fn parse_source_budgeted(
  budget : Int,
  text : String
) : Result(List(Item), ParseFailure) =
  match layout(text) of
    Err(e) => Err(ParseLex(e))
    Ok(tokens) =>
      match parse_program(cursor_of(tokens, str_len(text)), budget) of
        PTook(items, _c) => Ok(items)
        PStuck(c) => Err(ParseSyntax(cursor_diagnostic(c)))
        PFault(d) => Err(ParseSyntax(d))

-- | Parse one expression from a token cursor and require complete consumption.
pub fn parse_expr_tokens(
  tokens : List(Token),
  stop : Int
) : Result(Sp(Expr), Diagnostic) =
  let c0 = cursor_of(tokens, stop)
  match parse_expr(c0, depth_budget()) of
    PStuck(c) => Err(cursor_diagnostic(c))
    PFault(d) => Err(d)
    PTook(expr, c1) =>
      match cursor_expect_end(c1) of
        Took(_, _) => Ok(expr)
        Stuck(c2) => Err(cursor_diagnostic(c2))

-- | Lex, lay out, and parse a standalone expression. Layout wraps a complete
-- input in its top-level virtual block, so the expression entry removes that
-- envelope before requiring the stream end.
pub fn parse_expr_source(text : String) : Result(Sp(Expr), ParseFailure) =
  match layout(text) of
    Err(e) => Err(ParseLex(e))
    Ok(tokens) =>
      let c0 = cursor_of(tokens, str_len(text))
      match take_kind(c0, TVOpen) of
        PStuck(c1) => Err(ParseSyntax(cursor_diagnostic(c1)))
        PFault(d) => Err(ParseSyntax(d))
        PTook(_, c1) =>
          match parse_expr(c1, depth_budget()) of
            PStuck(c2) => Err(ParseSyntax(cursor_diagnostic(c2)))
            PFault(d) => Err(ParseSyntax(d))
            PTook(expr, c2) =>
              match take_kind(c2, TVClose) of
                PStuck(c3) => Err(ParseSyntax(cursor_diagnostic(c3)))
                PFault(d) => Err(ParseSyntax(d))
                PTook(_, c3) =>
                  match cursor_expect_end(c3) of
                    Took(_, _) => Ok(expr)
                    Stuck(c4) => Err(ParseSyntax(cursor_diagnostic(c4)))

Canonical AST construction for a parser: every spanned node a production creates goes through a named builder here, so the meaning of a span or a synthesis bit is encoded once instead of being re-decided at hundreds of record literals.

The span discipline these builders enforce, the one the compiler's own exporter observes: a node's span runs from its first token's start to its last consumed token's end; a delimiter widens the span of the node it wraps; a node the parser invents (the list a multi-index desugars to, the pieces of an interpolated string) is synthesized, and a piece that corresponds to no source text of its own is zero-width at the position it conceptually occupies.
modules.source:
-- | Canonical AST construction for a parser: every spanned node a production
-- creates goes through a named builder here, so the meaning of a span or a
-- synthesis bit is encoded once instead of being re-decided at hundreds of
-- record literals.
--
-- The span discipline these builders enforce, the one the compiler's own
-- exporter observes: a node's span runs from its first token's start to its
-- last consumed token's end; a delimiter widens the span of the node it
-- wraps; a node the parser invents (the list a multi-index desugars to, the
-- pieces of an interpolated string) is synthesized, and a piece that
-- corresponds to no source text of its own is zero-width at the position it
-- conceptually occupies.

import Syntax.Source (..)

import Syntax.Ast (..)

-- | An authored node covering `[lo, hi)`: written by the user, spanned by its
-- own tokens.
pub fn authored(node : a, lo : Int, hi : Int) : Sp(a) =
  Sp {
    node = node,
    span = Span { lo = lo, hi = hi },
    synth = false
  }

-- | A synthesized node covering `[lo, hi)`: invented by the parser while
-- desugaring an authored form, spanning the source it stands for.
pub fn synthesized(node : a, lo : Int, hi : Int) : Sp(a) =
  Sp {
    node = node,
    span = Span { lo = lo, hi = hi },
    synth = true
  }

-- | A zero-width node at `at`: a piece that corresponds to no source text of
-- its own, carrying the position it conceptually occupies.
pub fn zero_width(node : a, at : Int) : Sp(a) =
  Sp {
    node = node,
    span = Span { lo = at, hi = at },
    synth = false
  }

-- | Rewrap a node with a delimiter's extent: parentheses and brackets widen
-- the span of the node they enclose while the node itself is unchanged.
pub fn widened(x : Sp(a), lo : Int, hi : Int) : Sp(a) =
  Sp {
    node = x.node,
    span = Span { lo = lo, hi = hi },
    synth = x.synth
  }

-- | The span an infix application covers: from its left operand's start to
-- its right operand's end.
pub fn operands_span(l : Sp(a), r : Sp(b)) : Span =
  Span { lo = l.span.lo, hi = r.span.hi }
