) : Parsed(GeneratedChild(Ty)) =
  if at_fixed(c, "!") then
    let braced = at_fixed(cursor_advance(c), "\{")
    generated_bind(generated_parse_effect_row(c, depth)) fn(row, c1)
      if at_fixed(c1, "@") then
        generated_bind(generated_parse_usage_parts(cursor_advance(c1))) fn(_parts, c2)
          PFault(
              refuse(
                  cursor_since(saved, c2),
                  "parenthesize the function type before `@`: write `((a) -> b ! \{E\}) @ fact`",
                ),
            )
      else
        match done of
          TypeDone(t, _) =>
            match t of
              TyFun(ps, _, cod) =>
                PTook(
                    TypeDone(
                        TyFun(ps, row, cod),
                        if braced then TRClosedEffect else TRBareEffect,
                      ),
                    c1,
                  )
              _ =>
                PFault(
                    refuse(
                        cursor_since(saved, c1),
                        "effect row `! \{..\}` only applies to a function type",
                      ),
                  )
  else
    PTook(done, c)

-- -------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Effect rows and the optional-argument completion state of labels
-- -------------------------------------------------------------------------

pub type GeneratedRowReceipt = GRClosedItem | GROptionalArgs

pub type GeneratedRowItem(a) = GeneratedRowItem(a, GeneratedRowReceipt)

type GeneratedDelimited(a) = GDClosed(List(a)) | GDOpen(List(a), String)

type GeneratedUsageParts = GeneratedUsageParts {
  facts: List(String),
  open_tail: Bool
}

pub fn generated_parse_effect_row(c : Cursor, depth : Int) : Parsed(Row) =
  generated_bind(take_fixed(c, "!")) fn(_bang, c1)
    if at_fixed(c1, "\{") then
      generated_parse_eff_labels_body(cursor_advance(c1), depth)
    else
      PTook(generated_empty_row(), c1)

pub fn generated_parse_eff_label(c : Cursor, depth : Int) : Parsed(EffLabel) =
  match generated_parse_eff_label_done(c, depth) of
    PStuck(c1) => PStuck(c1)
    PFault(d) => PFault(d)
    PTook(done, c1) =>
      match done of
        GeneratedRowItem(label, _) => PTook(label, c1)

fn generated_parse_eff_label_done(
  c : Cursor,
  depth : Int
) : Parsed(GeneratedRowItem(EffLabel)) =
  match cursor_peek(c) of
    Some(t) =>
      match t.kind of
        TIdent =>
          PTook(
              GeneratedRowItem(
                  EffLabel { name = token_text(t), args = Nil },
                  GRClosedItem,
                ),
              cursor_advance(c),
            )
        TUid => generated_parse_named_eff_label(t, c, depth)
        TQual => generated_parse_named_eff_label(t, c, depth)
        _ => generated_eff_label_miss(c)
    None => generated_eff_label_miss(c)

fn generated_parse_named_eff_label(
  t : Token,
  c : Cursor,
  depth : Int
) : Parsed(GeneratedRowItem(EffLabel)) =
  let c1 = cursor_advance(c)
  if at_fixed(c1, "(") then
    generated_bind(generated_parse_ctor_args(c1, depth, generated_parse_type_arg)) fn(args, c2)
      PTook(
          GeneratedRowItem(
              EffLabel { name = token_text(t), args = args },
              GRClosedItem,
            ),
          c2,
        )
  else
    PTook(
        GeneratedRowItem(
            EffLabel { name = token_text(t), args = Nil },
            GROptionalArgs,
          ),
        c1,
      )

fn generated_eff_label_miss(c : Cursor) : Parsed(GeneratedRowItem(EffLabel)) =
  PStuck(cursor_note(cursor_note(cursor_note(c, TIdent), TUid), TQual))

fn generated_parse_eff_labels_body(c : Cursor, depth : Int) : Parsed(Row) =
  match (generated_parse_delimited(c, depth, generated_parse_eff_label_done)) of
    PStuck(c1) => PStuck(c1)
    PFault(d) => PFault(d)
    PTook(items, c1) =>
      match items of
        GDClosed(labels) => PTook(Row { labels = labels, tail = None }, c1)
        GDOpen(labels, tail) =>
          PTook(Row { labels = labels, tail = Some(tail) }, c1)

fn generated_parse_delimited(
  c : Cursor,
  depth : Int,
  parse_item : (Cursor, Int) -> Parsed(GeneratedRowItem(a))
) : Parsed(GeneratedDelimited(a)) =
  if at_fixed(c, "\}") then
    PTook(GDClosed(Nil), cursor_advance(c))
  elif at_fixed(c, "|") then
    generated_parse_delimited_tail(cursor_advance(c), Nil)
  else
    match parse_item(c, depth) of
      PStuck(c1) => PStuck(generated_note_row_entry(c, c1))
      PFault(d) => PFault(d)
      PTook(item, c1) =>
        match item of
          GeneratedRowItem(value, receipt) =>
            generated_parse_delimited_more(
                c1,
                depth,
                parse_item,
                [value],
                receipt,
              )

fn generated_parse_delimited_more(
  c : Cursor,
  depth : Int,
  parse_item : (Cursor, Int) -> Parsed(GeneratedRowItem(a)),
  rev : List(a),
  receipt : GeneratedRowReceipt
) : Parsed(GeneratedDelimited(a)) =
  if at_fixed(c, "\}") then
    PTook(GDClosed(reverse(rev)), cursor_advance(c))
  elif at_fixed(c, "|") then
    generated_parse_delimited_tail(cursor_advance(c), rev)
  elif at_fixed(c, ",") then
    let c1 = cursor_advance(c)
    if at_fixed(c1, "\}") then
      PTook(GDClosed(reverse(rev)), cursor_advance(c1))
    elif at_fixed(c1, "|") then
      generated_parse_delimited_tail(cursor_advance(c1), rev)
    else
      match parse_item(c1, depth) of
        PStuck(c2) => PStuck(generated_note_row_entry(c1, c2))
        PFault(d) => PFault(d)
        PTook(item, c2) =>
          match item of
            GeneratedRowItem(value, next_receipt) =>
              generated_parse_delimited_more(
                  c2,
                  depth,
                  parse_item,
                  Cons(value, rev),
                  next_receipt,
                )
  else
    PStuck(generated_note_row_follow(c, receipt))

fn generated_note_row_entry(saved : Cursor, failed : Cursor) : Cursor =
  if failed.pos == saved.pos then
    cursor_note(cursor_note(failed, TFixed("|")), TFixed("\}"))
  else
    failed

fn generated_note_row_follow(
  c : Cursor,
  receipt : GeneratedRowReceipt
) : Cursor =
  let c1 = cursor_note(
      cursor_note(cursor_note(c, TFixed(",")), TFixed("|")),
      TFixed("\}"),
    )
  match receipt of
    GROptionalArgs => cursor_note(c1, TFixed("("))
    _ => c1

fn generated_parse_delimited_tail(
  c : Cursor,
  rev : List(a)
) : Parsed(GeneratedDelimited(a)) =
  generated_bind(take_word(c, TIdent)) fn(tail, c1)
    generated_bind(take_fixed(c1, "\}")) fn(_close, c2)
      PTook(GDOpen(reverse(rev), tail), c2)

-- -------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Usage rows
-- -------------------------------------------------------------------------

fn generated_parse_usage_parts(c : Cursor) : Parsed(GeneratedUsageParts) =
  if at_fixed(c, "\{") then
    generated_parse_usage_braces(cursor_advance(c))
  else
    match take_word(c, TIdent) of
      PStuck(c1) => PStuck(generated_note_same(c, c1, TFixed("\{")))
      PFault(d) => PFault(d)
      PTook(fact, c1) =>
        PTook(GeneratedUsageParts { facts = [fact], open_tail = false }, c1)

fn generated_parse_usage_braces(c : Cursor) : Parsed(GeneratedUsageParts) =
  match generated_parse_delimited(c, 0, generated_parse_usage_item) of
    PStuck(c1) => PStuck(c1)
    PFault(d) => PFault(d)
    PTook(items, c1) =>
      match items of
        GDClosed(facts) =>
          PTook(GeneratedUsageParts { facts = facts, open_tail = false }, c1)
        GDOpen(facts, _) =>
          PTook(GeneratedUsageParts { facts = facts, open_tail = true }, c1)

fn generated_parse_usage_item(
  c : Cursor,
  _depth : Int
) : Parsed(GeneratedRowItem(String)) =
  match take_word(c, TIdent) of
    PStuck(c1) => PStuck(c1)
    PFault(d) => PFault(d)
    PTook(fact, c1) => PTook(GeneratedRowItem(fact, GRClosedItem), c1)

The support layer of a production parser: the three-way parse outcome, the recursion budget, and the token classification every grammar family shares.

`Syntax.Cursor` owns the mechanics (peek, advance, expect, expectation merging); this module owns parser policy. The cursor's `Reply` expresses an unmet expectation and nothing else, which is right for a token fault and wrong for the two other refusals a real parser needs: a deliberate diagnostic whose message names a rewrite rather than a token menu, and a depth refusal when nesting exhausts the recursion budget. `Parsed` carries all three, and a deliberate refusal travels as a `Diagnostic` value, never as a sentinel expectation name.
modules.source:
-- | The support layer of a production parser: the three-way parse outcome,
-- the recursion budget, and the token classification every grammar family
-- shares.
--
-- `Syntax.Cursor` owns the mechanics (peek, advance, expect, expectation
-- merging); this module owns parser policy. The cursor's `Reply` expresses an
-- unmet expectation and nothing else, which is right for a token fault and
-- wrong for the two other refusals a real parser needs: a deliberate
-- diagnostic whose message names a rewrite rather than a token menu, and a
-- depth refusal when nesting exhausts the recursion budget. `Parsed` carries
-- all three, and a deliberate refusal travels as a `Diagnostic` value, never
-- as a sentinel expectation name.

import Syntax.Source (..)

import Syntax.Token (..)

import Syntax.Diagnostic (..)

import Syntax.Cursor (..)

import Data.String (contains, index_of)

-- | One parse step: the value and the cursor after it, an unmet expectation
-- held in the cursor's failure record, or a finished diagnostic that no
-- expectation set can express.
pub type Parsed(a) = PTook(a, Cursor) | PStuck(Cursor) | PFault(Diagnostic)

-- | Lift a cursor reply into a parse outcome.
pub fn from_reply(r : Reply(a)) : Parsed(a) =
  match r of
    Took(x, c) => PTook(x, c)
    Stuck(c) => PStuck(c)

-- | Finish a parse outcome as the diagnostic it refuses with: the cursor's
-- own merged-expectation diagnostic for a stuck parse, the carried diagnostic
-- for a fault, and None for a success.
pub fn parsed_fault(p : Parsed(a)) : Option(Diagnostic) =
  match p of
    PTook(_, _) => None
    PStuck(c) => Some(cursor_diagnostic(c))
    PFault(d) => Some(d)

-- -------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Deliberate refusals and the recursion budget
-- -------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- | A deliberate parse refusal: the general parse code, the given span, the
-- given message, and no generic expectation set, because the message names
-- the exact rewrite or bound rather than a token menu. Migration diagnostics
-- are built with this.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Syntax.Cursor (..)
-- refuse(span_at(3), "the retired form").code
-- ```
-- ```output
-- E7100
-- ```
pub fn refuse(s : Span, msg : String) : Diagnostic =
  Diagnostic {
    code = parse_syntax_code(),
    phase = DPParse,
    span = s,
    message = msg,
    expected = Nil,
    related = Nil
  }

-- | The recursion budget a whole-file parse starts with. Deep enough that no
-- authored program meets it, small enough that a generated hostile input is
-- refused with a diagnostic instead of exhausting the stack; the supported
-- bound is pinned by test, one point below and one beyond.
pub fn depth_budget() : Int = 2048

-- | Spend one level of the budget, or refuse structurally: a nesting depth
-- past the budget is a diagnostic at the current token, never an abort.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Syntax.Cursor (..)
-- match descend(1, cursor_of(Nil, 0)) of
--   PTook(d, _) => d
--   _ => -1
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 0
-- ```
pub fn descend(depth : Int, c : Cursor) : Parsed(Int) =
  if depth > 0 then
    PTook(depth - 1, c)
  else
    PFault(
        Diagnostic {
          code = "E7102",
          phase = DPParse,
          span = cursor_span(c),
          message = "nesting exceeds the parser's depth budget",
          expected = Nil,
          related = Nil
        },
      )

-- -------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Token classification
-- -------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- | The decoded text a token carries, empty for a fixed token.
pub fn token_text(t : Token) : String =
  match t.value of
    None => ""
    Some(v) => v

-- | The decoded text at the read position without consuming it, empty at the
-- end or on a fixed token: the one lookahead a contextual keyword needs.
pub fn peek_word(c : Cursor) : String =
  match cursor_peek(c) of
    None => ""
    Some(t) => token_text(t)

-- | Match Rust's stable `f64` debug spelling used by syntax artifacts. The
-- Prism lexer has already round-tripped the value through `show_float`, which
-- omits the `.0` on integral finite values.
pub fn surface_float(s : String) : String =
  let ep = index_of("e+", s)
  let cap_ep = index_of("E+", s)
  if ep >= 0 then
    concat(substring(s, 0, ep + 1), substring(s, ep + 2, byte_len(s) - ep - 2))
  elif cap_ep >= 0 then
    concat(
        substring(s, 0, cap_ep + 1),
        substring(s, cap_ep + 2, byte_len(s) - cap_ep - 2),
      )
  elif contains(".", s) || contains("e", s) || contains("E", s) then
    s
  else
    concat(s, ".0")

-- | Canonical decimal spelling of an already-validated integer token.
pub fn surface_int(s : String) : String =
  match parse_int(s) of
    Some(n) => show_int(n)
    None => s

-- | Whether the token at the read position is the fixed spelling `s`.
pub fn at_fixed(c : Cursor, s : String) : Bool =
  match cursor_peek(c) of
    None => false
    Some(t) => t.kind == TFixed(s)

-- | Whether the token at the read position is of kind `k`.
pub fn at_kind(c : Cursor, k : TokenKind) : Bool =
  match cursor_kind(c) of
    None => false
    Some(kk) => kk == k

-- | Require the fixed spelling `s`, as a parse outcome.
pub fn take_fixed(c : Cursor, s : String) : Parsed(Token) =
  from_reply(cursor_expect_fixed(c, s))

-- | Require a token of kind `k`, as a parse outcome.
pub fn take_kind(c : Cursor, k : TokenKind) : Parsed(Token) =
  from_reply(cursor_expect(c, k))

-- | Require a token of kind `k` and return its decoded text.
pub fn take_word(c : Cursor, k : TokenKind) : Parsed(String) =
  match take_kind(c, k) of
    PTook(t, c2) => PTook(token_text(t), c2)
    PStuck(c2) => PStuck(c2)
    PFault(d) => PFault(d)

-- | Consume the fixed spelling `s` if it is there, reporting whether it was:
-- the optional-token step every trailing separator and modifier needs.
pub fn skip_fixed(c : Cursor, s : String) : (Bool, Cursor) =
  if at_fixed(c, s) then
    (true, cursor_advance(c))
  else
    (false, c)

-- | Stable public facade for the generated surface-type parser.
--
-- Structural ownership lives in Syntax.Parse.GeneratedType. The generated
-- parser preserves its exact LR completion receipt internally; this facade
-- erases that private state only at the established Parsed(Ty) boundary.

import Syntax.Ast (..)

import Syntax.Cursor (..)

import Syntax.Parse.Support (..)

import Syntax.Parse.GeneratedType (..)

-- | Parse one complete surface type.
pub fn parse_type(c : Cursor, depth : Int) : Parsed(Ty) =
  strip_type_done(generated_parse_type(c, depth))

-- | Parse through the arrow layer while leaving a trailing effect suffix for
-- declaration return-annotation disambiguation.
pub fn parse_type_head(c : Cursor, depth : Int) : Parsed(Ty) =
  strip_type_done(generated_parse_type_head(c, depth))

-- | Parse a type-constructor argument, including row and natural arguments.
pub fn parse_type_arg(c : Cursor, depth : Int) : Parsed(Ty) =
  strip_type_done(generated_parse_type_arg(c, depth))

-- | Parse an effect suffix including its leading `!`.
pub fn parse_effect_row(c : Cursor, depth : Int) : Parsed(Row) =
  generated_parse_effect_row(c, depth)

-- | Parse one effect label with optional constructor arguments.
pub fn parse_eff_label(c : Cursor, depth : Int) : Parsed(EffLabel) =
  generated_parse_eff_label(c, depth)

fn strip_type_done(p : Parsed(GeneratedChild(Ty))) : Parsed(Ty) =
  match p of
    PStuck(c) => PStuck(c)
    PFault(d) => PFault(d)
    PTook(done, c) =>
      match done of
        TypeDone(t, receipt) =>
          PTook(t, generated_type_note_if_live(c, receipt))

modules.source:
-- | Semantic checks behind the generated structural type parser.
--
-- This module deliberately knows nothing about Type grammar control flow.
-- GeneratedType calls the one public hook only after consuming a complete
-- usage row, keeping diagnostics typed without threading parser callbacks
-- through recursive productions.

import Data.List (..)

import Syntax.Ast (..)

import Syntax.Cursor (..)

import Syntax.Parse.Support (..)

pub fn validate_usage(
  saved : Cursor,
  base : Ty,
  facts : List(String),
  open_tail : Bool,
  c : Cursor
) : Parsed(Ty) =
  let span = cursor_since(saved, c)
  if open_tail then
    PFault(
        refuse(
            span,
            "usage-row polymorphism (`@ \{fact | tail\}`) is reserved but not implemented",
          ),
      )
  else
    match validate_usage_facts(facts, Nil) of
      Ok(validated) => PTook(TyUsage(base, validated), c)
      Err(msg) => PFault(refuse(span, msg))

fn validate_usage_facts(
  facts : List(String),
  accepted : List(String)
) : Result(List(String), String) =
  match facts of
    Nil =>
      if is_nil(accepted) then
        Err("a usage row cannot be empty")
      else
        Ok(accepted)
    Cons(fact, rest) =>
      if not(known_usage_fact(fact)) then
        Err("unknown usage fact `{fact}`")
      elif has_usage_fact(fact, accepted) then
        Err("duplicate usage fact `{fact}`")
      else
        match conflicting_usage_fact(fact, accepted) of
          Some(prior) =>
            Err(
                "usage facts `{prior}` and `{fact}` contradict each other (same axis)",
              )
          None => validate_usage_facts(rest, insert_usage_fact(fact, accepted))

fn known_usage_fact(fact : String) : Bool =
  fact == "aliased"
    || fact == "bounded_stack"
    || fact == "linear"
    || fact == "local"
    || fact == "many"
    || fact == "noalloc"
    || fact == "noescape"
    || fact == "once"
    || fact == "portable"
    || fact == "unique"

fn usage_axis(fact : String) : String =
  if fact == "portable" then
    "mobility"
  elif fact == "local" || fact == "noescape" then
    "escape"
  elif fact == "once" || fact == "many" then
    "multiplicity"
  elif fact == "unique" || fact == "aliased" then
    "aliasing"
  elif fact == "noalloc" then
    "allocation"
  else
    "fip"

fn usage_axis_exclusive(fact : String) : Bool =
  fact /= "linear" && fact /= "bounded_stack"

fn conflicting_usage_fact(
  fact : String,
  accepted : List(String)
) : Option(String) =
  match accepted of
    Nil => None
    Cons(prior, rest) =>
      if (usage_axis_exclusive(fact) && usage_axis(prior) == usage_axis(fact)) then
        Some(prior)
      else
        conflicting_usage_fact(fact, rest)

fn has_usage_fact(fact : String, facts : List(String)) : Bool =
  match facts of
    Nil => false
    Cons(x, rest) =>
      if x == fact then
        true
      else
        has_usage_fact(fact, rest)

fn insert_usage_fact(fact : String, facts : List(String)) : List(String) =
  match facts of
    Nil => [fact]
    Cons(x, rest) =>
      if fact < x then
        Cons(fact, facts)
      else
        Cons(x, insert_usage_fact(fact, rest))

modules.doc:
A source query over a decoded `prism-syntax-tokens-v1` artifact.

This is a *consumer* of the public token representation, not part of the compiler. Given a `TokensDoc` (the exact source text plus the compiler's own raw stream, layout-resolved parse stream, and trivia), it reports a stable, machine-readable inventory of the source: the content digest, the ordered imports, the comment spans, the ordered top-level declaration heads, and a token-kind histogram in first-seen order.

Every field is a pure function of the artifact bytes. Nothing here reads ambient workspace state: the same artifact always yields the same report, byte for byte. The inventory is a *source-identity* view. Two programs that differ only in comments or formatting have different digests and different comment spans here, yet elaborate to the identical Core; that duality is the point of the query.
modules.source:
-- | A source query over a decoded `prism-syntax-tokens-v1` artifact.
--
-- This is a *consumer* of the public token representation, not part of the
-- compiler. Given a `TokensDoc` (the exact source text plus the compiler's own
-- raw stream, layout-resolved parse stream, and trivia), it reports a stable,
-- machine-readable inventory of the source: the content digest, the ordered
-- imports, the comment spans, the ordered top-level declaration heads, and a
-- token-kind histogram in first-seen order.
--
-- Every field is a pure function of the artifact bytes. Nothing here reads
-- ambient workspace state: the same artifact always yields the same report,
-- byte for byte. The inventory is a *source-identity* view. Two programs that
-- differ only in comments or formatting have different digests and different
-- comment spans here, yet elaborate to the identical Core; that duality is the
-- point of the query.

import Data.List (map, flatten, reverse, filter)

import Syntax.Source (..)

import Syntax.Token (..)

import Syntax.Codec (..)

-- | The head of a top-level declaration: its leading keyword, the first name it
-- binds, and the keyword's start offset.
pub type DeclHead = DeclHead {
  keyword: String,
  name: String,
  lo: Int
} deriving (Eq, Show)

-- | One bucket of the token-kind histogram: a wire kind and how many raw tokens
-- carried it.
pub type KindCount = KindCount { kind: String, count: Int } deriving (Eq, Show)

-- | The full source inventory of an artifact.
pub type QueryReport = QueryReport {
  digest: String,
  imports: List(String),
  comments: List(Span),
  decls: List(DeclHead),
  kinds: List(KindCount)
} deriving (Eq)

-- The value a token carries, or the empty string for a value-free kind.
fn q_val(t : Token) : String =
  match t.value of
    Some(s) => s
    None => ""

-- Whether a kind carries an identifier-like name (ident, uid, or qualified).
fn q_is_name(k : TokenKind) : Bool =
  match k of
    TIdent => true
    TUid => true
    TQual => true
    _ => false

-- The comment spans of a trivia stream, in order.
fn q_comments(ts : List(Trivia)) : List(Span) =
  match ts of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(t, rest) =>
      match t of
        TComment(s) => Cons(s, q_comments(rest))
        _ => q_comments(rest)

-- Record `k` in a first-seen-order histogram: bump an existing bucket or append
-- a fresh one at the end.
fn q_bump(acc : List(KindCount), k : String) : List(KindCount) =
  match acc of
    Nil => Cons(KindCount { kind = k, count = 1 }, Nil)
    Cons(p, rest) =>
      if p.kind == k then
        Cons(KindCount { kind = k, count = p.count + 1 }, rest)
      else
        Cons(p, q_bump(rest, k))

-- The kind histogram of a raw token stream, in first-seen order.
fn q_kinds_go(ts : List(Token), acc : List(KindCount)) : List(KindCount) =
  match ts of
    Nil => acc
    Cons(t, rest) => q_kinds_go(rest, q_bump(acc, kind_name(t.kind)))

fn q_kinds(ts : List(Token)) : List(KindCount) = q_kinds_go(ts, Nil)

-- Push the current (reversed) item onto the output if it holds any token,
-- restoring source order.
fn q_flush(cur : List(Token), out : List(List(Token))) : List(List(Token)) =
  match cur of
    Nil => out
    Cons(_, _) => Cons(reverse(cur), out)

-- Split the layout-resolved parse stream into top-level items. Only depth-one
-- tokens (a declaration's head, before its body block opens) are retained, and
-- only a depth-one virtual semicolon ends an item; nested layout is skipped.
fn q_items_go(
  ts : List(Token),
  depth : Int,
  cur : List(Token),
  out : List(List(Token))
) : List(List(Token)) =
  match ts of
    Nil => reverse(q_flush(cur, out))
    Cons(t, rest) =>
      match t.kind of
        TVOpen => q_items_go(rest, depth + 1, cur, out)
        TVClose => q_items_go(rest, depth - 1, cur, out)
        TVSemi =>
          if depth == 1 then
            q_items_go(rest, depth, Nil, q_flush(cur, out))
          else
            q_items_go(rest, depth, cur, out)
        _ =>
          if depth == 1 then
            q_items_go(rest, depth, Cons(t, cur), out)
          else
            q_items_go(rest, depth, cur, out)

fn q_items(parse : List(Token)) : List(List(Token)) =
  q_items_go(parse, 0, Nil, Nil)

-- Drop a leading `pub` visibility modifier from an item's head tokens.
fn q_drop_pub(item : List(Token)) : List(Token) =
  match item of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(h, rest) =>
      if kind_name(h.kind) == "pub" then
        rest
      else
        item

-- The first identifier-like name in a token list, or the empty string.
fn q_first_name(ts : List(Token)) : String =
  match ts of
    Nil => ""
    Cons(t, rest) =>
      if q_is_name(t.kind) then
        q_val(t)
      else
        q_first_name(rest)

-- The declaration head of one item, if it has a leading keyword.
fn q_head(item : List(Token)) : Option(DeclHead) =
  match q_drop_pub(item) of
    Nil => None
    Cons(h, rest) =>
      Some(
          DeclHead {
            keyword = kind_name(h.kind),
            name = q_first_name(rest),
            lo = h.span.lo
          },
        )

fn q_heads(items : List(List(Token))) : List(DeclHead) =
  match items of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(it, rest) =>
      match q_head(it) of
        Some(d) => Cons(d, q_heads(rest))
        None => q_heads(rest)

-- The ordered top-level declaration heads of a parse stream.
fn q_decls(parse : List(Token)) : List(DeclHead) = q_heads(q_items(parse))

-- The import module names among a declaration list, in order.
fn q_imports(decls : List(DeclHead)) : List(String) =
  match decls of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(d, rest) =>
      if d.keyword == "import" then
        Cons(d.name, q_imports(rest))
      else
        q_imports(rest)

-- | The full source inventory of a decoded artifact.
pub fn query(doc : TokensDoc) : QueryReport =
  let ds = q_decls(doc.parse)
  QueryReport {
    digest = doc.source.digest,
    imports = q_imports(ds),
    comments = q_comments(doc.trivia),
    decls = ds,
    kinds = q_kinds(doc.raw)
  }

-- | The inventory rendered as one stable line per fact: a `digest` line, then
-- an `import` line per module, a `comment` line per span, a `decl` line per
-- declaration head, and a `kind` line per histogram bucket. The ordering is
-- deterministic, so the text is a machine-readable fingerprint of the source's
-- surface identity.
pub fn query_lines(r : QueryReport) : List(String) =
  flatten([
      ["digest {r.digest}"],
      map(\(m) -> "import {m}", r.imports),
      map(\(s) -> "comment {show_int(s.lo)} {show_int(s.hi)}", r.comments),
      map(\(d) -> "decl {d.keyword} {d.name} {show_int(d.lo)}", r.decls),
      map(\(k) -> "kind {k.kind} {show_int(k.count)}", r.kinds),
    ])

-- Join report lines with newlines, no trailing newline.
fn q_join(ls : List(String)) : String =
  match ls of
    Nil => ""
    Cons(l, Nil) => l
    Cons(l, rest) => "{l}\n{q_join(rest)}"

-- | The inventory rendered as one newline-joined block, ready to print in a
-- single call. Same content and ordering as `query_lines`.
pub fn query_text(r : QueryReport) : String = q_join(query_lines(r))

Rename as a join against the resolver, not as a tree walk.

The resolver has already decided what every name in a program means. A rename tool that walks the syntax and works scoping out again is a second, weaker answer to a question already answered, and the two disagree at exactly the cases that matter. So nothing here computes scope: it queries the `prism-resolved-syntax-v1` document, which carries a node id, a form kind, and an exact byte span for every node, and emits span-addressed edits for `Syntax.Edit` to apply.

What that seam supports, and what it does not, decides this module's shape. Every variable *reference* is a `var` node whose span covers exactly its identifier, so references are addressable and countable. No *binding* occurrence is: a `let` node's span starts at the `let` keyword, a parameter is a bare name with no span at all, and there is no edge from a reference to the binder it resolved to. A use-only rewrite of a name whose binder lives in the same file therefore produces a file where the uses no longer name their binder, which is a corrupt program dressed up as a refactor.

Rather than guess, `rn_plan` refuses whenever the seam cannot prove the rewrite is complete. The proof it demands is cheap and exact: lex the source, take every identifier token spelling the old name, and require that each one is a `var` occurrence the resolver recorded. If some mention is not (a binder, a declaration head, a parameter list, an import), the plan is refused. What survives is the case the seam really does cover: renaming every reference to a name bound outside this document.

The refusals are the useful part of the result, and they are the gap to report: when the seam grows a binder-identity fact, this module tightens without an interface change.

-- | Rename as a join against the resolver, not as a tree walk.
--
-- The resolver has already decided what every name in a program means. A rename
-- tool that walks the syntax and works scoping out again is a second, weaker
-- answer to a question already answered, and the two disagree at exactly the
-- cases that matter. So nothing here computes scope: it queries the
-- `prism-resolved-syntax-v1` document, which carries a node id, a form kind, and
-- an exact byte span for every node, and emits span-addressed edits for
-- `Syntax.Edit` to apply.
--
-- What that seam supports, and what it does not, decides this module's shape.
-- Every variable *reference* is a `var` node whose span covers exactly its
-- identifier, so references are addressable and countable. No *binding*
-- occurrence is: a `let` node's span starts at the `let` keyword, a parameter is
-- a bare name with no span at all, and there is no edge from a reference to the
-- binder it resolved to. A use-only rewrite of a name whose binder lives in the
-- same file therefore produces a file where the uses no longer name their
-- binder, which is a corrupt program dressed up as a refactor.
--
-- Rather than guess, `rn_plan` refuses whenever the seam cannot prove the
-- rewrite is complete. The proof it demands is cheap and exact: lex the source,
-- take every identifier token spelling the old name, and require that each one
-- is a `var` occurrence the resolver recorded. If some mention is not (a binder,
-- a declaration head, a parameter list, an import), the plan is refused. What
-- survives is the case the seam really does cover: renaming every reference to a
-- name bound outside this document.
--
-- The refusals are the useful part of the result, and they are the gap to
-- report: when the seam grows a binder-identity fact, this module tightens
-- without an interface change.

import Data.Foldable (length)

import Data.List (concat_map, filter, map)

import Syntax.Edit (..)

import Syntax.Lex (..)

import Syntax.Resolved (..)

import Syntax.Source (..)

import Syntax.Token (..)

-- | One variable reference: the node id the checker facts join on, the exact
-- span of the identifier, and the identifier text sliced from the embedded
-- source.
pub type RnUse = RnUse { id: Int, span: Span, name: String }

-- | Why a rename was refused. Every case is a fact about the document, not a
-- guess about the programmer's intent.
pub type RenameRefusal
  = RnNotAnIdent(String)
  | RnTaken(String)
  | RnUnknown(String)
  | RnUnaddressed(Span)
  | RnBinderInDocument(String, Span)
  | RnSourceUnreadable(LexError)
  deriving (Eq, Show)

-- | A human-readable account of a refusal.
pub fn rn_message(r : RenameRefusal) : String =
  match r of
    RnNotAnIdent(to) => "`{to}` is not a single identifier"
    RnTaken(to) => "`{to}` is already used in this document"
    RnUnknown(from) => "`{from}` is not referenced in this document"
    RnUnaddressed(s) =>
      "a reference at {show(s.lo)}..{show(s.hi)} is not addressable in the embedded source"
    RnBinderInDocument(from, s) =>
      "`{from}` is mentioned at {show(s.lo)}..{show(s.hi)} outside any recorded reference, so its binder is in this document and the seam cannot address it"
    RnSourceUnreadable(e) =>
      "the embedded source does not lex: {lex_message(e)}"

-- | Every variable reference in the document, in source order: the occurrence
-- table an editor's find-references is, and the join key column a checker uses
-- to pull `prism-tc-facts-v1` rows.
pub fn rn_occurrences(doc : ResolvedDoc) : List(RnUse) =
  concat_map(\(f) -> rn_fn_uses(doc.source, f), doc.functions)

fn rn_fn_uses(src : SourceFile, f : RFunction) : List(RnUse) =
  concat_map(\(n) -> rn_use(src, n), rnode_universe(f.body))

fn rn_use(src : SourceFile, n : RNode) : List(RnUse) =
  if n.kind == rkind_var() then
    match ed_span_text(src.text, n.span) of
      Some(name) => [RnUse { id = n.id, span = n.span, name = name }]
      None => []
  else
    []

-- | Every reference the embedded source cannot address. Non-empty means the
-- document and its source disagree, and every query here should be distrusted.
pub fn rn_unaddressed(doc : ResolvedDoc) : List(Span) =
  concat_map(\(f) -> rn_fn_unaddressed(doc.source, f), doc.functions)

fn rn_fn_unaddressed(src : SourceFile, f : RFunction) : List(Span) =
  concat_map(\(n) -> rn_bad_span(src, n), rnode_universe(f.body))

fn rn_bad_span(src : SourceFile, n : RNode) : List(Span) =
  if n.kind == rkind_var() then
    match ed_span_text(src.text, n.span) of
      Some(_) => []
      None => [n.span]
  else
    []

-- | Every reference to one name, in source order.
pub fn rn_uses_of(doc : ResolvedDoc, name : String) : List(RnUse) =
  filter(\(u) -> u.name == name, rn_occurrences(doc))

-- | How many times a name is referenced.
pub fn rn_use_count(doc : ResolvedDoc, name : String) : Int =
  length(rn_uses_of(doc, name))

-- | Whether a string is a single identifier, decided by the real lexer rather
-- than a hand-rolled character predicate. A keyword is not an identifier, so a
-- rename to one is refused here rather than discovered after the edit.
pub fn rn_is_ident(s : String) : Bool =
  match lex_raw(s) of
    Err(_) => false
    Ok(raw) =>
      match raw.tokens of
        Cons(t, Nil) => t.kind == TIdent
        _ => false

-- | The span of every identifier token spelling `name`, anywhere in the text.
-- This is the completeness check: a mention the resolver did not record as a
-- reference is a binder, a declaration head, or a parameter, and any of those
-- makes a use-only rewrite wrong.
pub fn rn_mentions(text : String, name : String) : Result(List(Span), LexError) =
  match lex_raw(text) of
    Err(e) => Err(e)
    Ok(raw) =>
      Ok(map(token_span, filter(\(t) -> rn_names(t, name), raw.tokens)))

fn token_span(t : Token) : Span = t.span

fn rn_names(t : Token, name : String) : Bool =
  match t.value of
    Some(v) => t.kind == TIdent && v == name
    None => false

-- | The edit set that renames every reference to `from` into `to`, or the
-- reason the seam cannot prove that rewrite is complete.
--
-- The checks run in a fixed order, so the refusal a caller sees is always the
-- first thing wrong: the source must lex, every reference must be addressable,
-- `to` must be a single identifier that occurs nowhere in the document, `from`
-- must be referenced at least once, and every mention of `from` must be one of
-- those references.
pub fn rn_plan(
  doc : ResolvedDoc,
  from : String,
  to : String
) : Result(List(Edit), RenameRefusal) =
  match rn_unaddressed(doc) of
    Cons(s, _) => Err(RnUnaddressed(s))
    Nil =>
      if not(rn_is_ident(to)) then
        Err(RnNotAnIdent(to))
      else
        rn_plan_checked(doc, from, to)

fn rn_plan_checked(
  doc : ResolvedDoc,
  from : String,
  to : String
) : Result(List(Edit), RenameRefusal) =
  match rn_mentions(doc.source.text, to) of
    Err(e) => Err(RnSourceUnreadable(e))
    Ok(Cons(_, _)) => Err(RnTaken(to))
    Ok(Nil) =>
      match rn_mentions(doc.source.text, from) of
        Err(e) => Err(RnSourceUnreadable(e))
        Ok(Nil) => Err(RnUnknown(from))
        Ok(mentions) =>
          rn_plan_complete(rn_uses_of(doc, from), mentions, from, to)

fn rn_plan_complete(
  uses : List(RnUse),
  mentions : List(Span),
  from : String,
  to : String
) : Result(List(Edit), RenameRefusal) =
  match uses of
    Nil => Err(RnUnknown(from))
    Cons(_, _) =>
      match rn_stray(map(use_span, uses), mentions) of
        Some(s) => Err(RnBinderInDocument(from, s))
        None => Ok(map(\(u) -> ed_replace(u.span, to), uses))

fn use_span(u : RnUse) : Span = u.span

-- The first mention that is not one of the recorded reference spans.
fn rn_stray(refs : List(Span), mentions : List(Span)) : Option(Span) =
  match mentions of
    Nil => None
    Cons(m, rest) =>
      if rn_covers(refs, m) then
        rn_stray(refs, rest)
      else
        Some(m)

fn rn_covers(refs : List(Span), m : Span) : Bool =
  match refs of
    Nil => false
    Cons(r, rest) =>
      if r.lo == m.lo && r.hi == m.hi then
        true
      else
        rn_covers(rest, m)

-- | Rename and apply, in one step: the plan, then the edits, then the re-lex
-- `Syntax.Edit` insists on. Either refusal comes back as itself.
pub fn rn_rename(
  doc : ResolvedDoc,
  from : String,
  to : String
) : Result(String, RenameError) =
  match rn_plan(doc, from, to) of
    Err(r) => Err(RnRefused(r))
    Ok(edits) =>
      match ed_apply(doc.source.text, edits) of
        Err(e) => Err(RnEdit(e))
        Ok(out) => Ok(out)

-- | The two ways a rename can fail: the seam refused to prove it, or the edits
-- did not survive being applied.
pub type RenameError
  = RnRefused(RenameRefusal)
  | RnEdit(EditError)
  deriving (Eq, Show)

Caret rendering for `Syntax.Diagnostic`: the plain-text report the compiler prints for a refused source.

It is rebuilt in Prism from the diagnostic and the source text alone. The target is exact bytes, not a lookalike, so the layout below is an executable specification of the compiler's renderer: the header line, the location line, the gutter, the source line with tabs expanded to four-column stops, the underline row, the arrow row carrying the label, and the closing rule. `Syntax.Diagnostic` supplies the data; this module is the only thing in Prism that can draw it.

The shape reproduced is one primary span drawn as a caret under one source line, which is every diagnostic the syntax boundary raises: a lexical fault is a zero-width caret at its offset, and a parse fault is the offending token's span or a caret at end of input. `rp_exact` is the predicate for that shape and `rp_report` answers `None` outside it rather than guessing. Three things fall outside.

A span crossing a line boundary, reachable through a multi-line string literal, draws the compiler's multi-line form instead: an arrow down the margin from the opening line to the closing one. That form is not implemented.

Several labels on one report, and the help and note trailers, belong to the structured type-error path rather than the syntax boundary. `related` is a reserved surface on `Diagnostic` and nothing populates it yet, so a second label has no source here to draw from.

A non-ASCII byte at or before the end of the diagnostic's own line changes the answer, and there the compiler's output is the right one: it draws one cell per character, while every column here is counted in bytes, so a two-byte character before the caret pulls this module's caret one cell further right. Counting characters would mean carrying a decoder the rest of the module has no use for, so the predicate below declines those lines instead.
modules.source:
-- | Caret rendering for `Syntax.Diagnostic`: the plain-text report the compiler
-- prints for a refused source.
--
-- It is rebuilt in Prism from the diagnostic and the source text alone. The
-- target is exact bytes, not a lookalike, so the layout below is an
-- executable specification of the compiler's renderer: the header line, the
-- location line, the gutter, the source line with tabs expanded to four-column
-- stops, the underline row, the arrow row carrying the label, and the closing
-- rule. `Syntax.Diagnostic` supplies the data; this module is the only thing in
-- Prism that can draw it.
--
-- The shape reproduced is one primary span drawn as a caret under one source
-- line, which is every diagnostic the syntax boundary raises: a lexical fault is
-- a zero-width caret at its offset, and a parse fault is the offending token's
-- span or a caret at end of input. `rp_exact` is the predicate for that shape
-- and `rp_report` answers `None` outside it rather than guessing. Three things
-- fall outside.
--
-- A span crossing a line boundary, reachable through a multi-line string
-- literal, draws the compiler's multi-line form instead: an arrow down the
-- margin from the opening line to the closing one. That form is not implemented.
--
-- Several labels on one report, and the help and note trailers, belong to the
-- structured type-error path rather than the syntax boundary. `related` is a
-- reserved surface on `Diagnostic` and nothing populates it yet, so a second
-- label has no source here to draw from.
--
-- A non-ASCII byte at or before the end of the diagnostic's own line changes the
-- answer, and there the compiler's output is the right one: it draws one cell
-- per character, while every column here is counted in bytes, so a two-byte
-- character before the caret pulls this module's caret one cell further right.
-- Counting characters would mean carrying a decoder the rest of the module has
-- no use for, so the predicate below declines those lines instead.

import Data.String (pad_left, slice_bytes, str_repeat)

import Syntax.Diagnostic (..)

import Syntax.Source (..)

-- The line table entry the compiler's renderer works from: a zero-based line
-- index and the half-open byte range the line covers, its terminator included.
type RpLine = RpLine { idx: Int, lo: Int, hi: Int }

-- A tab advances to the next four-column stop, the renderer's fixed tab width.
fn rp_tab_width() : Int = 4

-- The byte length of the line separator starting at `i`, or zero when none
-- starts there. The set is the renderer's seven: carriage return, line feed,
-- vertical tab, form feed, next line, line separator, paragraph separator. A
-- carriage return followed by a line feed is one terminator, not two.
fn rp_sep(text : String, i : Int) : Int =
  let b = byte_at(text, i)
  if b == 13 then
    if byte_at(text, i + 1) == 10 then
      2
    else
      1
  elif b == 10 || b == 11 || b == 12 then
    1
  elif b == 194 && byte_at(text, i + 1) == 133 then
    2
  elif b == 226 && byte_at(text, i + 1) == 128 then
    rp_sep_u2028(byte_at(text, i + 2))
  else
    0

-- The third byte of U+2028 and U+2029, the two separators spelled `e2 80 a8`
-- and `e2 80 a9`.
fn rp_sep_u2028(c : Int) : Int =
  if c == 168 || c == 169 then
    3
  else
    0

-- The byte just past the line starting at `lo`: past its terminator, or the end
-- of the text when the line runs to the end unterminated.
fn rp_line_end(text : String, lo : Int) : Int =
  let n = byte_len(text)
  var i := lo
  var e := -1
  while i < n && e < 0 do
    if rp_sep(text, i) > 0 then
      e := i + rp_sep(text, i)
    else
      i += 1
  if e < 0 then
    n
  else
    e

-- The line containing a byte offset: the last line whose start is at or before
-- it, so an offset at the very end of the text lands on the final line and an
-- empty text is one empty line.
fn rp_line_at(text : String, off : Int) : RpLine =
  let n = byte_len(text)
  var idx := 0
  var lo := 0
  var hi := rp_line_end(text, 0)
  while hi < n && hi <= off do
    idx += 1
    lo := hi
    hi := rp_line_end(text, lo)
  RpLine { idx = idx, lo = lo, hi = hi }

-- The number of characters in the byte range `[lo, hi)`: every byte that is not
-- a UTF-8 continuation byte starts one.
fn rp_chars(text : String, lo : Int, hi : Int) : Int =
  var i := lo
  var k := 0
  while i < hi do
    if byte_at(text, i) < 128 || byte_at(text, i) >= 192 then
      k += 1
    i += 1
  k

-- The byte range `[lo, hi)` of `text` as a string.
fn rp_bytes(text : String, lo : Int, hi : Int) : String =
  if lo >= hi then
    ""
  else
    string_of_buf(slice_bytes(text, lo, hi, buf_empty()))

-- The ASCII whitespace the renderer collapses to a single space: space, tab,
-- line feed, vertical tab, form feed, carriage return.
fn rp_ws(b : Int) : Bool =
  b == 32 || b == 9 || b == 10 || b == 11 || b == 12 || b == 13

-- A line with its trailing whitespace dropped, terminator included.
fn rp_trim_end(s : String) : String =
  var e := byte_len(s)
  while e > 0 && rp_ws(byte_at(s, e - 1)) do
    e -= 1
  rp_bytes(s, 0, e)

-- The columns the character at char index `i` of a trimmed line occupies. Past
-- the end of the line every column is one wide, which is what keeps the arrow
-- rows aligned once they run past the source text.
fn rp_width(line : String, i : Int) : Int =
  if i >= str_len(line) then
    1
  elif char_at(line, i) == 9 then
    (i / rp_tab_width() + 1) * rp_tab_width() - i
  else
    1

-- The source line as the renderer prints it: tabs expanded to the next stop,
-- every other whitespace character one space, everything else itself.
fn rp_body(line : String) : String =
  let n = str_len(line)
  var out := ""
  var i := 0
  while i < n do
    if rp_ws(char_at(line, i)) then
      out := concat(out, str_repeat(" ", rp_width(line, i)))
    else
      out := concat(out, substring(line, i, 1))
    i += 1
  out

-- The underline row: a rule under the span itself and a stem at the column the
-- label attaches to, each cell widened over the tab it sits on.
fn rp_under(line : String, arrow : Int, m : Int, lo : Int, hi : Int) : String =
  var out := ""
  var col := 0
  while col < arrow do
    out := concat(
        out,
        rp_cell(
            rp_under_head(col, m, lo, hi),
            rp_under_tail(col, m, lo, hi),
            rp_width(line, col),
          ),
      )
    col += 1
  out

-- The first cell character of the underline row at a column.
fn rp_under_head(col : Int, m : Int, lo : Int, hi : Int) : String =
  if col == m && lo <= col && col < hi then
    "┬"
  elif col == m then
    "│"
  elif lo <= col && col < hi then
    "─"
  else
    " "

-- The fill the underline row repeats across the rest of a wide cell.
fn rp_under_tail(col : Int, m : Int, lo : Int, hi : Int) : String =
  if col == m && lo <= col && col < hi then
    "─"
  elif col == m then
    " "
  elif lo <= col && col < hi then
    "─"
  else
    " "

-- The arrow row: a corner at the attach column and a rule running right from it
-- to the label.
fn rp_arrow(line : String, arrow : Int, m : Int) : String =
  var out := ""
  var col := 0
  while col < arrow do
    out := concat(
        out,
        rp_cell(
            rp_arrow_head(col, m),
            rp_arrow_tail(col, m),
            rp_width(line, col),
          ),
      )
    col += 1
  out

-- The first cell character of the arrow row at a column.
fn rp_arrow_head(col : Int, m : Int) : String =
  if col == m then
    "╰"
  elif col > m then
    "─"
  else
    " "

-- The fill the arrow row repeats across the rest of a wide cell.
fn rp_arrow_tail(col : Int, m : Int) : String =
  if col >= m then
    "─"
  else
    " "

-- One cell of an arrow row: the head once, then the fill for the remaining
-- columns the underlying character occupies.
fn rp_cell(head : String, tail : String, w : Int) : String =
  concat(head, str_repeat(tail, w - 1))

-- | The report-kind label the compiler stamps in the header for a phase.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Syntax.Diagnostic (..)
-- rp_kind(DPLex)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- Lexical Error
-- ```
pub fn rp_kind(p : DiagPhase) : String =
  match p of
    DPLex => "Lexical Error"
    DPParse => "Parse Error"

-- | The text on the caret's label. The end-of-input parse fault asks for more
-- input; every other diagnostic points `here`.
pub fn rp_label(d : Diagnostic) : String =
  if d.code == "E7101" then
    "expected more input here"
  else
    "here"

-- | The message on the header line. A parse fault's message already carries its
-- own position; a lexical fault's is followed by the line and column of its
-- caret.
pub fn rp_message(text : String, d : Diagnostic) : String =
  match d.phase of
    DPParse => d.message
    DPLex =>
      let lc = line_col(text, d.span.lo)
      "{d.message} at line {show_int(fst(lc))}:{show_int(snd(lc))}"

-- | Whether the compiler draws this diagnostic as one caret under one source
-- line, the shape this module reproduces byte for byte. False for a span that
-- crosses a line boundary, a span running past the end of the text, and a
-- source carrying a non-ASCII byte at or before the end of the caret's line.
pub fn rp_exact(text : String, d : Diagnostic) : Bool =
  span_valid(d.span)
    && d.span.hi <= byte_len(text)
    && rp_one_line(text, d.span)
    && rp_ascii(text, rp_line_at(text, d.span.lo).hi)

-- Whether a span begins and ends on the same line. The end is the last byte the
-- span covers, so a span ending exactly at a line break stays on that line.
fn rp_one_line(text : String, s : Span) : Bool =
  rp_line_at(text, s.lo).idx == rp_line_at(text, max(s.hi - 1, s.lo)).idx

-- Whether every byte below `upto` is ASCII, which is where byte columns and
-- character columns agree. Past that point the source may hold anything: a
-- character beyond the caret's line shifts neither the column nor the width of
-- anything drawn.
fn rp_ascii(text : String, upto : Int) : Bool =
  var i := 0
  var ok := true
  while i < upto && ok do
    if byte_at(text, i) >= 128 then
      ok := false
    i += 1
  ok

-- | The compiler's plain-text report for one diagnostic, or `None` when the
-- diagnostic falls outside the shape this module draws (see `rp_exact`). `name`
-- is the source name in the location line; the compiler passes `<source>` when
-- reporting on a single file. The result ends with a newline.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Data.Maybe (unwrap_or)
-- # import Syntax.Diagnostic (..)
-- # import Syntax.Source (..)
-- let d = Diagnostic {
--   code = "E7100",
--   phase = DPParse,
--   span = Span { lo = 12, hi = 13 },
--   message = "unexpected ')'",
--   expected = Nil,
--   related = Nil
-- }
-- print(unwrap_or("", rp_report("<source>", "fn main() = )\n", d)))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [E7100] Parse Error: unexpected ')'
--    ╭─[ <source>:1:13 ]
--    │
--  1 │ fn main() = )
--    │             ┬
--    │             ╰── here
-- ───╯
-- ```
pub fn rp_report(name : String, text : String, d : Diagnostic) : Option(String) =
  if rp_exact(text, d) then
    Some(rp_draw(name, text, d))
  else
    None

-- | Every diagnostic in a document rendered in order and concatenated, or
-- `None` when any one of them falls outside the shape this module draws. The
-- compiler stops at its first refusal, so a document carrying more than one
-- diagnostic has no single compiler report to compare against.
pub fn rp_report_doc(name : String, doc : DiagnosticsDoc) : Option(String) =
  rp_report_all(name, doc.source.text, doc.diagnostics, "")

fn rp_report_all(
  name : String,
  text : String,
  ds : List(Diagnostic),
  acc : String
) : Option(String) =
  match ds of
    Nil => Some(acc)
    Cons(d, rest) =>
      match rp_report(name, text, d) of
        None => None
        Some(s) => rp_report_all(name, text, rest, concat(acc, s))

-- Draw the six-part report. Every measurement is in characters relative to the
-- caret's line: `clo` and `chi` are the span's columns, `m` is the column the
-- label attaches to (the span's midpoint, never before its start), and the
-- arrow rows run two columns past the span's end.
fn rp_draw(name : String, text : String, d : Diagnostic) : String =
  let ln = rp_line_at(text, d.span.lo)
  let no = show_int(ln.idx + 1)
  let w = str_len(no)
  let line = rp_trim_end(rp_bytes(text, ln.lo, ln.hi))
  let clo = rp_chars(text, ln.lo, d.span.lo)
  let chi = rp_chars(text, ln.lo, d.span.hi)
  let m = max((clo + chi) / 2, clo)
  let arrow = chi + 2
  let gutter = str_repeat(" ", w + 2)
  let margin = concat(" ", concat(str_repeat(" ", w + 1), "│ "))
  let rule = str_repeat("─", w + 2)
  let head = "[{d.code}] {rp_kind(d.phase)}: {rp_message(text, d)}\n"
  let loc = "{gutter}╭─[ {name}:{no}:{show_int(clo + 1)} ]\n{gutter}│\n"
  let src = " {pad_left(no, w)} │ {rp_body(line)}\n"
  let bar = "{margin}{rp_under(line, arrow, m, clo, chi)}\n"
  let tip = "{margin}{rp_arrow(line, arrow, m)} {rp_label(d)}\n"
  concat(head, concat(loc, concat(src, concat(bar, concat(tip, "{rule}╯\n")))))

One document per source file: the embedded source identity and every user function's resolved body as a node-id-carrying tree. Each node's `id` is the same identity the `prism-tc-facts-v1` table keys on, so a Prism consumer traverses the structure here and joins the checker facts (type, resolution) there by id. modules.source:
-- | The typed vocabulary of the `prism-resolved-syntax-v1` artifact.
--
-- One document per source file: the embedded source identity and every user
-- function's resolved body as a node-id-carrying tree. Each node's `id` is the
-- same identity the `prism-tc-facts-v1` table keys on, so a Prism consumer
-- traverses the structure here and joins the checker facts (type, resolution)
-- there by id. The tree is the resolved Core-phase program: references are
-- resolved and the surface sugar forms have been desugared away, so it is a
-- traversable subset of the surface expression vocabulary.

import Control.Layer (..)

import Data.Foldable (elem, length)

import Syntax.Source (..)

-- | One resolved expression node: its NodeId (the join key), its
-- expression-form kind, its byte span, and its immediate children in source
-- order. A leaf carries the empty child list.
pub type RNode = RNode { id: Int, kind: String, span: Span, children: List(RNode) }

-- | One parameter of a resolved function: the binder its body's references
-- resolve to, and whether it is borrowed. A pattern parameter's name is the
-- synthesized binder the resolver assigned, because that is the name the body
-- actually mentions.
pub type RParam = RParam { name: String, is_borrow: Bool }

-- | One user function's resolved body tree, with its name and parameters.
pub type RFunction = RFunction { name: String, params: List(RParam), body: RNode }

-- | A decoded resolved-syntax document: the envelope identity, the embedded
-- source every span indexes into, and the user functions in source order.
pub type ResolvedDoc = ResolvedDoc {
  schema: String,
  compiler: String,
  source: SourceFile,
  functions: List(RFunction)
}

-- | The schema tag this vocabulary decodes.
pub fn resolved_schema() : String = "prism-resolved-syntax-v1"

-- | The node kinds the artifact spells, one function per form, so a consumer
-- matches on a named kind rather than retyping a bare string at each use site.
-- The list is the artifact's whole vocabulary: a kind outside it is a document
-- this version does not understand, which `rkind_known` is how to ask.
pub fn rkinds() : List(String) =
  [
      rkind_int(),
      rkind_float(),
      rkind_char(),
      rkind_bool(),
      rkind_unit(),
      rkind_str(),
      rkind_var(),
      rkind_hole(),
      rkind_bin(),
      rkind_neg(),
      rkind_if(),
      rkind_let(),
      rkind_lam(),
      rkind_call(),
      rkind_pipe(),
      rkind_match(),
      rkind_list(),
      rkind_tuple(),
      rkind_field(),
      rkind_unboxed_tuple(),
      rkind_unboxed_record(),
      rkind_unboxed_field(),
      rkind_record(),
      rkind_record_update(),
      rkind_record_update_path(),
      rkind_handle(),
      rkind_mask(),
      rkind_inst(),
      rkind_index(),
      rkind_index_set(),
      rkind_ann(),
    ]

-- | Whether a kind string is one this vocabulary names.
pub fn rkind_known(k : String) : Bool = elem(k, rkinds())

-- | An integer literal.
pub fn rkind_int() : String = "int"

-- | A float literal.
pub fn rkind_float() : String = "float"

-- | A character literal.
pub fn rkind_char() : String = "char"

-- | A boolean literal.
pub fn rkind_bool() : String = "bool"

-- | The unit value.
pub fn rkind_unit() : String = "unit"

-- | A string literal.
pub fn rkind_str() : String = "str"

-- | A variable reference. Its span covers exactly the identifier, which is what
-- makes references, and only references, addressable in the source.
pub fn rkind_var() : String = "var"

-- | A typed hole.
pub fn rkind_hole() : String = "hole"

-- | A binary operator application.
pub fn rkind_bin() : String = "bin"

-- | An arithmetic negation.
pub fn rkind_neg() : String = "neg"

-- | A conditional.
pub fn rkind_if() : String = "if"

-- | A let binding. Its span starts at the `let` keyword, so the bound name it
-- introduces is not separately addressable.
pub fn rkind_let() : String = "let"

-- | A lambda.
pub fn rkind_lam() : String = "lam"

-- | A function application.
pub fn rkind_call() : String = "call"

-- | A pipeline application.
pub fn rkind_pipe() : String = "pipe"

-- | A match expression.
pub fn rkind_match() : String = "match"

-- | A list literal.
pub fn rkind_list() : String = "list"

-- | A tuple literal.
pub fn rkind_tuple() : String = "tuple"

-- | A record field access.
pub fn rkind_field() : String = "field"

-- | An unboxed tuple literal.
pub fn rkind_unboxed_tuple() : String = "unboxed-tuple"

-- | An unboxed record literal.
pub fn rkind_unboxed_record() : String = "unboxed-record"

-- | An unboxed record field access.
pub fn rkind_unboxed_field() : String = "unboxed-field"

-- | A record construction.
pub fn rkind_record() : String = "record"

-- | A record update.
pub fn rkind_record_update() : String = "record-update"

-- | A nested-path record update.
pub fn rkind_record_update_path() : String = "record-update-path"

-- | An effect handler installation.
pub fn rkind_handle() : String = "handle"

-- | An effect mask.
pub fn rkind_mask() : String = "mask"

-- | An explicit instantiation.
pub fn rkind_inst() : String = "inst"

-- | An index read.
pub fn rkind_index() : String = "index"

-- | An index write.
pub fn rkind_index_set() : String = "index-set"

-- | A type annotation.
pub fn rkind_ann() : String = "ann"

-- | The immediate children of one resolved node, in source order. The one
-- constructor-naming site for `RNode` traversal; every generic walk derives
-- from it, so a consumer never re-matches the node shape.
pub fn rnode_children(n : RNode) : List(RNode) = n.children

-- | Put a replacement child list back into a resolved node, keeping its id,
-- kind, and span. Fails closed: a list of the wrong length yields the node
-- unchanged.
pub fn rnode_rebuild(n : RNode, cs : List(RNode)) : RNode =
  if length(cs) == length(n.children) then
    RNode { id = n.id, kind = n.kind, span = n.span, children = cs }
  else
    n

-- | The children-and-rebuild pair for resolved nodes, so every strategy in
-- `Control.Rewrite` and every query in `Control.Layer` works on a resolved
-- body.
pub fn rnode_layer() : Layer(RNode) =
  Layer { kids = rnode_children, rebuild = rnode_rebuild }

-- | Every node of a resolved body, root first, depth-first. The uniplate
-- `universe` over `RNode`, the traversal a Prism-written checker walks a body
-- with.
pub fn rnode_universe(n : RNode) : List(RNode) = lay_universe(rnode_layer(), n)

-- | The number of nodes in a resolved body.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Syntax.Source (Span)
-- rnode_count(RNode { id = 0, kind = "unit", span = Span { lo = 0, hi = 0 }, children = [] })
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 1
-- ```
pub fn rnode_count(n : RNode) : Int = lay_size(rnode_layer(), n)

modules.doc:
Source identity for the versioned syntax artifacts: source files and half-open byte spans.

Byte offsets are the canonical position vocabulary (line and column are projections for people, never a second identity), and these are the Prism-side types the token and surface-syntax exports decode into.
modules.source:
-- | Source identity for the versioned syntax artifacts: source files and
-- half-open byte spans.
--
-- Byte offsets are the canonical position vocabulary (line and column are
-- projections for people, never a second identity), and these are the
-- Prism-side types the token and surface-syntax exports decode into.

import Data.String (..)

-- | A half-open byte range `[lo, hi)` into one source text.
--
-- ```prism
-- span_len(Span { lo = 3, hi = 8 })
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 5
-- ```
pub type Span = Span { lo: Int, hi: Int } deriving (Eq, Show)

-- | The number of bytes a span covers.
pub fn span_len(s : Span) : Int = s.hi - s.lo

-- | Whether a span is well formed: non-negative start, start at or before end.
--
-- ```prism
-- (span_valid(Span { lo = 2, hi = 2 }), span_valid(Span { lo = 5, hi = 4 }))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- (true, false)
-- ```
pub fn span_valid(s : Span) : Bool = 0 <= s.lo && s.lo <= s.hi

-- | Whether a byte offset falls inside the span (half-open, so the end offset
-- is outside).
pub fn span_contains(s : Span, pos : Int) : Bool = s.lo <= pos && pos < s.hi

-- | One source file as an artifact embeds it: the exact text and its digest.
-- Every span in an artifact indexes this text, so a persisted document needs
-- no external file.
pub type SourceFile = SourceFile { digest: String, text: String } deriving (Eq)

-- | The one-based line and column of a byte offset, as a projection over the
-- text. Offsets past the end clamp to the final position.
--
-- ```prism
-- line_col("ab\ncd", 4)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- (2, 2)
-- ```
pub fn line_col(text : String, off : Int) : (Int, Int) =
  line_col_go(text, 0, min(off, str_len(text)), 1, 1)

fn line_col_go(s : String, i : Int, stop : Int, l : Int, c : Int) : (Int, Int) =
  if i >= stop then
    (l, c)
  elif char_at(s, i) == 10 then
    line_col_go(s, i + 1, stop, l + 1, 1)
  else
    line_col_go(s, i + 1, stop, l, c + 1)

The token vocabulary of the `prism-syntax-tokens-v1` artifact.

A fixed token's wire kind is its source spelling, so `TFixed` carries the spelling rather than enumerating every keyword and operator; value-carrying and virtual layout tokens each get a dedicated constructor matching the grammar's terminal aliases.
modules.source:
-- | The token vocabulary of the `prism-syntax-tokens-v1` artifact.
--
-- A fixed token's wire kind is its source spelling, so `TFixed` carries the
-- spelling rather than enumerating every keyword and operator; value-carrying
-- and virtual layout tokens each get a dedicated constructor matching the
-- grammar's terminal aliases.

import Data.Maybe (..)

import Syntax.Source (..)

-- | A token kind: a fixed token by exact spelling, or one of the special
-- value-carrying and virtual kinds.
pub type TokenKind
  = TFixed(String)
  | TIdent
  | TUid
  | TQual
  | TInt
  | TFloat
  | TChar
  | TStr
  | TIStart
  | TIMid
  | TIEnd
  | TVOpen
  | TVClose
  | TVSemi
  deriving (Eq)

-- | The canonical wire name of a token kind, matching the compiler's artifact
-- vocabulary (fixed tokens spell themselves; specials use the grammar's
-- terminal aliases).
--
-- ```prism
-- (kind_name(TIdent), kind_name(TVOpen), kind_name(TFixed("->")))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- (ident, v{, ->)
-- ```
pub fn kind_name(k : TokenKind) : String =
  match k of
    TFixed(s) => s
    TIdent => "ident"
    TUid => "uid"
    TQual => "qual"
    TInt => "int"
    TFloat => "float"
    TChar => "char"
    TStr => "str"
    TIStart => "istart"
    TIMid => "imid"
    TIEnd => "iend"
    TVOpen => "v\{"
    TVClose => "v\}"
    TVSemi => "v;"

-- | The token kind a wire name denotes. Any name that is not one of the
-- special aliases is a fixed token spelling; the fixed vocabulary itself is
-- pinned by the compiler's own tests, not re-enumerated here.
--
-- ```prism
-- (kind_of_name("uid") == TUid, kind_of_name("match") == TFixed("match"))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- (true, true)
-- ```
pub fn kind_of_name(s : String) : TokenKind =
  if s == "ident" then
    TIdent
  elif s == "uid" then
    TUid
  elif s == "qual" then
    TQual
  elif s == "int" then
    TInt
  elif s == "float" then
    TFloat
  elif s == "char" then
    TChar
  elif s == "str" then
    TStr
  elif s == "istart" then
    TIStart
  elif s == "imid" then
    TIMid
  elif s == "iend" then
    TIEnd
  elif s == "v\{" then
    TVOpen
  elif s == "v\}" then
    TVClose
  elif s == "v;" then
    TVSemi
  else
    TFixed(s)

-- | One token: its kind, its span in the embedded source, and, for
-- value-carrying kinds, the decoded payload (escapes resolved, digit
-- separators stripped). The original spelling is always recoverable from the
-- span.
pub type Token = Token { kind: TokenKind, span: Span, value: Option(String) }

-- | One trivia event between semantic tokens: a line comment, a delimited
-- comment, or a blank-line run.
pub type Trivia = TComment(Span) | TBlockComment(Span) | TBlank(Span)

-- | The wire name of a trivia event.
pub fn trivia_name(t : Trivia) : String =
  match t of
    TComment(_) => "comment"
    TBlockComment(_) => "block-comment"
    TBlank(_) => "blank"

-- | The span a trivia event covers.
pub fn trivia_span(t : Trivia) : Span =
  match t of
    TComment(s) => s
    TBlockComment(s) => s
    TBlank(s) => s

modules.doc:
Generic traversal over the surface syntax tree.

The design is uniplate-shaped: two hand-written total functions per sort give the immediate same-sort children of a node (`expr_children`) and put a replacement child list back (`expr_rebuild`), and every generic operation derives from that pair (`expr_universe`, `expr_count`, `expr_any`, `expr_fold`, and every strategy in `Control.Rewrite` applied to `expr_layer`). The one-layer functions are the only place that names constructors, so a new `Expr` constructor is one arm in each and every derived traversal follows; totality of the two matches is the drift guard.

The pair is written out rather than derived, and the reason is the span. `deriving (Plate)` walks *through* a carrier record, so a derived instance on `Expr` yields children of type `Expr` with the spanned wrappers already consumed: its `rebuild` puts the original spans back, but its `children` has dropped them, and a spanned child is what every query here returns. Deriving on the wrapper instead yields no children at all, because an `Sp(a)` holds no `Sp(a)`. The instance that would say the right thing is one at `Sp(Expr)`, and it cannot be written: a `deriving` clause names a declaration rather than an instantiation, and instance dispatch keys on the head constructor alone, so `Sp(Expr)` and `Sp(Pat)` would be a single instance.
