-- | Generic traversal over the surface syntax tree.
--
-- The design is uniplate-shaped: two hand-written total functions per sort
-- give the immediate same-sort children of a node (`expr_children`) and put a
-- replacement child list back (`expr_rebuild`), and every generic operation
-- derives from that pair (`expr_universe`, `expr_count`, `expr_any`,
-- `expr_fold`, and every strategy in `Control.Rewrite` applied to
-- `expr_layer`). The one-layer functions are the only place that names
-- constructors, so a new `Expr` constructor is one arm in each and every
-- derived traversal follows; totality of the two matches is the drift guard.
--
-- The pair is written out rather than derived, and the reason is the span.
-- `deriving (Plate)` walks *through* a carrier record, so a derived instance on
-- `Expr` yields children of type `Expr` with the spanned wrappers already
-- consumed: its `rebuild` puts the original spans back, but its `children` has
-- dropped them, and a spanned child is what every query here returns. Deriving
-- on the wrapper instead yields no children at all, because an `Sp(a)` holds no
-- `Sp(a)`. The instance that would say the right thing is one at `Sp(Expr)`, and
-- it cannot be written: a `deriving` clause names a declaration rather than an
-- instantiation, and instance dispatch keys on the head constructor alone, so
-- `Sp(Expr)` and `Sp(Pat)` would be a single instance.

import Control.Layer (..)

import Data.Foldable (any, length)

import Data.List (append, concat_map, drop, foldl, map, reverse, take)

import Syntax.Ast (..)

import Syntax.Source (..)

-- | The immediate `Expr` children of one node, in source order. Children held
-- inside carrier records (match arms, handler arms, qualifiers, path steps and
-- updates, parameter defaults, named fields) are included; a leaf yields the
-- empty list.
pub fn expr_children(e : Sp(Expr)) : List(Sp(Expr)) =
  match node_of(e) of
    EInt(_, _) => []
    EFloat(_) => []
    EChar(_) => []
    EBool(_) => []
    EUnit => []
    EStr(_) => []
    EVar(_) => []
    EHole(_) => []
    EBin(_, a, b) => [a, b]
    ENeg(a) => [a]
    EIf(c, t, f) => [c, t, f]
    ELet(_, v, rest) => [v, rest]
    ELam(ps, body) => append(concat_map(param_default, ps), [body])
    ECall(f, args) => Cons(f, args)
    EPipe(a, b) => [a, b]
    EMatch(scrut, arms) => Cons(scrut, concat_map(arm_children, arms))
    EList(xs) => xs
    ETuple(xs) => xs
    EField(r, _) => [r]
    EUnboxedTuple(xs) => xs
    EUnboxedRecord(fs) => map(named_value, fs)
    EUnboxedField(r, _) => [r]
    ERecord(_, fs) => map(named_value, fs)
    ERecordUpdate(r, _, fs) => Cons(r, map(named_value, fs))
    EPathUpdate(r, ups) => Cons(r, concat_map(update_children, ups))
    EHandle(action, arms, _) => Cons(action, map(handler_body, arms))
    EMask(_, a) => [a]
    EInst(a, _) => [a]
    EIndex(r, i) => [r, i]
    EIndexSet(r, i, v) => [r, i, v]
    EAnn(a, _) => [a]
    EMarker(_) => []
    ENamedHandle(_, action, arms) => Cons(action, map(handler_body, arms))
    EVarDecl(_, v, rest) => [v, rest]
    EAssign(_, v) => [v]
    EIndexAssign(r, i, v) => [r, i, v]
    EThrow(_, args) => args
    ETryCatch(body, arms) => Cons(body, map(catch_body, arms))
    EFor(_, src, quals, body) =>
      Cons(src, append(concat_map(qual_children, quals), [body]))
    EWhile(c, body) => [c, body]
    ELoop(body) => [body]
    EBreak => []
    EContinue => []
    EReturn(a) => [a]
    EComp(out, _, src, quals) =>
      Cons(out, Cons(src, concat_map(qual_children, quals)))
    EDefault(a, d) => [a, d]
    ETransact(a, b) => [a, b]
    EProbe(_, a) => [a]
    EReflect(_, _) => []
    EOptChain(r, _) => [r]
    ERange(parts, stop) => append(parts, [stop])
    ECompose(_, a, b) => [a, b]
    EReadPath(r, steps) => Cons(r, concat_map(step_children, steps))

-- | The `Expr` children carried by one match arm: the guard when present,
-- then the body.
fn arm_children(a : Arm) : List(Sp(Expr)) =
  match a.guard of
    Some(g) => [g, a.body]
    None => [a.body]

fn named_value(f : NamedExpr) : Sp(Expr) = f.value

fn update_value(u : PathUpdate) : Sp(Expr) =
  match u.op of
    POSet(v) => v
    POModify(v) => v

-- | The `Expr` children of one optic path step: the index or filter it
-- carries, if any.
fn step_children(s : PathStep) : List(Sp(Expr)) =
  match s of
    PSField(_) => []
    PSEach => []
    PSCase(_) => []
    PSIndex(i) => [i]
    PSWhere(g) => [g]

-- | The `Expr` children of one path update: the expressions inside the path it
-- walks, then the value written at its end.
fn update_children(u : PathUpdate) : List(Sp(Expr)) =
  append(concat_map(step_children, u.path), [update_value(u)])

-- | The default expression of one parameter, if it has one.
fn param_default(p : Param) : List(Sp(Expr)) =
  match p.dflt of
    Some(d) => [d]
    None => []

fn handler_body(h : HandlerArm) : Sp(Expr) =
  match h of
    HReturn(_, body) => body
    HOp(_, _, _, body) => body
    HOnce(_, _, body) => body
    HVal(_, body) => body
    HNever(_, _, body) => body

fn catch_body(c : CatchArm) : Sp(Expr) = c.body

fn qual_children(q : Qual) : List(Sp(Expr)) =
  match q of
    QGuard(g) => [g]
    QBind(_, src) => [src]

-- | Put a replacement child list back into one node, in `expr_children` order,
-- keeping the node's span and its synthetic bit.
--
-- This is the inverse half of `expr_children`, and the pair is everything a
-- generic strategy needs to descend a tree. It fails closed: a child list that
-- does not match the node's shape (a different length, a carrier arity that
-- does not line up) yields the node unchanged rather than a silently reshaped
-- one, so `expr_rebuild(e, expr_children(e))` is the identity and a garbage
-- child list cannot forge a node.
pub fn expr_rebuild(e : Sp(Expr), cs : List(Sp(Expr))) : Sp(Expr) =
  match wk_node(node_of(e), cs) of
    Some(n) => Sp { node = n, span = e.span, synth = e.synth }
    None => e

-- | The children-and-rebuild pair for spanned expressions, which is what every
-- strategy in `Control.Rewrite` and every query in `Control.Layer` takes.
pub fn expr_layer() : Layer(Sp(Expr)) =
  Layer { kids = expr_children, rebuild = expr_rebuild }

fn wk_leaf(e : Expr, cs : List(Sp(Expr))) : Option(Expr) =
  match cs of
    Nil => Some(e)
    _ => None

fn wk_same_len(xs : List(a), cs : List(Sp(Expr))) : Bool =
  length(xs) == length(cs)

fn wk_node(e : Expr, cs : List(Sp(Expr))) : Option(Expr) =
  match e of
    EInt(_, _) => wk_leaf(e, cs)
    EFloat(_) => wk_leaf(e, cs)
    EChar(_) => wk_leaf(e, cs)
    EBool(_) => wk_leaf(e, cs)
    EUnit => wk_leaf(e, cs)
    EStr(_) => wk_leaf(e, cs)
    EVar(_) => wk_leaf(e, cs)
    EHole(_) => wk_leaf(e, cs)
    EBin(op, _, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(a, Cons(b, Nil)) => Some(EBin(op, a, b))
        _ => None
    ENeg(_) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(a, Nil) => Some(ENeg(a))
        _ => None
    EIf(_, _, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(c, Cons(t, Cons(f, Nil))) => Some(EIf(c, t, f))
        _ => None
    ELet(n, _, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(v, Cons(rest, Nil)) => Some(ELet(n, v, rest))
        _ => None
    ELam(ps, _) =>
      let k = length(concat_map(param_default, ps))
      match wk_params(ps, take(k, cs)) of
        None => None
        Some(ps2) =>
          match drop(k, cs) of
            Cons(body, Nil) => Some(ELam(ps2, body))
            _ => None
    ECall(_, args) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(f, rest) =>
          if wk_same_len(args, rest) then
            Some(ECall(f, rest))
          else
            None
        _ => None
    EPipe(_, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(a, Cons(b, Nil)) => Some(EPipe(a, b))
        _ => None
    EMatch(_, arms) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(scrut, rest) =>
          match wk_arms(arms, rest) of
            None => None
            Some(arms2) => Some(EMatch(scrut, arms2))
        _ => None
    EList(xs) =>
      if wk_same_len(xs, cs) then
        Some(EList(cs))
      else
        None
    ETuple(xs) =>
      if wk_same_len(xs, cs) then
        Some(ETuple(cs))
      else
        None
    EField(_, n) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(r, Nil) => Some(EField(r, n))
        _ => None
    EUnboxedTuple(xs) =>
      if wk_same_len(xs, cs) then
        Some(EUnboxedTuple(cs))
      else
        None
    EUnboxedRecord(fs) =>
      match wk_fields(fs, cs) of
        None => None
        Some(fs2) => Some(EUnboxedRecord(fs2))
    EUnboxedField(_, n) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(r, Nil) => Some(EUnboxedField(r, n))
        _ => None
    ERecord(n, fs) =>
      match wk_fields(fs, cs) of
        None => None
        Some(fs2) => Some(ERecord(n, fs2))
    ERecordUpdate(_, n, fs) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(r, rest) =>
          match wk_fields(fs, rest) of
            None => None
            Some(fs2) => Some(ERecordUpdate(r, n, fs2))
        _ => None
    EPathUpdate(_, ups) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(r, rest) =>
          match wk_updates(ups, rest) of
            None => None
            Some(ups2) => Some(EPathUpdate(r, ups2))
        _ => None
    EHandle(_, arms, m) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(action, rest) =>
          match wk_handlers(arms, rest) of
            None => None
            Some(arms2) => Some(EHandle(action, arms2, m))
        _ => None
    EMask(n, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(a, Nil) => Some(EMask(n, a))
        _ => None
    EInst(_, ts) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(a, Nil) => Some(EInst(a, ts))
        _ => None
    EIndex(_, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(r, Cons(i, Nil)) => Some(EIndex(r, i))
        _ => None
    EIndexSet(_, _, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(r, Cons(i, Cons(v, Nil))) => Some(EIndexSet(r, i, v))
        _ => None
    EAnn(_, t) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(a, Nil) => Some(EAnn(a, t))
        _ => None
    EMarker(_) => wk_leaf(e, cs)
    ENamedHandle(n, _, arms) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(action, rest) =>
          match wk_handlers(arms, rest) of
            None => None
            Some(arms2) => Some(ENamedHandle(n, action, arms2))
        _ => None
    EVarDecl(n, _, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(v, Cons(rest, Nil)) => Some(EVarDecl(n, v, rest))
        _ => None
    EAssign(n, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(v, Nil) => Some(EAssign(n, v))
        _ => None
    EIndexAssign(_, _, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(r, Cons(i, Cons(v, Nil))) => Some(EIndexAssign(r, i, v))
        _ => None
    EThrow(n, args) =>
      if wk_same_len(args, cs) then
        Some(EThrow(n, cs))
      else
        None
    ETryCatch(_, arms) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(body, rest) =>
          match wk_catches(arms, rest) of
            None => None
            Some(arms2) => Some(ETryCatch(body, arms2))
        _ => None
    EFor(n, _, quals, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(src, rest) =>
          match wk_quals(quals, take(length(quals), rest)) of
            None => None
            Some(qs) =>
              match drop(length(quals), rest) of
                Cons(body, Nil) => Some(EFor(n, src, qs, body))
                _ => None
        _ => None
    EWhile(_, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(c, Cons(body, Nil)) => Some(EWhile(c, body))
        _ => None
    ELoop(_) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(body, Nil) => Some(ELoop(body))
        _ => None
    EBreak => wk_leaf(e, cs)
    EContinue => wk_leaf(e, cs)
    EReturn(_) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(a, Nil) => Some(EReturn(a))
        _ => None
    EComp(_, n, _, quals) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(out, Cons(src, rest)) =>
          match wk_quals(quals, rest) of
            None => None
            Some(qs) => Some(EComp(out, n, src, qs))
        _ => None
    EDefault(_, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(a, Cons(d, Nil)) => Some(EDefault(a, d))
        _ => None
    ETransact(_, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(a, Cons(b, Nil)) => Some(ETransact(a, b))
        _ => None
    EProbe(n, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(a, Nil) => Some(EProbe(n, a))
        _ => None
    EReflect(_, _) => wk_leaf(e, cs)
    EOptChain(_, n) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(r, Nil) => Some(EOptChain(r, n))
        _ => None
    ERange(parts, _) =>
      match reverse(cs) of
        Cons(stop, rparts) =>
          if wk_same_len(parts, rparts) then
            Some(ERange(reverse(rparts), stop))
          else
            None
        _ => None
    ECompose(op, _, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(a, Cons(b, Nil)) => Some(ECompose(op, a, b))
        _ => None
    EReadPath(_, steps) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(r, rest) =>
          match wk_steps(steps, rest) of
            None => None
            Some(steps2) => Some(EReadPath(r, steps2))
        _ => None

fn wk_arms(arms : List(Arm), cs : List(Sp(Expr))) : Option(List(Arm)) =
  match arms of
    Nil => wk_end(cs, Nil)
    Cons(a, more) =>
      match a.guard of
        Some(_) =>
          match cs of
            Cons(g, Cons(b, rest)) =>
              match wk_arms(more, rest) of
                None => None
                Some(tl) =>
                  Some(Cons(Arm { pat = a.pat, guard = Some(g), body = b }, tl))
            _ => None
        None =>
          match cs of
            Cons(b, rest) =>
              match wk_arms(more, rest) of
                None => None
                Some(tl) =>
                  Some(Cons(Arm { pat = a.pat, guard = None, body = b }, tl))
            _ => None

fn wk_fields(
  fs : List(NamedExpr),
  cs : List(Sp(Expr))
) : Option(List(NamedExpr)) =
  match fs of
    Nil => wk_end(cs, Nil)
    Cons(f, more) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(v, rest) =>
          match wk_fields(more, rest) of
            None => None
            Some(tl) => Some(Cons(NamedExpr { name = f.name, value = v }, tl))
        _ => None

fn wk_handlers(
  arms : List(HandlerArm),
  cs : List(Sp(Expr))
) : Option(List(HandlerArm)) =
  match arms of
    Nil => wk_end(cs, Nil)
    Cons(h, more) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(b, rest) =>
          match wk_handlers(more, rest) of
            None => None
            Some(tl) => Some(Cons(wk_handler(h, b), tl))
        _ => None

fn wk_handler(h : HandlerArm, b : Sp(Expr)) : HandlerArm =
  match h of
    HReturn(n, _) => HReturn(n, b)
    HOp(n, ps, k, _) => HOp(n, ps, k, b)
    HOnce(n, ps, _) => HOnce(n, ps, b)
    HVal(n, _) => HVal(n, b)
    HNever(n, ps, _) => HNever(n, ps, b)

fn wk_catches(
  arms : List(CatchArm),
  cs : List(Sp(Expr))
) : Option(List(CatchArm)) =
  match arms of
    Nil => wk_end(cs, Nil)
    Cons(c, more) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(b, rest) =>
          match wk_catches(more, rest) of
            None => None
            Some(tl) =>
              Some(
                  Cons(
                      CatchArm {
                        name = c.name,
                        binders = c.binders,
                        body = b,
                        span = c.span
                      },
                      tl,
                    ),
                )
        _ => None

fn wk_quals(quals : List(Qual), cs : List(Sp(Expr))) : Option(List(Qual)) =
  match quals of
    Nil => wk_end(cs, Nil)
    Cons(q, more) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(v, rest) =>
          match wk_quals(more, rest) of
            None => None
            Some(tl) => Some(Cons(wk_qual(q, v), tl))
        _ => None

fn wk_qual(q : Qual, v : Sp(Expr)) : Qual =
  match q of
    QGuard(_) => QGuard(v)
    QBind(n, _) => QBind(n, v)

fn wk_steps(
  steps : List(PathStep),
  cs : List(Sp(Expr))
) : Option(List(PathStep)) =
  match steps of
    Nil => wk_end(cs, Nil)
    Cons(s, more) =>
      match step_children(s) of
        Nil =>
          match wk_steps(more, cs) of
            None => None
            Some(tl) => Some(Cons(s, tl))
        _ =>
          match cs of
            Cons(v, rest) =>
              match wk_steps(more, rest) of
                None => None
                Some(tl) => Some(Cons(wk_step(s, v), tl))
            _ => None

fn wk_step(s : PathStep, v : Sp(Expr)) : PathStep =
  match s of
    PSIndex(_) => PSIndex(v)
    PSWhere(_) => PSWhere(v)
    _ => s

fn wk_updates(
  ups : List(PathUpdate),
  cs : List(Sp(Expr))
) : Option(List(PathUpdate)) =
  match ups of
    Nil => wk_end(cs, Nil)
    Cons(u, more) =>
      let k = length(concat_map(step_children, u.path))
      match wk_steps(u.path, take(k, cs)) of
        None => None
        Some(path2) =>
          match drop(k, cs) of
            Cons(v, rest) =>
              match wk_updates(more, rest) of
                None => None
                Some(tl) =>
                  Some(
                      Cons(
                          PathUpdate { path = path2, op = wk_op(u.op, v) },
                          tl,
                        ),
                    )
            _ => None

fn wk_op(o : PathOp, v : Sp(Expr)) : PathOp =
  match o of
    POSet(_) => POSet(v)
    POModify(_) => POModify(v)

fn wk_params(ps : List(Param), cs : List(Sp(Expr))) : Option(List(Param)) =
  match ps of
    Nil => wk_end(cs, Nil)
    Cons(p, more) =>
      match p.dflt of
        Some(_) =>
          match cs of
            Cons(v, rest) =>
              match wk_params(more, rest) of
                None => None
                Some(tl) => Some(Cons(wk_param(p, v), tl))
            _ => None
        None =>
          match wk_params(more, cs) of
            None => None
            Some(tl) => Some(Cons(p, tl))

fn wk_param(p : Param, v : Sp(Expr)) : Param =
  Param {
    name = p.name,
    pat = p.pat,
    ty = p.ty,
    is_borrow = p.is_borrow,
    dflt = Some(v)
  }

-- | The base case every carrier rebuild shares: the child list must be spent
-- exactly, so a longer one is a shape mismatch and not a silent truncation.
fn wk_end(cs : List(Sp(Expr)), done : b) : Option(b) =
  match cs of
    Nil => Some(done)
    _ => None

-- | Every node of the tree, root first, in depth-first source order.
--
-- ```prism
-- expr_count(lit_probe(7))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 1
-- ```
pub fn expr_universe(e : Sp(Expr)) : List(Sp(Expr)) =
  Cons(e, concat_map(expr_universe, expr_children(e)))

-- | A span-zero literal, a convenience for building test trees.
pub fn lit_probe(n : Int) : Sp(Expr) =
  Sp {
    node = EInt(show(n), SufNone),
    span = Span { lo = 0, hi = 0 },
    synth = false
  }

-- | The number of nodes in the tree.
pub fn expr_count(e : Sp(Expr)) : Int = length(expr_universe(e))

-- | Whether any node satisfies the predicate.
pub fn expr_any(p, e) =
  if p(e) then
    true
  else
    any(\(c) -> expr_any(p, c), expr_children(e))

-- | Left-fold the accumulator through every node, root first.
pub fn expr_fold(f, acc, e) =
  foldl(\(a, c) -> expr_fold(f, a, c), f(acc, e), expr_children(e))

modules.doc:
Arena: allocation as an algebraic effect.

On the dynamic axis, allocation is an ordinary effect a handler interprets. `with_arena(body)` installs a handler that services each eligible allocation out of a region owned by that activation: cells are carved from a bump pointer, are inert to reference counting while the region lives, and the whole region is reclaimed in one step when the handler returns. A value that escapes through the result is deep-promoted into ordinary reference-counted cells at the boundary, so escape costs a copy, never soundness. A program that installs no `Alloc` handler allocates exactly as before.

The `alloc` operation is compiler-internal: the arena-lowering pass rewrites a constructor built under a `with_arena` scope into a performed `alloc` (a raw cell) plus an in-place initialization, so `body` never spells `alloc` itself. This handler discharges each `alloc(n)` into `prim_arena_bump(n)`, the region bump entry point. An arena constructor is observably identical to a plain one; only where its words come from differs, which the determinism contract requires to be unobservable. `alloc` is `once`: a bump region assumes single-shot use, so it resumes at most once across the boundary.
modules.source:
-- | Arena: allocation as an algebraic effect.
--
-- On the dynamic axis, allocation is an ordinary effect a handler interprets.
-- `with_arena(body)` installs a handler that services each eligible allocation
-- out of a region owned by that activation: cells are carved from a bump
-- pointer, are inert to reference counting while the region lives, and the
-- whole region is reclaimed in one step when the handler returns. A value that
-- escapes through the result is deep-promoted into ordinary reference-counted
-- cells at the boundary, so escape costs a copy, never soundness. A program
-- that installs no `Alloc` handler allocates exactly as before.
--
-- The `alloc` operation is compiler-internal: the arena-lowering pass rewrites a
-- constructor built under a `with_arena` scope into a performed `alloc` (a raw
-- cell) plus an in-place initialization, so `body` never spells `alloc` itself.
-- This handler discharges each `alloc(n)` into `prim_arena_bump(n)`, the region
-- bump entry point. An arena constructor is observably identical to a plain
-- one; only where its words come from differs, which the determinism contract
-- requires to be unobservable.
-- `alloc` is `once`: a bump region assumes single-shot use, so it resumes at
-- most once across the boundary.

-- | The allocation effect. `alloc(n)` requests a raw `n`-word cell; a handler
-- decides where those words come from. Graded `once`: single-shot resumption
-- only, which is what a scratch region wants.
pub effect Alloc
  once alloc(Int) : Cell

-- | An opaque handle to a raw cell handed out by an allocator. It carries no
-- observable payload; the arena-lowering pass writes a constructor into it, and
-- user code never inspects it. The vestigial field keeps the type nominal.
pub type Cell = Cell(Int)

-- | Run `body`, servicing each eligible allocation out of this activation's
-- region and reclaiming the whole region when the handler returns. Anything the
-- result keeps is promoted to ordinary reference-counted cells at the boundary.
-- A `body` that allocates nothing runs unchanged, and code that never calls
-- `with_arena` allocates exactly as before.
--
-- ```prism
-- with_arena(\() -> [1, 2, 3])
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [1, 2, 3]
-- ```
pub fn with_arena(body : () -> a ! {Alloc}) : a =
  handle body() with
    once alloc(n) => prim_arena_bump(n)
    return r => r

modules.doc:
Range copy over the sequence types a real primitive can back.

One `blit` factored across the sequence-like types, instead of a separate copy routine per type. `blit(src, src_off, len, dst, dst_off)` returns a destination whose `len` elements starting at `dst_off` are the `len` elements of `src` starting at `src_off`, with the rest of `dst` unchanged. As with `memcpy`, the ranges `[src_off, src_off + len)` and `[dst_off, dst_off + len)` are expected to lie within the two sequences.

Instanced only where a real primitive backs the copy: `String` over the `substring` slice primitive, `Array` over the in-place `array_get` and `array_set` primitives, and `Bytes` over the byte buffer's in-place `buf_set`, so a uniquely owned array or buffer destination is overwritten without a fresh allocation. Plain lists stay uninstanced on purpose: a cons list has no random access or bulk copy, so a blit would be a structural walk that rebuilds the prefix rather than a copy.
modules.source:
-- | Range copy over the sequence types a real primitive can back.
--
-- One `blit` factored across the sequence-like types, instead of a separate copy
-- routine per type. `blit(src, src_off, len, dst, dst_off)` returns a
-- destination whose `len` elements starting at `dst_off` are the `len` elements
-- of `src` starting at `src_off`, with the rest of `dst` unchanged. As with
-- `memcpy`, the ranges `[src_off, src_off + len)` and `[dst_off, dst_off + len)`
-- are expected to lie within the two sequences.
--
-- Instanced only where a real primitive backs the copy: `String` over the
-- `substring` slice primitive, `Array` over the in-place `array_get` and
-- `array_set` primitives, and `Bytes` over the byte buffer's in-place `buf_set`,
-- so a uniquely owned array or buffer destination is overwritten without a fresh
-- allocation. Plain lists stay uninstanced on purpose: a cons list has no random
-- access or bulk copy, so a blit would be a structural walk that rebuilds the
-- prefix rather than a copy.

-- The `Bytes` instance below copies over the raw byte buffer; the type and its
-- representation seam (`bytes_of_buf`/`bytes_buf`/`bytes_at`) live in `Wire`.
import Wire (Bytes, bytes_of_buf, bytes_buf, bytes_at)

-- | Overwrite `dst[dst_off .. dst_off + len)` with `src[src_off .. src_off + len)`
-- and return the updated destination.
--
-- ```prism
-- blit("XY", 0, 2, "abcd", 1)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- aXYd
-- ```
pub class Blit(s)
  blit : (s, Int, Int, s, Int) -> s

-- | Splice the source range over the destination range with the string slice
-- primitive: the untouched prefix and suffix of `dst` are sliced out and
-- rejoined around the copied middle.
instance blitString : Blit(String)
  fn blit(src, src_off, len, dst, dst_off) =
    blit_string(src, src_off, len, dst, dst_off)

fn blit_string(
  src : String,
  src_off : Int,
  len : Int,
  dst : String,
  dst_off : Int
) : String =
  concat(
      substring(dst, 0, dst_off),
      concat(
          substring(src, src_off, len),
          substring(dst, dst_off + len, str_len(dst) - (dst_off + len)),
        ),
    )

-- | Overwrite `dst[dst_off + i]` with `src[src_off + i]` for each `i` in
-- `0 .. len` via `array_set`, which writes in place when `dst` is uniquely owned
-- and copies otherwise, so the observable result never depends on ownership.
instance blitArray : Blit(Array(a))
  fn blit(src, src_off, len, dst, dst_off) =
    blit_array_go(src, src_off, len, dst, dst_off, 0)

fn blit_array_go(
  src : Array(a),
  src_off : Int,
  len : Int,
  dst : Array(a),
  dst_off : Int,
  i : Int
) : Array(a) =
  if i >= len then
    dst
  else
    blit_array_go(
        src,
        src_off,
        len,
        array_set(dst, dst_off + i, array_get(src, src_off + i)),
        dst_off,
        i + 1,
      )

-- | Overwrite `dst[dst_off + i]` with `src[src_off + i]` for each `i` in
-- `0 .. len` via the buffer's `buf_set`, which writes in place when the
-- destination buffer is uniquely owned and copies otherwise, so the observable
-- result never depends on ownership.
instance blitBytes : Blit(Bytes)
  fn blit(src, src_off, len, dst, dst_off) =
    bytes_of_buf(blit_bytes_go(bytes_buf(dst), src, src_off, len, dst_off, 0))

fn blit_bytes_go(
  dst : Buf,
  src : Bytes,
  src_off : Int,
  len : Int,
  dst_off : Int,
  i : Int
) : Buf =
  if i >= len then
    dst
  else
    blit_bytes_go(
        buf_set(dst, dst_off + i, bytes_at(src, src_off + i)),
        src,
        src_off,
        len,
        dst_off,
        i + 1,
      )

CLI: an applicative command-line parser as a first-class value.

A parser is a pure value describing what a command accepts: typed options (long/short, valued or switch, with defaults), typed positionals, and named subcommands. Parsers compose applicatively (`build2`/`build3`/`build4` over `map_p`/`ap_p`/`pure_p`) into the user's own result type, so a well-typed parser yields _exactly_ that type or a rich error, never a half-filled record. The illegal state (a config with a missing required field, a subcommand without its arguments) is unrepresentable: the constructor cannot be applied until every part has parsed.

One description, three artifacts: the same `Command` value drives all three. It is the parser (`run_argv`), turning argv into the result type or an error. It is the help text (`help_text`), rendered from the option and argument specs the parser carries, so `--help` can never drift from what parses. And it is the errors (inside `run_argv`), which name the offending token, state the form expected, and print the usage line derived from those same specs.

Everything here is pure: a `Parser` reads a `Tokens` structure, and `Tokens` comes from lexing a `List(String)`. The tie to the real command line is `run_args`, which feeds `args()` (the `Env` capability) to `run_argv`. Because argv arrives through that capability, a recorded run replays its arguments from the `.replay` trace like any other observation: CLI parsing is inside the determinism contract, argv and all.
modules.source:
-- | CLI: an applicative command-line parser as a first-class value.
--
-- A parser is a pure value describing what a command accepts: typed options
-- (long/short, valued or switch, with defaults), typed positionals, and named
-- subcommands. Parsers compose applicatively (`build2`/`build3`/`build4` over
-- `map_p`/`ap_p`/`pure_p`) into the user's own result type, so a well-typed
-- parser yields _exactly_ that type or a rich error, never a half-filled record.
-- The illegal state (a config with a missing required field, a subcommand
-- without its arguments) is unrepresentable: the constructor cannot be applied
-- until every part has parsed.
--
-- One description, three artifacts: the same `Command` value drives all three.
-- It is the parser (`run_argv`), turning argv into the result type or an error.
-- It is the help text (`help_text`), rendered from the option and argument specs
-- the parser carries, so `--help` can never drift from what parses. And it is the
-- errors (inside `run_argv`), which name the offending token, state the form
-- expected, and print the usage line derived from those same specs.
--
-- Everything here is pure: a `Parser` reads a `Tokens` structure, and `Tokens`
-- comes from lexing a `List(String)`. The tie to the real command line is
-- `run_args`, which feeds `args()` (the `Env` capability) to `run_argv`. Because
-- argv arrives through that capability, a recorded run replays its arguments from
-- the `.replay` trace like any other observation: CLI parsing is inside the
-- determinism contract, argv and all.

import Data.List (map, filter, foldl, foldr, append, reverse, nth)

import Data.Maybe (..)

import Data.Result (..)

import Data.String (starts_with, str_join, pad_right, index_of, contains)

import Data.Char (is_digit)

-- ASCII byte of `-`, the flag sigil.
pub let dash : Int = 45

-- Column the help text aligns descriptions to.
pub let help_col : Int = 24

-- | A parse failure, carrying enough to name the offending token and the form
-- expected. Rendered to a message by `describe`.
pub type CliError
  = MissingFlag(String)
  | MissingArg(String)
  | UnexpectedArg(String)
  | NeedsValue(String)
  | BadValue(String, String)
  | UnknownFlag(String)
  | UnknownCommand(String)

-- | The static description of one option, carried by the parser for help and to
-- tell the lexer whether the flag consumes a following value.
pub type OptSpec = OptSpec {
  long: String,
  short: String,
  meta: String,
  help: String,
  takes_value: Bool
}

-- | The static description of one positional argument.
pub type ArgSpec = ArgSpec { meta: String, help: String, required: Bool }

-- | argv after lexing: options canonicalized to their long name, and the
-- positionals in order. `--help`/`-h` are handled before lexing (`has_help`), so
-- they never appear here.
pub type Tokens = Tokens { opts: List((String, String)), pos: List(String) }

-- | A parser for a value of type `a`: the option and positional specs it accepts
-- (the description help is rendered from) and a pure reader over lexed tokens
-- threading the positional cursor. Build these with the combinators below, never
-- by hand.
pub type Parser(a) = Parser {
  opts: List(OptSpec),
  args: List(ArgSpec),
  run: (Tokens, Int) -> Result((a, Int), CliError)
}

-- | One named subcommand: its key on the command line, a one-line description,
-- and the parser that runs when it is chosen.
pub type SubCmd(a) = SubCmd { key: String, about: String, sub: Parser(a) }

-- | A top-level command is either a single parser or a group of subcommands, all
-- producing the same result type (so distinct subcommands map to distinct
-- constructors of the user's ADT).
pub type Body(a) = Plain(Parser(a)) | Group(List(SubCmd(a)))

-- | A complete command: a program name and one-line description for usage, plus
-- its body.
pub type Command(a) = Command { name: String, about: String, body: Body(a) }

-- | The outcome of parsing argv: a value, a help request (carrying the rendered
-- text), or a usage error (carrying the rendered message).
pub type Outcome(a) = Parsed(a) | ShowHelp(String) | BadUsage(String)

-- Combinators -----------------------------------------------------------------

-- | A parser that consumes nothing and yields `x`. The applicative unit.
pub fn pure_p(x) = Parser { opts = Nil, args = Nil, run = \(_t, i) -> Ok((x, i)) }

-- | Map `f` over a parser's result, leaving what it consumes unchanged.
pub fn map_p(f, p : Parser(b)) =
  Parser { opts = p.opts, args = p.args, run = \(t, i) -> run_map(f, p, t, i) }

fn run_map(f, p : Parser(b), t : Tokens, i : Int) =
  match (p.run)(t, i) of
    Ok((a, j)) => Ok((f(a), j))
    Err(e) => Err(e)

-- | Applicative application: run `pf` then `px`, threading the positional cursor
-- left to right, and apply the function to the argument. This is what lets a
-- curried constructor be filled field by field.
pub fn ap_p(pf : Parser((b) -> c), px : Parser(b)) =
  Parser {
    opts = append(pf.opts, px.opts),
    args = append(pf.args, px.args),
    run = \(t, i) -> run_ap(pf, px, t, i)
  }

fn run_ap(pf : Parser((b) -> c), px : Parser(b), t : Tokens, i : Int) =
  match (pf.run)(t, i) of
    Err(e) => Err(e)
    Ok((g, j)) =>
      match (px.run)(t, j) of
        Err(e) => Err(e)
        Ok((b, k)) => Ok((g(b), k))

-- | Apply a two-argument curried constructor to two parsers.
pub fn build2(f, pa, pb) = ap_p(map_p(f, pa), pb)

-- | Apply a three-argument curried constructor to three parsers.
pub fn build3(f, pa, pb, pc) = ap_p(build2(f, pa, pb), pc)

-- | Apply a four-argument curried constructor to four parsers.
pub fn build4(f, pa, pb, pc, pd) = ap_p(build3(f, pa, pb, pc), pd)

-- Leaf parsers ----------------------------------------------------------------

fn mk_opt(long, short, meta, help, takes_value) =
  OptSpec {
    long = long,
    short = short,
    meta = meta,
    help = help,
    takes_value = takes_value
  }

-- | An optional string flag with a default when absent.
pub fn opt_str(long, short, meta, help, default) =
  Parser {
    opts = [mk_opt(long, short, meta, help, true)],
    args = Nil,
    run = \(t, i) -> read_opt_str(long, default, t, i)
  }

-- | A required string flag: an error when absent.
pub fn req_str(long, short, meta, help) =
  Parser {
    opts = [mk_opt(long, short, meta, help, true)],
    args = Nil,
    run = \(t, i) -> read_req_str(long, t, i)
  }

-- | An optional integer flag with a default; a non-integer value is an error.
pub fn opt_int(long, short, meta, help, default) =
  Parser {
    opts = [mk_opt(long, short, meta, help, true)],
    args = Nil,
    run = \(t, i) -> read_opt_int(long, default, meta, t, i)
  }

-- | A boolean switch: true when present, false when absent, never valued.
pub fn switch(long, short, help) =
  Parser {
    opts = [mk_opt(long, short, "", help, false)],
    args = Nil,
    run = \(t, i) -> read_switch(long, t, i)
  }

-- | A required string positional, consumed in declaration order.
pub fn arg_str(meta, help) =
  Parser {
    opts = Nil,
    args = [ArgSpec { meta = meta, help = help, required = true }],
    run = \(t, i) -> read_arg_str(meta, t, i)
  }

-- | An optional string positional, consumed in declaration order and yielding
-- `default` when absent. Help renders it as `[<META>]`.
pub fn arg_str_default(meta, help, default) =
  Parser {
    opts = Nil,
    args = [ArgSpec { meta = meta, help = help, required = false }],
    run = \(t, i) -> read_arg_str_default(default, t, i)
  }

-- | A required integer positional; a non-integer token is an error.
pub fn arg_int(meta, help) =
  Parser {
    opts = Nil,
    args = [ArgSpec { meta = meta, help = help, required = true }],
    run = \(t, i) -> read_arg_int(meta, t, i)
  }

fn lookup_opt(name, opts) =
  match opts of
    Nil => None
    Cons((k, v), rest) =>
      if str_eq(k, name) then
        Some(v)
      else
        lookup_opt(name, rest)

fn read_opt_str(long, default, t : Tokens, i) =
  match lookup_opt(long, t.opts) of
    Some(v) => Ok((v, i))
    None => Ok((default, i))

fn read_req_str(long, t : Tokens, i) =
  match lookup_opt(long, t.opts) of
    Some(v) => Ok((v, i))
    None => Err(MissingFlag(long))

fn read_opt_int(long, default, meta, t : Tokens, i) =
  match lookup_opt(long, t.opts) of
    None => Ok((default, i))
    Some(v) =>
      match parse_int(v) of
        Some(n) => Ok((n, i))
        None => Err(BadValue(v, meta))

fn read_switch(long, t : Tokens, i) =
  match lookup_opt(long, t.opts) of
    Some(_) => Ok((true, i))
    None => Ok((false, i))

fn read_arg_str(meta, t : Tokens, i) =
  match nth(i, t.pos) of
    Some(v) => Ok((v, i + 1))
    None => Err(MissingArg(meta))

fn read_arg_str_default(default, t : Tokens, i) =
  match nth(i, t.pos) of
    Some(v) => Ok((v, i + 1))
    None => Ok((default, i))

fn read_arg_int(meta, t : Tokens, i) =
  match nth(i, t.pos) of
    None => Err(MissingArg(meta))
    Some(v) =>
      match parse_int(v) of
        Some(n) => Ok((n, i + 1))
        None => Err(BadValue(v, meta))

-- Lexing ----------------------------------------------------------------------

fn is_help_tok(tok) = str_eq(tok, "--help") || str_eq(tok, "-h")

fn is_long_flag(tok) = starts_with("--", tok) && str_len(tok) > 2

fn is_short_flag(tok) =
  str_len(tok) >= 2
    && char_at(tok, 0) == dash
    && char_at(tok, 1) /= dash
    && not(is_digit(char_at(tok, 1)))

fn find_long(specs : List(OptSpec), name) =
  match specs of
    Nil => None
    Cons(s, rest) =>
      if str_eq(s.long, name) then
        Some(s)
      else
        find_long(rest, name)

fn find_short(specs : List(OptSpec), name) =
  match specs of
    Nil => None
    Cons(s, rest) =>
      if str_eq(s.short, name) then
        Some(s)
      else
        find_short(rest, name)

-- | Lex argv against the option specs (which say whether each flag takes a
-- value). Options are canonicalized to their long name; anything not a flag is a
-- positional. `--help`/`-h` are skipped here (detected earlier by `has_help`).
pub fn lex(specs, argv) = lex_go(specs, argv, Nil, Nil)

fn lex_go(specs, argv, opts_acc, pos_acc) =
  match argv of
    Nil => Ok(Tokens { opts = reverse(opts_acc), pos = reverse(pos_acc) })
    Cons(tok, rest) =>
      if is_help_tok(tok) then
        lex_go(specs, rest, opts_acc, pos_acc)
      elif is_long_flag(tok) then
        lex_long(specs, tok, rest, opts_acc, pos_acc)
      elif is_short_flag(tok) then
        lex_short(specs, tok, rest, opts_acc, pos_acc)
      else
        lex_go(specs, rest, opts_acc, Cons(tok, pos_acc))

fn lex_long(specs, tok, rest, opts_acc, pos_acc) =
  let name = substring(tok, 2, str_len(tok) - 2)
  if contains("=", name) then
    lex_eq(specs, name, rest, opts_acc, pos_acc)
  else
    match find_long(specs, name) of
      None => Err(UnknownFlag(tok))
      Some(spec) =>
        if spec.takes_value then
          lex_valued(specs, name, rest, opts_acc, pos_acc, tok)
        else
          lex_go(specs, rest, Cons((name, "true"), opts_acc), pos_acc)

fn lex_eq(specs, name, rest, opts_acc, pos_acc) =
  let eq = index_of("=", name)
  let k = substring(name, 0, eq)
  let v = substring(name, eq + 1, str_len(name) - eq - 1)
  match find_long(specs, k) of
    None => Err(UnknownFlag(concat("--", k)))
    Some(spec) =>
      if spec.takes_value then
        lex_go(specs, rest, Cons((k, v), opts_acc), pos_acc)
      else
        Err(UnknownFlag(concat("--", k)))

fn lex_valued(specs, name, rest, opts_acc, pos_acc, tok) =
  match rest of
    Nil => Err(NeedsValue(tok))
    Cons(v, rest2) => lex_go(specs, rest2, Cons((name, v), opts_acc), pos_acc)

fn lex_short(specs, tok, rest, opts_acc, pos_acc) =
  let name = substring(tok, 1, str_len(tok) - 1)
  match find_short(specs, name) of
    None => Err(UnknownFlag(tok))
    Some(spec) =>
      if spec.takes_value then
        lex_valued(specs, spec.long, rest, opts_acc, pos_acc, tok)
      else
        lex_go(specs, rest, Cons((spec.long, "true"), opts_acc), pos_acc)

-- Running ---------------------------------------------------------------------

fn run_leaf(p : Parser(a), argv) =
  match lex(p.opts, argv) of
    Err(e) => Err(e)
    Ok(toks) => finish_leaf(p, toks)

fn finish_leaf(p : Parser(a), toks) =
  match (p.run)(toks, 0) of
    Ok((a, i)) =>
      match nth(i, toks.pos) of
        None => Ok(a)
        Some(value) => Err(UnexpectedArg(value))
    Err(e) => Err(e)

fn find_sub(subs : List(SubCmd(a)), key) =
  match subs of
    Nil => None
    Cons(sc, rest) =>
      if str_eq(sc.key, key) then
        Some(sc)
      else
        find_sub(rest, key)

-- | Parse argv against a command, yielding a value, a help request, or a usage
-- error. argv is the argument list only (no program name); `cmd.name` supplies
-- the name for usage text.
--
-- ```prism
-- # let p = build2(\(host) -> \(port) -> (host, port), req_str("host", "H", "HOST", "server host"), opt_int("port", "p", "N", "listen port", 8080))
-- # let cmd = Command { name = "serve", about = "run the server", body = Plain(p) }
-- run_argv(cmd, ["--host", "example.com"])
-- ```
-- ```output
-- Cli.Parsed((example.com, 8080))
-- ```
pub fn run_argv(cmd : Command(a), argv) =
  match cmd.body of
    Plain(p) => run_plain(cmd, p, argv)
    Group(subs) => run_group(cmd, subs, argv)

fn run_plain(cmd : Command(a), p : Parser(a), argv) =
  if has_help(argv) then
    ShowHelp(plain_help(cmd, p))
  else
    match run_leaf(p, argv) of
      Ok(a) => Parsed(a)
      Err(e) => BadUsage(err_with_usage(synopsis(cmd, p), e))

fn run_group(cmd : Command(a), subs : List(SubCmd(a)), argv) =
  match argv of
    Nil => ShowHelp(group_help(cmd, subs))
    Cons(key, rest) =>
      if is_help_tok(key) then
        ShowHelp(group_help(cmd, subs))
      else
        dispatch(cmd, subs, key, rest)

fn dispatch(cmd : Command(a), subs : List(SubCmd(a)), key, rest) =
  match find_sub(subs, key) of
    None => BadUsage(err_with_usage(group_usage(cmd), UnknownCommand(key)))
    Some(sc) => run_sub(cmd, sc, rest)

fn run_sub(cmd : Command(a), sc : SubCmd(a), rest) =
  if has_help(rest) then
    ShowHelp(sub_help(cmd, sc))
  else
    match run_leaf(sc.sub, rest) of
      Ok(a) => Parsed(a)
      Err(e) => BadUsage(err_with_usage(sub_usage(cmd, sc), e))

fn has_help(argv) =
  match argv of
    Nil => false
    Cons(t, rest) =>
      if is_help_tok(t) then
        true
      else
        has_help(rest)

-- | The rendered help for a command: dispatches to the plain or group form.
--
-- ```prism
-- # let p = build2(\(host) -> \(port) -> (host, port), req_str("host", "H", "HOST", "server host"), opt_int("port", "p", "N", "listen port", 8080))
-- # let cmd = Command { name = "serve", about = "run the server", body = Plain(p) }
-- print(help_text(cmd))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- Usage: serve [--host HOST] [--port N] [--help]
--
-- run the server
--
-- Options:
--   -H, --host HOST       server host
--   -p, --port N          listen port
--   -h, --help            show this help and exit
-- ```
pub fn help_text(cmd : Command(a)) =
  match cmd.body of
    Plain(p) => plain_help(cmd, p)
    Group(subs) => group_help(cmd, subs)

-- Help and usage rendering ----------------------------------------------------

fn opt_synopsis(s : OptSpec) =
  if s.takes_value then
    concat_all(["[--", s.long, " ", s.meta, "]"])
  else
    concat_all(["[--", s.long, "]"])

fn arg_synopsis(ar : ArgSpec) =
  let body = concat_all(["<", ar.meta, ">"])
  if ar.required then
    body
  else
    concat_all(["[", body, "]"])

fn synopsis(cmd : Command(a), p : Parser(a)) =
  let opts = map(opt_synopsis, p.opts)
  let args = map(arg_synopsis, p.args)
  let parts = append(opts, append(args, ["[--help]"]))
  concat_all(["Usage: ", cmd.name, " ", str_join(" ", parts)])

fn group_usage(cmd : Command(a)) =
  concat_all(["Usage: ", cmd.name, " <command> [args]"])

fn sub_usage(cmd : Command(a), sc : SubCmd(a)) =
  let name = concat_all([cmd.name, " ", sc.key])
  synopsis(
      Command { name = name, about = sc.about, body = Plain(sc.sub) },
      sc.sub,
    )

fn opt_flags(s : OptSpec) =
  if str_eq(s.short, "") then
    concat_all(["      --", s.long])
  else
    concat_all(["  -", s.short, ", --", s.long])

fn opt_line(s : OptSpec) =
  let lhs =
    if s.takes_value then
      concat_all([opt_flags(s), " ", s.meta])
    else
      opt_flags(s)
  concat_all([pad_right(lhs, help_col), s.help])

fn arg_line(ar : ArgSpec) =
  concat_all(["  ", pad_right(ar.meta, help_col - 2), ar.help])

fn cmd_line(sc : SubCmd(a)) =
  concat_all(["  ", pad_right(sc.key, help_col - 2), sc.about])

-- The implicit `--help` option, rendered through the same `opt_line` as every
-- real option so its column lines up.
let help_spec : OptSpec =
  OptSpec {
    long = "help",
    short = "h",
    meta = "",
    help = "show this help and exit",
    takes_value = false
  }

-- The "Arguments:" section, or no lines at all when there are no positionals.
fn arg_section(specs : List(ArgSpec)) : List(String) =
  match specs of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(_, _) => Cons("", Cons("Arguments:", map(arg_line, specs)))

fn plain_help(cmd : Command(a), p : Parser(a)) =
  let header = [synopsis(cmd, p), "", cmd.about]
  let opt_sec = Cons("", Cons("Options:", append(map(opt_line, p.opts), [
      opt_line(help_spec),
    ])))
  str_join("\n", append(header, append(arg_section(p.args), opt_sec)))

fn group_help(cmd : Command(a), subs : List(SubCmd(a))) =
  let header = [group_usage(cmd), "", cmd.about, "", "Commands:"]
  let footer =
    ["", concat_all(["Run '", cmd.name, " <command> --help' for details."])]
  str_join("\n", append(header, append(map(cmd_line, subs), footer)))

fn sub_help(cmd : Command(a), sc : SubCmd(a)) =
  let name = concat_all([cmd.name, " ", sc.key])
  plain_help(
      Command { name = name, about = sc.about, body = Plain(sc.sub) },
      sc.sub,
    )

-- | A one-line description of a parse error, naming the offending token and the
-- form expected.
--
-- ```prism
-- describe(MissingFlag("host"))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- error: required flag '--host' was not provided
-- ```
pub fn describe(err) =
  match err of
    MissingFlag(f) =>
      concat_all(["error: required flag '--", f, "' was not provided"])
    MissingArg(m) => concat_all(["error: missing argument <", m, ">"])
    UnexpectedArg(value) =>
      concat_all(["error: unexpected argument '", value, "'"])
    NeedsValue(f) => concat_all(["error: flag '", f, "' expects a value"])
    BadValue(tok, exp) =>
      concat_all(["error: '", tok, "' is not a valid <", exp, ">"])
    UnknownFlag(f) => concat_all(["error: unknown flag '", f, "'"])
    UnknownCommand(c) => concat_all(["error: unknown command '", c, "'"])

fn err_with_usage(usage, err) = str_join("\n", [describe(err), "", usage])

-- The real command line -------------------------------------------------------

-- | Parse the process arguments against `cmd`. argv arrives through the `Env`
-- capability (`args`), so a recorded run replays its arguments from the trace:
-- CLI parsing is inside the determinism contract.
pub fn run_args(cmd) = run_argv(cmd, args())

modules.doc:
Cooperative async/await concurrency as a single handler, polymorphic in the effects the fibers perform.

`fork` spawns a fiber and returns a `Fiber` handle, `yield` reschedules, `await` blocks on a fiber's result, and `cancel` requests a cooperative cancellation. `channel`, `send`, and `recv` are a buffered FIFO channel for fiber-to-fiber messages. A fiber may perform any effect row `e` in addition to `Async`; `e` is a row-kinded parameter of the reified command type, so one run queue holds every fiber without existential types. Because a fiber's effects tie to the ambient row at `fork`, they flow out through `run_async`: `run_async : (() -> a ! {Async(a) | e}) -> a ! {e}`, so a fiber that performs `E` makes the whole run demand a handler for `E`. Nothing is smuggled past the scheduler.

Prism has no shared mutable cell, so the handler only REIFIES each step as a `Cmd`, and a pure `drive` loop threads the run queue, the finished results, the parked awaiters, and the channel buffers. Those parked continuations escape into the scheduler state, so a program using this is whole-program free-monad; it runs in constant native stack under PRISM_TRAMPOLINE.

Cancellation is a cooperative unwind, not a drop. `cancel(f)` marks `f` and all its descendants; each is stopped at its next suspension point (`yield`, `await`, `send`, `recv`), never mid-step, and unwinds through its `never` finalizers so every resource is released exactly once. Wrap a resource with `on_cancel(cleanup, body)` to run `cleanup` on that unwind. A cancelled fiber's awaiters observe it through `try_await` (which yields `Was_Cancelled` rather than hanging). An unhandled failure in any fiber aborts the cooperative run: every other live fiber and descendant is cancelled, runnable cleanups drain, and the failure re-emerges from `run_async`/`run_lifo`.

`scope` is a structured join: it forks a list of fibers and awaits them all on successful runs. It is not a failure-isolation boundary; the scheduler-global abort rule also cancels live fibers created outside the `scope`.

A channel carries the shared result type `a`; fibers in one run share `a` (use a sum type for mixed messages or results).
modules.source:
-- | Cooperative async/await concurrency as a single handler, polymorphic in the
-- effects the fibers perform.
--
-- `fork` spawns a fiber and returns a `Fiber` handle, `yield` reschedules,
-- `await` blocks on a fiber's result, and `cancel` requests a cooperative
-- cancellation. `channel`, `send`, and `recv` are a buffered FIFO channel for
-- fiber-to-fiber messages. A fiber may perform any effect row `e` in addition to
-- `Async`; `e` is a row-kinded parameter of the reified command type, so one run
-- queue holds every fiber without existential types. Because a fiber's effects
-- tie to the ambient row at `fork`, they flow out through `run_async`:
-- `run_async : (() -> a ! {Async(a) | e}) -> a ! {e}`, so a fiber that performs
-- `E` makes the whole run demand a handler for `E`. Nothing is smuggled past the
-- scheduler.
--
-- Prism has no shared mutable cell, so the handler only REIFIES each step as a
-- `Cmd`, and a pure `drive` loop threads the run queue, the finished results, the
-- parked awaiters, and the channel buffers. Those parked continuations escape
-- into the scheduler state, so a program using this is whole-program free-monad;
-- it runs in constant native stack under PRISM_TRAMPOLINE.
--
-- Cancellation is a cooperative unwind, not a drop. `cancel(f)` marks `f` and all
-- its descendants; each is stopped at its next suspension point (`yield`,
-- `await`, `send`, `recv`), never mid-step, and unwinds through its `never`
-- finalizers so every resource is released exactly once. Wrap a resource with
-- `on_cancel(cleanup, body)` to run `cleanup` on that unwind. A cancelled fiber's
-- awaiters observe it through `try_await` (which yields `Was_Cancelled` rather
-- than hanging). An unhandled failure in any fiber aborts the cooperative run:
-- every other live fiber and descendant is cancelled, runnable cleanups drain,
-- and the failure re-emerges from `run_async`/`run_lifo`.
--
-- `scope` is a structured join: it forks a list of fibers and awaits them all on
-- successful runs. It is not a failure-isolation boundary; the scheduler-global
-- abort rule also cancels live fibers created outside the `scope`.
--
-- A channel carries the shared result type `a`; fibers in one run share `a`
-- (use a sum type for mixed messages or results).

import Data.List (append)

-- | The async/await effect. `fork` spawns a fiber and returns its handle,
-- `yield` reschedules, `await` blocks on a fiber's result, and `cancel` requests
-- a cooperative cancellation; `channel`/`send`/`recv` are a buffered FIFO channel
-- for fiber-to-fiber messages. Discharge it with `run_async`.
--
-- The public `yield`/`await`/`send`/`recv` are thin wrappers (below) over the raw
-- `poll_*` operations, which return a cancellation `Signal`/`Wake` the wrapper
-- turns into a cooperative `kill`. `kill` and `vanished` never resume (per-site
-- bottom return `b`); `run_async` absorbs the whole effect, so none of the cancel
-- machinery surfaces in a fiber's row.
pub effect Async(a)
  fork(() -> a ! {Async(a) | e}) : Fiber
  poll_yield() : Signal
  poll_await(Fiber) : Wake(a)
  cancel(Fiber) : Unit
  channel() : Chan
  bounded(Int) : Chan
  poll_send(Chan, a) : Signal
  poll_recv(Chan) : Wake(a)
  never kill() : b
  never vanished() : b

-- | A handle to a spawned fiber, returned by `fork` and passed to `await`/`cancel`.
pub type Fiber = Fiber(Int)

-- | A handle to a buffered FIFO channel, opened with `channel`.
pub type Chan = Chan(Int)

-- The scheduler's answer to a `poll_yield`/`poll_send`: `Go` resumes normally,
-- `Stop` means this fiber has been cancelled and must unwind now.
type Signal = Go | Stop

-- The scheduler's answer to a `poll_await`/`poll_recv`: `Arrived` carries the
-- awaited value, `Gone` means the awaited fiber was cancelled, and `Halt` means
-- this (waiting) fiber has itself been cancelled and must unwind.
type Wake(a) = Arrived(a) | Gone | Halt

-- | The outcome of `try_await`: a fiber that completed with a value, or one that
-- was cancelled before it could.
pub type Outcome(a) = Completed(a) | Was_Cancelled

-- | Reschedule the current fiber. A cooperative yield point; also a cancellation
-- point (a cancelled fiber unwinds here instead of resuming).
pub fn yield() : Unit ! {Async(a)} =
  match poll_yield() of
    Go => ()
    Stop => kill()

-- | Block until fiber `f` finishes, returning its result. If `f` was cancelled,
-- this raises the in-scheduler `vanished` signal (observe it with `try_await`);
-- if the waiting fiber is itself cancelled, it unwinds here.
pub fn await(f : Fiber) : a ! {Async(a)} =
  match poll_await(f) of
    Arrived(v) => v
    Gone => vanished()
    Halt => kill()

-- | Send `v` on channel `c`. On a bounded channel a full buffer parks the sender
-- until a receiver drains it; a cancellation delivered while parked unwinds here.
pub fn send(c : Chan, v : a) : Unit ! {Async(a)} =
  match poll_send(c, v) of
    Go => ()
    Stop => kill()

-- | Receive a value from channel `c`, parking until one is available. A
-- cancellation delivered while parked unwinds here.
--
-- ```prism
-- fn producer(c : Chan) : Int ! {Async(Int)} =
--   send(c, 7)
--   0
--
-- fn scene() : Int ! {Async(Int)} =
--   let c = channel()
--   let f = fork(\() -> producer(c))
--   let v = recv(c)
--   await(f)
--   v
--
-- fn main() = println(run_async(scene))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 7
-- ```
pub fn recv(c : Chan) : a ! {Async(a)} =
  match poll_recv(c) of
    Arrived(v) => v
    Gone => kill()
    Halt => kill()

-- | Run `body`, and if it is cancelled (unwinds through `kill`), run `cleanup`
-- once before the cancellation propagates outward. This is a forwarding handler:
-- every `Async` operation `body` performs is relayed unchanged to the enclosing
-- `run_async`, so the finalizer is transparent except on the cancel path. A
-- normally returning body does not run `cleanup`. Nest these for stacked
-- resources; cancellation runs each installed cleanup exactly once, innermost
-- first. Once an unwind starts, repeated cancellation is masked for that fiber,
-- so a cleanup may suspend and resume normally. A child forked by a cleanup is
-- born cancelled and cannot escape the unwind. If a cleanup itself fails,
-- `try_await` does not manufacture `Was_Cancelled`: the whole scheduler run fails.
-- A cleanup parked with no runnable producer likewise ends in the scheduler's
-- deterministic no-progress failure; a cleanup that keeps producing work may
-- diverge like any other computation.
pub fn on_cancel(
  cleanup : () -> Unit ! {| e},
  body : () -> r ! {Async(a) | e}
) : r =
  handle body() with
    fork(child) resume k => k(fork(child))
    poll_yield() resume k => k(poll_yield())
    poll_await(f) resume k => k(poll_await(f))
    cancel(f) resume k => k(cancel(f))
    channel() resume k => k(channel())
    bounded(n) resume k => k(bounded(n))
    poll_send(c, v) resume k => k(poll_send(c, v))
    poll_recv(c) resume k => k(poll_recv(c))
    never vanished() => vanished()
    never kill() =>
      cleanup()
      kill()
    return r => r

-- | Await fiber `f`, observing cancellation as a value instead of a signal:
-- `Completed(v)` if `f` finished, `Was_Cancelled` if it was cancelled. Never
-- hangs on a cancelled fiber, and does not report `Was_Cancelled` until the
-- target's cancellation unwind (including its `on_cancel` cleanups) has reached
-- the scheduler. A forwarding handler that catches only the `vanished` signal
-- `await` raises for a cancelled target. If that unwind fails or never completes,
-- `try_await` produces no outcome; the enclosing run fails or diverges instead.
pub fn try_await(f : Fiber) : Outcome(a) =
  handle Completed(await(f)) with
    fork(child) resume k => k(fork(child))
    poll_yield() resume k => k(poll_yield())
    poll_await(g) resume k => k(poll_await(g))
    cancel(g) resume k => k(cancel(g))
    channel() resume k => k(channel())
    bounded(n) resume k => k(bounded(n))
    poll_send(c, v) resume k => k(poll_send(c, v))
    poll_recv(c) resume k => k(poll_recv(c))
    never kill() => kill()
    never vanished() => Was_Cancelled
    return r => r

-- One reified step of a fiber, over the fiber effect row `e`. The captured
-- continuation performs `e` when resumed, off the native stack.
type Cmd(a, e : Row)
  = Forked((Fiber) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {e}, () -> a ! {Async(a) | e})
  | Yielded((Signal) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {e})
  | Awaited(Int, (Wake(a)) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {e})
  | Cancelling(Int, (Unit) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {e})
  | Opened((Chan) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {e})
  | OpenedCap(Int, (Chan) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {e})
  | Sent(Int, a, (Signal) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {e})
  | Recving(Int, (Wake(a)) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {e})
  | Died
  | Failed
  | Finished(a)

-- Run a fiber body to its next effect, reifying that effect as a command. The
-- three `never` clauses catch the fiber's terminal control signals when they
-- reach its top: `kill`/`vanished` (a completed cancellation unwind) and an
-- unhandled `fail()` (a fiber failure, which makes the nursery fail-fast).
fn step(body : () -> a ! {Async(a) | e}) : Cmd(a, e) =
  handle body() with
    fork(child) resume k => Forked(k, child)
    poll_yield() resume k => Yielded(k)
    poll_await(f) resume k =>
      match f of
        Fiber(fid) => Awaited(fid, k)
    cancel(f) resume k =>
      match f of
        Fiber(fid) => Cancelling(fid, k)
    channel() resume k => Opened(k)
    bounded(cap) resume k => OpenedCap(cap, k)
    poll_send(c, v) resume k =>
      match c of
        Chan(cid) => Sent(cid, v, k)
    poll_recv(c) resume k =>
      match c of
        Chan(cid) => Recving(cid, k)
    never kill() => Died
    never vanished() => Died
    never fail() => Failed
    return r => Finished(r)

-- A runnable fiber: its id plus two resume thunks. `go` resumes it normally;
-- `stop` delivers its cancellation (drives it into its `kill` unwind). `run_next`
-- picks `stop` exactly when the fiber is in the `cancelled` set, so a cancel that
-- lands while the fiber sits in the run queue is honoured at dequeue time.
type Ready(a, e : Row) = Ready(
  Int,
  () -> Cmd(a, e) ! {e},
  () -> Cmd(a, e) ! {e}
)

-- `enq` is the scheduling policy: it decides where a newly-runnable fiber enters
-- the run queue, and is the ONLY thing that varies between schedulers. FIFO
-- (`run_async`) appends to the back for round-robin fairness; LIFO (`run_lifo`)
-- pushes to the front for depth-first, run-newest-first order. `drive` threads it
-- untouched, so a new policy is another handler over the same `Async` effect with
-- no change to the fibers: swap `enq`, swap the policy.
--
-- `kids` records fork parentage so `cancel` reaches a fiber's descendants.
-- `cancelled` is the deterministic set of fibers asked to stop, `finalizing`
-- records fibers already unwinding (and masks their cleanups from repeated
-- cancellation), and `died` records fibers whose unwind has reached the top.
-- `failed` holds a run-wide abort open while ready cancellation work drains.
-- Keeping request and completion distinct makes `try_await` a join: it cannot
-- report `Was_Cancelled` before the target's finalizers have finished.
type Sched(a, e : Row) = Sched {
  queue: List(Ready(a, e)),
  results: List((Int, a)),
  waiters: List((Int, Int, (Wake(a)) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {e})),
  cancelled: List(Int),
  finalizing: List(Int),
  died: List(Int),
  failed: Bool,
  kids: List((Int, Int)),
  chans: List((Int, List(a))),
  caps: List((Int, Int)),
  recv_waiters: List((Int, Int, (Wake(a)) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {e})),
  senders: List((Int, Int, a, (Signal) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {e})),
  next: Int,
  enq: (List(Ready(a, e)), Ready(a, e)) -> List(Ready(a, e))
}

fn lookup_result(fid : Int, rs : List((Int, a))) : Option(a) =
  match rs of
    Nil => None
    Cons((i, v), r) =>
      if i == fid then
        Some(v)
      else
        lookup_result(fid, r)

fn is_member(fid : Int, xs : List(Int)) : Bool =
  match xs of
    Nil => false
    Cons(x, r) =>
      if x == fid then
        true
      else
        is_member(fid, r)

-- The direct children of `p` recorded in the fork tree.
fn children_of(p : Int, kids : List((Int, Int))) : List(Int) =
  match kids of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons((par, ch), rest) =>
      if par == p then
        Cons(ch, children_of(p, rest))
      else
        children_of(p, rest)

-- `roots` and all their transitive descendants, accumulated into `acc` (a set).
fn descendants(
  roots : List(Int),
  kids : List((Int, Int)),
  acc : List(Int)
) : List(Int) =
  match roots of
    Nil => acc
    Cons(r, rest) =>
      if is_member(r, acc) then
        descendants(rest, kids, acc)
      else
        descendants(append(children_of(r, kids), rest), kids, Cons(r, acc))

-- Add each of `xs` to the set `acc` (idempotent), skipping duplicates.
fn fold_add(xs : List(Int), acc : List(Int)) : List(Int) =
  match xs of
    Nil => acc
    Cons(x, rest) =>
      if is_member(x, acc) then
        fold_add(rest, acc)
      else
        fold_add(rest, Cons(x, acc))

-- Remove every member of `excluded` from `xs`.
fn without(xs : List(Int), excluded : List(Int)) : List(Int) =
  match xs of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(x, rest) =>
      if is_member(x, excluded) then
        without(rest, excluded)
      else
        Cons(x, without(rest, excluded))

-- Move every awaiter of `fid` into the run queue, resumed with `w` (the `go`
-- delivery) or `Halt` (the `stop` delivery), entering the queue by policy `enq`.
fn wake(
  fid : Int,
  w : Wake(a),
  ws : List((Int, Int, (Wake(a)) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e})),
  acc : List(Ready(a, e)),
  enq : (List(Ready(a, e)), Ready(a, e)) -> List(Ready(a, e))
) : (List((Int, Int, (Wake(a)) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e})), List(Ready(a, e))) =
  match ws of
    Nil => (Nil, acc)
    Cons((f, who, k), rest) =>
      if f == fid then
        wake(
            fid,
            w,
            rest,
            enq(acc, Ready(who, \() -> k(w), \() -> k(Halt))),
            enq,
          )
      else
        match wake(fid, w, rest, acc, enq) of
          (kept, out) => (Cons((f, who, k), kept), out)

-- Take the head of channel `cid`'s buffer if any, returning it with the buffers
-- updated; `None` when the channel is empty.
fn chan_take(
  cid : Int,
  chans : List((Int, List(a)))
) : Option((a, List((Int, List(a))))) =
  match chans of
    Nil => None
    Cons((c, buf), rest) =>
      if c == cid then
        match buf of
          Nil => None
          Cons(h, t) => Some((h, Cons((c, t), rest)))
      else
        match chan_take(cid, rest) of
          None => None
          Some((v, kept)) => Some((v, Cons((c, buf), kept)))

-- Append `v` to channel `cid`'s buffer.
fn chan_put(
  cid : Int,
  v : a,
  chans : List((Int, List(a)))
) : List((Int, List(a))) =
  match chans of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons((c, buf), rest) =>
      if c == cid then
        Cons((c, append(buf, [v])), rest)
      else
        Cons((c, buf), chan_put(cid, v, rest))

-- Remove the first receiver blocked on channel `cid`, returning it plus the rest.
fn take_recv(
  cid : Int,
  rws : List((Int, Int, (Wake(a)) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e}))
) : Option((Int, (Wake(a)) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e}, List((Int, Int, (Wake(a)) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e})))) =
  match rws of
    Nil => None
    Cons((c, who, k), rest) =>
      if c == cid then
        Some((who, k, rest))
      else
        match take_recv(cid, rest) of
          None => None
          Some((who2, k2, kept)) => Some((who2, k2, Cons((c, who, k), kept)))

fn list_len(xs : List(a)) : Int =
  match xs of
    Nil => 0
    Cons(_, r) => 1 + list_len(r)

-- The capacity of channel `cid`, or `None` if it is unbounded.
fn cap_of(cid : Int, caps : List((Int, Int))) : Option(Int) =
  match caps of
    Nil => None
    Cons((c, n), rest) =>
      if c == cid then
        Some(n)
      else
        cap_of(cid, rest)

-- The number of values currently buffered on channel `cid`.
fn chan_len(cid : Int, chans : List((Int, List(a)))) : Int =
  match chans of
    Nil => 0
    Cons((c, buf), rest) =>
      if c == cid then
        list_len(buf)
      else
        chan_len(cid, rest)

-- Remove the first sender blocked on channel `cid` (its value and resume thunk),
-- returning it plus the remaining blocked senders.
fn take_sender(
  cid : Int,
  ss : List((Int, Int, a, (Signal) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e}))
) : Option((Int, a, (Signal) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e}, List((Int, Int, a, (Signal) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e})))) =
  match ss of
    Nil => None
    Cons((c, who, v, k), rest) =>
      if c == cid then
        Some((who, v, k, rest))
      else
        match take_sender(cid, rest) of
          None => None
          Some((w2, v2, k2, kept)) =>
            Some((w2, v2, k2, Cons((c, who, v, k), kept)))

-- Pull every waiter belonging to a cancelled fiber out of `ws`, enqueuing each so
-- it runs its `kill` unwind (`Halt` delivery), and return the remaining waiters
-- with the grown queue. Used when a cancel lands on a fiber parked on `await`.
fn evict_waiters(
  victims : List(Int),
  ws : List((Int, Int, (Wake(a)) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e})),
  q : List(Ready(a, e)),
  enq : (List(Ready(a, e)), Ready(a, e)) -> List(Ready(a, e))
) : (List((Int, Int, (Wake(a)) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e})), List(Ready(a, e))) =
  match ws of
    Nil => (Nil, q)
    Cons((f, who, k), rest) =>
      if is_member(who, victims) then
        evict_waiters(
            victims,
            rest,
            enq(q, Ready(who, \() -> k(Halt), \() -> k(Halt))),
            enq,
          )
      else
        match evict_waiters(victims, rest, q, enq) of
          (kept, out) => (Cons((f, who, k), kept), out)

-- Pull every blocked sender belonging to a cancelled fiber out of `ss`, enqueuing
-- each so it runs its `kill` unwind (`Stop` delivery).
fn evict_senders(
  victims : List(Int),
  ss : List((Int, Int, a, (Signal) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e})),
  q : List(Ready(a, e)),
  enq : (List(Ready(a, e)), Ready(a, e)) -> List(Ready(a, e))
) : (List((Int, Int, a, (Signal) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e})), List(Ready(a, e))) =
  match ss of
    Nil => (Nil, q)
    Cons((c, who, v, k), rest) =>
      if is_member(who, victims) then
        evict_senders(
            victims,
            rest,
            enq(q, Ready(who, \() -> k(Stop), \() -> k(Stop))),
            enq,
          )
      else
        match evict_senders(victims, rest, q, enq) of
          (kept, out) => (Cons((c, who, v, k), kept), out)

-- Mark `roots` and their descendants cancelled (idempotently), and reschedule any
-- of them parked on `await`/`recv`/`send` so they get a turn to run their
-- finalizers. Fibers still in the run queue need no surgery: `run_next` delivers
-- their `stop` thunk once they are in `cancelled`.
fn cancel_tree(roots : List(Int), s : Sched(a, e)) : Sched(a, e) =
  let victims = without(descendants(roots, s.kids, Nil), s.finalizing)
  let cancelled2 = fold_add(victims, s.cancelled)
  match evict_waiters(victims, s.waiters, s.queue, s.enq) of
    (waiters2, q1) =>
      match evict_waiters(victims, s.recv_waiters, q1, s.enq) of
        (recv2, q2) =>
          match evict_senders(victims, s.senders, q2, s.enq) of
            (senders2, q3) =>
              Sched {
                ..s,
                cancelled = cancelled2,
                waiters = waiters2,
                recv_waiters = recv2,
                senders = senders2,
                queue = q3
              }

-- Every live fiber except `me`: the ids in the run queue, waiters, recv-waiters,
-- and senders. Used by the scheduler-global abort path when one fiber fails.
fn others(me : Int, s : Sched(a, e)) : List(Int) =
  let a1 = queue_ids(s.queue, Nil)
  let a2 = waiter_ids(s.waiters, a1)
  let a3 = waiter_ids(s.recv_waiters, a2)
  let a4 = sender_ids(s.senders, a3)
  remove(me, a4)

fn queue_ids(q : List(Ready(a, e)), acc : List(Int)) : List(Int) =
  match q of
    Nil => acc
    Cons(Ready(id, _, _), rest) => queue_ids(rest, Cons(id, acc))

fn waiter_ids(
  ws : List((Int, Int, (Wake(a)) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e})),
  acc : List(Int)
) : List(Int) =
  match ws of
    Nil => acc
    Cons((_, who, _), rest) => waiter_ids(rest, Cons(who, acc))

fn sender_ids(
  ss : List((Int, Int, a, (Signal) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e})),
  acc : List(Int)
) : List(Int) =
  match ss of
    Nil => acc
    Cons((_, who, _, _), rest) => sender_ids(rest, Cons(who, acc))

fn remove(x : Int, xs : List(Int)) : List(Int) =
  match xs of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(y, rest) =>
      if x == y then
        remove(x, rest)
      else
        Cons(y, remove(x, rest))

-- Interpret the command produced by fiber `me`, threading the scheduler `s`. The
-- main fiber has id 0; when it finishes, the whole run returns its result.
fn drive(me : Int, cmd : Cmd(a, e), s : Sched(a, e)) : a =
  match cmd of
    Forked(parent, child) =>
      let cid = s.next
      let q = (s.enq)(
          s.queue,
          Ready(cid, \() -> step(child), \() -> step(\() -> kill())),
        )
      let s2 =
        Sched { ..s, next = cid + 1, queue = q, kids = Cons((me, cid), s.kids) }
      let s3 =
        if is_member(me, s.finalizing) then
          cancel_tree([cid], s2)
        else
          s2
      if me == 0 && s3.failed then
        let q2 = (s3.enq)(
            s3.queue,
            Ready(me, \() -> parent(Fiber(cid)), \() -> step(\() -> kill())),
          )
        run_next(Sched { ..s3, queue = q2 })
      else
        drive(me, parent(Fiber(cid)), s3)
    Yielded(k) =>
      run_next(
          Sched {
            ..s,
            queue = (s.enq)(s.queue, Ready(me, \() -> k(Go), \() -> k(Stop)))
          },
        )
    Awaited(fid, k) =>
      match lookup_result(fid, s.results) of
        Some(v) => drive(me, k(Arrived(v)), s)
        None =>
          if is_member(fid, s.died) then
            drive(me, k(Gone), s)
          else
            run_next(Sched { ..s, waiters = append(s.waiters, [(fid, me, k)]) })
    Cancelling(fid, k) =>
      let s2 = cancel_tree([fid], s)
      let s3 =
        if fid == 0 then
          Sched { ..s2, failed = true }
        else
          s2
      if me == 0 && s3.failed then
        let q = (s3.enq)(
            s3.queue,
            Ready(me, \() -> k(()), \() -> step(\() -> kill())),
          )
        run_next(Sched { ..s3, queue = q })
      else
        drive(me, k(()), s3)
    Opened(k) =>
      let cid = s.next
      drive(
          me,
          k(Chan(cid)),
          Sched { ..s, next = cid + 1, chans = Cons((cid, Nil), s.chans) },
        )
    OpenedCap(cap, k) =>
      let cid = s.next
      drive(
          me,
          k(Chan(cid)),
          Sched {
            ..s,
            next = cid + 1,
            chans = Cons((cid, Nil), s.chans),
            caps = Cons((cid, cap), s.caps)
          },
        )
    Sent(cid, v, k) =>
      match take_recv(cid, s.recv_waiters) of
        Some((who, kr, rest)) =>
          let q =
            (s.enq)(s.queue, Ready(who, \() -> kr(Arrived(v)), \() -> kr(Halt)))
          let s2 = Sched { ..s, recv_waiters = rest, queue = q }
          if me == 0 && s2.failed then
            let q2 = (s2.enq)(s2.queue, Ready(me, \() -> k(Go), \() -> k(Stop)))
            run_next(Sched { ..s2, queue = q2 })
          else
            drive(me, k(Go), s2)
        None =>
          match cap_of(cid, s.caps) of
            Some(cap) =>
              if chan_len(cid, s.chans) >= cap then
                run_next(
                    Sched {
                      ..s,
                      senders = append(s.senders, [(cid, me, v, k)])
                    },
                  )
              else
                drive(
                    me,
                    k(Go),
                    Sched { ..s, chans = chan_put(cid, v, s.chans) },
                  )
            None =>
              drive(me, k(Go), Sched { ..s, chans = chan_put(cid, v, s.chans) })
    Recving(cid, k) =>
      match chan_take(cid, s.chans) of
        Some((v, chans2)) =>
          match take_sender(cid, s.senders) of
            Some((who, sv, sk, srest)) =>
              let q =
                (s.enq)(s.queue, Ready(who, \() -> sk(Go), \() -> sk(Stop)))
              let s2 = Sched {
                ..s,
                chans = chan_put(cid, sv, chans2),
                senders = srest,
                queue = q
              }
              if me == 0 && s2.failed then
                let q2 = (s2.enq)(
                    s2.queue,
                    Ready(me, \() -> k(Arrived(v)), \() -> k(Halt)),
                  )
                run_next(Sched { ..s2, queue = q2 })
              else
                drive(me, k(Arrived(v)), s2)
            None => drive(me, k(Arrived(v)), Sched { ..s, chans = chans2 })
        None =>
          match take_sender(cid, s.senders) of
            Some((who, sv, sk, srest)) =>
              let q =
                (s.enq)(s.queue, Ready(who, \() -> sk(Go), \() -> sk(Stop)))
              let s2 = Sched { ..s, senders = srest, queue = q }
              if me == 0 && s2.failed then
                let q2 = (s2.enq)(
                    s2.queue,
                    Ready(me, \() -> k(Arrived(sv)), \() -> k(Halt)),
                  )
                run_next(Sched { ..s2, queue = q2 })
              else
                drive(me, k(Arrived(sv)), s2)
            None =>
              run_next(
                  Sched {
                    ..s,
                    recv_waiters = append(s.recv_waiters, [(cid, me, k)])
                  },
                )
    Died =>
      if me == 0 then
        fail()
      else
        let died2 = fold_add([me], s.died)
        match wake(me, Gone, s.waiters, s.queue, s.enq) of
          (ws, q) =>
            run_next(
                Sched {
                  ..s,
                  finalizing = remove(me, s.finalizing),
                  died = died2,
                  waiters = ws,
                  queue = q
                },
              )
    Failed =>
      let victims = others(me, s)
      let s1 = Sched { ..s, finalizing = remove(me, s.finalizing) }
      let s2 = cancel_tree(victims, s1)
      run_next(Sched { ..s2, failed = true })
    Finished(r) =>
      if me == 0 then
        if s.failed then
          fail()
        else
          r
      else
        match wake(me, Arrived(r), s.waiters, s.queue, s.enq) of
          (ws, q) =>
            run_next(
                Sched {
                  ..s,
                  results = Cons((me, r), s.results),
                  waiters = ws,
                  queue = q
                },
              )

-- Dequeue the next runnable fiber. A cancelled fiber runs its `stop` thunk (into
-- its `kill` unwind); otherwise its `go` thunk. While failure is pending, fiber
-- 0 waits behind every other ready fiber; once it is alone, it may enter or resume
-- its cancellation unwind, while its ordinary continuation re-raises failure.
-- This failed-main branch intentionally precedes the generic cancelled branch:
-- even a requested main stop rotates until all other ready cleanup has run.
fn run_next(s : Sched(a, e)) : a =
  match s.queue of
    Nil => fail()
    Cons(Ready(id, go, stop), rest) =>
      if s.failed && id == 0 then
        match rest of
          Cons(_, _) =>
            run_next(Sched { ..s, queue = append(rest, [Ready(id, go, stop)]) })
          Nil =>
            if is_member(id, s.cancelled) then
              drive(
                  id,
                  stop(),
                  Sched {
                    ..s,
                    queue = Nil,
                    cancelled = remove(id, s.cancelled),
                    finalizing = fold_add([id], s.finalizing)
                  },
                )
            elif is_member(id, s.finalizing) then
              drive(id, go(), Sched { ..s, queue = Nil })
            else
              fail()
      elif is_member(id, s.cancelled) then
        drive(
            id,
            stop(),
            Sched {
              ..s,
              queue = rest,
              cancelled = remove(id, s.cancelled),
              finalizing = fold_add([id], s.finalizing)
            },
          )
      else
        drive(id, go(), Sched { ..s, queue = rest })

-- The initial scheduler state, parameterised only by the enqueue policy `enq`.
fn fresh(enq : (List(Ready(a, e)), Ready(a, e)) -> List(Ready(a, e))) : Sched(a, e) =
  Sched {
    queue = Nil,
    results = Nil,
    waiters = Nil,
    cancelled = Nil,
    finalizing = Nil,
    died = Nil,
    failed = false,
    kids = Nil,
    chans = Nil,
    caps = Nil,
    recv_waiters = Nil,
    senders = Nil,
    next = 1,
    enq = enq
  }

-- | Run `main` and its fibers cooperatively under the FIFO (round-robin) policy,
-- returning `main`'s result. The fibers' effects `e` flow out unchanged, so the
-- caller still handles them. The schedule is deterministic, so a run's output
-- is reproducible.
--
-- ```prism
-- fn task() : Int ! {Async(Int)} = await(fork(\() -> 21)) * 2
--
-- fn main() = println(run_async(task))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 42
-- ```
pub fn run_async(main : () -> a ! {Async(a) | e}) : a =
  drive(0, step(main), fresh(\(q, r) -> append(q, [r])))

-- | The policy-neutral entry point: run `main` under the deployment's default
-- cooperative scheduler. It is `run_async` (FIFO) by default, and the `--scheduler`
-- flag (or `PRISM_SCHEDULER`) retargets it to another shipped policy such as
-- `run_lifo` with no source change, because the scheduler is only a handler for
-- `Async` and swapping it never touches the fibers. Call this when you want the
-- configured default; call `run_async` or `run_lifo` directly to pin a policy.
pub fn run_cooperative(main : () -> a ! {Async(a) | e}) : a = run_async(main)

-- | A second scheduling policy over the same `Async` effect: LIFO (depth-first),
-- which runs the most-recently-forked or most-recently-woken fiber next by pushing
-- it to the front of the run queue. It discharges `fork`/`yield`/`await`/channels
-- exactly as `run_async` does and returns the same result for a determinate
-- computation; only the interleaving (and so the order of observable effects like
-- prints) differs. This is the concrete proof that policy is a handler: the fibers
-- are unchanged, only the run function is swapped.
