-- | JSON: a dynamic value tree, a total parser, a canonical encoder, and a typed
-- layer.
--
-- Two layers, following the wire discipline of `lib/std/Wire.pr`:
--
--   - The dynamic layer is the `Json` tree and a total `decode`/`encode` pair for
--     payloads whose shape you do not control. `decode` never partially succeeds:
--     a malformed input is one `JsonError` carrying a message and a line/column,
--     never a panic or a truncated value. Nesting is depth-limited, and any input
--     left over after the top-level value is rejected.
--   - The typed layer is the `ToJson`/`FromJson` classes with instances for the
--     base types and the containers, so a declared type converts to and from a
--     `Json` tree structurally. (Derivation is a manual typeclass rather than
--     `deriving (Json)`: the derivable set is fixed, so a new derivable class is a
--     compiler change; the class-and-instances form is pure library code.)
--
-- The JSON contract is deliberately narrow:
--
--   - Number semantics are exact-or-error by default. An integer literal decodes
--     to `JInt` (`Int` is arbitrary precision, so no integer overflows); a number
--     decodes to `JFloat` only when its lexeme is already the canonical form the
--     owned formatter would print (`show_int` / `show_float`). A non-canonical
--     spelling (`1.0`, `1e3`, `0.10`) is a decode error under `decode`, and
--     accepted, normalized, under `decode_lossy`. No silent rounding, no silent
--     `1e999`-to-infinity.
--   - Encoding is canonical and byte-deterministic: object keys are sorted, every
--     number is printed by the owned formatter, strings use one fixed escaping,
--     and there are no whitespace options. Two machines encoding equal values
--     produce equal bytes, so a `Json` value has a well-defined hash and diff, and
--     `decode(encode(v))` returns `v` (with the one deliberate normalization that
--     an integer-valued `JFloat` prints as an integer and decodes back to `JInt`,
--     since JSON does not distinguish the two).
--
-- Strings are validated UTF-8 by construction (the `String` type), so invalid
-- UTF-8 is rejected at the byte boundary that builds the input, before the parser
-- ever runs. Streaming (gigabyte, SAX-style) JSON is a package; this codec is
-- value-oriented and total.

import Control.Layer (..)

import Data.Foldable (length)

import Data.List (..)

import Data.Maybe (..)

import Data.Result (..)

import Data.String (..)

import Data.Char (is_digit)

import Data.Bytes (Bytes, bytes_concat, bytes_index, bytes_length, bytes_slice, bytes_to_string, string_to_bytes)

-- | A dynamic JSON value. Numbers split into `JInt` and `JFloat` so the
-- exact-or-error decode is a structural distinction rather than a hidden flag: an
-- object is an association list in parse order (duplicate keys are preserved, not
-- merged).
--
-- ```prism
-- encode(JObj([("ok", JBool(true)), ("n", JInt(3))]))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- {"n":3,"ok":true}
-- ```
pub type Json
  = JNull
  | JBool(Bool)
  | JInt(Int)
  | JFloat(Float)
  | JStr(String)
  | JArr(List(Json))
  | JObj(List((String, Json)))

-- | A decode failure: a human-readable message and the 1-based line and column of
-- the offending byte.
pub type JsonError = JsonError(String, Int, Int)

-- | Render a `JsonError` as `line L col C: message`.
--
-- ```prism
-- json_error_message(JsonError("unexpected character", 1, 5))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- line 1 col 5: unexpected character
-- ```
pub fn json_error_message(e : JsonError) : String =
  match e of
    JsonError(m, l, c) => "line {l} col {c}: {m}"

-- The maximum nesting depth the parser admits before rejecting, which also bounds
-- its own recursion so a hostile deeply-nested input fails cleanly rather than
-- exhausting the native stack.
fn max_depth() : Int = 512

-- The one-character string of a scalar value given as an `Int` code point.
fn char_str(cp : Int) : String = str_of_char(chr(cp))

-- ASCII code points used by the grammar, named where a bare number would be
-- opaque. `is_digit` (Data.Char) covers `0`-`9`.
fn is_ws(c : Int) : Bool = c == 32 || c == 9 || c == 10 || c == 13

-- The scanner walks raw UTF-8 bytes: `bytes_index` is constant-time where the
-- codepoint accessors re-walk the prefix on every call, which turned the whole
-- parser quadratic in the input. Every structural byte JSON dispatches on is
-- ASCII, and a UTF-8 lead or continuation byte is >= 128, so byte comparisons
-- against ASCII codes can never misfire inside multi-byte text.

-- Advance past any run of JSON whitespace starting at byte `i`.
fn skip_ws(b : Bytes, n : Int, i : Int) : Int =
  if i < n && is_ws(bytes_index(b, i)) then
    skip_ws(b, n, i + 1)
  else
    i

-- The 1-based line and column of byte index `i`, for a positioned error. The
-- column counts codepoints, so a continuation byte advances the walk without
-- advancing the column.
fn line_col_go(
  b : Bytes,
  j : Int,
  i : Int,
  line : Int,
  col : Int
) : (Int, Int) =
  if j >= i then
    (line, col)
  else
    let c = bytes_index(b, j)
    if c == 10 then
      line_col_go(b, j + 1, i, line + 1, 1)
    elif c >= 128 && c < 192 then
      line_col_go(b, j + 1, i, line, col)
    else
      line_col_go(b, j + 1, i, line, col + 1)

fn mk_err(b : Bytes, n : Int, i : Int, msg : String) : JsonError =
  let (l, c) = line_col_go(b, 0, min(i, n), 1, 1)
  JsonError(msg, l, c)

-- True when the ASCII literal `lit` occurs at byte index `i`.
fn lit_at(b : Bytes, n : Int, i : Int, lit : String) : Bool =
  i + byte_len(lit) <= n && lit_at_go(b, i, lit, 0, byte_len(lit))

fn lit_at_go(b : Bytes, i : Int, lit : String, k : Int, m : Int) : Bool =
  if k >= m then
    true
  elif bytes_index(b, i + k) == byte_at(lit, k) then
    lit_at_go(b, i, lit, k + 1, m)
  else
    false

-- The value of a single hex digit, or `None`.
fn hex_val(c : Int) : Option(Int) =
  if c >= 48 && c <= 57 then
    Some(c - 48)
  elif c >= 97 && c <= 102 then
    Some(c - 97 + 10)
  elif c >= 65 && c <= 70 then
    Some(c - 65 + 10)
  else
    None

-- Four hex digits at bytes `[i, i+4)` as a code point, or `None`.
fn hex4(b : Bytes, n : Int, i : Int) : Option(Int) =
  if i + 4 > n then
    None
  else
    match ((
          hex_val(bytes_index(b, i)),
          hex_val(bytes_index(b, i + 1)),
          hex_val(bytes_index(b, i + 2)),
          hex_val(bytes_index(b, i + 3)),
        )) of
      (Some(h1), Some(h2), Some(h3), Some(h4)) =>
        Some(((h1 * 16 + h2) * 16 + h3) * 16 + h4)
      _ => None

-- Parse a JSON string body starting at the opening quote `i`, returning the
-- decoded string and the byte index just past the closing quote. The raw run
-- between escapes is sliced from the input whole, so an escape-free string
-- costs one slice; only an escape forces the decoded prefix to be copied.
fn parse_string(
  b : Bytes,
  n : Int,
  i : Int
) : Result((String, Int), JsonError) =
  str_run(b, n, i + 1, i + 1, bytes_slice(b, 0, 0))

-- Scan the raw run that began at `start` with the cursor at `j`; `acc` holds
-- the decoded bytes before `start`.
fn str_run(
  b : Bytes,
  n : Int,
  start : Int,
  j : Int,
  acc : Bytes
) : Result((String, Int), JsonError) =
  if j >= n then
    Err(mk_err(b, n, j, "unterminated string"))
  else
    let c = bytes_index(b, j)
    if c == 34 then
      let whole = bytes_concat(acc, bytes_slice(b, start, j - start))
      match bytes_to_string(whole) of
        Some(text) => Ok((text, j + 1))
        None => Err(mk_err(b, n, j, "invalid UTF-8 in string"))
    elif c == 92 then
      parse_escape(
          b,
          n,
          j + 1,
          bytes_concat(acc, bytes_slice(b, start, j - start)),
        )
    elif c < 32 then
      Err(mk_err(b, n, j, "unescaped control character in string"))
    else
      str_run(b, n, start, j + 1, acc)

-- Append one decoded scalar to `acc` and resume the raw run at `k`.
fn esc_emit(
  b : Bytes,
  n : Int,
  k : Int,
  acc : Bytes,
  cp : Int
) : Result((String, Int), JsonError) =
  str_run(b, n, k, k, bytes_concat(acc, string_to_bytes(char_str(cp))))

fn parse_escape(
  b : Bytes,
  n : Int,
  i : Int,
  acc : Bytes
) : Result((String, Int), JsonError) =
  if i >= n then
    Err(mk_err(b, n, i, "unterminated escape"))
  else
    let c = bytes_index(b, i)
    if c == 34 then
      esc_emit(b, n, i + 1, acc, 34)
    elif c == 92 then
      esc_emit(b, n, i + 1, acc, 92)
    elif c == 47 then
      esc_emit(b, n, i + 1, acc, 47)
    elif c == 98 then
      esc_emit(b, n, i + 1, acc, 8)
    elif c == 102 then
      esc_emit(b, n, i + 1, acc, 12)
    elif c == 110 then
      esc_emit(b, n, i + 1, acc, 10)
    elif c == 114 then
      esc_emit(b, n, i + 1, acc, 13)
    elif c == 116 then
      esc_emit(b, n, i + 1, acc, 9)
    elif c == 117 then
      parse_unicode(b, n, i + 1, acc)
    else
      Err(mk_err(b, n, i, "invalid escape"))

-- Parse a `\uXXXX` escape (the `\u` already consumed), joining a surrogate pair
-- into one scalar. A lone or mismatched surrogate is an error, so the decoded
-- string is always valid Unicode.
fn parse_unicode(
  b : Bytes,
  n : Int,
  i : Int,
  acc : Bytes
) : Result((String, Int), JsonError) =
  match hex4(b, n, i) of
    None => Err(mk_err(b, n, i, "invalid \\u escape"))
    Some(cp) =>
      if cp >= 55296 && cp <= 56319 then
        if lit_at(b, n, i + 4, "\\u") then
          match hex4(b, n, i + 6) of
            Some(lo) =>
              if lo >= 56320 && lo <= 57343 then
                let scalar = 65536 + (cp - 55296) * 1024 + lo - 56320
                esc_emit(b, n, i + 10, acc, scalar)
              else
                Err(mk_err(b, n, i, "invalid low surrogate in \\u escape"))
            None => Err(mk_err(b, n, i, "invalid \\u escape"))
        else
          Err(mk_err(b, n, i, "unpaired high surrogate in \\u escape"))
      elif cp >= 56320 && cp <= 57343 then
        Err(mk_err(b, n, i, "unpaired low surrogate in \\u escape"))
      else
        esc_emit(b, n, i + 4, acc, cp)

-- Number lexing: validate a JSON number's grammar and find its end. Returns the
-- end index and whether the token has a fraction or exponent (so is a float).

fn skip_digits(b : Bytes, n : Int, i : Int) : Int =
  if i < n && is_digit(bytes_index(b, i)) then
    skip_digits(b, n, i + 1)
  else
    i

-- Integer part after the optional sign: a single `0`, or `[1-9][0-9]*`.
fn lex_int_part(b : Bytes, n : Int, i : Int) : Option(Int) =
  if i >= n || not(is_digit(bytes_index(b, i))) then
    None
  elif bytes_index(b, i) == 48 then
    Some(i + 1)
  else
    Some(skip_digits(b, n, i))

-- Optional fraction: a `.` followed by at least one digit.
fn lex_frac(b : Bytes, n : Int, i : Int) : Option((Int, Bool)) =
  if i < n && bytes_index(b, i) == 46 then
    let j = i + 1
    if j < n && is_digit(bytes_index(b, j)) then
      Some((skip_digits(b, n, j), true))
    else
      None
  else
    Some((i, false))

-- Optional exponent: `e`/`E`, an optional sign, then at least one digit.
fn lex_exp(b : Bytes, n : Int, i : Int) : Option((Int, Bool)) =
  if i < n && (bytes_index(b, i) == 101 || bytes_index(b, i) == 69) then
    let j =
      if (i + 1 < n
          && (bytes_index(b, i + 1) == 43 || bytes_index(b, i + 1) == 45)) then
        i + 2
      else
        i + 1
    if j < n && is_digit(bytes_index(b, j)) then
      Some((skip_digits(b, n, j), true))
    else
      None
  else
    Some((i, false))

fn lex_number(b : Bytes, n : Int, i0 : Int) : Option((Int, Bool)) =
  let i1 =
    if i0 < n && bytes_index(b, i0) == 45 then
      i0 + 1
    else
      i0
  match lex_int_part(b, n, i1) of
    None => None
    Some(i2) =>
      match lex_frac(b, n, i2) of
        None => None
        Some((i3, hf)) =>
          match lex_exp(b, n, i3) of
            None => None
            Some((i4, he)) => Some((i4, hf || he))

-- Apply the exact-or-error number policy to a validated lexeme.
fn classify_number(
  lossy : Bool,
  lexeme : String,
  is_dec : Bool
) : Option(Json) =
  if is_dec then
    let f = parse_float(lexeme)
    if lossy || str_eq(show_float(f), lexeme) then
      Some(JFloat(f))
    else
      None
  else
    match parse_int(lexeme) of
      Some(n) =>
        if lossy || str_eq(show_int(n), lexeme) then
          Some(JInt(n))
        else
          None
      None =>
        if lossy then
          Some(JFloat(parse_float(lexeme)))
        else
          None

fn parse_number(
  lossy : Bool,
  b : Bytes,
  n : Int,
  i : Int
) : Result((Json, Int), JsonError) =
  match lex_number(b, n, i) of
    None => Err(mk_err(b, n, i, "invalid number"))
    Some((end, is_dec)) =>
      -- A validated number lexeme is pure ASCII, so the conversion is total.
      let lexeme =
        match bytes_to_string(bytes_slice(b, i, end - i)) of
          Some(text) => text
          None => ""
      match classify_number(lossy, lexeme, is_dec) of
        Some(v) => Ok((v, end))
        None =>
          Err(
              mk_err(
                  b,
                  n,
                  i,
                  "number not exactly representable (use decode_lossy)",
                ),
            )

-- The recursive-descent core, threading the `lossy` flag and the nesting depth.

fn parse_value(
  lossy : Bool,
  b : Bytes,
  n : Int,
  i : Int,
  d : Int
) : Result((Json, Int), JsonError) =
  let j = skip_ws(b, n, i)
  if j >= n then
    Err(mk_err(b, n, j, "unexpected end of input"))
  else
    let c = bytes_index(b, j)
    if c == 123 then
      parse_object(lossy, b, n, j, d)
    elif c == 91 then
      parse_array(lossy, b, n, j, d)
    elif c == 34 then
      match parse_string(b, n, j) of
        Ok((str, k)) => Ok((JStr(str), k))
        Err(e) => Err(e)
    elif c == 45 || is_digit(c) then
      parse_number(lossy, b, n, j)
    elif lit_at(b, n, j, "true") then
      Ok((JBool(true), j + 4))
    elif lit_at(b, n, j, "false") then
      Ok((JBool(false), j + 5))
    elif lit_at(b, n, j, "null") then
      Ok((JNull, j + 4))
    else
      Err(mk_err(b, n, j, "unexpected character"))

fn parse_array(
  lossy : Bool,
  b : Bytes,
  n : Int,
  i : Int,
  d : Int
) : Result((Json, Int), JsonError) =
  if d + 1 > max_depth() then
    Err(mk_err(b, n, i, "maximum nesting depth exceeded"))
  else
    let j = skip_ws(b, n, i + 1)
    if j < n && bytes_index(b, j) == 93 then
      Ok((JArr(Nil), j + 1))
    else
      array_elems(lossy, b, n, i + 1, d + 1, Nil)

fn array_elems(
  lossy : Bool,
  b : Bytes,
  n : Int,
  i : Int,
  d : Int,
  acc : List(Json)
) : Result((Json, Int), JsonError) =
  match parse_value(lossy, b, n, i, d) of
    Err(e) => Err(e)
    Ok((v, k)) =>
      let acc2 = Cons(v, acc)
      let j = skip_ws(b, n, k)
      if j >= n then
        Err(mk_err(b, n, j, "unterminated array"))
      else
        let c = bytes_index(b, j)
        if c == 93 then
          Ok((JArr(reverse(acc2)), j + 1))
        elif c == 44 then
          array_elems(lossy, b, n, j + 1, d, acc2)
        else
          Err(mk_err(b, n, j, "expected ',' or ']' in array"))

fn parse_object(
  lossy : Bool,
  b : Bytes,
  n : Int,
  i : Int,
  d : Int
) : Result((Json, Int), JsonError) =
  if d + 1 > max_depth() then
    Err(mk_err(b, n, i, "maximum nesting depth exceeded"))
  else
    let j = skip_ws(b, n, i + 1)
    if j < n && bytes_index(b, j) == 125 then
      Ok((JObj(Nil), j + 1))
    else
      object_members(lossy, b, n, i + 1, d + 1, Nil)

fn object_members(
  lossy : Bool,
  b : Bytes,
  n : Int,
  i : Int,
  d : Int,
  acc : List((String, Json))
) : Result((Json, Int), JsonError) =
  let j = skip_ws(b, n, i)
  if j >= n || bytes_index(b, j) /= 34 then
    Err(mk_err(b, n, j, "expected string key in object"))
  else
    match parse_string(b, n, j) of
      Err(e) => Err(e)
      Ok((key, k)) =>
        let k2 = skip_ws(b, n, k)
        if k2 >= n || bytes_index(b, k2) /= 58 then
          Err(mk_err(b, n, k2, "expected ':' after object key"))
        else
          match parse_value(lossy, b, n, k2 + 1, d) of
            Err(e) => Err(e)
            Ok((v, m)) =>
              let acc2 = Cons((key, v), acc)
              let m2 = skip_ws(b, n, m)
              if m2 >= n then
                Err(mk_err(b, n, m2, "unterminated object"))
              else
                let c = bytes_index(b, m2)
                if c == 125 then
                  Ok((JObj(reverse(acc2)), m2 + 1))
                elif c == 44 then
                  object_members(lossy, b, n, m2 + 1, d, acc2)
                else
                  Err(mk_err(b, n, m2, "expected ',' or '\}' in object"))

fn decode_with(lossy : Bool, s : String) : Result(Json, JsonError) =
  let b = string_to_bytes(s)
  let n = bytes_length(b)
  match parse_value(lossy, b, n, 0, 0) of
    Err(e) => Err(e)
    Ok((v, k)) =>
      let j = skip_ws(b, n, k)
      if j >= n then
        Ok(v)
      else
        Err(mk_err(b, n, j, "trailing input after top-level value"))

-- | Decode a JSON document with exact number semantics: a number decodes only
-- when its lexeme is already canonical, otherwise a decode error. Total: any
-- malformed or lossy input is an `Err` with a position.
--
-- ```prism
-- decode("[1, 2, 3]")
-- ```
-- ```output
-- Ok(Json.JArr([Json.JInt(1), Json.JInt(2), Json.JInt(3)]))
-- ```
pub fn decode(s : String) : Result(Json, JsonError) = decode_with(false, s)

-- | Decode a JSON document, accepting any well-formed number and normalizing it
-- to `JInt` (exact integer in range) or the nearest `JFloat`. Still total, and
-- still rejects structurally malformed input.
--
-- ```prism
-- decode_lossy("1e3")
-- ```
-- ```output
-- Ok(Json.JFloat(1000))
-- ```
pub fn decode_lossy(s : String) : Result(Json, JsonError) = decode_with(true, s)

-- Canonical encoding.

-- Escape a string into a canonical JSON string literal: the two mandatory
-- escapes, the five short control escapes, and `\uXXXX` for the remaining
-- controls. Non-ASCII scalars pass through as UTF-8. The walk is byte-level
-- and flushes the raw run between escapes as one slice, so a string with no
-- escapes is copied once; every escape byte is ASCII, so a run boundary can
-- never split a multi-byte scalar.
fn encode_string(s : String) : String =
  let b = string_to_bytes(s)
  let n = bytes_length(b)
  concat("\"", concat(esc_run(b, n, 0, 0, ""), "\""))

fn esc_run(b : Bytes, n : Int, start : Int, j : Int, acc : String) : String =
  if j >= n then
    concat(acc, raw_run(b, start, j))
  else
    let c = bytes_index(b, j)
    if c == 34 || c == 92 || c < 32 then
      let flushed = concat(concat(acc, raw_run(b, start, j)), esc_char(c))
      esc_run(b, n, j + 1, j + 1, flushed)
    else
      esc_run(b, n, start, j + 1, acc)

-- The bytes `[start, end)` as text. A run breaks only at ASCII escape bytes,
-- so the slice is always whole scalars; the empty fallback is unreachable.
fn raw_run(b : Bytes, start : Int, end : Int) : String =
  match bytes_to_string(bytes_slice(b, start, end - start)) of
    Some(text) => text
    None => ""

fn esc_char(c : Int) : String =
  if c == 34 then
    "\\\""
  elif c == 92 then
    "\\\\"
  elif c == 8 then
    "\\b"
  elif c == 12 then
    "\\f"
  elif c == 10 then
    "\\n"
  elif c == 13 then
    "\\r"
  elif c == 9 then
    "\\t"
  elif c < 32 then
    concat("\\u00", hex2(c))
  else
    char_str(c)

-- Two lowercase hex digits of a byte-sized value, for the `\u00XX` control form.
fn hex2(c : Int) : String = concat(hex_digit(c / 16), hex_digit(mod(c, 16)))

fn hex_digit(n : Int) : String =
  if n < 10 then
    show_int(n)
  else
    char_str(97 + n - 10)

-- A finite float prints via the owned formatter; a non-finite one is not
-- representable in JSON and encodes as `null` (the JavaScript convention).
fn is_finite(f : Float) : Bool = f == f && f - f == 0.0

fn encode_float(f : Float) : String =
  if is_finite(f) then
    show_float(f)
  else
    "null"

-- Merge sort object members by key, so the encoding is independent of insertion
-- order.
fn sort_pairs(xs : List((String, Json))) : List((String, Json)) =
  match xs of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(_, Nil) => xs
    _ =>
      let (l, r) = split_alt(xs)
      merge_pairs(sort_pairs(l), sort_pairs(r))

-- Split a list into two halves by alternating elements, so merge sort needs no
-- length or indexing.
fn split_alt(xs : List((String, Json))) : (List((String, Json)), List((String, Json))) =
  match xs of
    Nil => (Nil, Nil)
    Cons(a, Nil) => (Cons(a, Nil), Nil)
    Cons(a, Cons(b, rest)) =>
      let (l, r) = split_alt(rest)
      (Cons(a, l), Cons(b, r))

fn merge_pairs(
  a : List((String, Json)),
  b : List((String, Json))
) : List((String, Json)) =
  match (a, b) of
    (Nil, _) => b
    (_, Nil) => a
    (Cons(x, xs), Cons(y, ys)) =>
      match (x, y) of
        ((kx, _), (ky, _)) =>
          if str_cmp(kx, ky) <= 0 then
            Cons(x, merge_pairs(xs, b))
          else
            Cons(y, merge_pairs(a, ys))

fn encode_member(kv : (String, Json)) : String =
  match kv of
    (k, v) => concat(encode_string(k), concat(":", encode(v)))

-- | Encode a `Json` value to its canonical byte-deterministic string: object keys
-- sorted, numbers by the owned formatter, one fixed string escaping, no optional
-- whitespace. Equal values encode to equal bytes.
--
-- ```prism
-- encode(JObj([("b", JInt(2)), ("a", JInt(1))]))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- {"a":1,"b":2}
-- ```
pub fn encode(j : Json) : String =
  match j of
    JNull => "null"
    JBool(b) =>
      if b then
        "true"
      else
        "false"
    JInt(n) => show_int(n)
    JFloat(f) => encode_float(f)
    JStr(s) => encode_string(s)
    JArr(xs) => concat("[", concat(str_join(",", map(encode, xs)), "]"))
    JObj(kvs) =>
      concat(
          "\{",
          concat(str_join(",", map(encode_member, sort_pairs(kvs))), "\}"),
        )

-- The typed layer: structural conversion between declared types and `Json`.

-- | Convert a value to a `Json` tree.
--
-- `deriving (ToJson)` writes the instance structurally, for a type whose schema
-- is its own declaration. One constructor becomes one object: a record
-- constructor's keys are its declared field names, a positional one's are its
-- argument positions (`_0`, `_1`), and a sum additionally names the variant it
-- holds under the key `$`, which no field name can spell. A document therefore
-- names the constructor it holds rather than an index that quietly changes
-- meaning when a constructor is inserted; a single-constructor type has nothing
-- to discriminate and carries no tag. Constructor and field order are the
-- declaration's, so one value has one tree, and `encode` sorts keys, so it has
-- one string. Derive it in a pair with `FromJson`: a type that encodes but
-- cannot decode is a document nobody can read back.
--
-- This is not the wire codec. A `Wire.Serialize` byte format is frozen and
-- versioned; a JSON document is read by something that was not compiled against
-- this program, so the encoding is self-describing rather than compact, and
-- nothing here promises stability across a change to the declaration.
--
-- ```prism
-- to_json([1, 2, 3])
-- ```
-- ```output
-- Json.JArr([Json.JInt(1), Json.JInt(2), Json.JInt(3)])
-- ```
pub class ToJson(a)
  to_json : (a) -> Json

-- | Recover a value from a `Json` tree, failing (through `Fail`) on a structural
-- mismatch. A decode of foreign data is one ordinary failure channel.
--
-- `deriving (FromJson)` reads back exactly what the derived `ToJson` wrote, by
-- the same keys: `from_json(to_json(x))` is `x`. A tree that is not an object, a
-- sum whose `$` names no constructor of the type, a missing key, and a field
-- that will not itself decode all leave through the same `Fail`. That failure
-- carries no payload, so it reports that the document did not fit and not where:
-- `Fail` is a nullary operation, and reporting a path would mean a different
-- effect on this class's signature and so on every hand-written instance too.
-- Catch it with `optional`, `default`, or `succeeds`, as with any other `Fail`.
--
-- ```prism
-- from_json(JInt(41)) + 1
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 42
-- ```
pub class FromJson(a)
  from_json : (Json) -> a ! {Fail | e}

instance toJsonInt : ToJson(Int)
  fn to_json(n) = JInt(n)

instance toJsonFloat : ToJson(Float)
  fn to_json(f) = JFloat(f)

instance toJsonBool : ToJson(Bool)
  fn to_json(b) = JBool(b)

instance toJsonString : ToJson(String)
  fn to_json(s) = JStr(s)

instance toJsonList : ToJson(List(a)) given ToJson(a)
  fn to_json(xs) = JArr(map(to_json, xs))

-- `None` maps to `null`; `Some(x)` maps to the encoding of `x`.
instance toJsonOption : ToJson(Option(a)) given ToJson(a)
  fn to_json(o) =
    match o of
      None => JNull
      Some(x) => to_json(x)

instance toJsonPair : ToJson((a, b)) given ToJson(a), ToJson(b)
  fn to_json(p) =
    match p of
      (x, y) => JArr(Cons(to_json(x), Cons(to_json(y), Nil)))

instance fromJsonInt : FromJson(Int)
  fn from_json(j) =
    match j of
      JInt(n) => n
      _ => fail()

instance fromJsonFloat : FromJson(Float)
  fn from_json(j) =
    match j of
      JFloat(f) => f
      JInt(n) => to_float(n)
      _ => fail()

instance fromJsonBool : FromJson(Bool)
  fn from_json(j) =
    match j of
      JBool(b) => b
      _ => fail()

instance fromJsonString : FromJson(String)
  fn from_json(j) =
    match j of
      JStr(s) => s
      _ => fail()

instance fromJsonList : FromJson(List(a)) given FromJson(a)
  fn from_json(j) =
    match j of
      JArr(xs) => from_json_each(xs)
      _ => fail()

-- `null` is the empty option; anything else is `Some` of its decoding.
instance fromJsonOption : FromJson(Option(a)) given FromJson(a)
  fn from_json(j) =
    match j of
      JNull => None
      _ => Some(from_json(j))

instance fromJsonPair : FromJson((a, b)) given FromJson(a), FromJson(b)
  fn from_json(j) =
    match j of
      JArr(Cons(x, Cons(y, Nil))) => (from_json(x), from_json(y))
      _ => fail()

-- Decode each element of a JSON array, threading `Fail` so one bad element fails
-- the whole list.
fn from_json_each(xs : List(Json)) : List(a) given FromJson(a) =
  match xs of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(y, rest) => Cons(from_json(y), from_json_each(rest))

-- | The member named `key` of an object's member list, or `fail()` when there is
-- none. Members are kept in parse order and duplicates are preserved, so the
-- first occurrence wins, which is what makes a decode a function of the document
-- rather than of a hash order. `deriving (ToJson, FromJson)` reads every field
-- through this, so a missing field and a mistyped one leave through the same
-- channel.
--
-- ```prism
-- json_field([("a", JInt(1)), ("b", JInt(2))], "b")
-- ```
-- ```output
-- Json.JInt(2)
-- ```
pub fn json_field(kvs : List((String, Json)), key : String) : Json ! {Fail | e} =
  match kvs of
    Nil => fail()
    Cons(kv, rest) =>
      match kv of
        (k, v) =>
          if k == key then
            v
          else
            json_field(rest, key)

-- | Encode a typed value straight to a canonical JSON string.
--
-- ```prism
-- to_json_string((1, true))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [1,true]
-- ```
pub fn to_json_string(x : a) : String given ToJson(a) = encode(to_json(x))

-- | The immediate `Json` children of a value: an array's elements, an object's
-- field values in field order, and nothing at a scalar.
--
-- ```prism
-- json_children(JObj([("x", JInt(1)), ("ok", JBool(true))]))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [Json.JInt(1), Json.JBool(true)]
-- ```
pub fn json_children(j : Json) : List(Json) =
  match j of
    JArr(items) => items
    JObj(fields) => map(json_field_value, fields)
    _ => []

fn json_field_value(kv : (String, Json)) : Json =
  match kv of
    (_, v) => v

-- | Put a replacement child list back, in `json_children` order, keeping an
-- object's field names. Fails closed: a list of the wrong length yields the
-- value unchanged rather than a truncated or padded one.
--
-- ```prism
-- json_rebuild(JObj([("x", JInt(1))]), [JInt(2)])
-- ```
-- ```output
-- Json.JObj([(x, Json.JInt(2))])
-- ```
pub fn json_rebuild(j : Json, cs : List(Json)) : Json =
  match j of
    JArr(items) =>
      if length(items) == length(cs) then
        JArr(cs)
      else
        j
    JObj(fields) =>
      match json_rekey(fields, cs) of
        Some(fs) => JObj(fs)
        None => j
    _ => j

fn json_rekey(
  fields : List((String, Json)),
  cs : List(Json)
) : Option(List((String, Json))) =
  match (fields, cs) of
    (Nil, Nil) => Some(Nil)
    (Cons(kv, more), Cons(v, rest)) =>
      match json_rekey(more, rest) of
        None => None
        Some(tl) => Some(Cons((json_field_name(kv), v), tl))
    _ => None

fn json_field_name(kv : (String, Json)) : String =
  match kv of
    (k, _) => k

-- | The children-and-rebuild pair for JSON, so every strategy in
-- `Control.Rewrite` and every query in `Control.Layer` works on a decoded
-- document.
pub fn json_layer() : Layer(Json) =
  Layer { kids = json_children, rebuild = json_rebuild }

Named mathematical constants, matching Rust's `f64::consts` surface.

Purely additive: the transcendental functions (`sin`, `cos`, `exp`, `ln`, `sqrt`, ...) stay owned builtins routing through the vendored libm, and `pi`/`e`/`tau` stay Base-global. This module only names the derived constants, as exact `Float` literals pinned bit-for-bit, so importing it never shadows a Base name. Opt-in: not in Base.

-- | Named mathematical constants, matching Rust's `f64::consts` surface.
--
-- Purely additive: the transcendental functions (`sin`, `cos`, `exp`, `ln`,
-- `sqrt`, ...) stay owned builtins routing through the vendored libm, and
-- `pi`/`e`/`tau` stay Base-global. This module only names the derived
-- constants, as exact `Float` literals pinned bit-for-bit, so importing it never
-- shadows a Base name. Opt-in: not in Base.

-- | The square root of 2.
pub let sqrt2 : Float = 1.4142135623730951

-- | The reciprocal of the square root of 2 (`1 / sqrt2`).
pub let sqrt1_2 : Float = 0.7071067811865476

-- | The natural logarithm of 2.
pub let ln2 : Float = 0.6931471805599453

-- | The natural logarithm of 10.
pub let ln10 : Float = 2.302585092994046

-- | The base-2 logarithm of `e`.
pub let log2e : Float = 1.4426950408889634

-- | The base-10 logarithm of `e`.
pub let log10e : Float = 0.4342944819032518

-- | The golden ratio, `(1 + sqrt(5)) / 2`.
--
-- ```prism
-- [sqrt2 > 1.4, phi > 1.6, inv_pi < 0.32]
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [true, true, true]
-- ```
pub let phi : Float = 1.618033988749895

-- | Half of pi (`pi / 2`).
pub let half_pi : Float = 1.5707963267948966

-- | A quarter of pi (`pi / 4`).
pub let quarter_pi : Float = 0.7853981633974483

-- | The reciprocal of pi (`1 / pi`).
pub let inv_pi : Float = 0.3183098861837907

Property testing: run a boolean property over many generated inputs and report the first counterexample, deterministically.

A `Gen(a)` is a seeded, sized function producing an `a`. It draws its randomness from the ambient `Random` effect, and the runner discharges that effect with a seeded SplitMix64 handler, so a whole run is a pure function of its seed. There is no real IO here: `quickcheck` performs no `prim_rand`, only the seeded stream, so a property that fails fails the same way on every backend and reruns identically from the reported seed. Determinism is the language's contract, and a flaky property test would violate it.

The generator TYPE and its combinators live here; a derived `Arbitrary(a)` class (see `Wire`/deriving) supplies `arbitrary : Gen(a)` for user types by composing these combinators, so a derived instance plugs in with no rework.

Shrinking is intentionally omitted. The seam is the seed and size carried on a failing `Outcome`: a counterexample reproduces exactly via `gen_at`, and a future `shrink : (a) -> List(a)` hook would thread through `check_go` without changing this surface.

-- | Property testing: run a boolean property over many generated inputs and
-- report the first counterexample, deterministically.
--
-- A `Gen(a)` is a seeded, sized function producing an `a`. It draws its
-- randomness from the ambient `Random` effect, and the runner discharges that
-- effect with a seeded SplitMix64 handler, so a whole run is a pure function of
-- its seed. There is no real IO here: `quickcheck` performs no `prim_rand`, only
-- the seeded stream, so a property that fails fails the same way on every
-- backend and reruns identically from the reported seed. Determinism is the
-- language's contract, and a flaky property test would violate it.
--
-- The generator TYPE and its combinators live here; a derived `Arbitrary(a)`
-- class (see `Wire`/deriving) supplies `arbitrary : Gen(a)` for user types by
-- composing these combinators, so a derived instance plugs in with no rework.
--
-- Shrinking is intentionally omitted. The seam is the seed and size carried on a
-- failing `Outcome`: a counterexample reproduces exactly via `gen_at`, and a
-- future `shrink : (a) -> List(a)` hook would thread through `check_go` without
-- changing this surface.

import Data.List (..)

import Data.Foldable (..)

-- The SplitMix64 mixing constants (the increment gamma and the two output
-- multipliers) and its three output shift distances, named once here so the
-- pseudo-random stream is one canonical definition.
let splitmix_gamma : U64 = 11400714819323198485u64

let splitmix_mix1 : U64 = 13787848793156543929u64

let splitmix_mix2 : U64 = 10723151780598845931u64

let shift_a : U64 = 30u64

let shift_b : U64 = 27u64

let shift_c : U64 = 31u64

-- The SplitMix64 output for counter state `s`: advance the counter by gamma,
-- then avalanche it. The state is just the incrementing counter, so `sm_next`
-- is the raw advance and `sm_out` mixes the advanced value.
fn sm_out(s : U64) : U64 =
  let z0 = s + splitmix_gamma
  let z1 = u64_xor(z0, u64_shr(z0, shift_a)) * splitmix_mix1
  let z2 = u64_xor(z1, u64_shr(z1, shift_b)) * splitmix_mix2
  u64_xor(z2, u64_shr(z2, shift_c))

fn sm_next(s : U64) : U64 = s + splitmix_gamma

-- | Run `action` with the `Random` effect served by a seeded SplitMix64 stream,
-- so the result is a pure function of `seed`. This is the REPLAYABLE handler the
-- runner installs; call it directly to reproduce a single draw off a seed.
--
-- ```prism
-- run_seeded(1u64, \() -> gen_run(gen_int, 5))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 1
-- ```
pub fn run_seeded(seed : U64, action : () -> a ! {Random | e}) =
  let f =
    handle action() with
      rng_rand() resume k => \(s) -> k(int_of_u64(sm_out(s)))(sm_next(s))
      return r => \(_s) -> r
  f(seed)

-- A random natural in `[0, n)`, folded from a full-width draw so it never goes
-- negative regardless of the drawn sign. Requires `n > 0`.
fn nat_below(n : Int) = int_of_u64(to_u64(rand()) % to_u64(n))

-- | A seeded, sized generator of `a`. Apply it with `gen_run`; build one with
-- the combinators below. The size bounds recursive shapes (list length, tree
-- depth); make it explicit so derived instances for recursive types stay finite.
pub type Gen(a) = Gen((Int) -> a ! {Random})

-- | Draw one value from `g` at the given size, performing `Random`. Discharge the
-- `Random` with `run_seeded` (or use `gen_at`) to run it.
--
-- ```prism
-- run_seeded(1u64, \() -> gen_run(gen_const(9), 5))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 9
-- ```
pub fn gen_run(g : Gen(a), size : Int) =
  match g of
    Gen(f) => f(size)

-- | Draw a value from `g` deterministically off `seed` at `size`, no IO. This is
-- the reproduce-a-counterexample entry point.
--
-- ```prism
-- gen_at(gen_int, 42u64, 10)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- -6
-- ```
pub fn gen_at(g : Gen(a), seed : U64, size : Int) : a =
  run_seeded(seed, \() -> gen_run(g, size))

-- | The generator that ignores size and randomness and always yields `x`.
--
-- ```prism
-- gen_at(gen_const(7), 1u64, 5)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 7
-- ```
pub fn gen_const(x : a) : Gen(a) = Gen(\(_size) -> x)

-- | Map `f` over every value a generator produces.
--
-- ```prism
-- gen_at(gen_map(\(x) -> x + 1, gen_const(4)), 1u64, 5)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 5
-- ```
pub fn gen_map(f : (a) -> b, g : Gen(a)) : Gen(b) =
  Gen(\(size) -> f(gen_run(g, size)))

-- | Combine two generators with `f`, drawing both at the same size.
--
-- ```prism
-- gen_at(gen_map2(\(a, b) -> a + b, gen_const(2), gen_const(3)), 1u64, 5)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 5
-- ```
pub fn gen_map2(f : (a, b) -> c, ga : Gen(a), gb : Gen(b)) : Gen(c) =
  Gen(\(size) -> f(gen_run(ga, size), gen_run(gb, size)))

-- | Monadic bind: draw an `a`, then draw from the generator `f` picks for it.
--
-- ```prism
-- gen_at(gen_bind(gen_const(3), \(x) -> gen_const(x * 2)), 1u64, 5)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 6
-- ```
pub fn gen_bind(g : Gen(a), f : (a) -> Gen(b)) : Gen(b) =
  Gen(\(size) -> gen_run(f(gen_run(g, size)), size))

-- | Build a generator that sees the current size, for recursive shapes that
-- branch on remaining fuel.
--
-- ```prism
-- gen_at(gen_sized(\(sz) -> gen_const(sz)), 1u64, 12)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 12
-- ```
pub fn gen_sized(f : (Int) -> Gen(a)) : Gen(a) =
  Gen(\(size) -> gen_run(f(size), size))

-- | Run `g` at a fixed size, ignoring the ambient one (shrink a recursive
-- position by resizing it smaller).
--
-- ```prism
-- gen_at(gen_resize(4, gen_sized(\(sz) -> gen_const(sz))), 1u64, 99)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 4
-- ```
pub fn gen_resize(n : Int, g : Gen(a)) : Gen(a) = Gen(\(_size) -> gen_run(g, n))

-- Total non-empty indexing: `first` when `i <= 0`, else walk `rest`, falling
-- back to `first` past the end (unreachable, since callers draw `i` in range).
-- Taking the collection as head-plus-tail makes non-emptiness a type guarantee,
-- so there is no `Fail` and the generator row stays `{Random}`.
fn nth_nonempty(first : a, rest : List(a), i : Int) : a =
  if i <= 0 then
    first
  else
    match rest of
      Cons(h, t) => nth_nonempty(h, t, i - 1)
      Nil => first

-- | Pick one of `g0`/`rest` uniformly, then draw from it (one arm per
-- constructor, the shape a derived sum-type instance uses).
--
-- ```prism
-- gen_at(gen_choose(gen_const(1), [gen_const(2)]), 5u64, 3)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 1
-- ```
pub fn gen_choose(g0 : Gen(a), rest : List(Gen(a))) : Gen(a) =
  Gen() fn(size)
    gen_run(nth_nonempty(g0, rest, nat_below(1 + length(rest))), size)

-- | Pick one of the given values uniformly (`x0` or one of `rest`).
--
-- ```prism
-- gen_at(gen_one_of(10, [20, 30]), 5u64, 3)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 30
-- ```
pub fn gen_one_of(x0 : a, rest : List(a)) : Gen(a) =
  Gen(\(_size) -> nth_nonempty(x0, rest, nat_below(1 + length(rest))))

-- A signed value in `[-(size+1), size+1)`, the small readable band the numeric
-- generators fall back to between edge cases.
fn small_signed(size : Int) =
  let m = size + 1
  nat_below(2 * m) - m

-- Draw an `Int`, mixing the edge cases (`0`, `1`, `-1`, a full-width value)
-- with a small readable one so both corner and typical inputs are covered.
fn int_at(size : Int) =
  let pick = nat_below(8)
  if pick == 0 then
    0
  elif pick == 1 then
    1
  elif pick == 2 then
    -1
  elif pick == 3 then
    rand()
  else
    small_signed(size)

-- | Generator of `Int`, biased toward the edge cases (`0`, `1`, `-1`, and a
-- full-width draw) alongside small readable values.
--
-- ```prism
-- gen_at(gen_int, 42u64, 10)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- -6
-- ```
pub let gen_int : Gen(Int) = Gen(int_at)

-- | Generator of `I64`, reusing the `Int` distribution.
pub let gen_i64 : Gen(I64) = gen_map(\(x) -> to_i64(x), gen_int)

-- | Generator of `U64`, reusing the `Int` distribution (negatives wrap).
pub let gen_u64 : Gen(U64) = gen_map(\(x) -> to_u64(x), gen_int)

-- | Generator of `Bool`.
--
-- ```prism
-- gen_at(gen_bool, 7u64, 3)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- false
-- ```
pub let gen_bool : Gen(Bool) = Gen(\(_size) -> nat_below(2) == 0)

-- The nasty float draw: zeros, one, and the three non-finite values, so a
-- roundtrip or ordering property meets `NaN` and the infinities.
fn float_at(size : Int) =
  let pick = nat_below(9)
  if pick == 0 then
    0.0
  elif pick == 1 then
    1.0
  elif pick == 2 then
    0.0 - 1.0
  elif pick == 3 then
    1.0 / 0.0
  elif pick == 4 then
    (0.0 - 1.0) / 0.0
  elif pick == 5 then
    0.0 / 0.0
  else
    let m = size + 1
    to_float(small_signed(size)) / to_float(m)

-- | Generator of `Float`, including the nasty values (`+/-0`, `+/-inf`, `NaN`).
pub let gen_float : Gen(Float) = Gen(float_at)

-- | Generator of a printable-ASCII `Char`.
pub let gen_char : Gen(Char) = Gen(\(_size) -> chr(32 + nat_below(95)))

fn rand_bytes(n : Int, buf : Buf) =
  if n <= 0 then
    buf
  else
    rand_bytes(n - 1, buf_push(buf, 32 + nat_below(95)))

-- | Generator of a printable-ASCII `String`, length bounded by size.
pub let gen_string : Gen(String) =
  Gen(\(size) -> string_of_buf(rand_bytes(nat_below(size + 1), buf_empty())))

fn list_of(g : Gen(a), size : Int, n : Int) =
  if n <= 0 then
    Nil
  else
    Cons(gen_run(g, size), list_of(g, size, n - 1))

-- | Generator of a `List(a)` whose length is bounded by size.
--
-- ```prism
-- gen_at(gen_list(gen_const(1)), 7u64, 4)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [1, 1]
-- ```
pub fn gen_list(g : Gen(a)) : Gen(List(a)) =
  Gen(\(size) -> list_of(g, size, nat_below(size + 1)))

-- | Generator of `Option(a)`: `None` a quarter of the time, else `Some`.
--
-- ```prism
-- gen_at(gen_option(gen_const(5)), 3u64, 3)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- Some(5)
-- ```
pub fn gen_option(g : Gen(a)) : Gen(Option(a)) =
  Gen() fn(size)
    if nat_below(4) == 0 then
      None
    else
      Some(gen_run(g, size))

-- | Generator of a pair, both drawn at the same size.
--
-- ```prism
-- gen_at(gen_pair(gen_const(1), gen_const(2)), 1u64, 3)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- (1, 2)
-- ```
pub fn gen_pair(ga : Gen(a), gb : Gen(b)) : Gen((a, b)) =
  Gen(\(size) -> (gen_run(ga, size), gen_run(gb, size)))

-- | Generator of a triple, all drawn at the same size.
--
-- ```prism
-- gen_at(gen_triple(gen_const(1), gen_const(2), gen_const(3)), 1u64, 3)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- (1, 2, 3)
-- ```
pub fn gen_triple(ga : Gen(a), gb : Gen(b), gc : Gen(c)) : Gen((a, b, c)) =
  Gen(\(size) -> (gen_run(ga, size), gen_run(gb, size), gen_run(gc, size)))

-- | How a property run configures the seeded stream: the base `seed`, the number
-- of cases to try (`count`), and the largest size handed to a generator
-- (`max_size`).
pub type Config = Cfg { seed: U64, count: Int, max_size: Int }

-- | The default configuration: a fixed base seed, 100 cases, sizes up to 20.
--
-- ```prism
-- default_config.count
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 100
-- ```
pub let default_config : Config =
  Cfg { seed = 2463534242u64, count = 100, max_size = 20 }

-- | The result of a property run: `Passed(n)` after `n` cases held, or
-- `Failed(value, index, seed, size)` with the first counterexample and the seed
-- and size that reproduce it via `gen_at`.
pub type Outcome(a) = Passed(Int) | Failed(a, Int, U64, Int)

-- The per-case seed: a well-mixed function of the base seed and the case index,
-- so each case is independent and any single one reproduces on its own.
fn seed_for(base : U64, i : Int) : U64 =
  sm_out(base + to_u64(i) * splitmix_gamma)

fn check_go(
  cfg : Config,
  gen : Gen(a),
  prop : (a) -> Bool,
  i : Int
) : Outcome(a) =
  if i >= cfg.count then
    Passed(i)
  else
    let sz = 1 + mod(i, cfg.max_size)
    let sd = seed_for(cfg.seed, i)
    let x = gen_at(gen, sd, sz)
    if prop(x) then
      check_go(cfg, gen, prop, i + 1)
    else
      Failed(x, i, sd, sz)

-- | Run `prop` over `cfg.count` inputs from `gen`, returning the first
-- counterexample or the count that passed. Deterministic in `cfg.seed`.
--
-- ```prism
-- check_with(default_config, gen_const(2), \(x) -> x == 2)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- Quickcheck.Passed(100)
-- ```
pub fn check_with(cfg : Config, gen : Gen(a), prop : (a) -> Bool) : Outcome(a) =
  check_go(cfg, gen, prop, 0)

-- | Run `prop` over the default configuration.
--
-- ```prism
-- quickcheck(gen_int, \(x) -> x + 0 == x)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- Quickcheck.Passed(100)
-- ```
pub fn quickcheck(gen : Gen(a), prop : (a) -> Bool) : Outcome(a) =
  check_with(default_config, gen, prop)

-- | True when a run found no counterexample.
--
-- ```prism
-- passed(quickcheck(gen_int, \(x) -> x + 1 > x))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- true
-- ```
pub fn passed(o : Outcome(a)) : Bool =
  match o of
    Passed(_) => true
    Failed(_, _, _, _) => false

-- | Render an outcome for `name` as one report line (pass) or a block naming the
-- counterexample and the seed and size that reproduce it.
--
-- ```prism
-- show_outcome("positivity", Failed(0, 12, 42u64, 5))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- positivity: FAILED after 12 tests.
--   counterexample: 0
--   reproduce: seed 42 size 5
-- ```
pub fn show_outcome(name : String, o : Outcome(a)) : String given Show(a) =
  match o of
    Passed(n) => concat_all([name, ": OK, passed ", show(n), " tests."])
    Failed(x, i, sd, sz) =>
      concat_all([
          name,
          ": FAILED after ",
          show(i),
          " tests.\n  counterexample: ",
          show(x),
          "\n  reproduce: seed ",
          show(sd),
          " size ",
          show(sz),
        ])

Record/replay handlers for the capability effects.

`record` runs an action against the real world, logging each observation into a trace; `replay` re-runs the same action against a trace, performing no real IO. The trace and its entry type stay private to this module: a caller only ever threads the opaque trace `record` returns back into `replay`.

-- | Record/replay handlers for the capability effects.
--
-- `record` runs an action against the real world, logging each observation
-- into a trace; `replay` re-runs the same action against a trace, performing
-- no real IO. The trace and its entry type stay private to this module: a
-- caller only ever threads the opaque trace `record` returns back into
-- `replay`.

import Data.List (..)

import Data.String (..)

-- A raw byte read (`fs_read_bytes`) has no valid-UTF-8 string form, so it rides
-- the trace as a `TStr` carrying lowercase hex (byte-identical to the interpreter
-- recorder's frame). `hex_encode`/`hex_decode` and the `Buf` <-> `Bytes` seam do
-- that conversion; no new trace tag is needed.
import Data.Bytes (hex_encode, hex_decode)

import Wire (bytes_of_buf, bytes_buf)

type TraceEntry
  = TInt(Int)
  | TStr(String)
  | TBool(Bool)
  | TOut

alias Trace = List(TraceEntry)

-- A single multi-effect handle discharges all eight ops, parameter-passing the
-- trace through every resume (the `sfold` shape). Each arm performs the real op
-- with the matching prim_*, wraps the result as a TraceEntry, and conses it on;
-- `return` reverses the log into call order and pairs it with the result. The
-- prim_* calls give `record` the row ! {IO}.
fn rec_int(k, t, x) = k(x)(Cons(TInt(x), t))

fn rec_str(k, t, x) = k(x)(Cons(TStr(x), t))

-- A byte read: the op resumes with the raw `Buf`, but the frame stores its hex.
fn rec_bytes(k, t, buf) = k(buf)(Cons(TStr(hex_encode(bytes_of_buf(buf))), t))

fn rec_bool(k, t, x) = k(x)(Cons(TBool(x), t))

-- | Run `action` against the real world, logging every capability observation
-- (console, file, random, and environment reads) into a trace. Returns
-- `(result, trace)`; feed the trace to `replay` to reproduce the run without IO.
--
-- ```prism,no_run
-- record(\(u) -> rng_rand() + rng_rand())
-- ```
pub fn record(action) =
  let g =
    handle action(()) with
      con_read_int() resume k => \(t) -> rec_int(k, t, prim_read_int())
      con_read_line() resume k => \(t) -> rec_str(k, t, prim_read_line())
      fs_read_file(p) resume k => \(t) -> rec_str(k, t, prim_read_file(p))
      fs_read_bytes(p) resume k => \(t) -> rec_bytes(k, t, prim_read_bytes(p))
      fs_file_exists(p) resume k => \(t) -> rec_bool(k, t, prim_file_exists(p))
      rng_rand() resume k => \(t) -> rec_int(k, t, prim_rand())
      env_get(s) resume k => \(t) -> rec_str(k, t, prim_getenv(s))
      env_argc() resume k => \(t) -> rec_int(k, t, prim_args_count())
      env_arg(i) resume k => \(t) -> rec_str(k, t, prim_arg(i))
      return r => \(t) -> (r, reverse(t))
  g(Nil)

-- Pop the next entry, unwrap it to the op's result type, and resume with the
-- remainder. A wrong variant or an exhausted trace is a `fail()`, so a trace
-- that does not match the action surfaces as a recoverable failure.
fn rep_int(k, t) =
  match t of
    Cons(TInt(x), rest) => k(x)(rest)
    _ => fail()

fn rep_str(k, t) =
  match t of
    Cons(TStr(x), rest) => k(x)(rest)
    _ => fail()

-- Decode a recorded hex frame back to the raw `Buf` the byte read resumes with; a
-- payload that is not the hex a byte read wrote is a corrupt trace, so `fail`.
fn buf_of_hex(s) =
  match hex_decode(s) of
    Some(bs) => bytes_buf(bs)
    None => fail()

fn rep_bytes(k, t) =
  match t of
    Cons(TStr(s), rest) => k(buf_of_hex(s))(rest)
    _ => fail()

fn rep_bool(k, t) =
  match t of
    Cons(TBool(x), rest) => k(x)(rest)
    _ => fail()

-- | Re-run `action` against a recorded `trace`, performing no real IO: each
-- capability read is served from the trace and output is dropped, reproducing the
-- original result. Fails if the trace does not match the action.
--
-- ```prism,no_run
-- let (first, trace) = record(\(u) -> rng_rand())
-- replay(trace, \(u) -> rng_rand()) == first
-- ```
pub fn replay(trace, action) =
  let g =
    handle action(()) with
      con_read_int() resume k => \(t) -> rep_int(k, t)
      con_read_line() resume k => \(t) -> rep_str(k, t)
      fs_read_file(p) resume k => \(t) -> rep_str(k, t)
      fs_read_bytes(p) resume k => \(t) -> rep_bytes(k, t)
      fs_file_exists(p) resume k => \(t) -> rep_bool(k, t)
      rng_rand() resume k => \(t) -> rep_int(k, t)
      env_get(s) resume k => \(t) -> rep_str(k, t)
      env_argc() resume k => \(t) -> rep_int(k, t)
      env_arg(i) resume k => \(t) -> rep_str(k, t)
      out_print(x) resume k => \(t) -> k(())(t)
      out_println(x) resume k => \(t) -> k(())(t)
      return r => \(_t) -> r
  g(trace)

-- Durable trace serialization over ground types. Each TraceEntry encodes as a
-- tag char (I/S/B), the char-length of its payload, a ':' delimiter, then the
-- payload itself. The length prefix makes any payload (newlines, ':' included)
-- round-trip, so deserialize(serialize(t)) == t for every trace.
fn enc_field(tag, payload) =
  concat(tag, concat(show_int(str_len(payload)), concat(":", payload)))

fn enc_entry(e) =
  match e of
    TInt(n) => enc_field("I", show_int(n))
    TStr(s) => enc_field("S", s)
    TBool(b) => enc_field("B", if b then "1" else "0")
    TOut => enc_field("O", "")

-- | Encode a trace to a self-delimiting string for durable storage, read back
-- with `deserialize`.
--
-- ```prism,no_run
-- let (r, trace) = record(\(u) -> rng_rand())
-- write_file("run.trace", serialize(trace))
-- ```
pub fn serialize(trace) = str_join("", map(enc_entry, trace))

fn un_int(o) =
  match o of
    Some(x) => x
    None => 0

fn de_entry(tag, payload) =
  if str_eq(tag, "I") then
    TInt(un_int(parse_int(payload)))
  elif str_eq(tag, "B") then
    TBool(str_eq(payload, "1"))
  elif str_eq(tag, "O") then
    TOut
  else
    TStr(payload)

-- Parse from offset i: one tag char, decimal length up to ':', then that many
-- payload chars; advance past the payload and continue.
fn de_go(s, i, colon) =
  if i >= str_len(s) then
    Nil
  else
    let tag = substring(s, i, 1)
    let c = index_of_from(colon, s, i + 1)
    let len = un_int(parse_int(substring(s, i + 1, c - i - 1)))
    let payload = substring(s, c + 1, len)
    Cons(de_entry(tag, payload), de_go(s, c + 1 + len, colon))

-- | Decode a trace produced by `serialize`; `deserialize(serialize(t))` is `t`.
--
-- The frames are self-delimiting (tag, length, `:`, payload), so the encoding
-- round-trips through text:
--
-- ```prism
-- serialize(deserialize("I2:42S3:abc"))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- I2:42S3:abc
-- ```
pub fn deserialize(s) = de_go(s, 0, char_at(":", 0))

-- Durable record/replay driver. A persisted log freezes the observations of an
-- interrupted run; a re-run replays that prefix (no real IO) and, once it is
-- exhausted, performs each NEW op for real. The state threaded through every
-- resume is just the remaining-to-replay trace: an op consumes its head when
-- replaying, and when the trace runs out the op goes live. Each live observation
-- appends ONE self-delimiting frame to the log (O(1), not a whole-file rewrite),
-- so the total cost is linear and a crash leaves a well-formed prefix.
fn persist_entry(path, e) = append_file(path, enc_entry(e))

-- An input op: serve its recorded value from the trace head while replaying, or
-- perform the real read and append the recorded value once the trace is spent. A
-- head of the wrong variant means the trace does not match the action, a `fail`.
fn step_int(path, k, t, real) =
  match t of
    Cons(TInt(x), rest) => k(x)(rest)
    Cons(_, _) => fail()
    Nil =>
      let x = real(())
      persist_entry(path, TInt(x))
      k(x)(Nil)

fn step_str(path, k, t, real) =
  match t of
    Cons(TStr(x), rest) => k(x)(rest)
    Cons(_, _) => fail()
    Nil =>
      let x = real(())
      persist_entry(path, TStr(x))
      k(x)(Nil)

-- The byte-read counterpart of `step_str`: replay a recorded hex frame as the raw
-- `Buf`, or perform the real read and append its hex once the trace is spent.
fn step_bytes(path, k, t, real) =
  match t of
    Cons(TStr(s), rest) => k(buf_of_hex(s))(rest)
    Cons(_, _) => fail()
    Nil =>
      let buf = real(())
      persist_entry(path, TStr(hex_encode(bytes_of_buf(buf))))
      k(buf)(Nil)

fn step_bool(path, k, t, real) =
  match t of
    Cons(TBool(x), rest) => k(x)(rest)
    Cons(_, _) => fail()
    Nil =>
      let x = real(())
      persist_entry(path, TBool(x))
      k(x)(Nil)

-- An output op records a `TOut` marker interleaved with the inputs, so an output
-- that already ran is replayed (dropped) rather than re-performed. While the
-- trace head is that marker the output is suppressed; once the trace is spent the
-- output goes live. The marker is committed BEFORE the real emit, so a resumed
-- run never double-prints an already-recorded output; the only residual window
-- is a crash between the frame append and the emit itself (one observation wide),
-- which the wire codec's atomic frame will later close.
fn out_step(path, k, t, real) =
  match t of
    Cons(TOut, rest) => k(())(rest)
    Cons(_, _) => fail()
    Nil =>
      persist_entry(path, TOut)
      real(())
      k(())(Nil)

-- | Durable record/replay against a persisted log at `path`: replay the recorded
-- prefix with no real IO, then perform each new observation for real, appending a
-- frame per observation so an interrupted run resumes where it left off, exactly
-- once at the crash boundary.
--
-- ```prism,no_run
-- durable("target/run.log", \(u) -> rng_rand() + rng_rand())
-- ```
pub fn durable(path, action) =
  let loaded =
    if prim_file_exists(path) then
      deserialize(prim_read_file(path))
    else
      Nil
  let g =
    handle action(()) with
      con_read_int() resume k =>
        \(t) -> step_int(path, k, t, \(_z) -> prim_read_int())
      con_read_line() resume k =>
        \(t) -> step_str(path, k, t, \(_z) -> prim_read_line())
      fs_read_file(p) resume k =>
        \(t) -> step_str(path, k, t, \(_z) -> prim_read_file(p))
      fs_read_bytes(p) resume k =>
        \(t) -> step_bytes(path, k, t, \(_z) -> prim_read_bytes(p))
      fs_file_exists(p) resume k =>
        \(t) -> step_bool(path, k, t, \(_z) -> prim_file_exists(p))
      rng_rand() resume k => \(t) -> step_int(path, k, t, \(_z) -> prim_rand())
      env_get(s) resume k =>
        \(t) -> step_str(path, k, t, \(_z) -> prim_getenv(s))
      env_argc() resume k =>
        \(t) -> step_int(path, k, t, \(_z) -> prim_args_count())
      env_arg(i) resume k => \(t) -> step_str(path, k, t, \(_z) -> prim_arg(i))
      out_print(x) resume k =>
        \(t) -> out_step(path, k, t, \(_z) -> prim_print(x))
      out_println(x) resume k =>
        \(t) -> out_step(path, k, t, \(_z) -> prim_println(x))
      return r => \(_t) -> r
  g(loaded)

The one lazy iteration protocol: pull-based sequences with natural names.

A `Sequence` is a pull producer: a thunk that, when forced with `(())`, yields one `Step` -- either `SDone` (exhausted) or `SMore(x, rest)`, the next element `x` paired with the thunk producing the remainder. Nothing is materialized up front; each `(())` advances the stream by one element. A transformer (`map`, `filter`, `take`, ...) wraps a producer in a new producer that pulls, reshapes, and re-yields; a consumer (`fold`, `sum`, `to_list`, ...) drives the producer to exhaustion and folds the elements into a value.

## Type

```text
type Step(a) = SDone | SMore(a, (Unit) -> Step(a))
Seq(a)       = (Unit) -> Step(a)          -- read `Seq(a)` in the prose as this
```

The step continuation is ordinary data, not an effect, so every combinator is a total pure function over `Step`. That is the whole reason this substrate exists: an earlier push design routed elements through a shared `Emit` effect, and a single `Emit(a)` label per scope made element-type changes, heterogeneous `zip`, and mixing two element types in one function unrepresentable. On pull `Step` the element type is a plain type parameter, so `map : Seq(a) -> Seq(b)` type-changes freely, `zip : (Seq(a), Seq(b)) -> Seq((a, b))` is genuinely heterogeneous, and a consumer's per-element function may perform any ambient effect (it runs directly, with no handler closing the row over it). Every combinator below exercises one of those, and the correctness corpus in `tests/cases/run` pins them on both backends.

## Effect-polymorphic consumers

`for_each`'s function argument runs in the ambient row: `for_each(s, \(x) -> println(x))` threads `IO` straight out with no annotation, because the driver is a plain recursion and installs no handler. This is the effectful-mapper case the push substrate could not express.

## Naming and the import idiom

The combinators keep their natural names (`map`, `filter`, `take`, `zip`, ...), which collide with Base's eager `List` surface. That is why this module is opt-in and NOT in Base: the flat namespace has no shadowing, so the documented idiom is a qualified import at the use site:

```text
import Sequence as Seq          -- qualified: Seq.map, Seq.filter, Seq.take
Seq.to_list(Seq.filter(Seq.map(Seq.range(1, 100), \(x) -> x * x), even))
```

A selective `import Sequence (unfold, iterate)` also works for names that do not clash with Base.

## Fusion and allocation

A pull pipeline is correct and constant-space per stage. At `-O1`, each transformer stage allocates one `SMore` cons and one step thunk per element. At `-O2`, stream fusion collapses the supported `range`/`map`/`filter`/`take` and fold pipelines through the module boundary, so they allocate no intermediate step cells. The performance gates pin that zero slope; shapes outside the recognizer retain the per-stage allocation. The algebraic-effect `EOp` counter remains zero because pulling a sequence performs no effects. The eager `Data.List` surface fuses through FBIP reuse and remains the natural choice for strict traversal, while `Sequence` provides early exit and infinite producers.

-- | The one lazy iteration protocol: pull-based sequences with natural names.
--
-- A `Sequence` is a pull producer: a thunk that, when forced with `(())`, yields
-- one `Step` -- either `SDone` (exhausted) or `SMore(x, rest)`, the next element
-- `x` paired with the thunk producing the remainder. Nothing is materialized up
-- front; each `(())` advances the stream by one element. A transformer (`map`,
-- `filter`, `take`, ...) wraps a producer in a new producer that pulls, reshapes,
-- and re-yields; a consumer (`fold`, `sum`, `to_list`, ...) drives the producer to
-- exhaustion and folds the elements into a value.
--
-- ## Type
--
-- ```text
-- type Step(a) = SDone | SMore(a, (Unit) -> Step(a))
-- Seq(a)       = (Unit) -> Step(a)          -- read `Seq(a)` in the prose as this
-- ```
--
-- The step continuation is ordinary data, not an effect, so every combinator is a
-- total pure function over `Step`. That is the whole reason this substrate exists:
-- an earlier push design routed elements through a shared `Emit` effect, and a
-- single `Emit(a)` label per scope made element-type changes, heterogeneous `zip`,
-- and mixing two element types in one function unrepresentable. On pull `Step` the
-- element type is a plain type parameter, so `map : Seq(a) -> Seq(b)` type-changes
-- freely, `zip : (Seq(a), Seq(b)) -> Seq((a, b))` is genuinely heterogeneous, and a
-- consumer's per-element function may perform any ambient effect (it runs directly,
-- with no handler closing the row over it). Every combinator below exercises one of
-- those, and the correctness corpus in `tests/cases/run` pins them on both backends.
--
-- ## Effect-polymorphic consumers
--
-- `for_each`'s function argument runs in the ambient row: `for_each(s, \(x) ->
-- println(x))` threads `IO` straight out with no annotation, because the driver is
-- a plain recursion and installs no handler. This is the effectful-mapper case the
-- push substrate could not express.
--
-- ## Naming and the import idiom
--
-- The combinators keep their natural names (`map`, `filter`, `take`, `zip`, ...),
-- which collide with Base's eager `List` surface. That is why this module is
-- opt-in and NOT in Base: the flat namespace has no shadowing, so the
-- documented idiom is a qualified import at the use site:
--
-- ```text
-- import Sequence as Seq          -- qualified: Seq.map, Seq.filter, Seq.take
-- Seq.to_list(Seq.filter(Seq.map(Seq.range(1, 100), \(x) -> x * x), even))
-- ```
--
-- A selective `import Sequence (unfold, iterate)` also works for names that do not
-- clash with Base.
--
-- ## Fusion and allocation
--
-- A pull pipeline is correct and constant-space per stage. At `-O1`, each
-- transformer stage allocates one `SMore` cons and one step thunk per element. At
-- `-O2`, stream fusion collapses the supported `range`/`map`/`filter`/`take` and
-- fold pipelines through the module boundary, so they allocate no intermediate
-- step cells. The performance gates pin that zero slope; shapes outside the
-- recognizer retain the per-stage allocation. The algebraic-effect `EOp` counter
-- remains zero because pulling a sequence performs no effects. The eager
-- `Data.List` surface fuses through FBIP reuse and remains the natural choice for
-- strict traversal, while `Sequence` provides early exit and infinite producers.

-- `reverse`/`tail` are the only list helpers not shadowed by a combinator name
-- here; list append is written locally as `app_list` because `append` is the
-- sequence combinator below. Bytes iteration rides the `Data.Bytes` vocabulary.
import Data.List (reverse, tail)

import Data.Bytes (Bytes, bytes_empty, bytes_push, bytes_length, bytes_index)

-- The pull step: `SDone` ends the stream, `SMore(x, rest)` yields `x` and the thunk
-- producing everything after it.
pub type Step(a) = SDone | SMore(a, (Unit) -> Step(a))

-- ============================================================================
-- Producers
-- ============================================================================

-- | The empty sequence: yields nothing.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.to_list(Seq.empty())
-- ```
-- ```output
-- []
-- ```
pub fn empty() : (Unit) -> Step(a) = \(u) -> SDone

-- | The one-element sequence yielding `x`.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.to_list(Seq.singleton(42))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [42]
-- ```
pub fn singleton(x : a) : (Unit) -> Step(a) = \(u) -> SMore(x, \(v) -> SDone)

-- | The ascending integers in `[lo, hi)`. Self-recursive: the continuation is the
-- next `range`, so no element is built until pulled.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.to_list(Seq.range(1, 5))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [1, 2, 3, 4]
-- ```
pub fn range(lo : Int, hi : Int) : (Unit) -> Step(Int) =
  \(u) -> if lo < hi then SMore(lo, range(lo + 1, hi)) else SDone

-- | The container boundary in: the elements of list `xs`, in order.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.to_list(Seq.from_list([1, 2, 3]))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [1, 2, 3]
-- ```
pub fn from_list(xs : List(a)) : (Unit) -> Step(a) =
  \(u) -> match xs of { Nil => SDone, Cons(x, rest) => SMore(x, from_list(rest)) }

-- | The infinite sequence `x, f(x), f(f(x)), ...`. Bound it with `take`.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.to_list(Seq.take(Seq.iterate(1, \(x) -> x * 2), 4))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [1, 2, 4, 8]
-- ```
pub fn iterate(x : a, f : (a) -> a) : (Unit) -> Step(a) =
  \(u) -> SMore(x, iterate(f(x), f))

-- | The infinite sequence of `x` repeated. Bound it with `take`.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.to_list(Seq.take(Seq.repeat(7), 3))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [7, 7, 7]
-- ```
pub fn repeat(x : a) : (Unit) -> Step(a) = \(u) -> SMore(x, repeat(x))

-- | The generator producer: yield `x` for each `Some((x, seed'))` that `step`
-- returns from the running seed, stopping at `None`. Every finite producer is a
-- special case; on pull `Step` a generator is just a fold over the seed, needing no
-- coroutine or handler.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.to_list(Seq.unfold(1, \(n) -> if n <= 3 then Some((n, n + 1)) else None))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [1, 2, 3]
-- ```
pub fn unfold(seed : s, step : (s) -> Option((a, s))) : (Unit) -> Step(a) =
  \(u) -> match step(seed) of { None => SDone, Some(pair) => match pair of { (x, seed2) => SMore(x, unfold(seed2, step)) } }

-- ============================================================================
-- Transformers (each a new producer wrapping its input)
-- ============================================================================

-- | Apply `f` to every element. Type-changing: `Seq(a) -> Seq(b)`.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.to_list(Seq.map(Seq.range(1, 4), \(x) -> x * x))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [1, 4, 9]
-- ```
pub fn map(s : (Unit) -> Step(a), f : (a) -> b) : (Unit) -> Step(b) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => SMore(f(x), map(next, f)) }

-- | Keep only the elements satisfying `p`.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.to_list(Seq.filter(Seq.range(1, 7), \(x) -> mod(x, 2) == 0))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [2, 4, 6]
-- ```
pub fn filter(s : (Unit) -> Step(a), p : (a) -> Bool) : (Unit) -> Step(a) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => if p(x) then SMore(x, filter(next, p)) else filter(next, p)(()) }

-- | Map and filter in one pass: yield `y` for each `f(x) == Some(y)`, dropping the
-- `None`s.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.to_list(Seq.filter_map(Seq.range(1, 5), \(x) -> if x > 2 then Some(x * 10) else None))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [30, 40]
-- ```
pub fn filter_map(s : (Unit) -> Step(a), f : (a) -> Option(b)) : (Unit) -> Step(b) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => match f(x) of { None => filter_map(next, f)(()), Some(y) => SMore(y, filter_map(next, f)) } }

-- | Concatenate two sequences: all of `s`, then all of `t`.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.to_list(Seq.append(Seq.range(1, 3), Seq.range(10, 12)))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [1, 2, 10, 11]
-- ```
pub fn append(s : (Unit) -> Step(a), t : (Unit) -> Step(a)) : (Unit) -> Step(a) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => t(()), SMore(x, next) => SMore(x, append(next, t)) }

-- | For each element `x`, splice in the sequence `f(x)`.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.to_list(Seq.flat_map(Seq.range(1, 4), \(x) -> Seq.range(0, x)))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [0, 0, 1, 0, 1, 2]
-- ```
pub fn flat_map(
  s : (Unit) -> Step(a),
  f : (a) -> (Unit) -> Step(b)
) : (Unit) -> Step(b) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => append(f(x), flat_map(next, f))(()) }

-- | The first `n` elements, stopping the producer once the budget is spent.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.to_list(Seq.take(Seq.range(1, 100), 3))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [1, 2, 3]
-- ```
pub fn take(s : (Unit) -> Step(a), n : Int) : (Unit) -> Step(a) =
  \(u) -> if n <= 0 then SDone else match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => SMore(x, take(next, n - 1)) }

-- | Skip the first `n` elements, yielding the rest.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.to_list(Seq.drop(Seq.range(1, 6), 2))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [3, 4, 5]
-- ```
pub fn drop(s : (Unit) -> Step(a), n : Int) : (Unit) -> Step(a) =
  \(u) -> if n <= 0 then s(()) else match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => drop(next, n - 1)(()) }

-- | The longest prefix whose elements satisfy `p`; stops at the first failure.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.to_list(Seq.take_while(Seq.range(1, 10), \(x) -> x < 4))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [1, 2, 3]
-- ```
pub fn take_while(s : (Unit) -> Step(a), p : (a) -> Bool) : (Unit) -> Step(a) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => if p(x) then SMore(x, take_while(next, p)) else SDone }

-- | Drop the longest prefix satisfying `p`, yielding the rest.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.to_list(Seq.drop_while(Seq.range(1, 6), \(x) -> x < 3))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [3, 4, 5]
-- ```
pub fn drop_while(s : (Unit) -> Step(a), p : (a) -> Bool) : (Unit) -> Step(a) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => if p(x) then drop_while(next, p)(()) else SMore(x, next) }

-- | Drop consecutive duplicates, keeping the first of each run (needs `Eq(a)`).
-- Left unsigned so the `Eq(a)` constraint is inferred from `==`.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.to_list(Seq.dedup(Seq.from_list([1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3])))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [1, 2, 3]
-- ```
pub fn dedup(s) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => SMore(x, dedup_after(x, next)) }

-- | Helper for `dedup`: drop elements equal to the just-emitted `prev`.
fn dedup_after(prev, s) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => if x == prev then dedup_after(prev, next)(()) else SMore(x, dedup_after(x, next)) }

-- | Pair each element with its zero-based index, yielding `(i, x)`.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.to_list(Seq.enumerate(Seq.from_list(["a", "b"])))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [(0, a), (1, b)]
-- ```
pub fn enumerate(s : (Unit) -> Step(a)) : (Unit) -> Step((Int, a)) =
  enumerate_from(s, 0)

-- | Helper for `enumerate`: index from `i`.
fn enumerate_from(s, i) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => SMore((i, x), enumerate_from(next, i + 1)) }

-- | The running left-fold, streamed: yield `z`, then each successive accumulator.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.to_list(Seq.scan(Seq.range(1, 4), 0, \(acc, x) -> acc + x))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [0, 1, 3, 6]
-- ```
pub fn scan(s : (Unit) -> Step(a), z : b, f : (b, a) -> b) : (Unit) -> Step(b) =
  \(u) -> SMore(z, scan_go(s, z, f))

-- | Helper for `scan`: yield the accumulator after each element.
fn scan_go(s, z, f) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => let z2 = f(z, x) in SMore(z2, scan_go(next, z2, f)) }

-- | Alternate elements of `s` and `t` (`s0, t0, s1, t1, ...`); when one runs out,
-- yield the whole remainder of the other. Streamed, no materialization.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.to_list(Seq.interleave(Seq.range(1, 4), Seq.range(10, 12)))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [1, 10, 2, 11, 3]
-- ```
pub fn interleave(
  s : (Unit) -> Step(a),
  t : (Unit) -> Step(a)
) : (Unit) -> Step(a) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => t(()), SMore(x, next) => SMore(x, interleave(t, next)) }

-- ============================================================================
-- Binary combinators (heterogeneous: the pull-substrate win over push `Emit`)
-- ============================================================================

-- | Pair two sequences element-wise, stopping at the shorter. Genuinely
-- heterogeneous: `Seq(a)` and `Seq(b)` yield `Seq((a, b))`.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.to_list(Seq.zip(Seq.range(1, 4), Seq.from_list(["a", "b", "c"])))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [(1, a), (2, b), (3, c)]
-- ```
pub fn zip(s : (Unit) -> Step(a), t : (Unit) -> Step(b)) : (Unit) -> Step((a, b)) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, sn) => match t(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(y, tn) => SMore((x, y), zip(sn, tn)) } }

-- | Combine two sequences element-wise with `f`, stopping when either runs out.
-- Heterogeneous in both operand types.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.to_list(Seq.zip_with(Seq.range(1, 4), Seq.range(10, 13), \(a, b) -> a + b))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [11, 13, 15]
-- ```
pub fn zip_with(
  s : (Unit) -> Step(a),
  t : (Unit) -> Step(b),
  f : (a, b) -> c
) : (Unit) -> Step(c) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, sn) => match t(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(y, tn) => SMore(f(x, y), zip_with(sn, tn, f)) } }

-- ============================================================================
-- Chunking and windowing (buffer O(n) elements by nature; still streamed)
-- ============================================================================

-- | Group elements into consecutive lists of length `n` (the final chunk may be
-- shorter). Pulls one group at a time, holding only the current group.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.to_list(Seq.chunk(Seq.range(1, 6), 2))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [[1, 2], [3, 4], [5]]
-- ```
pub fn chunk(s : (Unit) -> Step(a), n : Int) : (Unit) -> Step(List(a)) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => match chunk_grab(next, n - 1, Cons(x, Nil)) of { (group, rest) => SMore(group, chunk(rest, n)) } }

-- | Helper for `chunk`: grab up to `n` more elements into the reversed `acc`,
-- returning the finished (forward-order) group and the remaining sequence.
fn chunk_grab(s, n, acc) =
  if n <= 0 then
    (reverse(acc), s)
  else
    match s(()) of
      SDone => (reverse(acc), empty())
      SMore(x, next) => chunk_grab(next, n - 1, Cons(x, acc))

-- | Every contiguous length-`n` sliding window, in order. Fewer than `n` elements
-- yields nothing. Holds one window (`n` elements) at a time.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.to_list(Seq.window(Seq.range(1, 5), 2))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [[1, 2], [2, 3], [3, 4]]
-- ```
pub fn window(s : (Unit) -> Step(a), n : Int) : (Unit) -> Step(List(a)) =
  \(u) -> match grab_n(s, n, Nil) of { None => SDone, Some(pair) => match pair of { (buf, rest) => SMore(buf, window_slide(buf, rest)) } }

-- | Helper for `window`: pull exactly `n` elements, or `None` if fewer remain.
fn grab_n(s, n, acc) =
  if n <= 0 then
    Some((reverse(acc), s))
  else
    match s(()) of
      SDone => None
      SMore(x, next) => grab_n(next, n - 1, Cons(x, acc))

-- | Helper for `window`: slide by dropping the oldest element and appending the
-- next one pulled from `rest`.
fn window_slide(buf, rest) =
  \(u) -> match rest(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => let buf2 = app_list(tail(buf), Cons(x, Nil)) in SMore(buf2, window_slide(buf2, next)) }

-- | Local list append (`append` names the sequence combinator above).
fn app_list(xs, ys) =
  match xs of
    Nil => ys
    Cons(x, r) => Cons(x, app_list(r, ys))

-- ============================================================================
-- Consumers (drive the producer, folding elements into a value)
-- ============================================================================

-- | Left-fold the sequence with `f` from initial accumulator `z`.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.fold(Seq.range(1, 5), 0, \(acc, x) -> acc + x)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 10
-- ```
pub fn fold(s, z, f) =
  match s(()) of
    SDone => z
    SMore(x, next) => fold(next, f(z, x), f)

-- | Run `f` for its effects on each element, in order. Effect-polymorphic: `f` runs
-- in the ambient row (no handler intervenes), so `for_each(s, \(x) -> println(x))`
-- threads `IO` out. The explicit `{| e}` row matters: unsigned, the
-- self-recursion would infer `f` as pure and reject an effectful body.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.for_each(Seq.range(1, 4), \(x) -> println(show(x)))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 1
-- 2
-- 3
-- ```
pub fn for_each(s : (Unit) -> Step(a), f : (a) -> Unit ! {| e}) =
  match s(()) of
    SDone => ()
    SMore(x, next) =>
      f(x)
      for_each(next, f)

-- | Sum a sequence of integers.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.sum(Seq.range(1, 5))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 10
-- ```
pub fn sum(s) = fold(s, 0, \(acc, x) -> acc + x)

-- | Product of a sequence of integers.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.product(Seq.range(1, 5))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 24
-- ```
pub fn product(s) = fold(s, 1, \(acc, x) -> acc * x)

-- | The number of elements.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.count(Seq.range(1, 100))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- 99
-- ```
pub fn count(s) = fold(s, 0, \(acc, x) -> acc + 1)

-- | Collect the sequence into a list, in order. The container boundary out.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.to_list(Seq.map(Seq.range(1, 4), \(x) -> x + 100))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- [101, 102, 103]
-- ```
pub fn to_list(s) = reverse(fold(s, Nil, \(acc, x) -> Cons(x, acc)))

-- | The first element, or `None` if the sequence is empty.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.head(Seq.range(5, 10))
-- ```
-- ```output
-- Some(5)
-- ```
pub fn head(s) =
  match s(()) of
    SDone => None
    SMore(x, next) => Some(x)

-- | The first element satisfying `p`, or `None`; stops the producer at the match.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.find(Seq.range(1, 100), \(x) -> x > 10)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- Some(11)
-- ```
pub fn find(s, p) =
  match s(()) of
    SDone => None
    SMore(x, next) =>
      if p(x) then
        Some(x)
      else
        find(next, p)

-- | True when some element satisfies `p`; short-circuits.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.any(Seq.range(1, 5), \(x) -> x == 3)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- true
-- ```
pub fn any(s, p) =
  match find(s, p) of
    Some(u) => true
    None => false

-- | True when every element satisfies `p`; short-circuits on the first failure.
--
-- ```prism
-- # import Sequence as Seq
-- Seq.all(Seq.range(1, 5), \(x) -> x < 10)
-- ```
-- ```output
-- true
-- ```
pub fn all(s, p) =
  match find(s, \(x) -> not(p(x))) of
    Some(u) => false
    None => true

-- ============================================================================
-- Bytes boundary
-- ============================================================================

-- | The bytes of `bs` as a sequence of ints in `0..255`, in order.
pub fn from_bytes(bs : Bytes) : (Unit) -> Step(Int) = from_bytes_at(bs, 0)

-- | Helper for `from_bytes`: yield from index `i`.
fn from_bytes_at(bs, i) =
  \(u) -> if i < bytes_length(bs) then SMore(bytes_index(bs, i), from_bytes_at(bs, i + 1)) else SDone

-- | Collect a sequence of ints (each masked to a byte) into a `Bytes`. The Bytes
-- container boundary out.
pub fn to_bytes(s) = fold(s, bytes_empty, \(acc, x) -> bytes_push(acc, x))

The checked mobility boundary for portable, single-use computations.

`teleport` runs such a computation as a unit that is safe to move to a fresh runtime. The closure handed to it must capture only content-addressed code and portable data (`@ portable`) and be invoked at most once (`@ once`); the compiler proves that contract at every call site. Running a teleported closure is observationally identical to calling it directly -- how a computation is placed is never observable, the same invariant that makes tier and backend choice invisible -- so `teleport` is the checked boundary, not a change in behavior. Compose it with `Replay.record` for a durable, replayable mobile run.
