defs.doc: Structural sequencing via `bind`. Side effects ride the effect system, so this is for `List`/`Option`-style structure rather than do-notation.

defs.name: monadList
defs.source:
instance monadList : Monad(List)
  fn bind(xs, g) = concat_map(g, xs)

defs.name: monadOption
defs.source:
instance monadOption : Monad(Option)
  fn bind(o, g) = option_bind(o, g)

defs.name: Traversable
defs.source:
class Traversable(t) given Functor(t), Foldable(t)
  traverse : ((a) -> b ! {| e}, t(a)) -> t(b) ! {| e}
defs.doc: An effect-polymorphic traversal: `traverse` is an effectful `map`, the per-element effect row `e` replacing the classic `Applicative` parameter.

defs.name: traversableList
defs.source:
instance traversableList : Traversable(List)
  fn traverse(g, xs) = map(g, xs)

defs.name: traversableOption
defs.source:
instance traversableOption : Traversable(Option)
  fn traverse(g, o) = map_option(g, o)

defs.name: insert_by_ord
defs.source:
fn insert_by_ord(x : a, xs : List(a)) : List(a) given Ord(a) =
  match xs of
    Nil => Cons(x, Nil)
    Cons(y, rest) =>
      if cmp(x, y) <= 0 then
        Cons(x, xs)
      else
        Cons(y, insert_by_ord(x, rest))
defs.doc:
Insert `x` into an already-sorted list, keeping it sorted (`Ord`).

```prism
insert_by_ord(3, [1, 2, 4])
```

```output
[1, 2, 3, 4]
```

defs.name: merge_by_ord
defs.source:
fn merge_by_ord(xs : List(a), ys : List(a)) : List(a) given Ord(a) =
  match xs of
    Nil => ys
    Cons(x, xr) =>
      match ys of
        Nil => xs
        Cons(y, yr) =>
          if cmp(x, y) <= 0 then
            Cons(x, merge_by_ord(xr, ys))
          else
            Cons(y, merge_by_ord(xs, yr))
defs.doc:
Stable merge of two already-sorted lists. The recursive `Cons` becomes a loop by tail-recursion-modulo-cons, and Perceus reuses the consumed cells.

```prism
merge_by_ord([1, 3], [2, 4])
```

```output
[1, 2, 3, 4]
```

defs.name: sort_by_ord
defs.source:
fn sort_by_ord(xs : List(a)) : List(a) given Ord(a) =
  match xs of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(_, Nil) => xs
    _ =>
      let mid = length(xs) / 2
      let (l, r) = split_at(mid, xs)
      merge_by_ord(sort_by_ord(l), sort_by_ord(r))
defs.doc: The generic stable merge sort behind `sort`, for any `Ord` element type.

defs.name: Fresh
defs.source:
effect Fresh
  fresh() : Int
defs.doc: Draw the next integer from the monotonic counter.

defs.name: run_fresh
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (() -> a ! {Control.Fresh.Fresh, Var@n@5, e0}) -> a ! {e0}
defs.source: fn run_fresh(action : () -> a ! {Fresh | e}) : a = run_fresh_from(0, action)
defs.doc:
Run `action` with a fresh-name counter starting at `0`, discharging `Fresh`.

```prism
run_fresh(\() -> [gensym("tmp"), gensym("tmp")])
```

```output
[tmp0, tmp1]
```

defs.name: run_fresh_from
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (Int, () -> a ! {Control.Fresh.Fresh, Var@n@5, e0}) -> a ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn run_fresh_from(start : Int, action : () -> a ! {Fresh | e}) : a =
  var n := start
  handle action() with
    fresh() resume k =>
      let v = n
      n := n + 1
      k(v)
    return r => r
defs.doc:
Run `action` with the counter starting at `start`.

```prism
run_fresh_from(10, \() -> [fresh(), fresh()])
```

```output
[10, 11]
```

defs.name: gensym
defs.source:
fn gensym(prefix : String) : String ! {Fresh} =
  concat(prefix, show_int(fresh()))
defs.doc: A fresh string identifier: `prefix` followed by the next counter value.

defs.name: Layer
defs.source: type Layer(a) = Layer { kids: (a) -> List(a), rebuild: (a, List(a)) -> a }
defs.doc: One node sort's one-layer view: its immediate children and the inverse that replaces them. `rebuild(x, kids(x))` must return a node equal to `x`, and `rebuild` must fail closed (return `x` unchanged) when the replacement list does not match the node's shape.

defs.name: plate_layer
defs.source:
fn plate_layer() : Layer(a) given Plate(a) =
  Layer { kids = children, rebuild = plate_rebuild }
defs.doc:
The layer a `Plate` instance supplies, so a sort that derived `Plate` joins every traversal here and in `Control.Rewrite` without a hand-written pair.

The two interfaces agree on the shape and disagree only on how they report a violation of it, and that disagreement is the whole of the translation: `rebuild` raises `Fail` on a replacement list that does not match the node, and a layer says the same thing by returning the node unchanged. Nothing else is adapted, because `children` is already the order `kids` promises.

defs.name: plate_rebuild
defs.source:
fn plate_rebuild(x : a, cs : List(a)) : a given Plate(a) =
  handle rebuild(x, cs) with
    never fail() => x
    return r => r

defs.name: lay_kids
defs.source: fn lay_kids(p : Layer(a), x : a) : List(a) = (p.kids)(x)
defs.doc: The immediate children of `x`, in the layer's fixed order.

defs.name: lay_rebuild
defs.source: fn lay_rebuild(p : Layer(a), x : a, cs : List(a)) : a = (p.rebuild)(x, cs)
defs.doc: `x` with its immediate children replaced by `cs`, in the layer's order.

defs.name: lay_descend
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (Control.Layer.Layer(a), (a) -> a ! {e0}, a) -> a ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn lay_descend(p : Layer(a), f : (a) -> a ! {| e}, x : a) : a ! { | e} =
  lay_rebuild(p, x, map(f, lay_kids(p, x)))
defs.doc: Apply `f` to each immediate child of `x` and rebuild. The one-layer map: it never recurses, so a traversal scheme built on it controls its own depth.

defs.name: lay_universe
defs.source:
fn lay_universe(p : Layer(a), x : a) : List(a) =
  Cons(x, concat_map(\(c) -> lay_universe(p, c), lay_kids(p, x)))
defs.doc: Every node of the tree, root first, depth first in `kids` order.

defs.name: lay_size
defs.source: fn lay_size(p : Layer(a), x : a) : Int = length(lay_universe(p, x))
defs.doc:
The number of nodes in the tree.

```prism
# let countdown = Layer { kids = \(n) -> if n > 0 then [n - 1] else [], rebuild = \(n, _cs) -> n }
lay_size(countdown, 3)
```

```output
4
```

defs.name: lay_depth
defs.source:
fn lay_depth(p : Layer(a), x : a) : Int =
  1 + foldl(\(acc, c) -> max(acc, lay_depth(p, c)), 0, lay_kids(p, x))
defs.doc:
The height of the tree: `1` at a leaf.

```prism
# let countdown = Layer { kids = \(n) -> if n > 0 then [n - 1] else [], rebuild = \(n, _cs) -> n }
lay_depth(countdown, 3)
```

```output
4
```

defs.name: lay_collect
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (Control.Layer.Layer(a), (a) -> Bool ! {e0}, a) -> List(a) ! {e0}
defs.doc:
Every node satisfying `q`, root first, depth first. The gather half of an analysis pass: one predicate replaces a hand-written collecting recursion.

```prism
# let countdown = Layer { kids = \(n) -> if n > 0 then [n - 1] else [], rebuild = \(n, _cs) -> n }
lay_collect(countdown, even, 3)
```

```output
[2, 0]
```

defs.name: lay_count_where
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (Control.Layer.Layer(a), (a) -> Bool ! {e0}, a) -> Int ! {e0}
defs.doc: How many nodes satisfy `q`.

defs.name: lay_any
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (Control.Layer.Layer(a), (a) -> Bool ! {e0}, a) -> Bool ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn lay_any(p : Layer(a), q : (a) -> Bool ! {| e}, x : a) : Bool ! { | e} =
  if q(x) then
    true
  else
    lay_any_list(p, q, lay_kids(p, x))
defs.doc: Whether any node satisfies `q`. Short-circuits: the first accepting node ends the walk, so a hit near the root costs nothing.

defs.name: lay_any_list
defs.source:
fn lay_any_list(
  p : Layer(a),
  q : (a) -> Bool ! {| e},
  xs : List(a)
) : Bool ! { | e} =
  match xs of
    Nil => false
    Cons(c, rest) =>
      if lay_any(p, q, c) then
        true
      else
        lay_any_list(p, q, rest)

defs.name: lay_summarize
defs.ty: forall e0 a b. (Control.Layer.Layer(a), (a) -> b ! {e0}, (b, b) -> b ! {e0}, b, a) -> b ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn lay_summarize(
  p : Layer(a),
  measure : (a) -> b ! {| e},
  combine : (b, b) -> b ! {| e},
  unit : b,
  x : a
) : b ! { | e} =
  foldl(\(acc, n) -> combine(acc, measure(n)), unit, lay_universe(p, x))
defs.doc: Fold a per-node summary over the whole tree: `measure` scores one node and `combine` merges two summaries, starting from `unit`. The caller supplies the combining operation, so one walk serves counting, maximizing, and collecting alike.

defs.name: lay_index_where
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (Control.Layer.Layer(a), (a) -> Bool ! {e0}, a) -> List(Int) ! {e0}
defs.doc: The preorder index of every node satisfying `q`. An index is a deterministic address into the tree: `0` is the root, and the numbering is fixed because `kids` is.

defs.name: lay_index_go
defs.ty: forall e0 a. ((a) -> Bool ! {e0}, List(a), Int) -> List(Int) ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn lay_index_go(
  q : (a) -> Bool ! {| e},
  xs : List(a),
  i : Int
) : List(Int) ! { | e} =
  match xs of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(n, rest) =>
      if q(n) then
        Cons(i, lay_index_go(q, rest, i + 1))
      else
        lay_index_go(q, rest, i + 1)

defs.name: lay_at_index
defs.source:
fn lay_at_index(p : Layer(a), i : Int, x : a) : Option(a) =
  nth(i, lay_universe(p, x))
defs.doc: The node at a preorder index, or `None` when the index is past the end.

defs.name: lay_path_to
defs.source:
fn lay_path_to(p : Layer(a), i : Int, x : a) : Option(List(Int)) =
  lay_path_go(p, i, 0, x)
defs.doc:
The preorder index path from the root to the node at index `i`: the index of each ancestor, root first, ending at `i` itself. `None` when the index is past the end. The path is what a pass reports when it must point at a node without carrying the node.

```prism
# let countdown = Layer { kids = \(n) -> if n > 0 then [n - 1] else [], rebuild = \(n, _cs) -> n }
lay_path_to(countdown, 3, 3)
```

```output
Some([0, 1, 2, 3])
```

defs.name: lay_path_go
defs.ty: forall a. (Control.Layer.Layer(a), Int, Int, a) -> Option(List(Int))
defs.source:
fn lay_path_go(
  p : Layer(a),
  target : Int,
  here : Int,
  x : a
) : Option(List(Int)) =
  if here == target then
    Some([here])
  else
    lay_path_kids(p, target, here + 1, lay_kids(p, x), here)

defs.name: lay_path_kids
defs.ty: forall a. (Control.Layer.Layer(a), Int, Int, List(a), Int) -> Option(List(Int))
defs.source:
fn lay_path_kids(
  p : Layer(a),
  target : Int,
  base : Int,
  cs : List(a),
  parent : Int
) : Option(List(Int)) =
  match cs of
    Nil => None
    Cons(c, rest) =>
      let span = lay_size(p, c)
      if target < base + span then
        match lay_path_go(p, target, base, c) of
          Some(rest_path) => Some(Cons(parent, rest_path))
          None => None
      else
        lay_path_kids(p, target, base + span, rest, parent)

defs.name: lay_indexed
defs.source:
fn lay_indexed(p : Layer(a), x : a) : List((Int, a)) =
  lay_indexed_go(lay_universe(p, x), 0)
defs.doc: Every node's preorder index paired with the node, root first. The indexed walk an occurrence table is built from.

defs.name: lay_indexed_go
defs.source:
fn lay_indexed_go(xs : List(a), i : Int) : List((Int, a)) =
  match xs of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(n, rest) => Cons((i, n), lay_indexed_go(rest, i + 1))

defs.name: lay_edges
defs.doc: The immediate children of every node, flattened: the one-layer relation of the whole tree as parent-child pairs in preorder. A dependency or occurrence graph is one `map` off this.

defs.name: Reader
defs.source:
effect Reader(r)
  ask() : r
defs.doc: Read the ambient environment of type `r`.

defs.name: run_reader
defs.ty: forall e0 a b. (a, () -> b ! {Control.Reader.Reader(a), e0}) -> b ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn run_reader(env : r, action : () -> a ! {Reader(r) | e}) : a =
  handle action() with
    ask() resume k => k(env)
    return x => x
defs.doc:
Run `action` with `env` as the ambient environment, discharging `Reader(r)`.

```prism
run_reader("hello", \() -> asks(str_len))
```

```output
5
```

defs.name: asks
defs.source: fn asks(f : (r) -> a) : a ! {Reader(r)} = f(ask())
defs.doc: Read a projection `f` of the environment.

defs.name: local
defs.ty: forall e0 a b. ((a) -> a, () -> b ! {Control.Reader.Reader(a), Control.Reader.Reader(a), e0}) -> b ! {Control.Reader.Reader(a), e0}
defs.source:
fn local(f : (r) -> r, action : () -> a ! {Reader(r) | e}) : a =
  run_reader(f(ask()), action)
defs.doc:
Run `action` under the environment transformed by `f`. The transformed environment is scoped to `action`; the outer environment is unchanged.

```prism
run_reader(10, \() -> [ask(), local(\(n) -> n + 5, \() -> ask()), ask()])
```

```output
[10, 15, 10]
```

defs.name: Rewrite
defs.source: alias Rewrite(a, e) = (a) -> Option(a) ! {| e}
defs.doc:
A partial rewrite on nodes of sort `a`: `Some` for a rule that applied here, `None` for one that declined.

The row variable `e` is the whole story on effects. It is open and it is threaded, never discharged: a rule that needs nothing instantiates it to the empty row and reads as a pure function, and a rule that draws fresh names or records refusals instantiates it to whatever it uses. No combinator below handles, masks, or requires an effect, so a caller never installs a handler to satisfy the traversal, only to satisfy its own rule.

defs.name: rw_id
defs.source: fn rw_id(x : a) : Option(a) = Some(x)
defs.doc: The rewrite that accepts every node and changes nothing: the unit of `rw_then` and the right-hand side of `rw_try`. Never declines, always terminates.

defs.name: rw_fail
defs.source: fn rw_fail(_x : a) : Option(a) = None
defs.doc: The rewrite that declines everywhere: the unit of `rw_or_else`. Always declines, always terminates.

defs.name: rw_then
defs.ty: forall e0 a. ((a) -> Option(a) ! {e0}, (a) -> Option(a) ! {e0}) -> (a) -> Option(a) ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn rw_then(s1 : Rewrite(a, e), s2 : Rewrite(a, e)) : Rewrite(a, e) =
  \(x) -> match s1(x) of { None => None, Some(y) => s2(y) }
defs.doc: Run `s1`, then `s2` on its result. Declines if either declines, so a sequence is all-or-nothing and `s2` never sees a node `s1` refused. Terminates whenever both do.

defs.name: rw_or_else
defs.ty: forall e0 a. ((a) -> Option(a) ! {e0}, (a) -> Option(a) ! {e0}) -> (a) -> Option(a) ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn rw_or_else(s1 : Rewrite(a, e), s2 : Rewrite(a, e)) : Rewrite(a, e) =
  \(x) -> match s1(x) of { Some(y) => Some(y), None => s2(x) }
defs.doc:
Left-biased choice: run `s1`, and only if it declines run `s2` on the original node, not on anything `s1` produced. Declines only when both decline. The bias is the point; a rule list is an `rw_or_else` chain and the first matching rule wins, exactly as a hand-written match would. Terminates whenever both do.

```prism
# let positive = \(n) -> if n > 0 then Some(n + 1) else None
# let times_ten = \(n) -> Some(n * 10)
(rw_or_else(positive, times_ten)(2), rw_or_else(positive, times_ten)(-2))
```

```output
(Some(3), Some(-20))
```

defs.name: rw_try
defs.source: fn rw_try(s : Rewrite(a, e)) : Rewrite(a, e) = rw_or_else(s, rw_id)
defs.doc: Make a rewrite total: `s` where it applies, the node unchanged where it declines. The result never declines, which is what the traversal schemes want when a rule is meant to fire only in places. Terminates whenever `s` does.

defs.name: rw_at
defs.ty: forall e0 a. ((a) -> Bool ! {e0}, (a) -> Option(a) ! {e0}) -> (a) -> Option(a) ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn rw_at(q : (a) -> Bool ! {| e}, s : Rewrite(a, e)) : Rewrite(a, e) =
  \(x) -> if q(x) then s(x) else None
defs.doc: Run `s` only at nodes satisfying `q`, declining everywhere else and declining wherever `s` itself declines. The cheap way to scope a rule without folding the test into the rule itself. Terminates whenever `q` and `s` do.

defs.name: rw_where
defs.source:
fn rw_where(q : (a) -> Bool ! {| e}) : Rewrite(a, e) =
  \(x) -> if q(x) then Some(x) else None
defs.doc: The rewrite that accepts exactly the nodes satisfying `q`, unchanged, and declines at the rest. Useful as the left half of an `rw_then` guard. Terminates whenever `q` does.

defs.name: rw_apply
defs.ty: forall e0 a. ((a) -> Option(a) ! {e0}, a) -> a ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn rw_apply(s : Rewrite(a, e), x : a) : a ! { | e} =
  match s(x) of
    Some(y) => y
    None => x
defs.doc: Run a rewrite for its result, keeping `x` when it declines, so the decline becomes a no-op rather than a value the caller has to unwrap. The usual way to finish: a traversal wrapped in `rw_try` never declines, and this drops the `Option`. Terminates whenever `s` does.

defs.name: rw_traverse
defs.ty: forall e0 a. ((a) -> Option(a) ! {e0}, List(a)) -> Option(List(a)) ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn rw_traverse(s : Rewrite(a, e), xs : List(a)) : Option(List(a)) ! { | e} =
  match xs of
    Nil => Some(Nil)
    Cons(x, rest) =>
      match s(x) of
        None => None
        Some(y) =>
          match rw_traverse(s, rest) of
            None => None
            Some(ys) => Some(Cons(y, ys))

defs.name: rw_all
defs.source:
fn rw_all(p : Layer(a), s : Rewrite(a, e)) : Rewrite(a, e) =
  \(x) -> match rw_traverse(s, lay_kids(p, x)) of { None => None, Some(cs) => Some(lay_rebuild(p, x, cs)) }
defs.doc: Run `s` on every immediate child and rebuild. Declines if any child declines, and then declines as a whole: no partial rebuild is ever returned, so a failed child cannot leave a half-rewritten node. At a leaf there is nothing to decline, so it accepts unchanged, which is the base case every recursive scheme bottoms out on. One pass over the children, so it terminates whenever `s` does.

defs.name: rw_first
defs.ty: forall e0 a. ((a) -> Option(a) ! {e0}, List(a), List(a)) -> Option(List(a)) ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn rw_first(
  s : Rewrite(a, e),
  seen : List(a),
  xs : List(a)
) : Option(List(a)) ! { | e} =
  match xs of
    Nil => None
    Cons(x, rest) =>
      match s(x) of
        Some(y) => Some(append(reverse(seen), Cons(y, rest)))
        None => rw_first(s, Cons(x, seen), rest)

defs.name: rw_one
defs.source:
fn rw_one(p : Layer(a), s : Rewrite(a, e)) : Rewrite(a, e) =
  \(x) -> match rw_first(s, Nil, lay_kids(p, x)) of { None => None, Some(cs) => Some(lay_rebuild(p, x, cs)) }
defs.doc: Run `s` on the leftmost child that accepts, leaving the others alone. Declines when no child accepts, so at a leaf it always declines. That decline is essential because it tells the fixpoint schemes below there is no redex left. One pass over the children, so it terminates whenever `s` does.

defs.name: rw_bottom_up
defs.source:
fn rw_bottom_up(p : Layer(a), s : Rewrite(a, e)) : Rewrite(a, e) =
  \(x) -> rw_then(rw_all(p, \(c) -> rw_bottom_up(p, s)(c)), s)(x)
defs.doc:
Children first, then the node: rewrite every child with `rw_bottom_up`, then run `s` on the rebuilt node. Declines if `s` declines anywhere, at any depth, because `rw_all` and `rw_then` are both all-or-nothing, so the usual spelling is `rw_bottom_up(p, rw_try(rule))` and the bare form is for a rule that really must fire at every node.

Terminates whenever `s` does. The recursion descends the *input* tree, and each of its nodes is visited exactly once, so nothing `s` produces is ever traversed. A rule that grows the tree is therefore safe here.

defs.name: rw_top_down
defs.source:
fn rw_top_down(p : Layer(a), s : Rewrite(a, e)) : Rewrite(a, e) =
  \(x) -> rw_then(s, rw_all(p, \(c) -> rw_top_down(p, s)(c)))(x)
defs.doc:
The node first, then children. Same all-or-nothing decline discipline as `rw_bottom_up`, and a node rewritten here is not revisited, so a rule that produces a shape it also matches fires only once per position; closing that over is what `rw_outermost` is for.

Termination is conditional, unlike `rw_bottom_up`. The children traversed are those of the *rewritten* node, so a rule that reproduces a matching node below itself descends forever. Where that is possible, use `rw_bottom_up`, or use `rw_outermost`, whose fuel bounds it.

defs.name: rw_everywhere
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (Control.Layer.Layer(a), (a) -> Option(a) ! {e0}, a) -> a ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn rw_everywhere(p : Layer(a), s : Rewrite(a, e), x : a) : a ! { | e} =
  rw_apply(rw_bottom_up(p, rw_try(s)), x)
defs.doc:
Run `s` everywhere it applies, bottom up, and keep the result. The common case: a total pass built from a partial rule. Cannot decline, because `rw_try` turns every refusal into "leave this node alone"; a rule that applies nowhere returns the tree unchanged. Terminates whenever `s` does.

```prism
# import Json (..)
# let bump = \(j) -> match j of { JInt(n) => Some(JInt(n + 1)), _ => None }
rw_everywhere(json_layer(), bump, JArr([JInt(1), JBool(true), JInt(2)]))
```

```output
Json.JArr([Json.JInt(2), Json.JBool(true), Json.JInt(3)])
```

defs.name: rw_everywhere_td
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (Control.Layer.Layer(a), (a) -> Option(a) ! {e0}, a) -> a ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn rw_everywhere_td(p : Layer(a), s : Rewrite(a, e), x : a) : a ! { | e} =
  rw_apply(rw_top_down(p, rw_try(s)), x)
defs.doc: Run `s` everywhere it applies, top down, and keep the result. Cannot decline, on the same grounds as `rw_everywhere`, and carries `rw_top_down`'s conditional termination: a rule that rebuilds a matching node below itself does not terminate here.

defs.name: rw_once_bottom_up
defs.source:
fn rw_once_bottom_up(p : Layer(a), s : Rewrite(a, e)) : Rewrite(a, e) =
  \(x) -> rw_or_else(rw_one(p, \(c) -> rw_once_bottom_up(p, s)(c)), s)(x)
defs.doc: The single leftmost-innermost application of `s`: try the children first, and only if none accepted try the node, so exactly one node changes. Declines when `s` applies nowhere in the tree, which is the termination test the fixpoint schemes read. Terminates whenever `s` does: one pass, no rewritten output is traversed.

defs.name: rw_once_top_down
defs.source:
fn rw_once_top_down(p : Layer(a), s : Rewrite(a, e)) : Rewrite(a, e) =
  \(x) -> rw_or_else(s, rw_one(p, \(c) -> rw_once_top_down(p, s)(c)))(x)
defs.doc: The single outermost-leftmost application of `s`: try the node first, and only if it declined try the children, so exactly one node changes. Declines when `s` applies nowhere in the tree. Terminates whenever `s` does: the descent happens only along the declining path, so no rewritten node is revisited within one application.

defs.name: RwFix
defs.source: type RwFix(a) = RwFix { tree: a, steps: Int, converged: Bool }
defs.doc: The outcome of a fueled fixpoint: the tree it reached, how many steps it took, and whether it converged. `converged` is false exactly when the fuel ran out with the rewrite still applying, which is the only way a caller learns that a rule set does not terminate on this input.

defs.name: rw_repeat
defs.ty: forall e0 a. ((a) -> Option(a) ! {e0}, Int, a) -> Control.Rewrite.RwFix(a) ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn rw_repeat(s : Rewrite(a, e), fuel : Int, x : a) : RwFix(a) ! { | e} =
  rw_repeat_go(s, fuel, x, 0)
defs.doc:
Apply `s` to its own output until it declines, at most `fuel` times.

Always terminates, whatever `s` does, and that is the whole reason it exists. The termination condition is explicit: stop when `s` declines, reporting `converged = true` and the number of applications; or stop when `fuel` applications have been made and `s` still accepts, reporting `converged = false` and the tree as it stood before the refused step. There is deliberately no unfueled closer, because a rewrite loop that may not terminate should be a value a test can assert on rather than a hang. Zero or negative fuel yields the input unchanged, converged only if `s` declines on it.

```prism
# let down = \(n) -> if n > 0 then Some(n - 1) else None
let r = rw_repeat(down, 10, 3)
(r.tree, r.steps, r.converged)
```

```output
(0, 3, true)
```

defs.name: rw_repeat_go
defs.ty: forall e0 a. ((a) -> Option(a) ! {e0}, Int, a, Int) -> Control.Rewrite.RwFix(a) ! {e0}

defs.name: rw_innermost
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (Control.Layer.Layer(a), (a) -> Option(a) ! {e0}, Int, a) -> Control.Rewrite.RwFix(a) ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn rw_innermost(
  p : Layer(a),
  s : Rewrite(a, e),
  fuel : Int,
  x : a
) : RwFix(a) ! { | e} =
  rw_repeat(rw_once_bottom_up(p, s), fuel, x)
defs.doc:
Rewrite to a fixpoint innermost-first: repeat the single leftmost-innermost application until no rule applies. The normalizing order, so a rule that exposes a new redex below itself is picked up on the next step.

Always terminates, bounded by `fuel` steps. It converges exactly when `s` declines at every node of the tree it reaches; `converged = false` means the fuel ran out with a redex still present, and is the honest report that this rule set does not normalize this input in that budget. Never declines: the result is a record, and a rule that applies nowhere converges in zero steps.

defs.name: rw_outermost
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (Control.Layer.Layer(a), (a) -> Option(a) ! {e0}, Int, a) -> Control.Rewrite.RwFix(a) ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn rw_outermost(
  p : Layer(a),
  s : Rewrite(a, e),
  fuel : Int,
  x : a
) : RwFix(a) ! { | e} =
  rw_repeat(rw_once_top_down(p, s), fuel, x)
defs.doc:
Rewrite to a fixpoint outermost-first: repeat the single outermost-leftmost application until no rule applies. The lazy order, which reaches a normal form for rules whose innermost order diverges, and the fueled way to run a rule that `rw_top_down` would descend into forever.

Always terminates, bounded by `fuel` steps, with the same convergence report as `rw_innermost`. Never declines.

defs.name: rw_choose
defs.source:
fn rw_choose(rules : List(Rewrite(a, e))) : Rewrite(a, e) =
  \(x) -> rw_choose_go(rules, x)
defs.doc: The first rule in the list that applies, run on the original node. Declines only when every rule declines, and an empty list is `rw_fail`. A rule table is an ordinary list, read in order, so priority is where the reader can see it. Terminates whenever every rule does; the list is finite and each rule is tried at most once.

defs.name: rw_choose_go
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (List((a) -> Option(a) ! {e0}), a) -> Option(a) ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn rw_choose_go(rules : List(Rewrite(a, e)), x : a) : Option(a) ! { | e} =
  match rules of
    Nil => None
    Cons(r, rest) =>
      match r(x) of
        Some(y) => Some(y)
        None => rw_choose_go(rest, x)

defs.name: rw_pipeline
defs.source:
fn rw_pipeline(rules : List(Rewrite(a, e))) : Rewrite(a, e) =
  \(x) -> Some(rw_pipeline_go(rules, x))
defs.doc: Run every rule in order, each on the previous result, keeping the node where a rule declines. Unlike `rw_choose` this is a pipeline, not a choice: all of them run. Never declines, so a stage's refusal is invisible to the caller and an empty list is `rw_id`. Terminates whenever every rule does; each runs exactly once.

defs.name: rw_pipeline_go
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (List((a) -> Option(a) ! {e0}), a) -> a ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn rw_pipeline_go(rules : List(Rewrite(a, e)), x : a) : a ! { | e} =
  match rules of
    Nil => x
    Cons(r, rest) => rw_pipeline_go(rest, rw_apply(r, x))

defs.name: rw_lift
defs.source: fn rw_lift(f : (a) -> a ! {| e}) : Rewrite(a, e) = \(x) -> Some(f(x))
defs.doc: Lift a total node function into a rewrite that always accepts. The bridge for an existing `(a) -> a` helper. Never declines, which makes it unsuitable as a fixpoint body: `rw_repeat` would never see the decline it stops on. Use `rw_lift_changed` there. Terminates whenever `f` does.

defs.name: rw_lift_changed
defs.ty: forall e0 a. ((a) -> a ! {e0}, (a, a) -> Bool ! {e0}) -> (a) -> Option(a) ! {e0}
defs.doc: Lift a total node function into a rewrite that accepts only where it changed something, given an equality. Declines exactly where `f` is the identity, which is what turns a normalizer into a rule a fixpoint can close over: the loop stops when the function stops moving. Terminates whenever `f` and `same` do.

defs.name: rw_changed
defs.ty: forall e0 a. ((a, a) -> Bool ! {e0}, a, a) -> Option(a) ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn rw_changed(
  same : (a, a) -> Bool ! {| e},
  x : a,
  y : a
) : Option(a) ! { | e} =
  if same(x, y) then
    None
  else
    Some(y)

defs.name: rw_steps
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (Control.Layer.Layer(a), (a) -> Option(a) ! {e0}, a) -> List(a) ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn rw_steps(p : Layer(a), s : Rewrite(a, e), x : a) : List(a) ! { | e} =
  rw_steps_at(p, s, x)
defs.doc:
Every result of applying `s` at each node of the tree in turn, one rewritten tree per node that accepted, in preorder. The enumeration a search or a mutation-testing pass wants: not one normal form, but every single-step neighbour.

Never declines; a rule that applies nowhere yields the empty list, and a decline at a node simply contributes nothing there. Terminates whenever `s` does, visiting each node of the input tree exactly once and never traversing a rewritten result.

defs.name: rw_steps_at
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (Control.Layer.Layer(a), (a) -> Option(a) ! {e0}, a) -> List(a) ! {e0}

defs.name: rw_steps_kids
defs.ty: forall a. (Control.Layer.Layer(a), (a) -> Option(a), a, List(a), List(a)) -> List(a)
defs.source:
fn rw_steps_kids(
  p : Layer(a),
  s : Rewrite(a, e),
  x : a,
  seen : List(a),
  cs : List(a)
) : List(a) ! { | e} =
  match cs of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(c, rest) =>
      let rebuilt = map(
          \(c2) -> lay_rebuild(p, x, append(reverse(seen), Cons(c2, rest))),
          rw_steps_at(p, s, c),
        )
      append(rebuilt, rw_steps_kids(p, s, x, Cons(c, seen), rest))

defs.name: State
defs.source:
effect State(s)
  get() : s
  put(s) : Unit
defs.doc: Read (`get`) and overwrite (`put`) a threaded state of type `s`.

defs.name: run_state
defs.ty: forall e0 a b. (a, () -> b ! {Control.State.State(a), Var@cell@3, e0}) -> (b, a) ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn run_state(init : s, action : () -> a ! {State(s) | e}) : (a, s) =
  var cell := init
  let r =
    handle action() with
      get() resume k => k(cell)
      put(s2) resume k =>
        cell := s2
        k(())
      return r => r
  (r, cell)
defs.doc:
Run `action`, threading `init` as the initial state; returns `(result, final_state)`. The state lives in a cell private to this run: `get` resumes with its current value, `put` overwrites it and resumes, and the final value is read back once the action returns.

```prism
run_state(1, \() -> state(\(s) -> (s * 2, s + 1)))
```

```output
(2, 2)
```

defs.name: eval_state
defs.ty: forall e0 a b. (a, () -> b ! {Control.State.State(a), Var@cell@3, e0}) -> b ! {e0}
defs.doc: Run `action` for its result only, discarding the final state.

defs.name: exec_state
defs.ty: forall e0 a b. (a, () -> b ! {Control.State.State(a), Var@cell@3, e0}) -> a ! {e0}
defs.doc: Run `action` for its final state only, discarding the result.

defs.name: modify
defs.source: fn modify(f : (s) -> s) : Unit ! {State(s)} = put(f(get()))
defs.doc:
Apply `f` to the current state, storing the result.

```prism
exec_state(3, \() -> modify(\(n) -> n * 2))
```

```output
6
```

defs.name: state
defs.source:
fn state(f : (s) -> (a, s)) : a ! {State(s)} =
  match f(get()) of
    (a, s2) =>
      put(s2)
      a
defs.doc: Run one combined read-and-write step: `f` maps the current state to a result and the next state, the result is returned and the state stored.

defs.name: gets
defs.source: fn gets(f : (s) -> a) : a ! {State(s)} = f(get())
defs.doc: Read a projection `f` of the current state.

defs.name: Validate
defs.source:
effect Validate(e)
  never refute(e) : a
  dispute(e) : Unit
defs.doc: Errors raised while validating values of type `e`.

defs.name: capture_validate
defs.ty: forall e0 a b. (() -> a ! {Control.Validate.Validate(b), e0}) -> (Option(a), List(b)) ! {e0}

defs.name: run_validate
defs.ty: forall e0 a b. (() -> a ! {Control.Validate.Validate(b), e0}) -> Data.Validation.Validation(b, a) ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn run_validate(action : () -> a ! {Validate(e) | r}) : Validation(e, a) =
  match capture_validate(action) of
    (Some(value), Nil) => Valid(value)
    (Some(_value), errs) => Invalid(errs)
    (None, errs) => Invalid(errs)
defs.doc:
Run a validation computation. Any fatal or non-fatal errors make the result `Invalid`; only a completed computation with no errors is `Valid`.

```prism
run_validate(\() -> disputes(["too small", "odd"]))
```

```output
Data.Validation.Invalid([too small, odd])
```

defs.name: exec_validate
defs.ty: forall e0 a b. (() -> a ! {Control.Validate.Validate(b), e0}) -> List(b) ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn exec_validate(action : () -> a ! {Validate(e) | r}) : List(e) =
  match run_validate(action) of
    Valid(_value) => Nil
    Invalid(errs) => errs
defs.doc: Run a validation computation and return its errors, or `Nil` on success.

defs.name: disputes
defs.source:
fn disputes(errs : List(e)) : Unit ! {Validate(e)} =
  match errs of
    Nil => ()
    Cons(err, rest) =>
      dispute(err)
      disputes(rest)
defs.doc: Raise each error as a non-fatal dispute, in list order.

defs.name: tolerate
defs.ty: forall e0 a b. (() -> a ! {Control.Validate.Validate(b), Control.Validate.Validate(b), e0}) -> Option(a) ! {Control.Validate.Validate(b), e0}
defs.source:
fn tolerate(action : () -> a ! {Validate(e) | r}) : Option(a) ! {Validate(e) | r} =
  match capture_validate(action) of
    (value, errs) =>
      disputes(errs)
      value
defs.doc:
Make fatal errors in `action` recoverable. A refuted branch becomes `None`; a branch that completes returns `Some(value)`, even if it raised disputes. All captured errors are re-raised as disputes in the outer validation, so the final run still fails unless another handler consumes them.

```prism
exec_validate(\() -> tolerate(\() -> refute("bad field")))
```

```output
[bad field]
```

defs.name: Writer
defs.source:
effect Writer(w)
  tell(w) : Unit
defs.doc: Append one item of type `w` to the accumulated log.

defs.name: run_writer
defs.ty: forall e0 a b. (() -> a ! {Control.Writer.Writer(b), Var@log@4, e0}) -> (a, List(b)) ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn run_writer(action : () -> a ! {Writer(w) | e}) : (a, List(w)) =
  var log := Nil
  let r =
    handle action() with
      tell(m) resume k =>
        log := Cons(m, log)
        k(())
      return r => r
  (r, reverse(log))
defs.doc:
Run `action`, collecting every `tell` into a log, and return the computation's result paired with that log in emission order.

```prism
run_writer(\() -> tells(["started", "finished"]))
```

```output
((), [started, finished])
```

defs.name: eval_writer
defs.ty: forall e0 a b. (() -> a ! {Control.Writer.Writer(b), Var@log@4, e0}) -> a ! {e0}
defs.doc: Run `action` and keep only its result, discarding the log.

defs.name: exec_writer
defs.ty: forall e0 a b. (() -> a ! {Control.Writer.Writer(b), Var@log@4, e0}) -> List(b) ! {e0}
defs.doc: Run `action` and keep only the log, discarding the result.

defs.name: listen
defs.ty: forall e0 a b. (() -> a ! {Control.Writer.Writer(b), Control.Writer.Writer(b), Var@log@4, e0}) -> (a, List(b)) ! {Control.Writer.Writer(b), e0}
defs.source:
fn listen(action : () -> a ! {Writer(w) | e}) : (a, List(w)) ! {Writer(w) | e} =
  match run_writer(action) of
    (r, log) =>
      tells(log)
      (r, log)
defs.doc: Run `action`, re-emit its log unchanged, and return the result paired with that log, so an outer writer both observes and keeps the inner output.

defs.name: censor
defs.ty: forall e0 a b. ((List(a)) -> List(a), () -> b ! {Control.Writer.Writer(a), Control.Writer.Writer(a), Var@log@4, e0}) -> b ! {Control.Writer.Writer(a), e0}
defs.doc:
Run `action`, rewrite its whole log with `f`, and re-emit the rewritten log, returning the result. The rewrite sees the log in emission order.

```prism
exec_writer(\() -> censor(reverse, \() -> tells(["a", "b"])))
```

```output
[b, a]
```

defs.name: tells
defs.source:
fn tells(log : List(w)) : Unit ! {Writer(w)} =
  match log of
    Nil => ()
    Cons(m, rest) =>
      tell(m)
      tells(rest)
defs.doc: Emit every item of `log` in order.

defs.name: Index
defs.source: type Index = MkIndex(Int) deriving (Eq, Ord, Show)
defs.doc:
The outward distance from a use site to the binder it refers to: `bind_index(0)` is the nearest enclosing binder.

The constructor is spelled `MkIndex` rather than `Index` on purpose: constructors share one flat namespace with every module in the program, so a constructor named for its type would rebind any other `Index` in scope and the failure would surface far from the declaration.

defs.name: Level
defs.source: type Level = MkLevel(Int) deriving (Eq, Ord, Show)
defs.doc: The inward distance from the root to a binder: `bind_level(0)` is the outermost binder in scope. Constructor named `MkLevel` for the same reason `Index` uses `MkIndex`.

defs.name: bind_index
defs.source: fn bind_index(n : Int) : Index = MkIndex(n)
defs.doc:
Brand a raw outward distance as an `Index`. One of the two ways in.

```prism
bind_index_int(bind_index(2))
```

```output
2
```

defs.name: bind_level
defs.source: fn bind_level(n : Int) : Level = MkLevel(n)
defs.doc:
Brand a raw inward distance as a `Level`. One of the two ways in.

```prism
bind_level_int(bind_level(2))
```

```output
2
```

defs.name: bind_index_int
defs.doc: The raw distance carried by an `Index`. One of the two ways out.

defs.name: bind_level_int
defs.doc: The raw distance carried by a `Level`. One of the two ways out.

defs.name: bind_index_at
defs.source:
fn bind_index_at(depth : Int, l : Level) : Index =
  MkIndex(depth - 1 - bind_level_int(l))
defs.doc:
The index a use site under `depth` binders must write to reach level `l`.

This and `bind_level_at` are the module's only conversions, and they are the same reflection, so at a fixed depth each undoes the other. Both are undefined outside `0 <= distance < depth`; a caller that might be out of scope should ask the environment instead.

```prism
bind_index_int(bind_index_at(3, bind_level(0)))
```

```output
2
```

defs.name: bind_level_at
defs.source:
fn bind_level_at(depth : Int, i : Index) : Level =
  MkLevel(depth - 1 - bind_index_int(i))
defs.doc:
The level that a use site under `depth` binders reaches by writing index `i`.

```prism
bind_level_int(bind_level_at(3, bind_index_at(3, bind_level(2))))
```

```output
2
```

defs.name: BindEnv
defs.source: type BindEnv(a) = BindEnv { slots: List((String, a)) }
defs.doc:
The binders in scope, innermost first, each with a name and a payload.

Shadowing is by position, not by rewriting: pushing a name that is already in scope hides the older slot from `bind_index_of` while leaving it reachable by its own index, which is what an interpreter walking a closure environment needs.

defs.name: bind_empty
defs.source: let bind_empty : BindEnv(a) = BindEnv { slots = Nil }
defs.doc: No binders in scope.

defs.name: bind_push
defs.source:
fn bind_push(env : BindEnv(a), name : String, payload : a) : BindEnv(a) =
  BindEnv { slots = Cons((name, payload), env.slots) }
defs.doc:
Push one binder, which becomes index `0`. Pushing a shadowing name keeps the older slot addressable at its previous index.

```prism
let env = bind_push(bind_push(bind_empty, "x", 1), "x", 2)
(bind_at(env, bind_index(0)), bind_at(env, bind_index(1)))
```

```output
(Some(2), Some(1))
```

defs.name: bind_push_all
defs.source:
fn bind_push_all(env : BindEnv(a), entries : List((String, a))) : BindEnv(a) =
  match entries of
    Nil => env
    Cons(e, rest) => bind_push_all(bind_push(env, fst(e), snd(e)), rest)
defs.doc:
Push several binders at once, leftmost outermost, the way a multi-parameter binder brings its parameters into scope.

```prism
bind_name_at(bind_push_all(bind_empty, [("x", 1), ("y", 2)]), bind_index(1))
```

```output
Some(x)
```

defs.name: bind_push_names
defs.doc:
Push binders that carry no payload beyond their own name.

```prism
bind_names(bind_push_names(bind_empty, ["x", "y"]))
```

```output
[y, x]
```

defs.name: bind_depth
defs.source: fn bind_depth(env : BindEnv(a)) : Int = length(env.slots)
defs.doc: How many binders are in scope. A use site here writes indices below this and levels below this.

defs.name: bind_names
defs.source: fn bind_names(env : BindEnv(a)) : List(String) = map(fst, env.slots)
defs.doc: Every name in scope, innermost first, with shadowed names still listed at their own index.

defs.name: bind_drop
defs.source:
fn bind_drop(env : BindEnv(a), n : Int) : BindEnv(a) =
  BindEnv { slots = drop(n, env.slots) }
defs.doc:
Drop the `n` innermost binders, leaving what was in scope before them.

```prism
bind_names(bind_drop(bind_push_names(bind_empty, ["x", "y", "z"]), 2))
```

```output
[x]
```

defs.name: bind_scan
defs.ty: forall a. (List((String, a)), String, Int) -> Option(Data.Bind.Index)
defs.source:
fn bind_scan(
  slots : List((String, a)),
  name : String,
  k : Int
) : Option(Index) =
  match slots of
    Nil => None
    Cons(e, rest) =>
      if fst(e) == name then
        Some(MkIndex(k))
      else
        bind_scan(rest, name, k + 1)

defs.name: bind_index_of
defs.source:
fn bind_index_of(env : BindEnv(a), name : String) : Option(Index) =
  bind_scan(env.slots, name, 0)
defs.doc:
The index of the innermost binder named `name`, or `None` when the name is free here.

```prism
match bind_index_of(bind_push_names(bind_empty, ["x", "y"]), "y") of
  None => -1
  Some(i) => bind_index_int(i)
```

```output
0
```

defs.name: bind_level_of
defs.source:
fn bind_level_of(env : BindEnv(a), name : String) : Option(Level) =
  match bind_index_of(env, name) of
    None => None
    Some(i) => Some(bind_level_at(bind_depth(env), i))
defs.doc: The level of the innermost binder named `name`, or `None` when the name is free here.

defs.name: bind_nth
defs.ty: forall a. (List((String, a)), Int) -> Option((String, a))
defs.source:
fn bind_nth(slots : List((String, a)), k : Int) : Option((String, a)) =
  if k < 0 then
    None
  else
    match slots of
      Nil => None
      Cons(e, rest) =>
        if k == 0 then
          Some(e)
        else
          bind_nth(rest, k - 1)

defs.name: bind_slot_at
defs.source:
fn bind_slot_at(env : BindEnv(a), i : Index) : Option((String, a)) =
  bind_nth(env.slots, bind_index_int(i))
defs.doc: The binder an index points at, name and payload, or `None` when the index escapes the environment.

defs.name: bind_at
defs.source:
fn bind_at(env : BindEnv(a), i : Index) : Option(a) =
  match bind_slot_at(env, i) of
    None => None
    Some(e) => Some(snd(e))
defs.doc: The payload an index points at.

defs.name: bind_name_at
defs.source:
fn bind_name_at(env : BindEnv(a), i : Index) : Option(String) =

defs.name: Nameless
defs.source:
type Nameless
  = NTok(String)
  | NLit(String)
  | NRef(String)
  | NScope(List(String), Nameless)
  | NSeq(List(Nameless))
  deriving (Eq, Show)
defs.doc:
A rendering skeleton that knows where the binders are.

The fold over it is the whole point: a term's own traversal decides which tokens to emit and which names it binds, and this decides how a reference is spelled. Because a bound reference is spelled by outward distance, two terms that differ only in the names of their binders render to the same bytes.

defs.name: bind_token
defs.source:
fn bind_token(s : String) : String =
  concat(show_int(byte_len(s)), concat(":", s))
defs.doc:
A token committed with its byte length, so no token can be confused with the concatenation of its neighbours.

```prism
bind_token("add")
```

```output
3:add
```

defs.name: bind_num_end
defs.source: let bind_num_end : String = ";"
defs.doc:
The character closing every run of digits a rendering writes.

Skeletons concatenate with no separator, so a digit run sitting beside a neighbour that also opens with a digit reads as one number and the boundary between them is lost. A binder index therefore closes with this character, and a caller emitting its own numeric tags through `NLit` closes them the same way to keep the whole rendering uniquely decodable.

defs.name: bind_nl_seq
defs.source:
fn bind_nl_seq(
  free : (String) -> String,
  env : BindEnv(String),
  ts : List(Nameless),
  acc : List(String)
) : List(String) =
  match ts of
    Nil => acc
    Cons(t, rest) => bind_nl_seq(free, env, rest, bind_nl_go(free, env, t, acc))

defs.name: bind_nl_go
defs.source:
fn bind_nl_go(
  free : (String) -> String,
  env : BindEnv(String),
  t : Nameless,
  acc : List(String)
) : List(String) =
  match t of
    NTok(s) => Cons(bind_token(s), acc)
    NLit(s) => Cons(s, acc)
    NRef(x) =>
      match bind_index_of(env, x) of
        Some(i) =>
          Cons(
              concat("b", concat(show_int(bind_index_int(i)), bind_num_end)),
              acc,
            )
        None => Cons(free(x), acc)
    NScope(xs, body) => bind_nl_go(free, bind_push_names(env, xs), body, acc)
    NSeq(ts) => bind_nl_seq(free, env, ts, acc)

defs.name: bind_nameless
defs.source:
fn bind_nameless(free : (String) -> String, t : Nameless) : String =
  str_join("", reverse(bind_nl_go(free, bind_empty, t, Nil)))
defs.doc:
Render a skeleton with binder references as outward distance and free names spelled by `free`.

A bound reference becomes `b`, its index, and `bind_num_end`. A free name is handed to `free`, which is where a caller substitutes whatever identity it has for a name it does not own: a content hash, a slot in the recursive group being hashed, or the name itself.

```prism
bind_nameless(\(x) -> x, NScope(["a"], NSeq([NTok("lam"), NRef("a")])))
```

```output
3:lamb0;
```

defs.name: bind_nameless_show
defs.source:
fn bind_nameless_show(t : Nameless) : String =
  bind_nameless(\(x) -> concat("f", bind_token(x)), t)
defs.doc:
Render with free names spelled as length-prefixed tokens under an `f` tag.

This is the rendering to compare two terms with when nothing outside them matters, which is exactly alpha-equivalence.

```prism
bind_nameless_show(NSeq([NRef("free"), NScope(["x"], NRef("x"))]))
```

```output
f4:freeb0;
```

defs.name: bind_alpha_eq
defs.source:
fn bind_alpha_eq(s : Nameless, t : Nameless) : Bool =
  bind_nameless_show(s) == bind_nameless_show(t)
defs.doc:
True when two skeletons differ only in the names of their bound variables.

```prism
bind_alpha_eq(
  NScope(["a"], NRef("a")),
  NScope(["b"], NRef("b")),
)
```

```output
true
```

defs.name: base64_encode_go
defs.source:
fn base64_encode_go(acc : Buf, bs : Bytes, i : Int, n : Int) : Buf =
  let remain = n - i
  if remain <= 0 then
    acc
  elif remain >= 3 then
    let v = bytes_index(bs, i) * byte_radix * byte_radix
      + bytes_index(bs, i + 1) * byte_radix
      + bytes_index(bs, i + 2)
    base64_encode_go(
        buf_push(
            buf_push(
                buf_push(
                    buf_push(acc, b64_char(v / b64_group)),
                    b64_char(mod(v / b64_hi, b64_mid)),
                  ),
                b64_char(mod(v / b64_mid, b64_mid)),
              ),
            b64_char(mod(v, b64_mid)),
          ),
        bs,
        i + 3,
        n,
      )
  elif remain == 2 then
    let v = bytes_index(bs, i) * byte_radix * byte_radix
      + bytes_index(bs, i + 1) * byte_radix
    buf_push(
        buf_push(
            buf_push(
                buf_push(acc, b64_char(v / b64_group)),
                b64_char(mod(v / b64_hi, b64_mid)),
              ),
            b64_char(mod(v / b64_mid, b64_mid)),
          ),
        ascii_eq,
      )
  else
    let v = bytes_index(bs, i) * byte_radix * byte_radix
    buf_push(
        buf_push(
            buf_push(
                buf_push(acc, b64_char(v / b64_group)),
                b64_char(mod(v / b64_hi, b64_mid)),
              ),
            ascii_eq,
          ),
        ascii_eq,
      )

defs.source:
fn b64_value(c : Int) : Int =
  if c >= ascii_upper_a && c <= 90 then
    c - ascii_upper_a
  elif c >= ascii_lower_a && c <= 122 then
    c - ascii_lower_a + 26
  elif c >= ascii_0 && c <= ascii_9 then
    c - ascii_0 + 52
  elif c == 43 then
    62
  elif c == 47 then
    63
  else
    -1

defs.name: base64_decode_go
defs.source:
fn base64_decode_go(acc : Buf, s : String, i : Int, n : Int) : Option(Bytes) =
  if i >= n then
    Some(bytes_of_buf(acc))
  else
    let c0 = b64_value(byte_at(s, i))
    let c1 = b64_value(byte_at(s, i + 1))
    let p2 = byte_at(s, i + 2) == ascii_eq
    let p3 = byte_at(s, i + 3) == ascii_eq
    -- The two high sextets are always present; each present sextet contributes to
    -- the 24-bit group value `v`, and the byte count follows the padding. Padding
    -- is only legal in the final quad, and `xx=x` (a gap) is rejected.
    if c0 < 0 || c1 < 0 then
      None
    elif p2 then
      if p3 && i + 4 >= n then
        Some(
            bytes_of_buf(
                buf_push(
                    acc,
                    (c0 * b64_group + c1 * b64_hi) / (byte_radix * byte_radix),
                  ),
              ),
          )
      else
        None
    else
      let c2 = b64_value(byte_at(s, i + 2))
      if c2 < 0 then
        None
      elif p3 then
        if i + 4 >= n then
          let v = c0 * b64_group + c1 * b64_hi + c2 * b64_mid
          Some(
              bytes_of_buf(
                  buf_push(
                      buf_push(acc, v / (byte_radix * byte_radix)),
                      mod(v / byte_radix, byte_radix),
                    ),
                ),
            )
        else
          None
      else
        let c3 = b64_value(byte_at(s, i + 3))
        if c3 < 0 then
          None
        else
          let v = c0 * b64_group + c1 * b64_hi + c2 * b64_mid + c3
          base64_decode_go(
              buf_push(
                  buf_push(
                      buf_push(acc, v / (byte_radix * byte_radix)),
                      mod(v / byte_radix, byte_radix),
                    ),
                  mod(v, byte_radix),
                ),
              s,
              i + 4,
              n,
            )

defs.name: Checked
defs.source:
class Checked(a)
  checked_add : (a, a) -> Option(a)
  checked_sub : (a, a) -> Option(a)
  checked_mul : (a, a) -> Option(a)
  checked_neg : (a) -> Option(a)
  checked_div : (a, a) -> Option(a)
  checked_mod : (a, a) -> Option(a)
  saturating_add : (a, a) -> a
  saturating_sub : (a, a) -> a
  saturating_mul : (a, a) -> a
  wrapping_add : (a, a) -> a
  wrapping_sub : (a, a) -> a
  wrapping_mul : (a, a) -> a
  wrapping_neg : (a) -> a
  overflowing_add : (a, a) -> (a, Bool)
  overflowing_sub : (a, a) -> (a, Bool)
  overflowing_mul : (a, a) -> (a, Bool)
defs.doc:
Safe arithmetic over a fixed- or arbitrary-width integer lane. Every method is total: the `checked_*` family reports overflow as `None`, `saturating_*` clamps, `wrapping_*` wraps, and `overflowing_*` pairs the wrapped result with an overflow flag. See the module header for the laws relating the families.

The four families, shown on an `I64` add that overflows the lane maximum:

```prism
(
  checked_add(to_i64(9223372036854775807), to_i64(1)),
  saturating_add(to_i64(9223372036854775807), to_i64(1)),
  wrapping_add(to_i64(9223372036854775807), to_i64(1)),
  overflowing_add(to_i64(9223372036854775807), to_i64(1)),
)
```

```output
(None, 9223372036854775807, -9223372036854775808, (-9223372036854775808, true))
```

A zero divisor is `None`, never a trap:

```prism
checked_div(10, 0)
```

```output
None
```

defs.name: Semilattice
defs.source:
class Semilattice(a)
  lat_bottom : () -> a
  lat_join : (a, a) -> a
  lat_leq : (a, a) -> Bool
defs.doc:
A carrier ordered by a least upper bound, with a least element: everything a fixpoint needs to know about the values it is solving for.

`lat_join` is the least upper bound, `lat_bottom` its identity, and `lat_leq` the partial order the join induces. The laws, for all `x`, `y`, `z`:

- associative: `lat_join(x, lat_join(y, z))` and `lat_join(lat_join(x, y), z)` - commutative: `lat_join(x, y)` and `lat_join(y, x)` - idempotent: `lat_join(x, x)` and `x` - identity: `lat_join(lat_bottom(), x)` and `x` - order: `lat_leq(x, y)` is true exactly when `lat_join(x, y)` and `y` agree

The equality every law is stated up to is `lat_equiv`, the equivalence the order induces, rather than structural equality: `Map` and `Option` carriers have no `Eq` instance to state it with, and two values at the same point of the order are interchangeable to every consumer here.

Instance resolution keys on the head type constructor, so a carrier admits exactly one instance: there is no second, set-specific `Map` instance beside the one below, and none is needed, because that one already is set union at `Map(k, Unit)`, which is how `Data.Set` spells a set. The same rule is why `Int` and `List` have no instance: `max` on `Int` is a join with no identity (`Int` has no least element), and a list admits several defensible joins (union, pointwise, concatenation) with nothing in the type to choose between them. A program that wants one declares it on its own type.

defs.name: latUnit
defs.doc: The one-point lattice. Trivial on its own; it is the payload that turns the map instance into set union, since there a key's presence is the information and its value carries none.

defs.name: latBool
defs.source:
instance latBool : Semilattice(Bool)
  fn lat_bottom() = false
  fn lat_join(x, y) = x || y
  fn lat_leq(x, y) = not(x) || y
defs.doc: Disjunction, ordered `false` below `true`: the carrier a reachability or "is this ever called" pass accumulates in.

defs.name: latOption
defs.doc: The lifted lattice: `None` strictly below every `Some`, and two `Some`s joined under the payload's own order. `None` is genuinely below `Some` of bottom, so "absent" and "present and empty" stay distinguishable, which is what a "has this node been reached at all" question needs.

defs.name: lat_option_join
defs.source:
fn lat_option_join(
  x : Option(a),
  y : Option(a)
) : Option(a) given Semilattice(a) =
  match (x, y) of
    (None, _) => y
    (_, None) => x
    (Some(u), Some(w)) => Some(lat_join(u, w))

defs.name: lat_option_leq
defs.source:
fn lat_option_leq(x : Option(a), y : Option(a)) : Bool given Semilattice(a) =
  match (x, y) of
    (None, _) => true
    (Some(_), None) => false
    (Some(u), Some(w)) => lat_leq(u, w)

defs.name: latPair
defs.doc: The product lattice: componentwise join, componentwise order. Two analyses run as one pass by pairing their carriers.

defs.name: lat_pair_join

defs.ty: forall a b. ((a, b), (a, b)) -> Bool

defs.name: latMap
defs.doc: The partial-map lattice: the empty map is bottom, an absent key is strictly below any present one, and two present keys join under the payload's order. At `Unit` that is exactly set union over `Data.Set` (presence is the only information a key carries); at a nested map it is the map of sets the compiler's own fixpoint is specialized to.

defs.name: lat_map_join
defs.ty: forall a b c d. (Map(c, d, a), Map(c, d, b)) -> Map(c, d, a)

defs.name: lat_map_add
defs.ty: forall a b c. (Map(b, c, a), (b, c)) -> Map(b, c, a)
defs.source:
fn lat_map_add(
  acc : Map(k, v),
  p : (k, v)
) : Map(k, v) given Ord(k), Semilattice(v) =
  match p of
    (key, u) =>
      match map_lookup(key, acc) of
        None => map_insert(key, u, acc)
        Some(w) => map_insert(key, lat_join(w, u), acc)

defs.name: lat_map_leq
defs.ty: forall a b c d. (Map(c, d, a), Map(c, d, b)) -> Bool

defs.name: lat_map_entry_leq
defs.ty: forall a b c. ((b, c), Map(b, c, a)) -> Bool
defs.source:
fn lat_map_entry_leq(
  p : (k, v),
  y : Map(k, v)
) : Bool given Ord(k), Semilattice(v) =
  match p of
    (key, u) =>
      match map_lookup(key, y) of
        None => false
        Some(w) => lat_leq(u, w)

defs.source:
fn lat_joins(xs : List(a)) : a given Semilattice(a) =
  foldl(\(acc, x) -> lat_join(acc, x), lat_bottom(), xs)
defs.doc:
The join of a list, bottom-first. The combining step a transfer function takes over its dependencies' values.

fn lat_equiv(x : a, y : a) : Bool given Semilattice(a) =
  lat_leq(x, y) && lat_leq(y, x)
defs.doc:

defs.name: fix_at
defs.ty: forall a b c. (Map(b, c, a), b) -> c
defs.source:
fn fix_at(assign : Map(k, a), key : k) : a given Ord(k), Semilattice(a) =
  match map_lookup(key, assign) of
    None => lat_bottom()
    Some(v) => v
defs.doc:
The value assigned to `key`, or bottom when the assignment says nothing about it. A transfer function reads its dependencies through this rather than matching on `map_lookup`, so an unmentioned node reads as the least element instead of an `Option` the caller has to decide about.

```prism
(
  fix_at(map_from_list([("seen", true)]), "seen"),
  fix_at(map_from_list([("other", false)]), "missing"),
)
```

```output

```

defs.name: fix_budget
defs.ty: forall a b c d. (Map(c, d, a), Map(c, List(c), b)) -> Int
defs.doc:
The default visit budget: `(n + 1) * (n + e + 1)` for `n` nodes and `e` dependency edges. It bounds the visits a solve over a carrier of height at most `n` can take, which covers the archetypal carrier (a set drawn from the node set itself) with room to spare. A taller carrier belongs in `fix_least_within` with a budget the caller can justify.

```prism
fix_budget(
  map_from_list([("a", false), ("b", false)]),
  map_from_list([("a", ["b"])]),
)
```

```output
12
```

defs.name: fix_least
defs.ty: forall e0 a b c d. (Map(c, d, a), Map(c, List(c), b), (c, Map(c, d, a)) -> d ! {Fail, e0}) -> Map(c, d, a) ! {Fail, e0}
defs.doc:
The least assignment above `seed` closed under `step`, by worklist.

`seed`'s keys are the node set, and the solution has exactly those keys. `uses` is the dependency relation, mapping a node to the nodes it reads; `step(key, current)` is the transfer function, returning `key`'s contribution under the current assignment. The result at a node is the join of its seed value and every contribution `step` made for it.

Two conditions are the caller's to keep, and the solver reports neither. `step(key, current)` may read `current` only at `key` itself and at the nodes `uses` lists for `key`, since those are the only changes that re-queue it; a transfer function that reads further gets an assignment that is closed with respect to the relation it declared and no other. And `step` must be monotone in `current`, or the result is merely some post-fixpoint rather than the least one. Neither slip can spin the solver, because the update accumulates; the budget is what covers the two failures that can.

```prism
fix_least(
    map_from_list([("a", false), ("b", true)]),
    map_from_list([("a", ["b"])]),
    \(_key, cur) -> fix_at(cur, "b"),
  ).map_to_list()
```

```output
[(a, true), (b, true)]
```

defs.name: fix_least_within
defs.ty: forall e0 a b c d. (Int, Map(c, d, a), Map(c, List(c), b), (c, Map(c, d, a)) -> d ! {Fail, e0}) -> Map(c, d, a) ! {Fail, e0}
defs.doc:
`fix_least` with an explicit visit budget. `fail()` when the budget is exhausted: the solve is abandoned rather than reported at whatever assignment it had reached, since a partial answer to a least-fixpoint question is a wrong answer, not an approximate one.

```prism
succeeds(\() ->
  fix_least_within(
    0,
    map_from_list([("a", false)]),
    map_empty,
    \(_key, _cur) -> true,
  ),
)
```

```output
false
```

defs.name: fix_go
defs.ty: forall e0 a b c d e. (Map(d, List(d), a), (d, Map(d, e, b)) -> e ! {Fail, e0}, (Map(d, e, b), List(d), Map(d, Unit, c), Int)) -> Map(d, e, b) ! {Fail, e0}
defs.source:
fn fix_go(
  dependents : Map(k, List(k)),
  step : (k, Map(k, a)) -> a ! {| e},
  st : (Map(k, a), List(k), Map(k, Unit), Int)
) : Map(k, a) ! {Fail | e} given Ord(k), Semilattice(a) =
  match st of
    (assign, queue, queued, budget) =>
      match queue of
        Nil => assign
        Cons(key, rest) =>
          if budget <= 0 then
            fail()
          else
            let old = fix_at(assign, key)
            let next = lat_join(old, step(key, assign))
            let waiting = set_delete(key, queued)
            if lat_leq(next, old) then
              fix_go(dependents, step, (assign, rest, waiting, budget - 1))
            else
              match (fix_enqueue(graph_successors(dependents, key), rest, waiting)) of
                (queue2, waiting2) =>
                  fix_go(dependents, step, (
                      map_insert(key, next, assign),
                      queue2,
                      waiting2,
                      budget - 1,
                    ))

defs.name: fix_enqueue
defs.ty: forall a b. (List(b), List(b), Map(b, Unit, a)) -> (List(b), Map(b, Unit, a))
defs.source:
fn fix_enqueue(
  ks : List(k),
  queue : List(k),
  queued : Map(k, Unit)
) : (List(k), Map(k, Unit)) given Ord(k) =
  match fix_fresh(ks, queued, Nil) of
    (fresh, queued2) => (append(queue, reverse(fresh)), queued2)

defs.name: fix_fresh
defs.ty: forall a b. (List(b), Map(b, Unit, a), List(b)) -> (List(b), Map(b, Unit, a))
defs.source:
fn fix_fresh(
  ks : List(k),
  queued : Map(k, Unit),
  acc : List(k)
) : (List(k), Map(k, Unit)) given Ord(k) =
  match ks of
    Nil => (acc, queued)
    Cons(x, rest) =>
      if set_member(x, queued) then
        fix_fresh(rest, queued, acc)
      else
        fix_fresh(rest, set_insert(x, queued), Cons(x, acc))

defs.name: fix_reverse_edges
defs.ty: forall a b c. (Map(c, List(c), a), Map(c, Unit, b), c, List(c)) -> Map(c, List(c), a)
defs.source:
fn fix_reverse_edges(
  g : Map(k, List(k)),
  nodes : Map(k, Unit),
  key : k,
  ds : List(k)
) : Map(k, List(k)) given Ord(k) =
  match ds of
    Nil => g
    Cons(d, rest) =>
      if set_member(d, nodes) then
        fix_reverse_edges(graph_add_edge(g, d, key), nodes, key, rest)
      else
        fix_reverse_edges(g, nodes, key, rest)

defs.name: fix_propagate
defs.ty: forall a b c d e. (Map(d, e, a), Map(d, List(d), b)) -> Map(d, e, c) ! {Fail}
defs.doc:
The transitive closure of a per-node contribution along a dependency relation: the least `x` with `x[k]` the join of `own[k]` and every `x[j]` for `j` in `uses[k]`.

This is what the compiler's own fixpoint is called for every time, with `own` the operations a function performs itself and `uses` its callees, and it is the reduction an occurrence or liveness pass makes: contribution, join, relation. The node set is every key of `own` together with every node the relation mentions, so a callee that contributes nothing itself still gets an answer.

```prism
map(
    set_to_list,
    map_values(
        fix_propagate(
            map_from_list([("f", set_from_list(["A"])), ("g", set_from_list(["B"]))]),
            map_from_list([("f", ["g"]), ("g", ["f"])]),
          ),
      ),
  )
```

```output
[[A, B], [A, B]]
```

defs.name: fix_gather
defs.ty: forall a b c. (b, Map(c, b, a), List(c)) -> b
defs.source:
fn fix_gather(

  cur : Map(k, a),
  ds : List(k)
) : a given Ord(k), Semilattice(a) =
  match ds of
    Nil => base
    Cons(d, rest) => fix_gather(lat_join(base, fix_at(cur, d)), cur, rest)

  match xs of
    Nil => Cons(x, Nil)
    Cons(y, rest) =>
      let c = cmp(x, y)
      if c < 0 then
        Cons(x, xs)
      elif c == 0 then
        xs
      else
        Cons(y, insert_sorted_uniq(x, rest))

defs.name: graph_dfs
defs.ty: forall a b. (Map(b, List(b), a), b) -> List(b)
defs.doc:
Depth-first preorder from `start`: `start`, then its successors' subtrees, successors taken in ascending order. Each node appears once.

```prism
# let g = graph_from_edges([(1, 2), (1, 3), (2, 4), (3, 4)])
(graph_dfs(g, 1), graph_bfs(g, 1))
```

```output
([1, 2, 4, 3], [1, 2, 3, 4])
```

defs.name: dfs_go
defs.ty: forall a b c. (Map(c, List(c), a), List(c), Map(c, Unit, b), List(c)) -> (Map(c, Unit, b), List(c))
defs.source:
fn dfs_go(
  g : Map(k, List(k)),
  stack : List(k),
  seen : Map(k, Unit),
  acc : List(k)
) : (Map(k, Unit), List(k)) given Ord(k) =
  match stack of
    Nil => (seen, acc)
    Cons(u, rest) =>
      if set_member(u, seen) then
        dfs_go(g, rest, seen, acc)
      else
        dfs_go(
            g,
            append(graph_successors(g, u), rest),
            set_insert(u, seen),
            Cons(u, acc),
          )

defs.name: graph_bfs
defs.ty: forall a b. (Map(b, List(b), a), b) -> List(b)
defs.source:
fn graph_bfs(g : Map(k, List(k)), start : k) : List(k) given Ord(k) =
  reverse(bfs_go(g, Cons(start, Nil), set_insert(start, set_empty), Nil))
defs.doc: Breadth-first order from `start`, successors taken in ascending order. Each node appears once.

defs.name: bfs_go
defs.ty: forall a b c. (Map(c, List(c), a), List(c), Map(c, Unit, b), List(c)) -> List(c)
defs.source:
fn bfs_go(
  g : Map(k, List(k)),
  queue : List(k),
  seen : Map(k, Unit),
  acc : List(k)
) : List(k) given Ord(k) =
  match queue of
    Nil => acc
    Cons(u, rest) =>
      match push_unseen(graph_successors(g, u), seen, Nil) of
        (fresh, seen2) =>
          bfs_go(g, append(rest, reverse(fresh)), seen2, Cons(u, acc))

defs.name: push_unseen
defs.ty: forall a b. (List(b), Map(b, Unit, a), List(b)) -> (List(b), Map(b, Unit, a))
defs.source:
fn push_unseen(
  vs : List(k),
  seen : Map(k, Unit),
  acc : List(k)
) : (List(k), Map(k, Unit)) given Ord(k) =
  match vs of
    Nil => (acc, seen)
    Cons(v, rest) =>
      if set_member(v, seen) then
        push_unseen(rest, seen, acc)
      else
        push_unseen(rest, set_insert(v, seen), Cons(v, acc))

defs.name: graph_reachable
defs.ty: forall a b. (Map(b, List(b), a), b) -> List(b)
defs.source:
fn graph_reachable(g : Map(k, List(k)), start : k) : List(k) given Ord(k) =
  set_to_list(set_from_list(graph_dfs(g, start)))
defs.doc: The nodes reachable from `start` (including `start`), in ascending order.

defs.name: graph_transitive_closure
defs.ty: forall a b c. (Map(c, List(c), a)) -> Map(c, List(c), b)
defs.doc:
The transitive closure: an edge `u -> v` for every `v` reachable from `u` via at least one step (so `u -> u` only when `u` lies on a cycle).

```prism
graph_successors(graph_transitive_closure(graph_from_edges([(1, 2), (2, 3)])), 1)
```

```output
[2, 3]
```

defs.name: reachable_from_succ
defs.ty: forall a b. (Map(b, List(b), a), b) -> List(b)

defs.name: graph_topo_sort
defs.ty: forall a b. (Map(b, List(b), a)) -> List(b)
defs.doc:
Topological order: a node before every node it points to. Deterministic via a depth-first postorder over nodes in ascending order, reversed. A graph with a cycle still yields a total order, but not a valid topo sort (a cycle admits none); pair it with `graph_scc` when cycles are possible.

```prism
graph_topo_sort(graph_from_edges([(1, 2), (1, 3), (2, 3)]))
```

```output
[1, 2, 3]
```

defs.name: topo_visit
defs.ty: forall a b c. (Map(c, List(c), a), c, (Map(c, Unit, b), List(c))) -> (Map(c, Unit, b), List(c))
defs.source:
fn topo_visit(
  g : Map(k, List(k)),
  u : k,
  st : (Map(k, Unit), List(k))
) : (Map(k, Unit), List(k)) given Ord(k) =
  match st of
    (seen, order) =>
      if set_member(u, seen) then
        st
      else
        match (foldl(
              \(s, v) -> topo_visit(g, v, s),
              (set_insert(u, seen), order),
              graph_successors(g, u),
            )) of
          (seen2, order2) => (seen2, Cons(u, order2))

defs.name: graph_scc
defs.ty: forall a b. (Map(b, List(b), a)) -> List(List(b))
defs.doc:
Tarjan's strongly-connected components, returned callee-first: a component comes after every component reachable from it, and each component's members are in ascending order. A node with no self-loop is its own singleton component. This mirrors the compiler's own SCC ordering exactly.

```prism
graph_scc(graph_from_edges([(1, 2), (2, 1), (2, 3)]))
```

```output
[[3], [1, 2]]
```

defs.name: scc_init
defs.ty: forall a b c. () -> (Map(c, (Int, Int), a), Map(c, Unit, b), List(c), Int, List(List(c)), List((c, List(c))))
defs.source:
fn scc_init() : (Map(k, (Int, Int)), Map(k, Unit), List(k), Int, List(List(k)), List((k, List(k)))) =
  (map_empty, set_empty, Nil, 0, Nil, Nil)

defs.name: scc_start
defs.ty: forall a b c d. (Map(d, List(d), a), d, (Map(d, (Int, Int), b), Map(d, Unit, c), List(d), Int, List(List(d)), List((d, List(d))))) -> (Map(d, (Int, Int), b), Map(d, Unit, c), List(d), Int, List(List(d)), List((d, List(d))))
defs.source:
fn scc_start(
  g : Map(k, List(k)),
  u : k,
  st : (Map(k, (Int, Int)), Map(k, Unit), List(k), Int, List(List(k)), List((k, List(k))))
) : (Map(k, (Int, Int)), Map(k, Unit), List(k), Int, List(List(k)), List((k, List(k)))) given Ord(k) =
  match st of
    (meta, on, cstk, next, sccs, _work) =>
      if map_member(u, meta) then
        st
      else
        scc_drive(g, (
            map_insert(u, (next, next), meta),
            set_insert(u, on),
            Cons(u, cstk),
            next + 1,
            sccs,
            Cons((u, graph_successors(g, u)), Nil),
          ))

defs.name: scc_drive
defs.ty: forall a b c d. (Map(d, List(d), a), (Map(d, (Int, Int), b), Map(d, Unit, c), List(d), Int, List(List(d)), List((d, List(d))))) -> (Map(d, (Int, Int), b), Map(d, Unit, c), List(d), Int, List(List(d)), List((d, List(d))))
defs.source:
fn scc_drive(
  g : Map(k, List(k)),
  st : (Map(k, (Int, Int)), Map(k, Unit), List(k), Int, List(List(k)), List((k, List(k))))
) : (Map(k, (Int, Int)), Map(k, Unit), List(k), Int, List(List(k)), List((k, List(k)))) given Ord(k) =
  match st of
    (meta, on, cstk, next, sccs, work) =>
      match work of
        Nil => st
        Cons(frame, rest) =>
          match frame of
            (v, succs) =>
              match succs of
                Cons(w, more) =>
                  let work2 = Cons((v, more), rest)
                  match map_lookup(w, meta) of
                    None =>
                      scc_drive(g, (
                          map_insert(w, (next, next), meta),
                          set_insert(w, on),
                          Cons(w, cstk),
                          next + 1,
                          sccs,
                          Cons((w, graph_successors(g, w)), work2),
                        ))
                    Some(mw) =>
                      match mw of
                        (iw, _lw) =>
                          if set_member(w, on) then
                            scc_drive(g, (
                                relax_low(meta, v, iw),
                                on,
                                cstk,
                                next,
                                sccs,
                                work2,
                              ))
                          else
                            scc_drive(g, (meta, on, cstk, next, sccs, work2))
                Nil =>
                  -- `v` is done: pop its component if it is a root, then push its
                  -- lowlink up to the parent frame. Inlined (not a mutually
                  -- recursive helper) so `scc_drive` only ever self-recurses,
                  -- which the dictionary elaborator handles cleanly.
                  let lv = low_of(meta, v)
                  match rooted(v, meta, on, cstk, sccs) of
                    (on2, cstk2, sccs2) =>
                      match rest of
                        Nil =>
                          scc_drive(g, (meta, on2, cstk2, next, sccs2, rest))
                        Cons(pf, _) =>
                          match pf of
                            (p, _ps) =>
                              scc_drive(g, (
                                  relax_low(meta, p, lv),
                                  on2,
                                  cstk2,
                                  next,
                                  sccs2,
                                  rest,
                                ))

defs.name: rooted
defs.ty: forall a b c. (c, Map(c, (Int, Int), a), Map(c, Unit, b), List(c), List(List(c))) -> (Map(c, Unit, b), List(c), List(List(c)))
defs.source:
fn rooted(
  v : k,
  meta : Map(k, (Int, Int)),
  on : Map(k, Unit),
  cstk : List(k),
  sccs : List(List(k))
) : (Map(k, Unit), List(k), List(List(k))) given Ord(k) =
  match map_lookup(v, meta) of
    Some((iv, lv)) =>
      if lv == iv then
        match pop_component(v, cstk, on, Nil) of
          (comp, cstk2, on2) => (on2, cstk2, Cons(sort(comp), sccs))
      else
        (on, cstk, sccs)
    None => (on, cstk, sccs)

defs.name: pop_component
defs.ty: forall a b. (b, List(b), Map(b, Unit, a), List(b)) -> (List(b), List(b), Map(b, Unit, a))
defs.source:
fn pop_component(
  v : k,
  stack : List(k),
  onstack : Map(k, Unit),
  acc : List(k)
) : (List(k), List(k), Map(k, Unit)) given Ord(k) =
  match stack of
    Nil => (acc, Nil, onstack)
    Cons(u, rest) =>
      let on2 = set_delete(u, onstack)
      if cmp(u, v) == 0 then
        (Cons(u, acc), rest, on2)
      else
        pop_component(v, rest, on2, Cons(u, acc))

defs.name: low_of
defs.ty: forall a b. (Map(b, (Int, Int), a), b) -> Int
defs.source:
fn low_of(meta : Map(k, (Int, Int)), v : k) : Int given Ord(k) =
  match map_lookup(v, meta) of
    Some((_iv, lv)) => lv
    None => 0

defs.name: relax_low
defs.ty: forall a b. (Map(b, (Int, Int), a), b, Int) -> Map(b, (Int, Int), a)
defs.source:
fn relax_low(
  meta : Map(k, (Int, Int)),
  v : k,
  n : Int
) : Map(k, (Int, Int)) given Ord(k) =
  match map_lookup(v, meta) of
    Some((iv, lv)) => map_insert(v, (iv, min(lv, n)), meta)
    None => meta

defs.name: IntMap
defs.source:
type IntMap(v)
  = IMEmpty
  | IMLeaf(I64, v)
  | IMBranch(U64, U64, IntMap(v), IntMap(v))
  deriving (Eq, Show)
defs.doc:
A map from `I64` keys to values of type `v`.

`IMEmpty` is the empty map, `IMLeaf(key, value)` a single binding, and `IMBranch(prefix, mask, zeros, ones)` a split: every key below it agrees with `prefix` above the single set bit of `mask`, `zeros` holds those whose branch bit is clear and `ones` those whose branch bit is set. Both subtrees of a branch are non-empty.

defs.name: im_word
defs.source: fn im_word(k : I64) : U64 = u64_xor(to_u64(int_of_i64(k)), int_sign)

defs.name: im_not
defs.source: fn im_not(x : U64) : U64 = u64_xor(x, int_ones)

defs.name: im_prefix
defs.source:
fn im_prefix(w : U64, m : U64) : U64 =
  u64_and(w, im_not(u64_shl(m, 1u64) - 1u64))

defs.name: im_zero
defs.source: fn im_zero(w : U64, m : U64) : Bool = u64_and(w, m) == 0u64

defs.name: im_nomatch
defs.source: fn im_nomatch(w : U64, p : U64, m : U64) : Bool = not(im_prefix(w, m) == p)

defs.name: im_high_bit
im_link
defs.ty: forall a. (U64, Data.IntMap.IntMap(a), U64, Data.IntMap.IntMap(a)) -> Data.IntMap.IntMap(a)

defs.name: im_bin
defs.ty: forall a. (U64, U64, Data.IntMap.IntMap(a), Data.IntMap.IntMap(a)) -> Data.IntMap.IntMap(a)
defs.source:
fn im_bin(p : U64, m : U64, l : IntMap(v), r : IntMap(v)) : IntMap(v) =
  match l of
    IMEmpty => r
    _ =>
      match r of
        IMEmpty => l
        _ => IMBranch(p, m, l, r)

defs.name: im_ins
defs.ty: forall e0 a. ((a, a) -> a ! {e0}, U64, I64, a, Data.IntMap.IntMap(a)) -> Data.IntMap.IntMap(a) ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn im_ins(g, w : U64, key : I64, value : v, t : IntMap(v)) : IntMap(v) =
  match t of
    IMEmpty => IMLeaf(key, value)
    IMLeaf(k2, v2) =>
      if k2 == key then
        IMLeaf(key, g(value, v2))
      else
        im_link(w, IMLeaf(key, value), im_word(k2), t)
    IMBranch(p, m, l, r) =>
      if im_nomatch(w, p, m) then
        im_link(w, IMLeaf(key, value), p, t)
      elif im_zero(w, m) then
        IMBranch(p, m, im_ins(g, w, key, value, l), r)
      else
        IMBranch(p, m, l, im_ins(g, w, key, value, r))

defs.name: intmap_lookup
defs.source:
fn intmap_lookup(key : I64, t : IntMap(v)) : Option(v) =
  im_look(im_word(key), key, t)
defs.doc:
The value bound to `key` as `Some`, or `None` when absent.

```prism
intmap_lookup(2i64, intmap_from_list([(1i64, "a"), (2i64, "b")]))
```

```output
Some(b)
```

defs.name: im_look
defs.source:
fn im_look(w : U64, key : I64, t : IntMap(v)) : Option(v) =
  match t of
    IMEmpty => None
    IMLeaf(k2, v2) =>
      if k2 == key then
        Some(v2)
      else
        None
    IMBranch(p, m, l, r) =>
      if im_nomatch(w, p, m) then
        None
      elif im_zero(w, m) then
        im_look(w, key, l)
      else
        im_look(w, key, r)

  match intmap_lookup(key, t) of
    None => false
    Some(_) => true
defs.doc:
True when `key` is bound.


defs.name: im_del
defs.source:
fn im_del(w : U64, key : I64, t : IntMap(v)) : IntMap(v) =
  match t of
    IMEmpty => IMEmpty
    IMLeaf(k2, _v2) =>
      if k2 == key then
        IMEmpty
      else
        t
    IMBranch(p, m, l, r) =>
      if im_nomatch(w, p, m) then
        t
      elif im_zero(w, m) then
        im_bin(p, m, im_del(w, key, l), r)
      else
        im_bin(p, m, l, im_del(w, key, r))

defs.name: intmap_size
defs.source:

  match t of
    IMEmpty => 0
    IMLeaf(_k, _v) => 1
    IMBranch(_p, _m, l, r) => intmap_size(l) + intmap_size(r)

defs.name: intmap_union
defs.source:
fn intmap_union(t1 : IntMap(v), t2 : IntMap(v)) : IntMap(v) =
  intmap_union_with(\(a, _b) -> a, t1, t2)
defs.doc:
The union of two maps, keeping the left value where a key is in both.

```prism

  intmap_union(
    intmap_from_list([(1i64, "a"), (2i64, "b")]),
```

defs.name: intmap_union_with
defs.ty: forall e0 a. ((a, a) -> a ! {e0}, Data.IntMap.IntMap(a), Data.IntMap.IntMap(a)) -> Data.IntMap.IntMap(a) ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn intmap_union_with(f, t1 : IntMap(v), t2 : IntMap(v)) : IntMap(v) =
  match t1 of
    IMEmpty => t2
    IMLeaf(k1, v1) => im_ins(f, im_word(k1), k1, v1, t2)
    IMBranch(p1, m1, l1, r1) =>
      match t2 of
        IMEmpty => t1
        IMLeaf(k2, v2) =>
          im_ins(\(new, old) -> f(old, new), im_word(k2), k2, v2, t1)
        IMBranch(p2, m2, l2, r2) =>
          if m1 > m2 then
            if im_nomatch(p2, p1, m1) then
              im_link(p1, t1, p2, t2)
            elif im_zero(p2, m1) then
              IMBranch(p1, m1, intmap_union_with(f, l1, t2), r1)
            else
              IMBranch(p1, m1, l1, intmap_union_with(f, r1, t2))
          elif m2 > m1 then
            if im_nomatch(p1, p2, m2) then
              im_link(p1, t1, p2, t2)
            elif im_zero(p1, m2) then
              IMBranch(p2, m2, intmap_union_with(f, t1, l2), r2)
            else
              IMBranch(p2, m2, l2, intmap_union_with(f, t1, r2))
          elif p1 == p2 then
            IMBranch(
                p1,
                m1,
                intmap_union_with(f, l1, l2),
                intmap_union_with(f, r1, r2),
              )
          else
            im_link(p1, t1, p2, t2)
defs.doc:
The union of two maps, combining a key present in both as `f(left, right)`.

The two branch nodes are walked together: the shallower one is descended into until the masks meet, so the merge costs the shape of the two tries rather than a re-insertion of every binding.

```prism
intmap_to_list(
  intmap_union_with(
    \(a, b) -> a + b,
    intmap_from_list([(1i64, 10), (2i64, 20)]),
    intmap_from_list([(2i64, 2), (3i64, 3)]),
  ),
)
```

```output
[(1, 10), (2, 22), (3, 3)]
```

defs.name: intmap_filter
defs.ty: forall e0 a. ((I64, a) -> Bool ! {e0}, Data.IntMap.IntMap(a)) -> Data.IntMap.IntMap(a) ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn intmap_filter(keep, t : IntMap(v)) : IntMap(v) =
  match t of
    IMEmpty => IMEmpty
    IMLeaf(k, v) =>
      if keep(k, v) then
        t
      else
        IMEmpty
    IMBranch(p, m, l, r) =>
      im_bin(p, m, intmap_filter(keep, l), intmap_filter(keep, r))
defs.doc:
The bindings satisfying `keep(key, value)`.

A surviving branch still splits on the highest bit two of its remaining keys differ on, because a branch whose child empties collapses, so filtering lands on the same tree the survivors would have built from scratch.

```prism
intmap_to_list(
  intmap_filter(
    \(_k, v) -> v > 1,
    intmap_from_list([(1i64, 1), (2i64, 2), (3i64, 3)]),
  ),
)
```

```output
[(2, 2), (3, 3)]
```

defs.name: intmap_map_values
defs.ty: forall e0 a b. ((a) -> b ! {e0}, Data.IntMap.IntMap(a)) -> Data.IntMap.IntMap(b) ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn intmap_map_values(f, t : IntMap(v)) : IntMap(w) =
  match t of
    IMEmpty => IMEmpty
    IMLeaf(k, v) => IMLeaf(k, f(v))
    IMBranch(p, m, l, r) =>
      IMBranch(p, m, intmap_map_values(f, l), intmap_map_values(f, r))
defs.doc:
Apply `f` to every value, keeping keys and tree shape.

```prism
intmap_values(
  intmap_map_values(\(v) -> v + 1, intmap_from_list([(1i64, 10), (2i64, 20)])),
)
```
