defs.ty: forall a. (List((String, Json.Json)), String, String, (Json.Json, String) -> a ! {Syntax.Codec.Decode}) -> Option(a) ! {Syntax.Codec.Decode}

defs.name: list_at
defs.ty: forall a. (List((String, Json.Json)), String, String, (Json.Json, String) -> a ! {Syntax.Codec.Decode}) -> List(a) ! {Syntax.Codec.Decode}

defs.name: req_arr
defs.ty: forall a. (List((String, Json.Json)), String, String, (Json.Json, String) -> a ! {Syntax.Codec.Decode}) -> List(a) ! {Syntax.Codec.Decode}

defs.name: strs_at
defs.source:
fn strs_at(
  fields : List((String, Json)),
  key : String,
  path : String
) : List(String) ! {Decode} =
  match jget(fields, key) of
    None => []
    Some(v) => strs_of(v, "{path}.{key}")

defs.name: decode_resolved
defs.source:
fn decode_resolved(text : String) : Result(ResolvedDoc, CodecError) =
  run_decode(\() -> decode_resolved_doc(text))
defs.doc: Decode a `prism-resolved-syntax-v1` document. Total: every malformed input lands on a `CodecError` naming the JSON path that refused. The node tree decodes recursively; a child list is bounded by the input's own nesting.

defs.name: decode_resolved_doc
validate_resolved
check_unique_ids
check_span_ends
defs.source:
fn check_span_ends(
  spans : List(Span),
  len : Int,
  path : String
) : Unit ! {Decode} =
  match spans of
    Nil => ()
    Cons(s, rest) =>
      if s.hi <= len then
        check_span_ends(rest, len, path)
      else
        fail_decode(
            CodecError {
              path = path,
              reason = "span [{s.lo}, {s.hi}) past source length {len}"
            },
          )

defs.name: decode_or_codec_error
defs.source:
fn decode_or_codec_error(text : String) : Result(Json, CodecError) =
  match decode(text) of
    Ok(j) => Ok(j)
    Err(e) => Err(CodecError { path = "$", reason = json_error_message(e) })

defs.name: rfunction_of
rparam_of
rnode_of
rnode_children_of
defs.source:
fn rnode_children_of(
  fields : List((String, Json)),
  path : String
) : List(RNode) ! {Decode} =
  match jget(fields, "children") of
    None => []
    Some(jc) =>
      map(
          \(jn) -> rnode_of(jn, "{path}.children"),
          arr_at(jc, "{path}.children"),
        )

defs.name: rnode_json
defs.source:
fn rnode_json(n : RNode) : Json =
  let base =
    [("id", JInt(n.id)), ("kind", JStr(n.kind)), ("span", span_json(n.span))]
  match n.children of
    Nil => JObj(base)
    Cons(_, _) =>
      JObj(append(base, [("children", JArr(map(rnode_json, n.children)))]))

defs.name: rfunction_json
rparam_json
defs.source:
fn rparam_json(p : RParam) : Json =
  JObj([("name", JStr(p.name)), ("borrow", JBool(p.is_borrow))])

defs.name: encode_resolved
span_join
defs.source:
fn span_join(a : Span, b : Span) : Span =
  Span { lo = min(a.lo, b.lo), hi = max(a.hi, b.hi) }
defs.doc:
The smallest span covering both: the earlier start and the later end. The one operation a parser needs to give a node built from parts the extent of those parts.

```prism
let s = span_join(span_at(2), span_at(11))
(s.lo, s.hi)
```

```output
(2, 11)
```

defs.name: span_at
defs.source: fn span_at(pos : Int) : Span = Span { lo = pos, hi = pos }
defs.doc:
The empty span at a byte offset: the caret a diagnostic points with when it has a position but nothing was consumed there.

```prism
let s = span_at(12)
(s.lo, s.hi)
```

```output
(12, 12)
```

defs.name: span_cover
defs.source:
fn span_cover(ss : List(Span)) : Option(Span) =
  match ss of
    Nil => None
    Cons(s, rest) => Some(cover_go(s, rest))
defs.doc: The smallest span covering every span in the list, or None for the empty list. Joining has no identity over spans (the empty span at offset zero is a position, not a neutral element), so the empty case is absent rather than invented.

defs.name: cover_go
defs.source:
fn cover_go(acc : Span, ss : List(Span)) : Span =
  match ss of
    Nil => acc
    Cons(s, rest) => cover_go(span_join(acc, s), rest)

defs.name: Cursor
defs.source:
type Cursor = Cursor {
  toks: Array(Token),
  pos: Int,
  stop: Int,
  far: Int,
  wanted: List(String)
}
defs.doc: A token cursor: the tokens being read, the read position, the byte offset the end-of-input caret points at, and the failure record (the furthest position at which an expectation was recorded, and the names recorded there). The failure record is part of the cursor rather than of a failure value because it must outlive every failure a parse recovers from.

defs.name: Reply
defs.source: type Reply(a) = Took(a, Cursor) | Stuck(Cursor)
defs.doc: The reply of a cursor step: the value and the advanced cursor, or the cursor alone. A refusal still carries a cursor, because the failure record it accumulated is the part worth reporting.

defs.name: cursor_of
defs.doc: A cursor over a token list. `stop` is the byte offset the end-of-input caret points at, normally the length of the source the tokens were lexed from, so a refusal past the last token still carries a position.

defs.name: cursor_count
defs.source: fn cursor_count(c : Cursor) : Int = array_len(c.toks)
defs.doc: The number of tokens the cursor reads over.

defs.name: cursor_at_end
defs.source: fn cursor_at_end(c : Cursor) : Bool = c.pos >= cursor_count(c)
defs.doc: Whether every token has been consumed.

defs.name: cursor_peek_at
defs.source:
fn cursor_peek_at(c : Cursor, k : Int) : Option(Token) =
  let i = c.pos + k
  if i >= 0 && i < cursor_count(c) then
    Some(array_get(c.toks, i))
  else
    None
defs.doc: The token `k` positions ahead of the read position, or None past the end.

defs.name: cursor_peek
defs.source: fn cursor_peek(c : Cursor) : Option(Token) = cursor_peek_at(c, 0)
defs.doc: The token at the read position, or None at the end. Peeking never consumes and never records an expectation: a parser that looks before it leaps says what it wanted with `cursor_note`.

defs.name: cursor_kind
defs.source:
fn cursor_kind(c : Cursor) : Option(TokenKind) =
  match cursor_peek(c) of
    None => None
    Some(t) => Some(t.kind)
defs.doc: The kind of the token at the read position, or None at the end.

defs.name: span_index
defs.source:
fn span_index(c : Cursor, i : Int) : Span =
  if i >= 0 && i < cursor_count(c) then
    array_get(c.toks, i).span
  else
    span_at(c.stop)

defs.name: cursor_span
defs.source: fn cursor_span(c : Cursor) : Span = span_index(c, c.pos)
defs.doc: The span the cursor points at: the next token's span, or the end-of-input caret when the stream is exhausted.

defs.name: cursor_advance
defs.doc: The cursor advanced past one token. At the end this is the identity, so a parser that advances on a token it did not check cannot run off the stream.

defs.name: cursor_since
defs.source:
fn cursor_since(saved : Cursor, c : Cursor) : Span =
  if c.pos <= saved.pos then
    span_at(cursor_span(c).lo)
  else
    span_join(span_index(saved, saved.pos), span_index(c, c.pos - 1))
defs.doc: The span covering the tokens consumed between `saved` and `c`, or the caret at the current position when nothing was consumed. A parser gives a node its extent by saving the cursor before it and asking for the run after it, rather than by joining the spans of its parts by hand and forgetting the delimiters.

defs.name: end_of_input
defs.source: fn end_of_input() : String = "end of input"
defs.doc: The name the end of the token stream is expected under. Not a token, so not a token kind, but an expectation like any other.

defs.name: has_name
defs.source:
fn has_name(xs : List(String), name : String) : Bool =
  match xs of
    Nil => false
    Cons(x, rest) =>
      if x == name then
        true
      else
        has_name(rest, name)

defs.name: add_name
defs.source:
fn add_name(xs : List(String), name : String) : List(String) =
  if has_name(xs, name) then
    xs
  else
    append(xs, [name])

defs.name: cursor_note_name
defs.doc:
Record `name` as admissible at the read position, consuming nothing.

The record only ever moves forward. A name recorded past the furthest position reached replaces the set and moves the mark; a name at the furthest position joins the set; a name behind it is dropped. That ordering is the whole point: a parse that tries an alternative, gets three tokens deep and fails, then rewinds, must still report what was wanted three tokens in, not what was wanted at the place it rewound to.

defs.name: cursor_note
defs.source:
fn cursor_note(c : Cursor, k : TokenKind) : Cursor =
  cursor_note_name(c, kind_name(k))
defs.doc: Record a token kind as admissible at the read position. The name recorded is the kind's wire name, so an expectation set, a token artifact, and a diagnostic's `expected` field all speak one vocabulary.

defs.name: cursor_expect
defs.source:
fn cursor_expect(c : Cursor, k : TokenKind) : Reply(Token) =
  match cursor_peek(c) of
    None => Stuck(cursor_note(c, k))
    Some(t) =>
      if t.kind == k then
        Took(t, cursor_advance(c))
      else
        Stuck(cursor_note(c, k))
defs.doc: Consume the next token when its kind is `k`. On a mismatch nothing is consumed and `k` joins the expectation set at this position, so a parser that tries several kinds in turn accumulates all of them: expecting one of a set is spelled as expecting each of its members at one position, never as a separate combinator.

defs.name: cursor_expect_fixed
defs.source:
fn cursor_expect_fixed(c : Cursor, s : String) : Reply(Token) =
  cursor_expect(c, TFixed(s))
defs.doc: Consume the next token when it is the fixed token spelled `s`.

defs.name: cursor_expect_end
defs.source:
fn cursor_expect_end(c : Cursor) : Reply(Unit) =
  if cursor_at_end(c) then
    Took((), c)
  else
    Stuck(cursor_note_name(c, end_of_input()))
defs.doc: Require that every token has been consumed, recording the end of the stream as the expectation when one is left over.

defs.name: cursor_restore
defs.source:
fn cursor_restore(saved : Cursor, c : Cursor) : Cursor =
  Cursor { ..saved, far = c.far, wanted = c.wanted }
defs.doc:
Rewind to a saved cursor while keeping the failure record reached since.

A parser that tries an alternative and gives it up restores with this: the position returns, the expectations do not. Rebuilding the saved cursor by hand instead is the classic way to report the expectations of the position the parse retreated to rather than of the position it died at.

```prism
let c0 = cursor_of(Nil, 0)
let c1 = cursor_note_name(c0, "ident")
str_join(", ", cursor_expected(cursor_restore(c0, c1)))
```

```output
ident
```

defs.name: cursor_expected
defs.source: fn cursor_expected(c : Cursor) : List(String) = c.wanted
defs.doc:
The names recorded at the furthest position reached, in the order they were first recorded.

```prism
let c = cursor_note_name(cursor_of(Nil, 3), "ident")
str_join(", ", cursor_expected(cursor_note_name(c, "int")))
```

```output
ident, int
```

defs.name: ins_name
defs.source:
fn ins_name(n : String, acc : List(String)) : List(String) =
  match acc of
    Nil => [n]
    Cons(h, t) =>
      if n < h then
        Cons(n, acc)
      elif n == h then
        acc
      else
        Cons(h, ins_name(n, t))

defs.name: cursor_canonical
defs.source: fn cursor_canonical(c : Cursor) : List(String) = foldr(ins_name, [], c.wanted)
defs.doc:
The canonical expectation set of a refusal: the recorded names deduplicated and byte-lexicographically sorted, so the set a diagnostic carries does not depend on the order alternatives were tried, and a harmless reordering of a parser's branches moves no artifact bytes.

```prism
let c = cursor_note_name(cursor_of(Nil, 3), "int")
str_join(", ", cursor_canonical(cursor_note_name(c, "ident")))
```

```output
ident, int
```

defs.name: cursor_far_span
defs.source: fn cursor_far_span(c : Cursor) : Span = span_index(c, c.far)
defs.doc: The span the failure record points at: the token at the furthest position reached, or the end-of-input caret.

defs.name: found_name
defs.source:
fn found_name(c : Cursor) : String =
  if c.far >= cursor_count(c) then
    end_of_input()
  else
    kind_name(array_get(c.toks, c.far).kind)

defs.name: cursor_message
defs.doc: The rendered message of an unmet expectation: the merged expectation set and what stood there instead.

defs.name: parse_syntax_code
defs.source: fn parse_syntax_code() : String = "E7100"
defs.doc: The compiler's general parse-fault code, the one home for the string on this side of the seam.

defs.name: parse_eof_code
defs.source: fn parse_eof_code() : String = "E7101"
defs.doc: The compiler's exhausted-stream code: the token stream itself ended while the parser wanted more.

defs.name: cursor_code
defs.source:
fn cursor_code(c : Cursor) : String =
  if c.far >= cursor_count(c) then
    parse_eof_code()
  else
    parse_syntax_code()
defs.doc: The stable code an unmet expectation carries: the parser's end-of-input code when the furthest position reached is past the last token, and its general syntax code otherwise. Both match the compiler's own parse codes.

defs.name: cursor_diagnostic
defs.doc: The refusal an unmet expectation produces: a parse-phase diagnostic at the furthest position reached, carrying the canonical expectation set. The message keeps the order alternatives were tried, for a reader; the set is sorted, for the artifact. A cursor failure is a diagnostic and never a bespoke error value, so a hand-written parser's refusals join the same document the compiler's own do.

defs.name: Assoc
defs.source: type Assoc = ALeft | ARight | ANone deriving (Eq)
defs.doc: How an infix operator groups a chain of its own level. A non-associative operator declines a second application at its level, leaving the second operator unconsumed for the caller to refuse.

defs.name: Infix
defs.source: type Infix = Infix { op: String, level: Int, assoc: Assoc }
defs.doc: One infix operator: the token spelling, its level (higher binds tighter), and how it associates.

defs.name: Prefix
defs.source: type Prefix = Prefix { op: String, level: Int }
defs.doc: One prefix operator: the token spelling and the level its operand is parsed at. An operator that binds tighter than that level is pulled into the operand; one that binds looser takes the prefix application as its left operand.

defs.name: infix_left_bp
defs.source:
fn infix_left_bp(i : Infix) : Int =
  match i.assoc of
    ARight => i.level * 2 + 1
    _ => i.level * 2
defs.doc:
The power binding an infix operator's left operand.

Levels are doubled so each has a half step above it. A left-associative operator's right power sits in that half step, which stops a second operator of the same level from being pulled into the right operand; a right associative operator's left power sits there instead, which lets it be. A non-associative operator is left-shaped here and refuses the repeat outright.

defs.name: infix_right_bp
defs.source:
fn infix_right_bp(i : Infix) : Int =
  match i.assoc of
    ARight => i.level * 2
    _ => i.level * 2 + 1
defs.doc: The power an infix operator's right operand is parsed at.

defs.name: prefix_bp
defs.source: fn prefix_bp(p : Prefix) : Int = p.level * 2
defs.doc: The power a prefix operator's operand is parsed at.

defs.name: infix_lookup
defs.source:
fn infix_lookup(tbl : List(Infix), op : String) : Option(Infix) =
  match tbl of
    Nil => None
    Cons(i, rest) =>
      if i.op == op then
        Some(i)
      else
        infix_lookup(rest, op)
defs.doc: The entry for an operator spelling in an infix table, or None when the spelling is not an infix operator.

defs.name: prefix_lookup
defs.source:
fn prefix_lookup(tbl : List(Prefix), op : String) : Option(Prefix) =
  match tbl of
    Nil => None
    Cons(p, rest) =>
      if p.op == op then
        Some(p)
      else
        prefix_lookup(rest, op)
defs.doc: The entry for an operator spelling in a prefix table, or None when the spelling is not a prefix operator.

defs.name: Pratt
defs.source:
type Pratt(a) = Pratt {
  infixes: List(Infix),
  prefixes: List(Prefix),
  leaf: (Cursor) -> Reply(a),
  bin: (String, a, a) -> a,
  pre: (String, a) -> a
}
defs.doc: Everything the driver needs that is not the cursor: the two operator tables, the leaf parser, and the two node builders. The leaf parser owns primaries, and so owns parentheses, and so owns the recursion back into the driver: the driver knows about operators and nothing else.

defs.name: spelling_at
defs.source:
fn spelling_at(c : Cursor) : Option(String) =
  match cursor_peek(c) of
    None => None
    Some(t) =>
      match t.kind of
        TFixed(s) => Some(s)
        _ => None

defs.name: prefix_at
defs.source:
fn prefix_at(sp : Pratt(a), c : Cursor) : Option(Prefix) =
  match spelling_at(c) of
    None => None
    Some(s) => prefix_lookup(sp.prefixes, s)

defs.name: infix_at
defs.source:
fn infix_at(sp : Pratt(a), c : Cursor) : Option(Infix) =
  match spelling_at(c) of
    None => None
    Some(s) => infix_lookup(sp.infixes, s)

defs.name: pratt_operand
defs.source:
fn pratt_operand(sp : Pratt(a), c : Cursor) : Reply(a) =
  match prefix_at(sp, c) of
    None => (sp.leaf)(c)
    Some(p) =>
      match pratt_expr(sp, cursor_advance(c), prefix_bp(p)) of
        Stuck(c2) => Stuck(c2)
        Took(x, c2) => Took((sp.pre)(p.op, x), c2)

defs.name: pratt_loop
defs.ty: forall a. (Syntax.Cursor.Pratt(a), a, Syntax.Cursor.Cursor, Int, Int) -> Syntax.Cursor.Reply(a)
defs.source:
fn pratt_loop(
  sp : Pratt(a),
  lhs : a,
  c : Cursor,
  min_bp : Int,
  blocked : Int
) : Reply(a) =
  match infix_at(sp, c) of
    None => Took(lhs, c)
    Some(ix) =>
      let repeat = ix.assoc == ANone && ix.level == blocked
      if infix_left_bp(ix) < min_bp || repeat then
        Took(lhs, c)
      else
        match pratt_expr(sp, cursor_advance(c), infix_right_bp(ix)) of
          Stuck(c2) => Stuck(c2)
          Took(rhs, c2) =>
            let next =
              if ix.assoc == ANone then
                ix.level
              else
                -1
            pratt_loop(sp, (sp.bin)(ix.op, lhs, rhs), c2, min_bp, next)

defs.name: pratt_expr
defs.source:
fn pratt_expr(sp : Pratt(a), c : Cursor, min_bp : Int) : Reply(a) =
  match pratt_operand(sp, c) of
    Stuck(c2) => Stuck(c2)
    Took(lhs, c2) => pratt_loop(sp, lhs, c2, min_bp, -1)
defs.doc: Parse one expression whose operators all bind at least as tightly as `min_bp`: one operand, then every operator that outbinds the caller.

defs.name: pratt_parse
defs.source: fn pratt_parse(sp : Pratt(a), c : Cursor) : Reply(a) = pratt_expr(sp, c, 0)
defs.doc: Parse one expression at the loosest binding power. Tokens after it are left for the caller, which is what makes this usable inside a larger grammar.

defs.name: pratt_all
defs.source:
fn pratt_all(sp : Pratt(a), c : Cursor) : Reply(a) =
  match pratt_parse(sp, c) of
    Stuck(c2) => Stuck(c2)
    Took(x, c2) =>
      match cursor_expect_end(c2) of
        Stuck(c3) => Stuck(c3)
        Took(_, c3) => Took(x, c3)
defs.doc: Parse one expression and require the whole token stream to be consumed. A trailing operator the driver declined (a repeated non-associative one) is refused here, at the position it stands.

defs.name: expr_infix_table
defs.source:
fn expr_infix_table() : List(Infix) =
  [
      Infix { op = "??", level = 1, assoc = ARight },
      Infix { op = "|>", level = 2, assoc = ALeft },
      Infix { op = ">>", level = 3, assoc = ALeft },
      Infix { op = "<<", level = 3, assoc = ALeft },
      Infix { op = "||", level = 4, assoc = ALeft },
      Infix { op = "&&", level = 5, assoc = ALeft },
      Infix { op = "==", level = 6, assoc = ANone },
      Infix { op = "/=", level = 6, assoc = ANone },
      Infix { op = "<", level = 6, assoc = ANone },
      Infix { op = "<=", level = 6, assoc = ANone },
      Infix { op = ">", level = 6, assoc = ANone },
      Infix { op = ">=", level = 6, assoc = ANone },
      Infix { op = "+", level = 7, assoc = ALeft },
      Infix { op = "-", level = 7, assoc = ALeft },
      Infix { op = "*", level = 8, assoc = ALeft },
      Infix { op = "/", level = 8, assoc = ALeft },
      Infix { op = "%", level = 8, assoc = ALeft },
      Infix { op = "^", level = 10, assoc = ARight },
    ]
defs.doc: The infix table of Prism's own expression grammar, loosest first. Levels are relative: only their order and each operator's associativity carry meaning, and both are pinned against the compiler's parser by a differential test rather than by this comment.

defs.name: expr_prefix_table
defs.source: fn expr_prefix_table() : List(Prefix) = [Prefix { op = "-", level = 9 }]
defs.doc: The prefix table of Prism's own expression grammar: unary minus, sitting between multiplication and exponentiation. `-x * y` is `(-x) * y` and, by the mathematical convention, `-x ^ y` is `-(x ^ y)`.

defs.name: DiagPhase
defs.source: type DiagPhase = DPLex | DPParse
defs.doc: The phase that raised a diagnostic.

defs.name: Diagnostic
defs.source:
type Diagnostic = Diagnostic {
  code: String,
  phase: DiagPhase,
  span: Span,
  message: String,
  expected: List(String),
  related: List(Span)
}
defs.doc: One diagnostic: the stable append-only code, the raising phase, the primary half-open byte span (a lex fault is a caret, `lo == hi`), the rendered message, the parser's canonical expectation set when it has one, and related spans.

defs.name: DiagnosticsDoc
defs.doc: A decoded diagnostics document: the envelope identity, the embedded source every span indexes into, and the diagnostics in source order.

defs.name: diagnostics_schema
defs.source: fn diagnostics_schema() : String = "prism-syntax-diagnostics-v1"
defs.doc: The schema tag this vocabulary decodes.

defs.name: doc_accepted
defs.source:
fn doc_accepted(d : DiagnosticsDoc) : Bool =
  match d.diagnostics of
    Nil => true
    Cons(_, _) => false
defs.doc: Whether the document accepted its source (no diagnostics).

defs.name: Edit
defs.source: type Edit = Edit { span: Span, text: String }
defs.doc: One edit: the byte span it replaces and the text that replaces it. An insertion is an empty span, a deletion is empty text.

defs.name: EditError
defs.source:
type EditError
  = EdBadSpan(Span)
  | EdPastEnd(Span, Int)
  | EdOverlap(Span, Span)
  | EdRelex(LexError)
  deriving (Eq, Show)
defs.doc: Why an edit set was refused. Every case names the offending span, so a tool can point at the edit it got wrong.

defs.name: ed_insert_at
defs.doc: An insertion at one offset.

defs.name: ed_delete
defs.source: fn ed_delete(span : Span) : Edit = Edit { span = span, text = "" }
defs.doc: A deletion of one span.

defs.name: ed_replace
defs.source:
fn ed_replace(span : Span, text : String) : Edit =
  Edit { span = span, text = text }
defs.doc: A replacement of one span.

defs.name: ed_span_text
defs.source:
fn ed_span_text(text : String, s : Span) : Option(String) =
  if span_valid(s) && s.hi <= str_len(text) then
    Some(substring(text, s.lo, span_len(s)))
  else
    None
defs.doc: The current text under a span, or `None` when the span does not address this text. What a rename reads to check that an occurrence still says what the plan assumed.

defs.name: ed_message
defs.source:
fn ed_message(e : EditError) : String =
  match e of
    EdBadSpan(s) => "edit span {show(s.lo)}..{show(s.hi)} is not well formed"
    EdPastEnd(s, n) =>
      "edit span {show(s.lo)}..{show(s.hi)} runs past the end of {show(n)} bytes"
    EdOverlap(a, b) =>
      "edits {show(a.lo)}..{show(a.hi)} and {show(b.lo)}..{show(b.hi)} overlap"
    EdRelex(le) => "the edited text does not lex: {lex_message(le)}"
defs.doc: A human-readable account of a refusal.

defs.name: ed_sort
defs.source: fn ed_sort(edits : List(Edit)) : List(Edit) = foldl(ed_place, Nil, edits)
defs.doc: The edits sorted by start offset, stably: two edits starting at the same offset keep their input order, so a caller that means "insert A then B here" gets it.

defs.name: ed_place
defs.source:
fn ed_place(sorted : List(Edit), e : Edit) : List(Edit) =
  match sorted of
    Nil => [e]
    Cons(x, rest) =>
      if x.span.lo <= e.span.lo then
        Cons(x, ed_place(rest, e))
      else
        Cons(e, sorted)

defs.name: ed_apply
defs.source:
fn ed_apply(text : String, edits : List(Edit)) : Result(String, EditError) =
  match ed_splice(text, ed_sort(edits), 0, None, "") of
    Err(e) => Err(e)
    Ok(out) => ed_relex(out)
defs.doc:
Apply an edit set to a source text.

The result is the spliced text when every edit is well formed, the edits do not overlap, and the splice still lexes. Otherwise it is the first refusal found, in that order.

defs.name: ed_count
defs.source: fn ed_count(edits : List(Edit)) : Int = length(edits)
defs.doc: How many edits an edit set holds: the count a plan reports before anything is applied.

defs.name: ed_relex
defs.source:
fn ed_relex(out : String) : Result(String, EditError) =
  match lex_raw(out) of
    Err(le) => Err(EdRelex(le))
    Ok(_) => Ok(out)

defs.name: ed_splice
defs.ty: (String, List(Syntax.Edit.Edit), Int, Option(Syntax.Source.Span), String) -> Result(String, Syntax.Edit.EditError)
defs.source:
fn ed_splice(
  text : String,
  edits : List(Edit),
  at : Int,
  prev : Option(Span),
  acc : String
) : Result(String, EditError) =
  match edits of
    Nil => Ok(concat(acc, substring(text, at, str_len(text) - at)))
    Cons(e, rest) =>
      if not(span_valid(e.span)) then
        Err(EdBadSpan(e.span))
      elif e.span.hi > str_len(text) then
        Err(EdPastEnd(e.span, str_len(text)))
      elif e.span.lo < at then
        Err(EdOverlap(ed_prev_span(prev, e.span), e.span))
      else
        ed_splice(
            text,
            rest,
            e.span.hi,
            Some(e.span),
            concat(concat(acc, substring(text, at, e.span.lo - at)), e.text),
          )

defs.name: ed_prev_span
defs.source:
fn ed_prev_span(prev : Option(Span), here : Span) : Span =
  match prev of
    Some(s) => s
    None => here

defs.name: fl_defined
defs.source:
fn fl_defined(doc : ResolvedDoc) : Map(String, Unit) =
  set_from_list(map(fl_fn_name, doc.functions))
defs.doc: The names the document defines, as a set.

defs.name: fl_fn_name
defs.source: fn fl_fn_name(f : RFunction) : String = f.name

defs.name: fl_references
defs.source:
fn fl_references(src : SourceFile, f : RFunction) : List(String) =
  concat_map(\(n) -> fl_reference(src, n), rnode_universe(f.body))
defs.doc: Every identifier one function's body references, in source order, sliced from the embedded source. A reference the source cannot address is dropped, which `Syntax.Rename`'s `rn_unaddressed` is how to detect before trusting any answer here.

defs.name: fl_reference
defs.source:
fn fl_reference(src : SourceFile, n : RNode) : List(String) =
  if n.kind == rkind_var() then
    match ed_span_text(src.text, n.span) of
      Some(name) => [name]
      None => []
  else
    []

defs.name: fl_calls
defs.doc: The call graph: an edge from each function to every function of this document it references. Every defined function is a node, so one that calls nothing still gets an answer, and successor lists are ascending and duplicate-free, so the iteration order below is a function of the document alone.

defs.name: fl_edges
defs.ty: forall a b. (Map(String, List(String), a), Syntax.Source.SourceFile, Map(String, Unit, b), Syntax.Resolved.RFunction) -> Map(String, List(String), a)
defs.source:
fn fl_edges(
  g : Map(String, List(String)),
  src : SourceFile,
  defined : Map(String, Unit),
  f : RFunction
) : Map(String, List(String)) =
  foldl(
      \(a, name) -> graph_add_edge(a, f.name, name),
      graph_add_node(g, f.name),
      filter(\(name) -> set_member(name, defined), fl_references(src, f)),
    )

defs.name: fl_direct
defs.ty: forall a b c d. (Map(d, List(d), a)) -> Map(d, Map(d, Unit, b), c)
defs.doc:
The immediate successors of a graph as a set per node: the per-node contribution a propagation starts from.

```prism
# import Data.Graph (..)
map(\(p) -> (fst(p), set_to_list(snd(p))), map_to_list(fl_direct(graph_from_edges([("f", "g")]))))
```

```output
[(f, [g])]
```

defs.name: fl_transitive
defs.ty: forall a b. (Syntax.Resolved.ResolvedDoc) -> Map(String, Map(String, Unit, a), b) ! {Fail}
defs.doc: Every function each function transitively calls: the least assignment with `x[f]` the union of `direct[f]` and every `x[g]` for `g` in `direct[f]`. The members of one cycle share one answer, and a function on a cycle lists itself.

defs.name: fl_live
defs.ty: forall a. (Syntax.Resolved.ResolvedDoc, List(String)) -> Map(String, Unit, a) ! {Fail}
defs.doc: The functions reachable from `roots`: the same solve with the calls relation reversed, so reachability flows from a caller to its callees, over the Boolean lattice. A root the document does not define contributes nothing.

defs.name: fl_reached
defs.ty: forall a b. (Map(String, Bool, a)) -> Map(String, Unit, b)
defs.source:
fn fl_reached(x : Map(String, Bool)) : Map(String, Unit) =
  set_from_list(map(fst, filter(\(p) -> snd(p), map_to_list(x))))

defs.name: fl_dead
defs.doc: The functions no root reaches, ascending: what a dead-code report is, once the document's entry points are named.

defs.name: fl_recursive
defs.doc: The functions that call themselves, directly or through a cycle, ascending. This is the question a plain traversal answers wrongly and the fixpoint answers by construction: mutual recursion is a cycle, not a self-edge.

defs.name: source_identity
defs.source: fn source_identity(f : SourceFile) : String = f.digest
defs.doc:
The source identity of an artifact: the digest of its exact bytes.

```prism
# import Syntax.Source (..)
source_identity(SourceFile { digest = "9f86d0", text = "fn main() = ()" })
```

```output
9f86d0
```

defs.name: surface_identity
defs.doc:
The surface identity of a decoded surface document: the canonical rendering of its schema tag and item tree with every span erased.

Two documents share a surface identity exactly when they are the same tree of the same schema, whatever text produced them. The identity is computed by re-encoding the document and stripping positions from the result, so it inherits the encoder's canonical layout rather than introducing a second one; an encoding that cannot be read back is reported, never silently accepted.

defs.name: surface_subject
defs.source:
fn surface_subject(j : Json) : Json =
  match j of
    JObj(fields) => strip_positions(JObj(filter(is_subject_field, fields)))
    _ => j

defs.name: is_subject_field
is_position_field
drop_spans
defs.source:

    JObj(fields) => Some(JObj(filter(is_position_field, fields)))
    _ => None

defs.name: strip_positions
defs.source: fn strip_positions(j : Json) : Json = rw_everywhere(json_layer(), drop_spans, j)

defs.name: ly_line_start
defs.source:
fn ly_line_start(text : String, off : Int) : Int =
  var j := off
  while j > 0 && byte_at(text, j - 1) /= 10 do
    j -= 1
  j

defs.name: ly_col
defs.source: fn ly_col(text : String, off : Int) : Int = off - ly_line_start(text, off)

defs.source:
fn ly_count_nl(text : String, a : Int, b : Int) : Int =
  var i := a
  var c := 0
  while i < b do
    if byte_at(text, i) == 10 then
      c += 1
    i += 1
  c

defs.name: ly_prev_line
defs.source:
fn ly_prev_line(st : LState) : Int =
  match st.prev_line of
    Some(l) => l
    None => 0

defs.name: ly_top
defs.source:
fn ly_top(xs : List(Int)) : Option(Int) =
  match xs of
    Nil => None
    Cons(h, _) => Some(h)

defs.name: ly_pop
defs.source:
fn ly_pop(xs : List(Int)) : List(Int) =
  match xs of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(_, t) => t

defs.name: ly_depth
defs.source:
fn ly_depth(xs : List(Int)) : Int =
  match xs of
    Nil => 0
    Cons(_, t) => 1 + ly_depth(t)

defs.name: ly_virt
ly_vopen

defs.name: ly_mem
defs.source:
fn ly_mem(s : String, xs : List(String)) : Bool =
  match xs of
    Nil => false
    Cons(h, t) => s == h || ly_mem(s, t)

defs.name: ly_opener_words
defs.source:
fn ly_opener_words() : List(String) =
  [
      "=",
      "then",
      "else",
      "=>",
      "of",
      "with",
      "handler",
      "fn",
      "try",
      "catch",
      "transact",
      "do",
      "where",
      "loop",
    ]

defs.name: ly_opens_block
defs.source:
fn ly_opens_block(k : TokenKind) : Bool =
  match k of
    TFixed(s) => ly_mem(s, ly_opener_words())
    _ => false

defs.name: ly_is_bopen
defs.source:
fn ly_is_bopen(k : TokenKind) : Bool =
  match k of
    TFixed(s) => s == "(" || s == "[" || s == "\{"
    _ => false

defs.name: ly_is_bclose
defs.source:
fn ly_is_bclose(k : TokenKind) : Bool =
  match k of
    TFixed(s) => s == ")" || s == "]" || s == "\}"
    _ => false

defs.name: ly_is_carry
defs.source:
fn ly_is_carry(k : TokenKind) : Bool =
  match k of
    TFixed(s) => s == "fn"
    _ => false

defs.source:
fn ly_opens_decl(k : TokenKind) : Bool =
  match k of

    _ => false

defs.name: ly_e_lo
defs.source:
fn ly_e_lo(e : LEntry) : Int =
  match e of
    LTok(t) => t.span.lo
    LHead(o) => o

defs.name: ly_e_hi
defs.source:
fn ly_e_hi(e : LEntry) : Int =
  match e of
    LTok(t) => t.span.hi
    LHead(o) => o

defs.name: ly_e_opener
defs.source:
fn ly_e_opener(e : LEntry) : Bool =
  match e of
    LTok(t) => ly_opens_block(t.kind)
    LHead(_) => true

defs.name: ly_e_bopen
defs.source:
fn ly_e_bopen(e : LEntry) : Bool =
  match e of
    LTok(t) => ly_is_bopen(t.kind)
    LHead(_) => false

defs.name: ly_e_bclose
defs.source:
fn ly_e_bclose(e : LEntry) : Bool =
  match e of
    LTok(t) => ly_is_bclose(t.kind)
    LHead(_) => false

defs.name: ly_e_carry
defs.source:
fn ly_e_carry(e : LEntry) : Bool =

    LTok(t) => ly_is_carry(t.kind)
    LHead(_) => false

defs.name: ly_has_nl
defs.source:
fn ly_has_nl(text : String, lo : Int, hi : Int) : Bool =
  if lo >= hi then
    false
  elif byte_at(text, lo) == 10 then
    true
  else
    ly_has_nl(text, lo + 1, hi)

defs.name: ly_same_line
defs.source:
fn ly_same_line(text : String, prev_hi : Int, next_lo : Int) : Bool =
  if ly_has_nl(text, prev_hi, next_lo) then
    false
  else
    true

defs.name: ly_inject
defs.source:
fn ly_inject(text : String, toks : List(Token)) : List(LEntry) =
  reverse(ly_inject_go(text, toks, Nil))

defs.name: ly_inject_go
defs.source:
fn ly_inject_go(
  text : String,
  toks : List(Token),
  acc : List(LEntry)
) : List(LEntry) =
  match toks of
    Nil => acc
    Cons(t, rest) =>
      if ly_opens_decl(t.kind) then
        match ly_head_run(text, rest, t.span.hi, Cons(LTok(t), acc)) of
          HeadR { rest = rest2, endoff = endoff, acc = acc2 } =>
            ly_inject_go(text, rest2, Cons(LHead(endoff), acc2))
      else
        ly_inject_go(text, rest, Cons(LTok(t), acc))

defs.name: ly_head_run
ly_stack_step
defs.source:
fn ly_stack_step(stack : List(Int), col : Int, floor : Int) : Close3 =
  match ly_top(stack) of
    None => CNone
    Some(top) =>
      if top > col && ly_depth(stack) > floor then
        CPop
      elif top == col then
        CSep
      else
        CNone

defs.name: ly_close_loop
ly_is_newline
defs.source:
fn ly_is_newline(prev : Option(Int), cur : Int) : Bool =
  match prev of
    None => true
    Some(pl) => cur > pl

defs.name: ly_first
defs.source:
fn ly_first(prev : Option(Int)) : Bool =
  match prev of
    None => true
    Some(_) => false

defs.name: ly_phase1
defs.ty: (Syntax.Layout@LEntry, Syntax.Layout@LState, Int, Int, Bool, Bool, Bool, List(Syntax.Token.Token)) -> Syntax.Layout@Ph1R
defs.source:
fn ly_phase1(
  e : LEntry,
  st : LState,
  lo : Int,
  col : Int,
  new_line : Bool,
  in_brackets : Bool,
  bopen : Bool,
  out : List(Token)
) : Ph1R =
  if in_brackets then
    Ph1R {
      stack = st.stack,
      out = out,
      po = st.pending_opener,
      carry = st.carrying
    }
  else
    let top_deeper =
      match ly_top(st.stack) of
        None => true
        Some(t) => col > t
    let opens = st.pending_opener && new_line && top_deeper
    let po1 = ly_e_opener(e)
    let carry1 = ly_e_carry(e) || st.carrying && ly_not(new_line) && bopen
    if opens || ly_first(st.prev_line) then
      Ph1R {
        stack = Cons(col, st.stack),
        out = Cons(ly_vopen(lo), out),
        po = po1,
        carry = carry1
      }
    elif new_line then
      match ly_close_loop(st.stack, col, st.last_hi, out) of
        CloseR { stack = stack2, out = out2 } =>
          Ph1R { stack = stack2, out = out2, po = po1, carry = carry1 }
    else
      Ph1R { stack = st.stack, out = out, po = po1, carry = carry1 }

defs.name: ly_not
defs.source:
fn ly_not(b : Bool) : Bool =
  if b then
    false
  else
    true

defs.name: ly_phase2
ly_step
ly_drain
defs.source:
fn ly_drain(stack : List(Int), last_hi : Int, out : List(Token)) : List(Token) =
  match stack of
    Nil => reverse(out)
    Cons(_, rest) => ly_drain(rest, last_hi, Cons(ly_vclose(last_hi), out))

defs.name: ly_run
defs.source:
fn ly_run(
  text : String,
  entries : List(LEntry),
  st : LState,
  out : List(Token)
) : List(Token) =
  match entries of
    Nil => ly_drain(st.stack, st.last_hi, out)
    Cons(e, rest) =>
      match ly_step(text, e, st, out) of
        StepR(st2, out2) => ly_run(text, rest, st2, out2)

defs.name: ly_layout
layout
defs.source:
fn layout(text : String) : Result(List(Token), LexError) =
  match lex_raw(text) of
    Err(e) => Err(e)
    Ok(r) => Ok(ly_layout(text, r.tokens))
defs.doc: Tokenize and lay out `text`, reproducing the compiler's post-layout `parse` stream: the raw tokens with the virtual block delimiters spliced in and the synthetic head openers stripped. A lexing failure is propagated unchanged.

defs.name: LexRaw
defs.source: type LexRaw = LexRaw { tokens: List(Token), trivia: List(Trivia) }
defs.doc: The raw token layer: the semantic token stream and the trivia interleaved between them, each keyed by absolute byte span into the lexed text.

defs.name: LexError
defs.source:
type LexError
  = LxInvalid(Int)
  | LxEmptyHole(Int)
  | LxUntermHole(Int)
  | LxUntermStr(Int)
  | LxNumberSep(Int)
  deriving (Eq, Show)
defs.doc: A lexing failure, mirroring the compiler's five `LexError` variants one for one: an invalid token, an empty interpolation hole, an unterminated hole, an unterminated string, and a misplaced numeric separator. Each carries the byte offset where scanning stuck. The variant, its stable code, and its rendered message travel as data (see `lex_offset`/`lex_code`/`lex_message`), never encoded into a message string.

defs.name: lex_offset
defs.source:
fn lex_offset(e : LexError) : Int =
  match e of
    LxInvalid(o) => o
    LxEmptyHole(o) => o
    LxUntermHole(o) => o
    LxUntermStr(o) => o
    LxNumberSep(o) => o
defs.doc: The byte offset where a lexing failure stuck.

defs.name: lex_code
defs.source:
fn lex_code(e : LexError) : String =
  match e of
    LxInvalid(_) => "E7000"
    LxEmptyHole(_) => "E7001"
    LxUntermHole(_) => "E7002"
    LxUntermStr(_) => "E7003"
    LxNumberSep(_) => "E7004"
defs.doc: The stable, append-only diagnostic code a lexing failure carries, matching the compiler's `LexError::code` (E7000 through E7004).

defs.name: lex_message
defs.source:
fn lex_message(e : LexError) : String =
  match e of
    LxInvalid(_) => "unexpected token"
    LxEmptyHole(_) => "empty interpolation hole `\{\}`"
    LxUntermHole(_) => "unterminated interpolation hole"
    LxUntermStr(_) => "unterminated string literal"
    LxNumberSep(_) =>
      "malformed numeric literal: `_` separators must sit between two digits"
defs.doc: The rendered message, matching the compiler's `LexError` `Display` strings byte for byte so a decoded diagnostic compares equal.

defs.name: LxStep
defs.source: type LxStep = LxComment(Int) | LxTok(TokenKind, Int) | LxErr(LexError)

defs.name: lx_eof
defs.source: fn lx_eof() : Int = 256

defs.name: lx_at
defs.source:
fn lx_at(text : String, i : Int) : Int =
  if i < byte_len(text) then
    byte_at(text, i)
  else
    lx_eof()

defs.name: lx_b
defs.source: fn lx_b(s : String) : Int = byte_at(s, 0)

defs.name: lx_word
defs.source: fn lx_word(c : Int) : Bool = is_alnum(c) || c == lx_b("_")

defs.name: lx_seg_start
defs.source: fn lx_seg_start(c : Int) : Bool = is_alpha(c) || c == lx_b("_")

defs.name: lx_digit_us
defs.source: fn lx_digit_us(c : Int) : Bool = is_digit(c) || c == lx_b("_")

defs.name: lx_skip_ws
defs.source:
fn lx_skip_ws(text : String, i : Int, n : Int) : Int =
  var j := i
  while j < n && lx_ws(byte_at(text, j)) do
    j += 1
  j

defs.name: lx_scan_word
defs.source:
fn lx_scan_word(text : String, i : Int, n : Int) : Int =
  var j := i
  while j < n && lx_word(byte_at(text, j)) do
    j += 1
  j

defs.name: lx_scan_digits
defs.source:
fn lx_scan_digits(text : String, i : Int, n : Int) : Int =
  var j := i
  while j < n && lx_digit_us(byte_at(text, j)) do
    j += 1
  j

defs.name: lx_scan_comment
defs.source:
fn lx_scan_comment(text : String, i : Int, n : Int) : Int =
  var j := i
  while j < n && byte_at(text, j) /= 10 do
    j += 1
  j

defs.name: lx_scan_exp
defs.source:
fn lx_scan_exp(text : String, k : Int, n : Int) : Int =
  let c = lx_at(text, k)
  if c == lx_b("e") || c == lx_b("E") then
    let m0 = k + 1
    let s = lx_at(text, m0)
    let m1 =
      if s == lx_b("+") || s == lx_b("-") then
        m0 + 1
      else
        m0
    if lx_digit_us(lx_at(text, m1)) then
      lx_scan_digits(text, m1, n)
    else
      k
  else
    k

defs.name: lx_scan_qual
defs.source:
fn lx_scan_qual(text : String, j : Int, n : Int) : Int =
  var k := j
  while (lx_at(text, k) == lx_b(".") && lx_seg_start(lx_at(text, k + 1))) do
    k := k + 2
    while k < n && lx_word(byte_at(text, k)) do
      k += 1
  k

defs.name: lx_cp_len
defs.source:
fn lx_cp_len(b : Int) : Int =
  if b < 128 then
    1
  elif b >= 240 then
    4
  elif b >= 224 then
    3
  elif b >= 192 then

fn lx_upper(text : String, i : Int, n : Int, kws : List(String)) : LxStep =

  if (lx_at(text, j) == lx_b(".") && lx_seg_start(lx_at(text, j + 1))) then
    LxTok(TQual, lx_scan_qual(text, j, n))
  else
    match lx_find_kw(text, i, j, kws) of
      Some(kw) => LxTok(TFixed(kw), j)

fn lx_char(text : String, i : Int, n : Int) : LxStep =
  let p = i + 1
  let c = lx_at(text, p)
  if c == lx_eof() then
    LxErr(LxInvalid(i))
  else
    let e =
      if c == lx_b("\\") then
        lx_skip_cp(text, p + 1, n)
      else
        lx_skip_cp(text, p, n)
    if lx_at(text, e) == lx_b("'") then
      LxTok(TChar, e + 1)
    else
      LxErr(LxInvalid(i))

defs.name: lx_margin
defs.ty: (String, Int, Int, Option((Int, Int))) -> Option((Int, Int))
defs.source:
fn lx_margin(
  text : String,
  p : Int,
  e : Int,
  m : Option((Int, Int))
) : Option((Int, Int)) =
  let q = lx_line_end(text, p, e)
  let m2 =
    if lx_blank(text, p, q) then
      m
    else
      let ind = lx_skip_h(text, p, q) - p
      match m of
        None => Some((p, ind))
        Some(prev) =>
          let (mo, ml) = prev
          Some((mo, lx_common(text, mo, p, 0, if ml < ind then ml else ind)))
  if q >= e then
    m2
  else
    lx_margin(text, q + 1, e, m2)

fn lx_raw_lines(
  text : String,
  p : Int,
  e : Int,
  ml : Int,
  first : Bool,
  buf : Buf
) : Buf =
  let q = lx_line_end(text, p, e)
  let sep =
    if first then
      buf
    else
      buf_push(buf, 10)
  let out =
    if lx_blank(text, p, q) then
      sep
    else
      lx_push_bytes(text, p + ml, q, sep)
  if q >= e then
    out
  else
    lx_raw_lines(text, q + 1, e, ml, false, out)

defs.name: lx_unterminated
defs.source:
fn lx_unterminated(
  depth : List(Int),
  quotes : List(Int),
  braces : List(Int)
) : LexError =
  if lx_head0(depth) > 0 then
    match braces of
      Cons(bo, _) => LxUntermHole(bo)
      Nil => LxUntermStr(lx_head0(quotes))
  else
    match quotes of
      Cons(qo, _) => LxUntermStr(qo)
      Nil => LxUntermHole(lx_head0(braces))

defs.name: lx_scan_str
defs.ty: (String, Int, Int, List(Int), List(Int), List(Int), Bool) -> Result(Int, Syntax.Lex.LexError)
defs.source:
fn lx_scan_str(
  text : String,
  p : Int,
  n : Int,
  depth : List(Int),
  quotes : List(Int),
  braces : List(Int),
  esc : Bool
) : Result(Int, LexError) =
  if p >= n then
    Err(lx_unterminated(depth, quotes, braces))
  elif esc then
    lx_scan_str(
        text,
        p + lx_cp_len(byte_at(text, p)),
        n,
        depth,
        quotes,
        braces,
        false,
      )
  else
    let b = byte_at(text, p)
    let top = lx_head0(depth)
    if b == lx_b("\\") then
      lx_scan_str(text, p + 1, n, depth, quotes, braces, true)
    elif b == lx_b("\"") && top == 0 then
      let d2 = lx_tail(depth)
      let q2 = lx_tail(quotes)
      match d2 of
        Nil => Ok(p + 1)
        Cons(_, _) => lx_scan_str(text, p + 1, n, d2, q2, braces, false)
    elif b == lx_b("\"") then
      lx_scan_str(
          text,
          p + 1,
          n,
          Cons(0, depth),
          Cons(p, quotes),
          braces,
          false,
        )
    elif b == lx_b("\{") then
      lx_scan_str(
          text,
          p + 1,
          n,
          Cons(top + 1, lx_tail(depth)),
          quotes,
          Cons(p, braces),
          false,
        )
    elif b == lx_b("\}") && top > 0 then
      lx_scan_str(
          text,
          p + 1,
          n,
          Cons(top - 1, lx_tail(depth)),
          quotes,
          lx_tail(braces),
          false,
        )
    else
      lx_scan_str(text, p + lx_cp_len(b), n, depth, quotes, braces, false)

defs.name: lx_hole_go
defs.source:
fn lx_hole_go(
  text : String,
  p : Int,
  n : Int,
  depth : List(Int),
  esc : Bool
) : Option(Int) =
  if p >= n then
    None
  elif esc then
    lx_hole_go(text, p + lx_cp_len(byte_at(text, p)), n, depth, false)
  else
    let b = byte_at(text, p)
    let top = lx_head0(depth)
    if b == lx_b("\\") then
      lx_hole_go(text, p + 1, n, depth, true)
    elif b == lx_b("\"") && top == 0 then
      lx_hole_go(text, p + 1, n, lx_tail(depth), false)
    elif b == lx_b("\"") then
      lx_hole_go(text, p + 1, n, Cons(0, depth), false)
    elif b == lx_b("\{") then
      lx_hole_go(text, p + 1, n, Cons(top + 1, lx_tail(depth)), false)
    elif b == lx_b("\}") && top > 0 then
      let d2 = Cons(top - 1, lx_tail(depth))
      if lx_zero_one(d2) then
        Some(p)
      else
        lx_hole_go(text, p + 1, n, d2, false)
    else
      lx_hole_go(text, p + lx_cp_len(b), n, depth, false)

    if b == lx_b("\\") then
      lx_has_hole(text, lo + 1 + lx_cp_len(lx_at(text, lo + 1)), hi)
    elif b == lx_b("\{") then
      true
    else
      lx_has_hole(text, lo + lx_cp_len(b), hi)

fn lx_cook_go(
  text : String,
  oq : Int,
  p : Int,
  hi : Int,
  buf : Buf
) : Result(String, LexError) =
  if p >= hi then
    Ok(string_of_buf(buf))
  else
    let b = byte_at(text, p)
    if b == lx_b("\\") then
      if p + 1 >= hi then
        Err(LxInvalid(oq))
      else
        match lx_esc_byte(byte_at(text, p + 1)) of
          Some(db) => lx_cook_go(text, oq, p + 2, hi, buf_push(buf, db))
          None => Err(LxInvalid(oq))
    else
      lx_cook_go(text, oq, p + lx_cp_len(b), hi, lx_push_cp(text, p, buf))

defs.name: lx_classify
defs.source:
fn lx_classify(text : String, i : Int, n : Int, tb : LxTabs) : LxStep =
  let c = byte_at(text, i)
  if c == lx_b("-") && lx_at(text, i + 1) == lx_b("-") then
    LxComment(lx_scan_comment(text, i, n))
  elif is_lower(c) || c == lx_b("_") then
    lx_lower(text, i, n, array_get(tb.lower, c))
  elif is_upper(c) then
    lx_upper(text, i, n, array_get(tb.upper, c))
  elif is_digit(c) then
    lx_number(text, i, n)
  elif c == lx_b("'") then
    lx_char(text, i, n)
  else
    lx_op(text, i, array_get(tb.ops, c))

fn lx_has_blank(text : String, lo : Int, hi : Int) : Bool =
  var i := lo
  var seen := 0
  while i < hi && seen < 2 do
    if byte_at(text, i) == 10 then
      seen += 1
    i += 1
  seen >= 2

  if b == lx_b("\\") then
    let e = byte_at(text, p + 1)
    if e == lx_b("'") then
