defs.name: Trivia
defs.source: type Trivia = TComment(Span) | TBlockComment(Span) | TBlank(Span)
defs.doc: One trivia event between semantic tokens: a line comment, a delimited comment, or a blank-line run.

defs.name: trivia_name
defs.source:
fn trivia_name(t : Trivia) : String =
  match t of
    TComment(_) => "comment"
    TBlockComment(_) => "block-comment"
    TBlank(_) => "blank"
defs.doc: The wire name of a trivia event.

defs.name: trivia_span
defs.source:
fn trivia_span(t : Trivia) : Span =
  match t of
    TComment(s) => s
    TBlockComment(s) => s
    TBlank(s) => s
defs.doc: The span a trivia event covers.

defs.name: expr_children
defs.source:
fn expr_children(e : Sp(Expr)) : List(Sp(Expr)) =
  match node_of(e) of
    EInt(_, _) => []
    EFloat(_) => []
    EChar(_) => []
    EBool(_) => []
    EUnit => []
    EStr(_) => []
    EVar(_) => []
    EHole(_) => []
    EBin(_, a, b) => [a, b]
    ENeg(a) => [a]
    EIf(c, t, f) => [c, t, f]
    ELet(_, v, rest) => [v, rest]
    ELam(ps, body) => append(concat_map(param_default, ps), [body])
    ECall(f, args) => Cons(f, args)
    EPipe(a, b) => [a, b]
    EMatch(scrut, arms) => Cons(scrut, concat_map(arm_children, arms))
    EList(xs) => xs
    ETuple(xs) => xs
    EField(r, _) => [r]
    EUnboxedTuple(xs) => xs
    EUnboxedRecord(fs) => map(named_value, fs)
    EUnboxedField(r, _) => [r]
    ERecord(_, fs) => map(named_value, fs)
    ERecordUpdate(r, _, fs) => Cons(r, map(named_value, fs))
    EPathUpdate(r, ups) => Cons(r, concat_map(update_children, ups))
    EHandle(action, arms, _) => Cons(action, map(handler_body, arms))
    EMask(_, a) => [a]
    EInst(a, _) => [a]
    EIndex(r, i) => [r, i]
    EIndexSet(r, i, v) => [r, i, v]
    EAnn(a, _) => [a]
    EMarker(_) => []
    ENamedHandle(_, action, arms) => Cons(action, map(handler_body, arms))
    EVarDecl(_, v, rest) => [v, rest]
    EAssign(_, v) => [v]
    EIndexAssign(r, i, v) => [r, i, v]
    EThrow(_, args) => args
    ETryCatch(body, arms) => Cons(body, map(catch_body, arms))
    EFor(_, src, quals, body) =>
      Cons(src, append(concat_map(qual_children, quals), [body]))
    EWhile(c, body) => [c, body]
    ELoop(body) => [body]
    EBreak => []
    EContinue => []
    EReturn(a) => [a]
    EComp(out, _, src, quals) =>
      Cons(out, Cons(src, concat_map(qual_children, quals)))
    EDefault(a, d) => [a, d]
    ETransact(a, b) => [a, b]
    EProbe(_, a) => [a]
    EReflect(_, _) => []
    EOptChain(r, _) => [r]
    ERange(parts, stop) => append(parts, [stop])
    ECompose(_, a, b) => [a, b]
    EReadPath(r, steps) => Cons(r, concat_map(step_children, steps))
defs.doc: The immediate `Expr` children of one node, in source order. Children held inside carrier records (match arms, handler arms, qualifiers, path steps and updates, parameter defaults, named fields) are included; a leaf yields the empty list.

defs.name: arm_children
defs.source:
fn arm_children(a : Arm) : List(Sp(Expr)) =
  match a.guard of
    Some(g) => [g, a.body]
    None => [a.body]
defs.doc: The `Expr` children carried by one match arm: the guard when present, then the body.

defs.name: named_value
defs.source: fn named_value(f : NamedExpr) : Sp(Expr) = f.value

defs.name: update_value
defs.source:
fn update_value(u : PathUpdate) : Sp(Expr) =
  match u.op of
    POSet(v) => v
    POModify(v) => v

defs.name: step_children
defs.source:
fn step_children(s : PathStep) : List(Sp(Expr)) =
  match s of
    PSField(_) => []
    PSEach => []
    PSCase(_) => []
    PSIndex(i) => [i]
    PSWhere(g) => [g]
defs.doc: The `Expr` children of one optic path step: the index or filter it carries, if any.

defs.name: update_children
defs.source:
fn update_children(u : PathUpdate) : List(Sp(Expr)) =
  append(concat_map(step_children, u.path), [update_value(u)])
defs.doc: The `Expr` children of one path update: the expressions inside the path it walks, then the value written at its end.

defs.name: param_default
defs.source:
fn param_default(p : Param) : List(Sp(Expr)) =
  match p.dflt of
    Some(d) => [d]
    None => []
defs.doc: The default expression of one parameter, if it has one.

defs.name: handler_body
defs.source:
fn handler_body(h : HandlerArm) : Sp(Expr) =
  match h of
    HReturn(_, body) => body
    HOp(_, _, _, body) => body
    HOnce(_, _, body) => body
    HVal(_, body) => body
    HNever(_, _, body) => body

defs.name: catch_body
defs.source: fn catch_body(c : CatchArm) : Sp(Expr) = c.body

defs.name: qual_children
defs.source:
fn qual_children(q : Qual) : List(Sp(Expr)) =
  match q of
    QGuard(g) => [g]
    QBind(_, src) => [src]

defs.name: expr_rebuild
defs.doc:
Put a replacement child list back into one node, in `expr_children` order, keeping the node's span and its synthetic bit.

This is the inverse half of `expr_children`, and the pair is everything a generic strategy needs to descend a tree. It fails closed: a child list that does not match the node's shape (a different length, a carrier arity that does not line up) yields the node unchanged rather than a silently reshaped one, so `expr_rebuild(e, expr_children(e))` is the identity and a garbage child list cannot forge a node.

defs.name: expr_layer
defs.source:
fn expr_layer() : Layer(Sp(Expr)) =
  Layer { kids = expr_children, rebuild = expr_rebuild }
defs.doc: The children-and-rebuild pair for spanned expressions, which is what every strategy in `Control.Rewrite` and every query in `Control.Layer` takes.

defs.name: wk_leaf
defs.source:
fn wk_leaf(e : Expr, cs : List(Sp(Expr))) : Option(Expr) =
  match cs of
    Nil => Some(e)
    _ => None

defs.name: wk_same_len
defs.source:
fn wk_same_len(xs : List(a), cs : List(Sp(Expr))) : Bool =
  length(xs) == length(cs)

defs.name: wk_node
defs.source:
fn wk_node(e : Expr, cs : List(Sp(Expr))) : Option(Expr) =
  match e of
    EInt(_, _) => wk_leaf(e, cs)
    EFloat(_) => wk_leaf(e, cs)
    EChar(_) => wk_leaf(e, cs)
    EBool(_) => wk_leaf(e, cs)
    EUnit => wk_leaf(e, cs)
    EStr(_) => wk_leaf(e, cs)
    EVar(_) => wk_leaf(e, cs)
    EHole(_) => wk_leaf(e, cs)
    EBin(op, _, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(a, Cons(b, Nil)) => Some(EBin(op, a, b))
        _ => None
    ENeg(_) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(a, Nil) => Some(ENeg(a))
        _ => None
    EIf(_, _, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(c, Cons(t, Cons(f, Nil))) => Some(EIf(c, t, f))
        _ => None
    ELet(n, _, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(v, Cons(rest, Nil)) => Some(ELet(n, v, rest))
        _ => None
    ELam(ps, _) =>
      let k = length(concat_map(param_default, ps))
      match wk_params(ps, take(k, cs)) of
        None => None
        Some(ps2) =>
          match drop(k, cs) of
            Cons(body, Nil) => Some(ELam(ps2, body))
            _ => None
    ECall(_, args) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(f, rest) =>
          if wk_same_len(args, rest) then
            Some(ECall(f, rest))
          else
            None
        _ => None
    EPipe(_, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(a, Cons(b, Nil)) => Some(EPipe(a, b))
        _ => None
    EMatch(_, arms) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(scrut, rest) =>
          match wk_arms(arms, rest) of
            None => None
            Some(arms2) => Some(EMatch(scrut, arms2))
        _ => None
    EList(xs) =>
      if wk_same_len(xs, cs) then
        Some(EList(cs))
      else
        None
    ETuple(xs) =>
      if wk_same_len(xs, cs) then
        Some(ETuple(cs))
      else
        None
    EField(_, n) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(r, Nil) => Some(EField(r, n))
        _ => None
    EUnboxedTuple(xs) =>
      if wk_same_len(xs, cs) then
        Some(EUnboxedTuple(cs))
      else
        None
    EUnboxedRecord(fs) =>
      match wk_fields(fs, cs) of
        None => None
        Some(fs2) => Some(EUnboxedRecord(fs2))
    EUnboxedField(_, n) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(r, Nil) => Some(EUnboxedField(r, n))
        _ => None
    ERecord(n, fs) =>
      match wk_fields(fs, cs) of
        None => None
        Some(fs2) => Some(ERecord(n, fs2))
    ERecordUpdate(_, n, fs) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(r, rest) =>
          match wk_fields(fs, rest) of
            None => None
            Some(fs2) => Some(ERecordUpdate(r, n, fs2))
        _ => None
    EPathUpdate(_, ups) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(r, rest) =>
          match wk_updates(ups, rest) of
            None => None
            Some(ups2) => Some(EPathUpdate(r, ups2))
        _ => None
    EHandle(_, arms, m) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(action, rest) =>
          match wk_handlers(arms, rest) of
            None => None
            Some(arms2) => Some(EHandle(action, arms2, m))
        _ => None
    EMask(n, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(a, Nil) => Some(EMask(n, a))
        _ => None
    EInst(_, ts) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(a, Nil) => Some(EInst(a, ts))
        _ => None
    EIndex(_, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(r, Cons(i, Nil)) => Some(EIndex(r, i))
        _ => None
    EIndexSet(_, _, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(r, Cons(i, Cons(v, Nil))) => Some(EIndexSet(r, i, v))
        _ => None
    EAnn(_, t) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(a, Nil) => Some(EAnn(a, t))
        _ => None
    EMarker(_) => wk_leaf(e, cs)
    ENamedHandle(n, _, arms) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(action, rest) =>
          match wk_handlers(arms, rest) of
            None => None
            Some(arms2) => Some(ENamedHandle(n, action, arms2))
        _ => None
    EVarDecl(n, _, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(v, Cons(rest, Nil)) => Some(EVarDecl(n, v, rest))
        _ => None
    EAssign(n, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(v, Nil) => Some(EAssign(n, v))
        _ => None
    EIndexAssign(_, _, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(r, Cons(i, Cons(v, Nil))) => Some(EIndexAssign(r, i, v))
        _ => None
    EThrow(n, args) =>
      if wk_same_len(args, cs) then
        Some(EThrow(n, cs))
      else
        None
    ETryCatch(_, arms) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(body, rest) =>
          match wk_catches(arms, rest) of
            None => None
            Some(arms2) => Some(ETryCatch(body, arms2))
        _ => None
    EFor(n, _, quals, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(src, rest) =>
          match wk_quals(quals, take(length(quals), rest)) of
            None => None
            Some(qs) =>
              match drop(length(quals), rest) of
                Cons(body, Nil) => Some(EFor(n, src, qs, body))
                _ => None
        _ => None
    EWhile(_, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(c, Cons(body, Nil)) => Some(EWhile(c, body))
        _ => None
    ELoop(_) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(body, Nil) => Some(ELoop(body))
        _ => None
    EBreak => wk_leaf(e, cs)
    EContinue => wk_leaf(e, cs)
    EReturn(_) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(a, Nil) => Some(EReturn(a))
        _ => None
    EComp(_, n, _, quals) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(out, Cons(src, rest)) =>
          match wk_quals(quals, rest) of
            None => None
            Some(qs) => Some(EComp(out, n, src, qs))
        _ => None
    EDefault(_, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(a, Cons(d, Nil)) => Some(EDefault(a, d))
        _ => None
    ETransact(_, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(a, Cons(b, Nil)) => Some(ETransact(a, b))
        _ => None
    EProbe(n, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(a, Nil) => Some(EProbe(n, a))
        _ => None
    EReflect(_, _) => wk_leaf(e, cs)
    EOptChain(_, n) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(r, Nil) => Some(EOptChain(r, n))
        _ => None
    ERange(parts, _) =>
      match reverse(cs) of
        Cons(stop, rparts) =>
          if wk_same_len(parts, rparts) then
            Some(ERange(reverse(rparts), stop))
          else
            None
        _ => None
    ECompose(op, _, _) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(a, Cons(b, Nil)) => Some(ECompose(op, a, b))
        _ => None
    EReadPath(_, steps) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(r, rest) =>
          match wk_steps(steps, rest) of
            None => None
            Some(steps2) => Some(EReadPath(r, steps2))
        _ => None

defs.name: wk_arms
defs.source:
fn wk_arms(arms : List(Arm), cs : List(Sp(Expr))) : Option(List(Arm)) =
  match arms of
    Nil => wk_end(cs, Nil)
    Cons(a, more) =>
      match a.guard of
        Some(_) =>
          match cs of
            Cons(g, Cons(b, rest)) =>
              match wk_arms(more, rest) of
                None => None
                Some(tl) =>
                  Some(Cons(Arm { pat = a.pat, guard = Some(g), body = b }, tl))
            _ => None
        None =>
          match cs of
            Cons(b, rest) =>
              match wk_arms(more, rest) of
                None => None
                Some(tl) =>
                  Some(Cons(Arm { pat = a.pat, guard = None, body = b }, tl))
            _ => None

defs.name: wk_fields
defs.source:
fn wk_fields(
  fs : List(NamedExpr),
  cs : List(Sp(Expr))
) : Option(List(NamedExpr)) =
  match fs of
    Nil => wk_end(cs, Nil)
    Cons(f, more) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(v, rest) =>
          match wk_fields(more, rest) of
            None => None
            Some(tl) => Some(Cons(NamedExpr { name = f.name, value = v }, tl))
        _ => None

defs.name: wk_handlers
defs.source:
fn wk_handlers(
  arms : List(HandlerArm),
  cs : List(Sp(Expr))
) : Option(List(HandlerArm)) =
  match arms of
    Nil => wk_end(cs, Nil)
    Cons(h, more) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(b, rest) =>
          match wk_handlers(more, rest) of
            None => None
            Some(tl) => Some(Cons(wk_handler(h, b), tl))
        _ => None

defs.name: wk_handler
defs.source:
fn wk_handler(h : HandlerArm, b : Sp(Expr)) : HandlerArm =
  match h of
    HReturn(n, _) => HReturn(n, b)
    HOp(n, ps, k, _) => HOp(n, ps, k, b)
    HOnce(n, ps, _) => HOnce(n, ps, b)
    HVal(n, _) => HVal(n, b)
    HNever(n, ps, _) => HNever(n, ps, b)

defs.name: wk_catches
defs.source:
fn wk_catches(
  arms : List(CatchArm),
  cs : List(Sp(Expr))
) : Option(List(CatchArm)) =
  match arms of
    Nil => wk_end(cs, Nil)
    Cons(c, more) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(b, rest) =>
          match wk_catches(more, rest) of
            None => None
            Some(tl) =>
              Some(
                  Cons(
                      CatchArm {
                        name = c.name,
                        binders = c.binders,
                        body = b,
                        span = c.span
                      },
                      tl,
                    ),
                )
        _ => None

defs.name: wk_quals
defs.source:
fn wk_quals(quals : List(Qual), cs : List(Sp(Expr))) : Option(List(Qual)) =
  match quals of
    Nil => wk_end(cs, Nil)
    Cons(q, more) =>
      match cs of
        Cons(v, rest) =>
          match wk_quals(more, rest) of
            None => None
            Some(tl) => Some(Cons(wk_qual(q, v), tl))
        _ => None

defs.name: wk_qual
defs.source:
fn wk_qual(q : Qual, v : Sp(Expr)) : Qual =
  match q of
    QGuard(_) => QGuard(v)
    QBind(n, _) => QBind(n, v)

defs.name: wk_steps
defs.source:
fn wk_steps(
  steps : List(PathStep),
  cs : List(Sp(Expr))
) : Option(List(PathStep)) =
  match steps of
    Nil => wk_end(cs, Nil)
    Cons(s, more) =>
      match step_children(s) of
        Nil =>
          match wk_steps(more, cs) of
            None => None
            Some(tl) => Some(Cons(s, tl))
        _ =>
          match cs of
            Cons(v, rest) =>
              match wk_steps(more, rest) of
                None => None
                Some(tl) => Some(Cons(wk_step(s, v), tl))
            _ => None

defs.name: wk_step
defs.source:
fn wk_step(s : PathStep, v : Sp(Expr)) : PathStep =
  match s of
    PSIndex(_) => PSIndex(v)
    PSWhere(_) => PSWhere(v)
    _ => s

defs.name: wk_updates
defs.source:
fn wk_updates(
  ups : List(PathUpdate),
  cs : List(Sp(Expr))
) : Option(List(PathUpdate)) =
  match ups of
    Nil => wk_end(cs, Nil)
    Cons(u, more) =>
      let k = length(concat_map(step_children, u.path))
      match wk_steps(u.path, take(k, cs)) of
        None => None
        Some(path2) =>
          match drop(k, cs) of
            Cons(v, rest) =>
              match wk_updates(more, rest) of
                None => None
                Some(tl) =>
                  Some(
                      Cons(
                          PathUpdate { path = path2, op = wk_op(u.op, v) },
                          tl,
                        ),
                    )
            _ => None

defs.name: wk_op
defs.source:
fn wk_op(o : PathOp, v : Sp(Expr)) : PathOp =
  match o of
    POSet(_) => POSet(v)
    POModify(_) => POModify(v)

defs.name: wk_params
defs.source:
fn wk_params(ps : List(Param), cs : List(Sp(Expr))) : Option(List(Param)) =
  match ps of
    Nil => wk_end(cs, Nil)
    Cons(p, more) =>
      match p.dflt of
        Some(_) =>
          match cs of
            Cons(v, rest) =>
              match wk_params(more, rest) of
                None => None
                Some(tl) => Some(Cons(wk_param(p, v), tl))
            _ => None
        None =>
          match wk_params(more, cs) of
            None => None
            Some(tl) => Some(Cons(p, tl))

defs.name: wk_param
wk_end
defs.source:
fn wk_end(cs : List(Sp(Expr)), done : b) : Option(b) =
  match cs of
    Nil => Some(done)
    _ => None
defs.doc: The base case every carrier rebuild shares: the child list must be spent exactly, so a longer one is a shape mismatch and not a silent truncation.

defs.name: expr_universe
defs.source:
fn expr_universe(e : Sp(Expr)) : List(Sp(Expr)) =
  Cons(e, concat_map(expr_universe, expr_children(e)))
defs.doc:
Every node of the tree, root first, in depth-first source order.

```prism
expr_count(lit_probe(7))
```

```output
1
```

defs.name: lit_probe
defs.doc: A span-zero literal, a convenience for building test trees.

defs.name: expr_count
defs.source: fn expr_count(e : Sp(Expr)) : Int = length(expr_universe(e))
defs.doc: The number of nodes in the tree.

defs.name: expr_any
defs.source:
fn expr_any(p, e) =
  if p(e) then
    true
  else
    any(\(c) -> expr_any(p, c), expr_children(e))
defs.doc: Whether any node satisfies the predicate.

defs.name: expr_fold
defs.ty: forall e0 a. ((a, Syntax.Ast.Sp(Syntax.Ast.Expr)) -> a ! {e0}, a, Syntax.Ast.Sp(Syntax.Ast.Expr)) -> a ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn expr_fold(f, acc, e) =
  foldl(\(a, c) -> expr_fold(f, a, c), f(acc, e), expr_children(e))
defs.doc: Left-fold the accumulator through every node, root first.

defs.name: Alloc
defs.source:
effect Alloc
  once alloc(Int) : Cell
defs.doc: The allocation effect. `alloc(n)` requests a raw `n`-word cell; a handler decides where those words come from. Graded `once`: single-shot resumption only, which is what a scratch region wants.

defs.name: Cell
defs.source: type Cell = Cell(Int)
defs.doc: An opaque handle to a raw cell handed out by an allocator. It carries no observable payload; the arena-lowering pass writes a constructor into it, and user code never inspects it. The vestigial field keeps the type nominal.

defs.name: with_arena
defs.source:
fn with_arena(body : () -> a ! {Alloc}) : a =
  handle body() with
    once alloc(n) => prim_arena_bump(n)
    return r => r
defs.doc:
Run `body`, servicing each eligible allocation out of this activation's region and reclaiming the whole region when the handler returns. Anything the result keeps is promoted to ordinary reference-counted cells at the boundary. A `body` that allocates nothing runs unchanged, and code that never calls `with_arena` allocates exactly as before.

```prism
with_arena(\() -> [1, 2, 3])
```

```output
[1, 2, 3]
```

defs.name: Blit
defs.source:
class Blit(s)
  blit : (s, Int, Int, s, Int) -> s
defs.doc:
Overwrite `dst[dst_off .. dst_off + len)` with `src[src_off .. src_off + len)` and return the updated destination.

```prism
blit("XY", 0, 2, "abcd", 1)
```

```output
aXYd
```

defs.name: blitString
defs.doc: Splice the source range over the destination range with the string slice primitive: the untouched prefix and suffix of `dst` are sliced out and rejoined around the copied middle.

defs.name: blit_string
defs.source:
fn blit_string(
  src : String,
  src_off : Int,
  len : Int,
  dst : String,
  dst_off : Int
) : String =
  concat(
      substring(dst, 0, dst_off),
      concat(
          substring(src, src_off, len),
          substring(dst, dst_off + len, str_len(dst) - (dst_off + len)),
        ),
    )

defs.name: blitArray
defs.doc: Overwrite `dst[dst_off + i]` with `src[src_off + i]` for each `i` in `0 .. len` via `array_set`, which writes in place when `dst` is uniquely owned and copies otherwise, so the observable result never depends on ownership.

defs.name: blit_array_go
defs.ty: forall a. (Array(a), Int, Int, Array(a), Int, Int) -> Array(a)
defs.source:
fn blit_array_go(
  src : Array(a),
  src_off : Int,
  len : Int,
  dst : Array(a),
  dst_off : Int,
  i : Int
) : Array(a) =
  if i >= len then
    dst
  else
    blit_array_go(
        src,
        src_off,
        len,
        array_set(dst, dst_off + i, array_get(src, src_off + i)),
        dst_off,
        i + 1,
      )

defs.name: blitBytes
defs.doc: Overwrite `dst[dst_off + i]` with `src[src_off + i]` for each `i` in `0 .. len` via the buffer's `buf_set`, which writes in place when the destination buffer is uniquely owned and copies otherwise, so the observable result never depends on ownership.

defs.name: blit_bytes_go
defs.ty: (Buf, Wire.Bytes, Int, Int, Int, Int) -> Buf
defs.source:
fn blit_bytes_go(
  dst : Buf,
  src : Bytes,
  src_off : Int,
  len : Int,
  dst_off : Int,
  i : Int
) : Buf =
  if i >= len then
    dst
  else
    blit_bytes_go(
        buf_set(dst, dst_off + i, bytes_at(src, src_off + i)),
        src,
        src_off,
        len,
        dst_off,
        i + 1,
      )

defs.name: dash
defs.source: let dash : Int = 45

defs.name: help_col
defs.source: let help_col : Int = 24

defs.name: CliError
defs.source:
type CliError
  = MissingFlag(String)
  | MissingArg(String)
  | UnexpectedArg(String)
  | NeedsValue(String)
  | BadValue(String, String)
  | UnknownFlag(String)
  | UnknownCommand(String)
defs.doc: A parse failure, carrying enough to name the offending token and the form expected. Rendered to a message by `describe`.

defs.name: OptSpec
defs.source:
type OptSpec = OptSpec {
  long: String,
  short: String,
  meta: String,
  help: String,
  takes_value: Bool
}
defs.doc: The static description of one option, carried by the parser for help and to tell the lexer whether the flag consumes a following value.

defs.name: ArgSpec
defs.source: type ArgSpec = ArgSpec { meta: String, help: String, required: Bool }
defs.doc: The static description of one positional argument.

defs.name: Tokens
defs.source: type Tokens = Tokens { opts: List((String, String)), pos: List(String) }
defs.doc: argv after lexing: options canonicalized to their long name, and the positionals in order. `--help`/`-h` are handled before lexing (`has_help`), so they never appear here.

defs.name: Parser
defs.doc: A parser for a value of type `a`: the option and positional specs it accepts (the description help is rendered from) and a pure reader over lexed tokens threading the positional cursor. Build these with the combinators below, never by hand.

defs.name: SubCmd
defs.source: type SubCmd(a) = SubCmd { key: String, about: String, sub: Parser(a) }
defs.doc: One named subcommand: its key on the command line, a one-line description, and the parser that runs when it is chosen.

defs.name: Body
defs.source: type Body(a) = Plain(Parser(a)) | Group(List(SubCmd(a)))
defs.doc: A top-level command is either a single parser or a group of subcommands, all producing the same result type (so distinct subcommands map to distinct constructors of the user's ADT).

defs.name: Command
defs.source: type Command(a) = Command { name: String, about: String, body: Body(a) }
defs.doc: A complete command: a program name and one-line description for usage, plus its body.

defs.name: Outcome
defs.source: type Outcome(a) = Parsed(a) | ShowHelp(String) | BadUsage(String)
defs.doc: The outcome of parsing argv: a value, a help request (carrying the rendered text), or a usage error (carrying the rendered message).

defs.name: pure_p
defs.source: fn pure_p(x) = Parser { opts = Nil, args = Nil, run = \(_t, i) -> Ok((x, i)) }
defs.doc: A parser that consumes nothing and yields `x`. The applicative unit.

defs.name: map_p
defs.ty: forall a b. ((b) -> a, Cli.Parser(b)) -> Cli.Parser(a)
defs.source:
fn map_p(f, p : Parser(b)) =
  Parser { opts = p.opts, args = p.args, run = \(t, i) -> run_map(f, p, t, i) }
defs.doc: Map `f` over a parser's result, leaving what it consumes unchanged.

defs.name: run_map
defs.ty: forall e0 a b. ((b) -> a ! {e0}, Cli.Parser(b), Cli.Tokens, Int) -> Result((a, Int), Cli.CliError) ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn run_map(f, p : Parser(b), t : Tokens, i : Int) =
  match (p.run)(t, i) of
    Ok((a, j)) => Ok((f(a), j))
    Err(e) => Err(e)

defs.name: ap_p
defs.ty: forall a b. (Cli.Parser((a) -> b), Cli.Parser(a)) -> Cli.Parser(b)
defs.doc: Applicative application: run `pf` then `px`, threading the positional cursor left to right, and apply the function to the argument. This is what lets a curried constructor be filled field by field.

defs.name: run_ap
defs.ty: forall a b. (Cli.Parser((a) -> b), Cli.Parser(a), Cli.Tokens, Int) -> Result((b, Int), Cli.CliError)
defs.source:
fn run_ap(pf : Parser((b) -> c), px : Parser(b), t : Tokens, i : Int) =
  match (pf.run)(t, i) of
    Err(e) => Err(e)
    Ok((g, j)) =>
      match (px.run)(t, j) of
        Err(e) => Err(e)
        Ok((b, k)) => Ok((g(b), k))

defs.name: build2
defs.ty: forall a b c. ((a) -> (c) -> b, Cli.Parser(a), Cli.Parser(c)) -> Cli.Parser(b)
defs.source: fn build2(f, pa, pb) = ap_p(map_p(f, pa), pb)
defs.doc: Apply a two-argument curried constructor to two parsers.

defs.name: build3
defs.ty: forall a b c d. ((a) -> (b) -> (d) -> c, Cli.Parser(a), Cli.Parser(b), Cli.Parser(d)) -> Cli.Parser(c)
defs.source: fn build3(f, pa, pb, pc) = ap_p(build2(f, pa, pb), pc)
defs.doc: Apply a three-argument curried constructor to three parsers.

defs.name: build4
defs.ty: forall a b c d e. ((a) -> (b) -> (c) -> (e) -> d, Cli.Parser(a), Cli.Parser(b), Cli.Parser(c), Cli.Parser(e)) -> Cli.Parser(d)
defs.source: fn build4(f, pa, pb, pc, pd) = ap_p(build3(f, pa, pb, pc), pd)
defs.doc: Apply a four-argument curried constructor to four parsers.

defs.name: lookup_opt
defs.source:
fn lookup_opt(name, opts) =
  match opts of
    Nil => None
    Cons((k, v), rest) =>
      if str_eq(k, name) then
        Some(v)
      else
        lookup_opt(name, rest)

defs.name: read_opt_str
defs.ty: forall a b. (String, String, Cli.Tokens, a) -> Result((String, a), b)
defs.source:
fn read_opt_str(long, default, t : Tokens, i) =
  match lookup_opt(long, t.opts) of
    Some(v) => Ok((v, i))
    None => Ok((default, i))

defs.name: read_req_str
defs.ty: forall a. (String, Cli.Tokens, a) -> Result((String, a), Cli.CliError)
defs.source:
fn read_req_str(long, t : Tokens, i) =
  match lookup_opt(long, t.opts) of
    Some(v) => Ok((v, i))
    None => Err(MissingFlag(long))

defs.name: read_opt_int
defs.ty: forall a. (String, Int, String, Cli.Tokens, a) -> Result((Int, a), Cli.CliError)
defs.source:
fn read_opt_int(long, default, meta, t : Tokens, i) =
  match lookup_opt(long, t.opts) of
    None => Ok((default, i))
    Some(v) =>
      match parse_int(v) of
        Some(n) => Ok((n, i))
        None => Err(BadValue(v, meta))

defs.name: read_switch
defs.ty: forall a b. (String, Cli.Tokens, a) -> Result((Bool, a), b)
defs.source:
fn read_switch(long, t : Tokens, i) =
  match lookup_opt(long, t.opts) of
    Some(_) => Ok((true, i))
    None => Ok((false, i))

defs.name: read_arg_str
defs.source:
fn read_arg_str(meta, t : Tokens, i) =
  match nth(i, t.pos) of
    Some(v) => Ok((v, i + 1))
    None => Err(MissingArg(meta))

defs.name: read_arg_str_default
defs.ty: forall a. (String, Cli.Tokens, Int) -> Result((String, Int), a)
defs.source:
fn read_arg_str_default(default, t : Tokens, i) =
  match nth(i, t.pos) of
    Some(v) => Ok((v, i + 1))
    None => Ok((default, i))

defs.name: read_arg_int
defs.source:
fn read_arg_int(meta, t : Tokens, i) =
  match nth(i, t.pos) of
    None => Err(MissingArg(meta))
    Some(v) =>
      match parse_int(v) of
        Some(n) => Ok((n, i + 1))
        None => Err(BadValue(v, meta))

defs.name: is_help_tok
defs.source: fn is_help_tok(tok) = str_eq(tok, "--help") || str_eq(tok, "-h")

defs.name: is_long_flag
defs.source: fn is_long_flag(tok) = starts_with("--", tok) && str_len(tok) > 2

defs.name: is_short_flag
defs.source:
fn is_short_flag(tok) =
  str_len(tok) >= 2
    && char_at(tok, 0) == dash
    && char_at(tok, 1) /= dash
    && not(is_digit(char_at(tok, 1)))

defs.name: find_long
defs.source:
fn find_long(specs : List(OptSpec), name) =
  match specs of
    Nil => None
    Cons(s, rest) =>
      if str_eq(s.long, name) then
        Some(s)
      else
        find_long(rest, name)

defs.name: find_short
defs.source:
fn find_short(specs : List(OptSpec), name) =
  match specs of
    Nil => None
    Cons(s, rest) =>
      if str_eq(s.short, name) then
        Some(s)
      else
        find_short(rest, name)

defs.name: lex
defs.source: fn lex(specs, argv) = lex_go(specs, argv, Nil, Nil)
defs.doc: Lex argv against the option specs (which say whether each flag takes a value). Options are canonicalized to their long name; anything not a flag is a positional. `--help`/`-h` are skipped here (detected earlier by `has_help`).

defs.name: lex_go
defs.ty: (List(Cli.OptSpec), List(String), List((String, String)), List(String)) -> Result(Cli.Tokens, Cli.CliError)
defs.source:
fn lex_go(specs, argv, opts_acc, pos_acc) =
  match argv of
    Nil => Ok(Tokens { opts = reverse(opts_acc), pos = reverse(pos_acc) })
    Cons(tok, rest) =>
      if is_help_tok(tok) then
        lex_go(specs, rest, opts_acc, pos_acc)
      elif is_long_flag(tok) then
        lex_long(specs, tok, rest, opts_acc, pos_acc)
      elif is_short_flag(tok) then
        lex_short(specs, tok, rest, opts_acc, pos_acc)
      else
        lex_go(specs, rest, opts_acc, Cons(tok, pos_acc))

defs.name: lex_long
defs.ty: (List(Cli.OptSpec), String, List(String), List((String, String)), List(String)) -> Result(Cli.Tokens, Cli.CliError)
defs.source:
fn lex_long(specs, tok, rest, opts_acc, pos_acc) =
  let name = substring(tok, 2, str_len(tok) - 2)
  if contains("=", name) then
    lex_eq(specs, name, rest, opts_acc, pos_acc)
  else
    match find_long(specs, name) of
      None => Err(UnknownFlag(tok))
      Some(spec) =>
        if spec.takes_value then
          lex_valued(specs, name, rest, opts_acc, pos_acc, tok)
        else
          lex_go(specs, rest, Cons((name, "true"), opts_acc), pos_acc)

defs.name: lex_eq
defs.ty: (List(Cli.OptSpec), String, List(String), List((String, String)), List(String)) -> Result(Cli.Tokens, Cli.CliError)

defs.name: lex_valued
defs.ty: (List(Cli.OptSpec), String, List(String), List((String, String)), List(String), String) -> Result(Cli.Tokens, Cli.CliError)
defs.source:
fn lex_valued(specs, name, rest, opts_acc, pos_acc, tok) =
  match rest of
    Nil => Err(NeedsValue(tok))
    Cons(v, rest2) => lex_go(specs, rest2, Cons((name, v), opts_acc), pos_acc)

defs.name: lex_short
defs.ty: (List(Cli.OptSpec), String, List(String), List((String, String)), List(String)) -> Result(Cli.Tokens, Cli.CliError)
defs.source:
fn lex_short(specs, tok, rest, opts_acc, pos_acc) =
  let name = substring(tok, 1, str_len(tok) - 1)
  match find_short(specs, name) of
    None => Err(UnknownFlag(tok))
    Some(spec) =>
      if spec.takes_value then
        lex_valued(specs, spec.long, rest, opts_acc, pos_acc, tok)
      else
        lex_go(specs, rest, Cons((spec.long, "true"), opts_acc), pos_acc)

defs.name: run_leaf
defs.source:
fn run_leaf(p : Parser(a), argv) =
  match lex(p.opts, argv) of
    Err(e) => Err(e)
    Ok(toks) => finish_leaf(p, toks)

defs.name: finish_leaf
defs.source:
fn finish_leaf(p : Parser(a), toks) =
  match (p.run)(toks, 0) of
    Ok((a, i)) =>
      match nth(i, toks.pos) of
        None => Ok(a)
        Some(value) => Err(UnexpectedArg(value))
    Err(e) => Err(e)

defs.name: find_sub
defs.source:
fn find_sub(subs : List(SubCmd(a)), key) =
  match subs of
    Nil => None
    Cons(sc, rest) =>
      if str_eq(sc.key, key) then
        Some(sc)
      else
        find_sub(rest, key)

defs.name: run_argv
defs.source:
fn run_argv(cmd : Command(a), argv) =
  match cmd.body of
    Plain(p) => run_plain(cmd, p, argv)
    Group(subs) => run_group(cmd, subs, argv)
defs.doc:
Parse argv against a command, yielding a value, a help request, or a usage error. argv is the argument list only (no program name); `cmd.name` supplies the name for usage text.

```prism
# let p = build2(\(host) -> \(port) -> (host, port), req_str("host", "H", "HOST", "server host"), opt_int("port", "p", "N", "listen port", 8080))
# let cmd = Command { name = "serve", about = "run the server", body = Plain(p) }
run_argv(cmd, ["--host", "example.com"])
```

```output
Cli.Parsed((example.com, 8080))
```

defs.name: run_plain
defs.source:
fn run_plain(cmd : Command(a), p : Parser(a), argv) =
  if has_help(argv) then
    ShowHelp(plain_help(cmd, p))
  else
    match run_leaf(p, argv) of
      Ok(a) => Parsed(a)
      Err(e) => BadUsage(err_with_usage(synopsis(cmd, p), e))

defs.name: run_group
defs.source:
fn run_group(cmd : Command(a), subs : List(SubCmd(a)), argv) =
  match argv of
    Nil => ShowHelp(group_help(cmd, subs))
    Cons(key, rest) =>
      if is_help_tok(key) then
        ShowHelp(group_help(cmd, subs))
      else
        dispatch(cmd, subs, key, rest)

defs.name: dispatch
defs.ty: forall a. (Cli.Command(a), List(Cli.SubCmd(a)), String, List(String)) -> Cli.Outcome(a)
defs.source:
fn dispatch(cmd : Command(a), subs : List(SubCmd(a)), key, rest) =
  match find_sub(subs, key) of
    None => BadUsage(err_with_usage(group_usage(cmd), UnknownCommand(key)))
    Some(sc) => run_sub(cmd, sc, rest)

defs.name: run_sub
defs.source:
fn run_sub(cmd : Command(a), sc : SubCmd(a), rest) =
  if has_help(rest) then
    ShowHelp(sub_help(cmd, sc))
  else
    match run_leaf(sc.sub, rest) of
      Ok(a) => Parsed(a)
      Err(e) => BadUsage(err_with_usage(sub_usage(cmd, sc), e))

defs.name: has_help
defs.source:
fn has_help(argv) =
  match argv of
    Nil => false
    Cons(t, rest) =>
      if is_help_tok(t) then
        true
      else
        has_help(rest)

defs.name: help_text
defs.source:
fn help_text(cmd : Command(a)) =
  match cmd.body of
    Plain(p) => plain_help(cmd, p)
    Group(subs) => group_help(cmd, subs)
defs.doc:
The rendered help for a command: dispatches to the plain or group form.

```prism
# let p = build2(\(host) -> \(port) -> (host, port), req_str("host", "H", "HOST", "server host"), opt_int("port", "p", "N", "listen port", 8080))
# let cmd = Command { name = "serve", about = "run the server", body = Plain(p) }
print(help_text(cmd))
```

```output
Usage: serve [--host HOST] [--port N] [--help]

run the server

Options:
  -H, --host HOST       server host
  -p, --port N          listen port
  -h, --help            show this help and exit
```

defs.name: opt_synopsis
defs.source:
fn opt_synopsis(s : OptSpec) =
  if s.takes_value then
    concat_all(["[--", s.long, " ", s.meta, "]"])
  else
    concat_all(["[--", s.long, "]"])

defs.name: arg_synopsis
synopsis
group_usage
defs.source:
fn group_usage(cmd : Command(a)) =
  concat_all(["Usage: ", cmd.name, " <command> [args]"])

defs.name: sub_usage
opt_flags
defs.source:
fn opt_flags(s : OptSpec) =
  if str_eq(s.short, "") then
    concat_all(["      --", s.long])
  else
    concat_all(["  -", s.short, ", --", s.long])

defs.name: opt_line
defs.source:
fn opt_line(s : OptSpec) =
  let lhs =
    if s.takes_value then
      concat_all([opt_flags(s), " ", s.meta])
    else
      opt_flags(s)
  concat_all([pad_right(lhs, help_col), s.help])

defs.name: arg_line
defs.source:
fn arg_line(ar : ArgSpec) =
  concat_all(["  ", pad_right(ar.meta, help_col - 2), ar.help])

defs.name: cmd_line
defs.source:
fn cmd_line(sc : SubCmd(a)) =
  concat_all(["  ", pad_right(sc.key, help_col - 2), sc.about])

defs.name: help_spec
arg_section
defs.source:
fn arg_section(specs : List(ArgSpec)) : List(String) =
  match specs of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(_, _) => Cons("", Cons("Arguments:", map(arg_line, specs)))

defs.name: plain_help
group_help
sub_help
describe
defs.source:
fn describe(err) =
  match err of
    MissingFlag(f) =>
      concat_all(["error: required flag '--", f, "' was not provided"])
    MissingArg(m) => concat_all(["error: missing argument <", m, ">"])
    UnexpectedArg(value) =>
      concat_all(["error: unexpected argument '", value, "'"])
    NeedsValue(f) => concat_all(["error: flag '", f, "' expects a value"])
    BadValue(tok, exp) =>
      concat_all(["error: '", tok, "' is not a valid <", exp, ">"])
    UnknownFlag(f) => concat_all(["error: unknown flag '", f, "'"])
    UnknownCommand(c) => concat_all(["error: unknown command '", c, "'"])
defs.doc:
A one-line description of a parse error, naming the offending token and the form expected.

```prism
describe(MissingFlag("host"))
```

```output
error: required flag '--host' was not provided
```

defs.name: err_with_usage
defs.source: fn err_with_usage(usage, err) = str_join("\n", [describe(err), "", usage])

defs.name: run_args
defs.source: fn run_args(cmd) = run_argv(cmd, args())
defs.doc: Parse the process arguments against `cmd`. argv arrives through the `Env` capability (`args`), so a recorded run replays its arguments from the trace: CLI parsing is inside the determinism contract.

defs.name: Async
defs.source:
effect Async(a)
  fork(() -> a ! {Async(a) | e}) : Fiber
  poll_yield() : Signal
  poll_await(Fiber) : Wake(a)
  cancel(Fiber) : Unit
  channel() : Chan
  bounded(Int) : Chan
  poll_send(Chan, a) : Signal
  poll_recv(Chan) : Wake(a)
  never kill() : b
  never vanished() : b
defs.doc:
The async/await effect. `fork` spawns a fiber and returns its handle, `yield` reschedules, `await` blocks on a fiber's result, and `cancel` requests a cooperative cancellation; `channel`/`send`/`recv` are a buffered FIFO channel for fiber-to-fiber messages. Discharge it with `run_async`.

The public `yield`/`await`/`send`/`recv` are thin wrappers (below) over the raw `poll_*` operations, which return a cancellation `Signal`/`Wake` the wrapper turns into a cooperative `kill`. `kill` and `vanished` never resume (per-site bottom return `b`); `run_async` absorbs the whole effect, so none of the cancel machinery surfaces in a fiber's row.

defs.name: Fiber
defs.source: type Fiber = Fiber(Int)
defs.doc: A handle to a spawned fiber, returned by `fork` and passed to `await`/`cancel`.

defs.name: Chan
defs.source: type Chan = Chan(Int)
defs.doc: A handle to a buffered FIFO channel, opened with `channel`.

defs.name: Signal
defs.source: type Signal = Go | Stop

defs.name: Wake
defs.source: type Wake(a) = Arrived(a) | Gone | Halt

defs.name: Outcome
defs.source: type Outcome(a) = Completed(a) | Was_Cancelled
defs.doc: The outcome of `try_await`: a fiber that completed with a value, or one that was cancelled before it could.

defs.name: yield
defs.source:
fn yield() : Unit ! {Async(a)} =
  match poll_yield() of
    Go => ()
    Stop => kill()
defs.doc: Reschedule the current fiber. A cooperative yield point; also a cancellation point (a cancelled fiber unwinds here instead of resuming).

defs.name: await
defs.source:
fn await(f : Fiber) : a ! {Async(a)} =
  match poll_await(f) of
    Arrived(v) => v
    Gone => vanished()
    Halt => kill()
defs.doc: Block until fiber `f` finishes, returning its result. If `f` was cancelled, this raises the in-scheduler `vanished` signal (observe it with `try_await`); if the waiting fiber is itself cancelled, it unwinds here.

defs.name: send
defs.source:
fn send(c : Chan, v : a) : Unit ! {Async(a)} =
  match poll_send(c, v) of
    Go => ()
    Stop => kill()
defs.doc: Send `v` on channel `c`. On a bounded channel a full buffer parks the sender until a receiver drains it; a cancellation delivered while parked unwinds here.

defs.name: recv
defs.source:
fn recv(c : Chan) : a ! {Async(a)} =
  match poll_recv(c) of
    Arrived(v) => v
    Gone => kill()
    Halt => kill()

defs.name: on_cancel
defs.ty: forall e0 a b. (() -> Unit ! {Concurrent.Async(a), e0}, () -> b ! {Concurrent.Async(a), Concurrent.Async(a), e0}) -> b ! {Concurrent.Async(a), e0}
defs.source:
fn on_cancel(
  cleanup : () -> Unit ! {| e},
  body : () -> r ! {Async(a) | e}
) : r =
  handle body() with
    fork(child) resume k => k(fork(child))
    poll_yield() resume k => k(poll_yield())
    poll_await(f) resume k => k(poll_await(f))
    cancel(f) resume k => k(cancel(f))
    channel() resume k => k(channel())
    bounded(n) resume k => k(bounded(n))
    poll_send(c, v) resume k => k(poll_send(c, v))
    poll_recv(c) resume k => k(poll_recv(c))
    never vanished() => vanished()
    never kill() =>
      cleanup()
      kill()
    return r => r
defs.doc: Run `body`, and if it is cancelled (unwinds through `kill`), run `cleanup` once before the cancellation propagates outward. This is a forwarding handler: every `Async` operation `body` performs is relayed unchanged to the enclosing `run_async`, so the finalizer is transparent except on the cancel path. A normally returning body does not run `cleanup`. Nest these for stacked resources; cancellation runs each installed cleanup exactly once, innermost first. Once an unwind starts, repeated cancellation is masked for that fiber, so a cleanup may suspend and resume normally. A child forked by a cleanup is born cancelled and cannot escape the unwind. If a cleanup itself fails, `try_await` does not manufacture `Was_Cancelled`: the whole scheduler run fails. A cleanup parked with no runnable producer likewise ends in the scheduler's deterministic no-progress failure; a cleanup that keeps producing work may diverge like any other computation.

defs.name: try_await
defs.source:
fn try_await(f : Fiber) : Outcome(a) =
  handle Completed(await(f)) with
    fork(child) resume k => k(fork(child))
    poll_yield() resume k => k(poll_yield())
    poll_await(g) resume k => k(poll_await(g))
    cancel(g) resume k => k(cancel(g))
    channel() resume k => k(channel())
    bounded(n) resume k => k(bounded(n))
    poll_send(c, v) resume k => k(poll_send(c, v))
    poll_recv(c) resume k => k(poll_recv(c))
    never kill() => kill()
    never vanished() => Was_Cancelled
    return r => r
defs.doc: Await fiber `f`, observing cancellation as a value instead of a signal: `Completed(v)` if `f` finished, `Was_Cancelled` if it was cancelled. Never hangs on a cancelled fiber, and does not report `Was_Cancelled` until the target's cancellation unwind (including its `on_cancel` cleanups) has reached the scheduler. A forwarding handler that catches only the `vanished` signal `await` raises for a cancelled target. If that unwind fails or never completes, `try_await` produces no outcome; the enclosing run fails or diverges instead.

defs.name: Cmd
defs.source:
type Cmd(a, e : Row)
  = Forked((Fiber) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {e}, () -> a ! {Async(a) | e})
  | Yielded((Signal) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {e})
  | Awaited(Int, (Wake(a)) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {e})
  | Cancelling(Int, (Unit) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {e})
  | Opened((Chan) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {e})
  | OpenedCap(Int, (Chan) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {e})
  | Sent(Int, a, (Signal) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {e})
  | Recving(Int, (Wake(a)) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {e})
  | Died
  | Failed
  | Finished(a)

defs.name: step
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (() -> a ! {Concurrent.Async(a), e0}) -> Concurrent@Cmd(a, {e0}) ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn step(body : () -> a ! {Async(a) | e}) : Cmd(a, e) =
  handle body() with
    fork(child) resume k => Forked(k, child)
    poll_yield() resume k => Yielded(k)
    poll_await(f) resume k =>
      match f of
        Fiber(fid) => Awaited(fid, k)
    cancel(f) resume k =>
      match f of
        Fiber(fid) => Cancelling(fid, k)
    channel() resume k => Opened(k)
    bounded(cap) resume k => OpenedCap(cap, k)
    poll_send(c, v) resume k =>
      match c of
        Chan(cid) => Sent(cid, v, k)
    poll_recv(c) resume k =>
      match c of
        Chan(cid) => Recving(cid, k)
    never kill() => Died
    never vanished() => Died
    never fail() => Failed
    return r => Finished(r)

defs.name: Ready
Sched
defs.source:
type Sched(a, e : Row) = Sched {
  queue: List(Ready(a, e)),
  results: List((Int, a)),
  waiters: List((Int, Int, (Wake(a)) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {e})),
  cancelled: List(Int),
  finalizing: List(Int),
  died: List(Int),
  failed: Bool,
  kids: List((Int, Int)),
  chans: List((Int, List(a))),
  caps: List((Int, Int)),
  recv_waiters: List((Int, Int, (Wake(a)) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {e})),
  senders: List((Int, Int, a, (Signal) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {e})),
  next: Int,
  enq: (List(Ready(a, e)), Ready(a, e)) -> List(Ready(a, e))
}

defs.name: lookup_result
defs.source:
fn lookup_result(fid : Int, rs : List((Int, a))) : Option(a) =
  match rs of
    Nil => None
    Cons((i, v), r) =>
      if i == fid then
        Some(v)
      else
        lookup_result(fid, r)

defs.name: is_member
defs.source:
fn is_member(fid : Int, xs : List(Int)) : Bool =
  match xs of
    Nil => false
    Cons(x, r) =>
      if x == fid then
        true
      else
        is_member(fid, r)

defs.name: children_of
defs.source:
fn children_of(p : Int, kids : List((Int, Int))) : List(Int) =
  match kids of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons((par, ch), rest) =>
      if par == p then
        Cons(ch, children_of(p, rest))
      else
        children_of(p, rest)

defs.name: descendants
defs.source:
fn descendants(
  roots : List(Int),
  kids : List((Int, Int)),
  acc : List(Int)
) : List(Int) =
  match roots of
    Nil => acc
    Cons(r, rest) =>
      if is_member(r, acc) then
        descendants(rest, kids, acc)
      else
        descendants(append(children_of(r, kids), rest), kids, Cons(r, acc))

defs.name: fold_add
defs.source:
fn fold_add(xs : List(Int), acc : List(Int)) : List(Int) =
  match xs of
    Nil => acc
    Cons(x, rest) =>
      if is_member(x, acc) then
        fold_add(rest, acc)
      else
        fold_add(rest, Cons(x, acc))

defs.name: without
defs.source:
fn without(xs : List(Int), excluded : List(Int)) : List(Int) =
  match xs of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(x, rest) =>
      if is_member(x, excluded) then
        without(rest, excluded)
      else
        Cons(x, without(rest, excluded))

defs.name: wake
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (Int, Concurrent@Wake(a), List((Int, Int, (Concurrent@Wake(a)) -> Concurrent@Cmd(a, {e0}) ! {e0})), List(Concurrent@Ready(a, {e0})), (List(Concurrent@Ready(a, {e0})), Concurrent@Ready(a, {e0})) -> List(Concurrent@Ready(a, {e0}))) -> (List((Int, Int, (Concurrent@Wake(a)) -> Concurrent@Cmd(a, {e0}) ! {e0})), List(Concurrent@Ready(a, {e0})))
defs.source:
fn wake(
  fid : Int,
  w : Wake(a),
  ws : List((Int, Int, (Wake(a)) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e})),
  acc : List(Ready(a, e)),
  enq : (List(Ready(a, e)), Ready(a, e)) -> List(Ready(a, e))
) : (List((Int, Int, (Wake(a)) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e})), List(Ready(a, e))) =
  match ws of
    Nil => (Nil, acc)
    Cons((f, who, k), rest) =>
      if f == fid then
        wake(
            fid,
            w,
            rest,
            enq(acc, Ready(who, \() -> k(w), \() -> k(Halt))),
            enq,
          )
      else
        match wake(fid, w, rest, acc, enq) of
          (kept, out) => (Cons((f, who, k), kept), out)

defs.name: chan_take
defs.ty: forall a. (Int, List((Int, List(a)))) -> Option((a, List((Int, List(a)))))
defs.source:
fn chan_take(
  cid : Int,
  chans : List((Int, List(a)))
) : Option((a, List((Int, List(a))))) =
  match chans of
    Nil => None
    Cons((c, buf), rest) =>
      if c == cid then
        match buf of
          Nil => None
          Cons(h, t) => Some((h, Cons((c, t), rest)))
      else
        match chan_take(cid, rest) of
          None => None
          Some((v, kept)) => Some((v, Cons((c, buf), kept)))

defs.name: chan_put
defs.ty: forall a. (Int, a, List((Int, List(a)))) -> List((Int, List(a)))
defs.source:
fn chan_put(
  cid : Int,
  v : a,
  chans : List((Int, List(a)))
) : List((Int, List(a))) =
  match chans of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons((c, buf), rest) =>
      if c == cid then
        Cons((c, append(buf, [v])), rest)
      else
        Cons((c, buf), chan_put(cid, v, rest))

defs.name: take_recv
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (Int, List((Int, Int, (Concurrent@Wake(a)) -> Concurrent@Cmd(a, {e0}) ! {e0}))) -> Option((Int, (Concurrent@Wake(a)) -> Concurrent@Cmd(a, {e0}) ! {e0}, List((Int, Int, (Concurrent@Wake(a)) -> Concurrent@Cmd(a, {e0}) ! {e0}))))
defs.source:
fn take_recv(
  cid : Int,
  rws : List((Int, Int, (Wake(a)) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e}))
) : Option((Int, (Wake(a)) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e}, List((Int, Int, (Wake(a)) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e})))) =
  match rws of
    Nil => None
    Cons((c, who, k), rest) =>
      if c == cid then
        Some((who, k, rest))
      else
        match take_recv(cid, rest) of
          None => None
          Some((who2, k2, kept)) => Some((who2, k2, Cons((c, who, k), kept)))

defs.name: list_len
defs.source:
fn list_len(xs : List(a)) : Int =
  match xs of
    Nil => 0
    Cons(_, r) => 1 + list_len(r)

defs.name: cap_of
defs.source:
fn cap_of(cid : Int, caps : List((Int, Int))) : Option(Int) =
  match caps of
    Nil => None
    Cons((c, n), rest) =>
      if c == cid then
        Some(n)
      else
        cap_of(cid, rest)

defs.name: chan_len
defs.source:
fn chan_len(cid : Int, chans : List((Int, List(a)))) : Int =
  match chans of
    Nil => 0
    Cons((c, buf), rest) =>
      if c == cid then
        list_len(buf)
      else
        chan_len(cid, rest)

defs.name: take_sender
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (Int, List((Int, Int, a, (Concurrent@Signal) -> Concurrent@Cmd(a, {e0}) ! {e0}))) -> Option((Int, a, (Concurrent@Signal) -> Concurrent@Cmd(a, {e0}) ! {e0}, List((Int, Int, a, (Concurrent@Signal) -> Concurrent@Cmd(a, {e0}) ! {e0}))))
defs.source:
fn take_sender(
  cid : Int,
  ss : List((Int, Int, a, (Signal) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e}))
) : Option((Int, a, (Signal) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e}, List((Int, Int, a, (Signal) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e})))) =
  match ss of
    Nil => None
    Cons((c, who, v, k), rest) =>
      if c == cid then
        Some((who, v, k, rest))
      else
        match take_sender(cid, rest) of
          None => None
          Some((w2, v2, k2, kept)) =>
            Some((w2, v2, k2, Cons((c, who, v, k), kept)))

defs.name: evict_waiters
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (List(Int), List((Int, Int, (Concurrent@Wake(a)) -> Concurrent@Cmd(a, {e0}) ! {e0})), List(Concurrent@Ready(a, {e0})), (List(Concurrent@Ready(a, {e0})), Concurrent@Ready(a, {e0})) -> List(Concurrent@Ready(a, {e0}))) -> (List((Int, Int, (Concurrent@Wake(a)) -> Concurrent@Cmd(a, {e0}) ! {e0})), List(Concurrent@Ready(a, {e0})))
defs.source:
fn evict_waiters(
  victims : List(Int),
  ws : List((Int, Int, (Wake(a)) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e})),
  q : List(Ready(a, e)),
  enq : (List(Ready(a, e)), Ready(a, e)) -> List(Ready(a, e))
) : (List((Int, Int, (Wake(a)) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e})), List(Ready(a, e))) =
  match ws of
    Nil => (Nil, q)
    Cons((f, who, k), rest) =>
      if is_member(who, victims) then
        evict_waiters(
            victims,
            rest,
            enq(q, Ready(who, \() -> k(Halt), \() -> k(Halt))),
            enq,
          )
      else
        match evict_waiters(victims, rest, q, enq) of
          (kept, out) => (Cons((f, who, k), kept), out)

defs.name: evict_senders
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (List(Int), List((Int, Int, a, (Concurrent@Signal) -> Concurrent@Cmd(a, {e0}) ! {e0})), List(Concurrent@Ready(a, {e0})), (List(Concurrent@Ready(a, {e0})), Concurrent@Ready(a, {e0})) -> List(Concurrent@Ready(a, {e0}))) -> (List((Int, Int, a, (Concurrent@Signal) -> Concurrent@Cmd(a, {e0}) ! {e0})), List(Concurrent@Ready(a, {e0})))
defs.source:
fn evict_senders(
  victims : List(Int),
  ss : List((Int, Int, a, (Signal) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e})),
  q : List(Ready(a, e)),
  enq : (List(Ready(a, e)), Ready(a, e)) -> List(Ready(a, e))
) : (List((Int, Int, a, (Signal) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e})), List(Ready(a, e))) =
  match ss of
    Nil => (Nil, q)
    Cons((c, who, v, k), rest) =>
      if is_member(who, victims) then
        evict_senders(
            victims,
            rest,
            enq(q, Ready(who, \() -> k(Stop), \() -> k(Stop))),
            enq,
          )
      else
        match evict_senders(victims, rest, q, enq) of
          (kept, out) => (Cons((c, who, v, k), kept), out)

defs.name: cancel_tree
defs.source:
fn cancel_tree(roots : List(Int), s : Sched(a, e)) : Sched(a, e) =
  let victims = without(descendants(roots, s.kids, Nil), s.finalizing)
  let cancelled2 = fold_add(victims, s.cancelled)
  match evict_waiters(victims, s.waiters, s.queue, s.enq) of
    (waiters2, q1) =>
      match evict_waiters(victims, s.recv_waiters, q1, s.enq) of
        (recv2, q2) =>
          match evict_senders(victims, s.senders, q2, s.enq) of
            (senders2, q3) =>
              Sched {
                ..s,
                cancelled = cancelled2,
                waiters = waiters2,
                recv_waiters = recv2,
                senders = senders2,
                queue = q3
              }

defs.name: others
queue_ids
defs.source:
fn queue_ids(q : List(Ready(a, e)), acc : List(Int)) : List(Int) =
  match q of
    Nil => acc
    Cons(Ready(id, _, _), rest) => queue_ids(rest, Cons(id, acc))

defs.name: waiter_ids
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (List((Int, Int, (Concurrent@Wake(a)) -> Concurrent@Cmd(a, {e0}) ! {e0})), List(Int)) -> List(Int)
defs.source:
fn waiter_ids(
  ws : List((Int, Int, (Wake(a)) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e})),
  acc : List(Int)
) : List(Int) =
  match ws of
    Nil => acc
    Cons((_, who, _), rest) => waiter_ids(rest, Cons(who, acc))

defs.name: sender_ids
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (List((Int, Int, a, (Concurrent@Signal) -> Concurrent@Cmd(a, {e0}) ! {e0})), List(Int)) -> List(Int)
defs.source:
fn sender_ids(
  ss : List((Int, Int, a, (Signal) -> Cmd(a, e) ! {| e})),
  acc : List(Int)
) : List(Int) =
  match ss of
    Nil => acc
    Cons((_, who, _, _), rest) => sender_ids(rest, Cons(who, acc))

defs.name: remove
defs.source:
fn remove(x : Int, xs : List(Int)) : List(Int) =
  match xs of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(y, rest) =>
      if x == y then
        remove(x, rest)
      else
        Cons(y, remove(x, rest))

defs.name: drive
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (Int, Concurrent@Cmd(a, {Fail, e0}), Concurrent@Sched(a, {Fail, e0})) -> a ! {Fail, e0}
defs.source:
fn drive(me : Int, cmd : Cmd(a, e), s : Sched(a, e)) : a =
  match cmd of
    Forked(parent, child) =>
      let cid = s.next
      let q = (s.enq)(
          s.queue,
          Ready(cid, \() -> step(child), \() -> step(\() -> kill())),
        )
      let s2 =
        Sched { ..s, next = cid + 1, queue = q, kids = Cons((me, cid), s.kids) }
      let s3 =
        if is_member(me, s.finalizing) then
          cancel_tree([cid], s2)
        else
          s2
      if me == 0 && s3.failed then
        let q2 = (s3.enq)(
            s3.queue,
            Ready(me, \() -> parent(Fiber(cid)), \() -> step(\() -> kill())),
          )
        run_next(Sched { ..s3, queue = q2 })
      else
        drive(me, parent(Fiber(cid)), s3)
    Yielded(k) =>
      run_next(
          Sched {
            ..s,
            queue = (s.enq)(s.queue, Ready(me, \() -> k(Go), \() -> k(Stop)))
          },
        )
    Awaited(fid, k) =>
      match lookup_result(fid, s.results) of
        Some(v) => drive(me, k(Arrived(v)), s)
        None =>
          if is_member(fid, s.died) then
            drive(me, k(Gone), s)
          else
            run_next(Sched { ..s, waiters = append(s.waiters, [(fid, me, k)]) })
    Cancelling(fid, k) =>
      let s2 = cancel_tree([fid], s)
      let s3 =
        if fid == 0 then
          Sched { ..s2, failed = true }
        else
          s2
      if me == 0 && s3.failed then
        let q = (s3.enq)(
            s3.queue,
            Ready(me, \() -> k(()), \() -> step(\() -> kill())),
          )
        run_next(Sched { ..s3, queue = q })
      else
        drive(me, k(()), s3)
    Opened(k) =>
      let cid = s.next
      drive(
          me,
          k(Chan(cid)),
          Sched { ..s, next = cid + 1, chans = Cons((cid, Nil), s.chans) },
        )
    OpenedCap(cap, k) =>
      let cid = s.next
      drive(
          me,
          k(Chan(cid)),
          Sched {
            ..s,
            next = cid + 1,
            chans = Cons((cid, Nil), s.chans),
            caps = Cons((cid, cap), s.caps)
          },
        )
    Sent(cid, v, k) =>
      match take_recv(cid, s.recv_waiters) of
        Some((who, kr, rest)) =>
          let q =
            (s.enq)(s.queue, Ready(who, \() -> kr(Arrived(v)), \() -> kr(Halt)))
          let s2 = Sched { ..s, recv_waiters = rest, queue = q }
          if me == 0 && s2.failed then
            let q2 = (s2.enq)(s2.queue, Ready(me, \() -> k(Go), \() -> k(Stop)))
            run_next(Sched { ..s2, queue = q2 })
          else
            drive(me, k(Go), s2)
        None =>
          match cap_of(cid, s.caps) of
            Some(cap) =>
              if chan_len(cid, s.chans) >= cap then
                run_next(
                    Sched {
                      ..s,
                      senders = append(s.senders, [(cid, me, v, k)])
                    },
                  )
              else
                drive(
                    me,
                    k(Go),
                    Sched { ..s, chans = chan_put(cid, v, s.chans) },
                  )
            None =>
              drive(me, k(Go), Sched { ..s, chans = chan_put(cid, v, s.chans) })
    Recving(cid, k) =>
      match chan_take(cid, s.chans) of
        Some((v, chans2)) =>
          match take_sender(cid, s.senders) of
            Some((who, sv, sk, srest)) =>
              let q =
                (s.enq)(s.queue, Ready(who, \() -> sk(Go), \() -> sk(Stop)))
              let s2 = Sched {
                ..s,
                chans = chan_put(cid, sv, chans2),
                senders = srest,
                queue = q
              }
              if me == 0 && s2.failed then
                let q2 = (s2.enq)(
                    s2.queue,
                    Ready(me, \() -> k(Arrived(v)), \() -> k(Halt)),
                  )
                run_next(Sched { ..s2, queue = q2 })
              else
                drive(me, k(Arrived(v)), s2)
            None => drive(me, k(Arrived(v)), Sched { ..s, chans = chans2 })
        None =>
          match take_sender(cid, s.senders) of
            Some((who, sv, sk, srest)) =>
              let q =
                (s.enq)(s.queue, Ready(who, \() -> sk(Go), \() -> sk(Stop)))
              let s2 = Sched { ..s, senders = srest, queue = q }
              if me == 0 && s2.failed then
                let q2 = (s2.enq)(
                    s2.queue,
                    Ready(me, \() -> k(Arrived(sv)), \() -> k(Halt)),
                  )
                run_next(Sched { ..s2, queue = q2 })
              else
                drive(me, k(Arrived(sv)), s2)
            None =>
              run_next(
                  Sched {
                    ..s,
                    recv_waiters = append(s.recv_waiters, [(cid, me, k)])
                  },
                )
    Died =>
      if me == 0 then
        fail()
      else
        let died2 = fold_add([me], s.died)
        match wake(me, Gone, s.waiters, s.queue, s.enq) of
          (ws, q) =>
            run_next(
                Sched {
                  ..s,
                  finalizing = remove(me, s.finalizing),
                  died = died2,
                  waiters = ws,
                  queue = q
                },
              )
    Failed =>
      let victims = others(me, s)
      let s1 = Sched { ..s, finalizing = remove(me, s.finalizing) }
      let s2 = cancel_tree(victims, s1)
      run_next(Sched { ..s2, failed = true })
    Finished(r) =>
      if me == 0 then
        if s.failed then
          fail()
        else
          r
      else
        match wake(me, Arrived(r), s.waiters, s.queue, s.enq) of
          (ws, q) =>
            run_next(
                Sched {
                  ..s,
                  results = Cons((me, r), s.results),
                  waiters = ws,
                  queue = q
                },
              )

defs.name: run_next
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (Concurrent@Sched(a, {Fail, e0})) -> a ! {Fail, e0}
defs.source:
fn run_next(s : Sched(a, e)) : a =
  match s.queue of
    Nil => fail()
    Cons(Ready(id, go, stop), rest) =>
      if s.failed && id == 0 then
        match rest of
          Cons(_, _) =>
            run_next(Sched { ..s, queue = append(rest, [Ready(id, go, stop)]) })
          Nil =>
            if is_member(id, s.cancelled) then
              drive(
                  id,
                  stop(),
                  Sched {
                    ..s,
                    queue = Nil,
                    cancelled = remove(id, s.cancelled),
                    finalizing = fold_add([id], s.finalizing)
                  },
                )
            elif is_member(id, s.finalizing) then
              drive(id, go(), Sched { ..s, queue = Nil })
            else
              fail()
      elif is_member(id, s.cancelled) then
        drive(
            id,
            stop(),
            Sched {
              ..s,
              queue = rest,
              cancelled = remove(id, s.cancelled),
              finalizing = fold_add([id], s.finalizing)
            },
          )
      else
        drive(id, go(), Sched { ..s, queue = rest })

defs.name: run_async
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (() -> a ! {Concurrent.Async(a), Fail, e0}) -> a ! {Fail, e0}
defs.source:
fn run_async(main : () -> a ! {Async(a) | e}) : a =
  drive(0, step(main), fresh(\(q, r) -> append(q, [r])))
defs.doc:
Run `main` and its fibers cooperatively under the FIFO (round-robin) policy, returning `main`'s result. The fibers' effects `e` flow out unchanged, so the caller still handles them. The schedule is deterministic, so a run's output is reproducible.

```prism
fn task() : Int ! {Async(Int)} = await(fork(\() -> 21)) * 2

fn main() = println(run_async(task))
```

```output
42
```

defs.name: run_cooperative
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (() -> a ! {Concurrent.Async(a), Fail, e0}) -> a ! {Fail, e0}
defs.source: fn run_cooperative(main : () -> a ! {Async(a) | e}) : a = run_async(main)
defs.doc: The policy-neutral entry point: run `main` under the deployment's default cooperative scheduler. It is `run_async` (FIFO) by default, and the `--scheduler` flag (or `PRISM_SCHEDULER`) retargets it to another shipped policy such as `run_lifo` with no source change, because the scheduler is only a handler for `Async` and swapping it never touches the fibers. Call this when you want the configured default; call `run_async` or `run_lifo` directly to pin a policy.

defs.name: run_lifo
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (() -> a ! {Concurrent.Async(a), Fail, e0}) -> a ! {Fail, e0}
defs.source:
fn run_lifo(main : () -> a ! {Async(a) | e}) : a =
  drive(0, step(main), fresh(\(q, r) -> Cons(r, q)))
defs.doc: A second scheduling policy over the same `Async` effect: LIFO (depth-first), which runs the most-recently-forked or most-recently-woken fiber next by pushing it to the front of the run queue. It discharges `fork`/`yield`/`await`/channels exactly as `run_async` does and returns the same result for a determinate computation; only the interleaving (and so the order of observable effects like prints) differs. This is the concrete proof that policy is a handler: the fibers are unchanged, only the run function is swapped.

defs.ty: forall e0 a. (List(() -> a ! {Concurrent.Async(a), e0})) -> List(Concurrent.Fiber) ! {Concurrent.Async(a), e0}
defs.source:
fn fork_all(tasks : List(() -> a ! {Async(a) | e})) : List(Fiber) =
  match tasks of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(t, rest) => Cons(fork(t), fork_all(rest))

fn await_all(fs : List(Fiber)) : List(a) =
  match fs of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(f, rest) => Cons(await(f), await_all(rest))

defs.name: scope
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (List(() -> a ! {Concurrent.Async(a), e0})) -> List(a) ! {Concurrent.Async(a), e0}
defs.source:
fn scope(tasks : List(() -> a ! {Async(a) | e})) : List(a) =
  await_all(fork_all(tasks))
defs.doc: Structured join: run `tasks` concurrently and await their results in order. On a successful run every task completes before `scope` returns. `scope` is not a failure-isolation boundary: an unhandled failure in one task triggers the scheduler-global abort rule, which cancels every other live fiber (including fibers created outside this call) and their descendants, drains runnable cancellation cleanups, and re-performs the failure at the enclosing `run_async`/`run_lifo` boundary.

defs.name: Clock
defs.source:
effect Clock
  now() : Int
  sleep(Int) : Unit
  wall_now() : Int
  mono_now() : Int
defs.doc: A logical-time capability: `now` reads the current tick and `sleep` advances it. Discharged by `run_clock`, which threads a pure counter, so time is virtual and deterministic: advance it in a test and behaviour is a function of it, with no real clock and no time primitive. A fiber may perform `Clock`; since the scheduler does not handle it, it flows out of `run_async` to an enclosing `run_clock` like any other capability. `now`/`sleep` are the logical scheduler clock (virtual ticks). `wall_now` and `mono_now` are the real-time reads (nanoseconds): the system wall clock (Unix epoch, UTC) and a monotonic counter. All four share the one `Clock` capability; which reading you get is a property of the installed handler, not the call. `run_clock` serves every op from the virtual counter (deterministic tests); `Time.run_clock_real` serves `wall_now`/`mono_now` from the recorded OS clock.

defs.name: run_clock
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (() -> a ! {Concurrent.Clock, e0}) -> a ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn run_clock(action : () -> a ! {Clock | e}) : a =
  let g =
    handle action() with
      now() resume k => \(t) -> k(t)(t)
      sleep(d) resume k => \(t) -> k(())(t + d)
      wall_now() resume k => \(t) -> k(t)(t)
      mono_now() resume k => \(t) -> k(t)(t)
      return r => \(_t) -> r
  g(0)
defs.doc:
Run `action` against a logical clock starting at 0, returning its result. `now()` reads the current time; `sleep(d)` advances it by `d`. Time is a pure threaded counter (the parameter-passing answer `Int -> a`), so the run is deterministic and reproducible under `Replay`.

```prism
fn timed() : Int ! {Clock} =
  sleep(5)
  sleep(2)
  now()

fn main() = println(run_clock(timed))
```

```output
7
```

defs.source:
fn demand(s : St(e), key : String) : (St(e), Bytes) =
  match map_lookup(key, st_tbl(s)) of
    None => (s, wire_empty)
    Some(InputN(bytes, _h)) => (s, bytes)
    Some(MemoN(th, deps, res)) =>
      match res of
        None => recompute(s, key, th)
        Some((rbytes, _rhash)) =>
          let vr = verify(s, deps)
          match vr of
            (s2, true) => (s2, rbytes)
            (s2, false) => recompute(s2, key, th)

defs.name: verify
defs.source:
fn verify(s : St(e), deps : List((String, String))) : (St(e), Bool) =
  match deps of
    Nil => (s, true)
    Cons((dk, dh), rest) =>
      let (s2, dv) = demand(s, dk)
      if str_eq(vhash(dv), dh) then
        verify(s2, rest)
      else
        (s2, false)

defs.source:
fn reg_memo(s, th) =
  let (s1, key) = st_fresh(s)
  if st_prefix_open(s1) then
    match map_lookup(key, st_warm(s1)) of
      Some(Warm(deps, bytes)) =>
        (
            st_add_persist(
                st_put(s1, key, MemoN(th, deps, Some((bytes, vhash(bytes))))),
                key,
              ),
            key,
          )
      None => (st_add_persist(st_put(s1, key, MemoN(th, Nil, None)), key), key)
  else
    (st_put(s1, key, MemoN(th, Nil, None)), key)

      else

defs.name: do_get
run_thunk
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (Incr@St({e0}), () -> a ! {Incr.IncrRaw, e0}) -> (Incr@St({e0}), a) ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn run_thunk(s : St(e), action : () -> a ! {IncrRaw | e}) : (St(e), a) =
  let f =
    handle action() with
      incr_input(bytes) resume k =>
        \(st) -> let (st2, key) = reg_input(st, bytes) in k(key)(st2)
      incr_memo(th) resume k =>
        \(st) -> let (st2, key) = reg_memo(st, th) in k(key)(st2)
      incr_set(key, bytes) resume k =>
        \(st) -> let st2 = do_set(st_close_prefix(st), key, bytes) in k(())(st2)
      incr_get(key) resume k =>
        \(st) -> let (st2, v) = do_get(st_close_prefix(st), key) in k(v)(st2)
      return x => \(st) -> (st, x)
  f(s)

  let live = get(scores)

fn snap_build(
  ks : List(String),
  dks : List(List(String)),
  dhs : List(List(String)),
  bys : List(Bytes)
) : Map(String, Warm) =
  match ks of
    Nil => map_empty
    Cons(k, kr) =>

        Cons(dk, dkr) =>

            Cons(dh, dhr) =>
              match bys of
                Cons(by, byr) =>
                  map_insert(
                      k,
                      Warm(snap_zip_deps(dk, dh), by),

run_incr_durable
defs.ty: forall a. (String, String, () -> a ! {Fail, Incr.IncrRaw}) -> a ! {Fail, IO}
defs.doc:
Discharge the `Incr` effect with a durable snapshot at `path`, tagged by `tag` (the caller-named program identity: a snapshot written under a different tag cold-starts). This is the file-substrate form of the production path, which rides the content-addressed store once a program can hold a runtime handle on it; the same reduced table is what that store persists.

The action must be pure up to `Fail`, so its row is closed at `{IncrRaw, Fail}`: a warm hit skips the memo thunk, and skipping a thunk that printed or drew a random would change the output, so only effect-free thunks may be reused across runs. Only the creation prefix (the memos built before the first `get`/`set`) is warmed and persisted; input-dependent memos stay scratch and recompute. Within those bounds a warm run's output is byte-identical to a cold run, and deleting or corrupting the snapshot changes only cost, never the result.

```prism,no_run
run_incr_durable("totals.snap", "report") fn
  let a = input(10)
  get(memo(\() -> get(a) * 2))
```

defs.name: run_incr_store
defs.ty: forall a. (String, String, () -> a ! {Fail, Incr.IncrRaw}) -> a ! {Fail, IO}
defs.doc:
Discharge the `Incr` effect with a durable snapshot on the content-addressed store rooted at `root`, tagged by `tag` (the caller-named program identity). The store form of `run_incr_durable`: the reduced memo table rides the real store's object layer (the blob keyed by its content hash) with a ref for `tag`, rather than a snapshot file. The file substrate stays available; a call site picks the substrate by picking the handler.

Every durability guarantee of the file form carries over. The action is pure up to `Fail`, so only the creation-prefix memos are warmed and persisted; a warm run's output is byte-identical to a cold run; and a missing, dangling, or corrupt store entry cold-starts, changing only cost, never the result.

```prism,no_run

  let a = input(10)
  get(memo(\() -> get(a) * 2))
```

fn t_record_edge(s, dep, dephash) =
  match s of
    TSt(m, d, _c, _w, _p, _ps, _rt) =>
      match d of
        Nil => s
        Cons(cur, _) =>
          match map_lookup(cur, m) of

defs.name: t_demand
defs.source:
fn t_demand(s : TSt(e), key : String, loud : Bool) : (TSt(e), Bytes) =
  match map_lookup(key, t_tbl(s)) of
    None => (s, wire_empty)
    Some(TInput(bytes, _h)) => (s, bytes)
    Some(TMemo(th, deps, res, _tr, emitted)) =>
      match res of
        None =>
          let (s1, rbytes) = t_recompute(s, key, th)
          if loud then
            (t_replay(s1, key), rbytes)
          else
            (s1, rbytes)
        Some((rbytes, _rhash)) =>
          let vr = t_verify(s, deps)
          match vr of
            (s2, false) =>
              let (s3, rb2) = t_recompute(s2, key, th)
              if loud then
                (t_replay(s3, key), rb2)
              else
                (s3, rb2)
            (s2, true) =>
              if loud then
                if emitted then
                  (s2, rbytes)
                else
                  (t_replay(s2, key), rbytes)
              else
                (s2, rbytes)

defs.name: t_verify
defs.source:
fn t_verify(s : TSt(e), deps : List((String, String))) : (TSt(e), Bool) =
  match deps of
    Nil => (s, true)
    Cons((dk, dh), rest) =>
      let (s2, dv) = t_demand(s, dk, false)
      if str_eq(vhash(dv), dh) then
        t_verify(s2, rest)
      else
        (s2, false)

defs.source:
fn t_reg_memo(s, th) =
  let (s1, key) = t_fresh(s)
  if t_prefix_open(s1) then
    match map_lookup(key, t_warm(s1)) of
      Some(TWarm(deps, bytes, trace)) =>
        (
            t_add_persist(
                t_put(
                    s1,
                    key,
                    TMemo(
                        t_widen(th),
                        deps,
                        Some((bytes, vhash(bytes))),
                        trace,
                        false,
                      ),
                  ),
                key,
              ),
            key,
          )
      None =>
        (
            t_add_persist(
                t_put(s1, key, TMemo(t_widen(th), Nil, None, Nil, false)),
                key,
              ),
            key,
          )
  else
    (t_put(s1, key, TMemo(t_widen(th), Nil, None, Nil, false)), key)

      else
        t_put(s, key, TInput(bytes, vhash(bytes)))

defs.ty: forall e0 a. (Incr@TSt({e0}), () -> a ! {Incr.IncrRaw, Output, e0}) -> (Incr@TSt({e0}), a) ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn t_run_thunk(
  s : TSt(e),
  action : () -> a ! {IncrRaw, Output | e}
) : (TSt(e), a) =
  let f =
    handle action() with
      incr_input(bytes) resume k =>
        \(st) -> let (st2, key) = t_reg_input(st, bytes) in k(key)(st2)
      incr_memo(th) resume k =>
        \(st) -> let (st2, key) = t_reg_memo(st, th) in k(key)(st2)
      incr_set(key, bytes) resume k =>
        \(st) -> let st2 = t_do_set(t_close_prefix(st), key, bytes) in k(())(st2)
      incr_get(key) resume k =>
        \(st) -> let (st2, v) = t_do_get(t_close_prefix(st), key) in k(v)(st2)
      out_println(x) resume k => \(st) -> k(())(t_capture(st, FPrintln(x)))
      out_print(x) resume k => \(st) -> k(())(t_capture(st, FPrint(x)))
      return x => \(st) -> (st, x)
  f(s)

fn t_snap_collect(s, keys) =
  match keys of
    Nil => TSnap(Nil, Nil, Nil, Nil, Nil)
    Cons(key, rest) =>
      match t_snap_collect(s, rest) of
        TSnap(ks, dks, dhs, bys, trs) =>
          match map_lookup(key, t_tbl(s)) of
            Some(TMemo(_, deps, Some((bytes, _h)), trace, _em)) =>
              TSnap(
                  Cons(key, ks),
                  Cons(map(fst, deps), dks),
                  Cons(map(snd, deps), dhs),
                  Cons(bytes, bys),
                  Cons(t_trace_encode(reverse(trace)), trs),

            _ => TSnap(ks, dks, dhs, bys, trs)

defs.name: t_snap_encode
t_snap_build
defs.ty: forall a. (List(String), List(List(String)), List(List(String)), List(Wire.Bytes), List(String)) -> Map(String, Incr@TWarm, a)
defs.source:
fn t_snap_build(
  ks : List(String),
  dks : List(List(String)),
  dhs : List(List(String)),
  bys : List(Bytes),
  trs : List(String)
) : Map(String, TWarm) =
  match ks of
    Nil => map_empty
    Cons(k, kr) =>
      match dks of
        Cons(dk, dkr) =>
          match dhs of
            Cons(dh, dhr) =>
              match bys of
                Cons(by, byr) =>
                  match trs of
                    Cons(tr, trr) =>
                      map_insert(
                          k,
                          TWarm(
                              snap_zip_deps(dk, dh),
                              by,
                              reverse(t_trace_decode(tr)),
                            ),
                          t_snap_build(kr, dkr, dhr, byr, trr),
                        )
                    Nil => map_empty
                Nil => map_empty
            Nil => map_empty
        Nil => map_empty

defs.name: t_snap_len_ok
defs.ty: forall a b c d e. (List(a), List(b), List(c), List(d), List(e)) -> Bool
defs.source:
fn t_snap_len_ok(
  ks : List(a),
  dks : List(b),
  dhs : List(c),
  bys : List(d),
  trs : List(f)
) : Bool =
  length(ks) == length(dks)
    && length(dks) == length(dhs)
    && length(dhs) == length(bys)
    && length(bys) == length(trs)

defs.name: t_snap_decode
defs.source:
fn t_snap_decode(body : String) : Map(String, TWarm) =
  match decode(snap_parse_bytes(body)) of
    (ks, r1) =>
      match decode(r1) of
        (dks, r2) =>
          match decode(r2) of
            (dhs, r3) =>
              match decode(r3) of
                (bys, r4) =>
                  match decode(r4) of
                    (trs, _r5) =>
                      if t_snap_len_ok(ks, dks, dhs, bys, trs) then
                        t_snap_build(ks, dks, dhs, bys, trs)
                      else
                        map_empty

defs.source:
fn t_snap_try(body) =
  handle t_snap_decode(body) with
    never fail() => map_empty
    return m => m

defs.name: t_store_save
run_incr_durable_replay
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (String, String, () -> a ! {Fail, IO, Incr.IncrRaw, Output, e0}) -> a ! {Fail, IO, e0}
defs.doc:
Discharge the `Incr` effect with a durable, trace-replay snapshot at `path`, tagged by `tag`. Unlike `run_incr_durable`, the memo thunks may perform any replayable effect: a cold run records each memo's output beside its result, and a durable warm hit REPLAYS that output instead of re-running the thunk, so a warm run's console is byte-identical to a cold run's, effects included. A missing, corrupt, foreign, or wrong-version snapshot is a silent cold start.

```prism,no_run
run_incr_durable_replay("run.snap", "job") fn
  let a = input(41)
  get(memo(\() -> get(a) + 1))
```

defs.name: run_incr_store_replay
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (String, String, () -> a ! {Fail, IO, Incr.IncrRaw, Output, e0}) -> a ! {Fail, IO, e0}
defs.doc:
The content-addressed-store form of `run_incr_durable_replay`: the traced memo table (results and output traces) rides the real store's object layer, keyed by `tag`, rather than a snapshot file. Every guarantee of the file form carries over; a missing, dangling, or corrupt store entry cold-starts.

```prism,no_run
run_incr_store_replay(".prism-store", "job") fn
  let a = input(41)
  get(memo(\() -> get(a) + 1))
```

defs.name: Json
defs.source:
type Json
  = JNull
  | JBool(Bool)
  | JInt(Int)
  | JFloat(Float)
  | JStr(String)
  | JArr(List(Json))
  | JObj(List((String, Json)))
defs.doc:
A dynamic JSON value. Numbers split into `JInt` and `JFloat` so the exact-or-error decode is a structural distinction rather than a hidden flag: an object is an association list in parse order (duplicate keys are preserved, not merged).

```prism
encode(JObj([("ok", JBool(true)), ("n", JInt(3))]))
```

```output
{"n":3,"ok":true}
```
