defs.name: line_col_go
defs.source:
fn line_col_go(
  b : Bytes,
  j : Int,
  i : Int,
  line : Int,
  col : Int
) : (Int, Int) =
  if j >= i then
    (line, col)
  else
    let c = bytes_index(b, j)
    if c == 10 then
      line_col_go(b, j + 1, i, line + 1, 1)
    elif c >= 128 && c < 192 then
      line_col_go(b, j + 1, i, line, col)
    else
      line_col_go(b, j + 1, i, line, col + 1)

defs.name: mk_err
lit_at
defs.source:
fn lit_at(b : Bytes, n : Int, i : Int, lit : String) : Bool =
  i + byte_len(lit) <= n && lit_at_go(b, i, lit, 0, byte_len(lit))

defs.name: lit_at_go
defs.source:
fn lit_at_go(b : Bytes, i : Int, lit : String, k : Int, m : Int) : Bool =
  if k >= m then
    true
  elif bytes_index(b, i + k) == byte_at(lit, k) then
    lit_at_go(b, i, lit, k + 1, m)
  else
    false

defs.name: hex_val
defs.source:
fn hex_val(c : Int) : Option(Int) =
  if c >= 48 && c <= 57 then
    Some(c - 48)
  elif c >= 97 && c <= 102 then
    Some(c - 97 + 10)
  elif c >= 65 && c <= 70 then
    Some(c - 65 + 10)
  else
    None

defs.name: hex4
defs.source:
fn hex4(b : Bytes, n : Int, i : Int) : Option(Int) =
  if i + 4 > n then
    None
  else
    match ((
          hex_val(bytes_index(b, i)),
          hex_val(bytes_index(b, i + 1)),
          hex_val(bytes_index(b, i + 2)),
          hex_val(bytes_index(b, i + 3)),
        )) of
      (Some(h1), Some(h2), Some(h3), Some(h4)) =>
        Some(((h1 * 16 + h2) * 16 + h3) * 16 + h4)
      _ => None

defs.name: parse_string
str_run
defs.ty: (Wire.Bytes, Int, Int, Int, Wire.Bytes) -> Result((String, Int), Json.JsonError)
defs.source:
fn str_run(
  b : Bytes,
  n : Int,
  start : Int,
  j : Int,
  acc : Bytes
) : Result((String, Int), JsonError) =
  if j >= n then
    Err(mk_err(b, n, j, "unterminated string"))
  else
    let c = bytes_index(b, j)
    if c == 34 then
      let whole = bytes_concat(acc, bytes_slice(b, start, j - start))
      match bytes_to_string(whole) of
        Some(text) => Ok((text, j + 1))
        None => Err(mk_err(b, n, j, "invalid UTF-8 in string"))
    elif c == 92 then
      parse_escape(
          b,
          n,
          j + 1,
          bytes_concat(acc, bytes_slice(b, start, j - start)),
        )
    elif c < 32 then
      Err(mk_err(b, n, j, "unescaped control character in string"))
    else
      str_run(b, n, start, j + 1, acc)

  n : Int,

defs.name: parse_escape
defs.ty: (Wire.Bytes, Int, Int, Wire.Bytes) -> Result((String, Int), Json.JsonError)
defs.source:
fn parse_escape(
  b : Bytes,
  n : Int,
  i : Int,
  acc : Bytes
) : Result((String, Int), JsonError) =
  if i >= n then
    Err(mk_err(b, n, i, "unterminated escape"))
  else
    let c = bytes_index(b, i)
    if c == 34 then
      esc_emit(b, n, i + 1, acc, 34)
    elif c == 92 then
      esc_emit(b, n, i + 1, acc, 92)
    elif c == 47 then
      esc_emit(b, n, i + 1, acc, 47)
    elif c == 98 then
      esc_emit(b, n, i + 1, acc, 8)
    elif c == 102 then
      esc_emit(b, n, i + 1, acc, 12)
    elif c == 110 then
      esc_emit(b, n, i + 1, acc, 10)
    elif c == 114 then
      esc_emit(b, n, i + 1, acc, 13)
    elif c == 116 then
      esc_emit(b, n, i + 1, acc, 9)
    elif c == 117 then
      parse_unicode(b, n, i + 1, acc)
    else
      Err(mk_err(b, n, i, "invalid escape"))

defs.name: parse_unicode
defs.ty: (Wire.Bytes, Int, Int, Wire.Bytes) -> Result((String, Int), Json.JsonError)
defs.source:
fn parse_unicode(
  b : Bytes,
  n : Int,
  i : Int,
  acc : Bytes
) : Result((String, Int), JsonError) =
  match hex4(b, n, i) of
    None => Err(mk_err(b, n, i, "invalid \\u escape"))
    Some(cp) =>
      if cp >= 55296 && cp <= 56319 then
        if lit_at(b, n, i + 4, "\\u") then
          match hex4(b, n, i + 6) of
            Some(lo) =>
              if lo >= 56320 && lo <= 57343 then
                let scalar = 65536 + (cp - 55296) * 1024 + lo - 56320
                esc_emit(b, n, i + 10, acc, scalar)
              else
                Err(mk_err(b, n, i, "invalid low surrogate in \\u escape"))
            None => Err(mk_err(b, n, i, "invalid \\u escape"))
        else
          Err(mk_err(b, n, i, "unpaired high surrogate in \\u escape"))
      elif cp >= 56320 && cp <= 57343 then
        Err(mk_err(b, n, i, "unpaired low surrogate in \\u escape"))
      else
        esc_emit(b, n, i + 4, acc, cp)

defs.name: skip_digits
defs.source:
fn skip_digits(b : Bytes, n : Int, i : Int) : Int =
  if i < n && is_digit(bytes_index(b, i)) then
    skip_digits(b, n, i + 1)
  else
    i

defs.name: lex_int_part
defs.source:
fn lex_int_part(b : Bytes, n : Int, i : Int) : Option(Int) =
  if i >= n || not(is_digit(bytes_index(b, i))) then
    None
  elif bytes_index(b, i) == 48 then
    Some(i + 1)
  else
    Some(skip_digits(b, n, i))

defs.name: lex_frac
defs.source:
fn lex_frac(b : Bytes, n : Int, i : Int) : Option((Int, Bool)) =
  if i < n && bytes_index(b, i) == 46 then
    let j = i + 1
    if j < n && is_digit(bytes_index(b, j)) then
      Some((skip_digits(b, n, j), true))
    else
      None
  else
    Some((i, false))

defs.name: lex_exp
defs.source:
fn lex_exp(b : Bytes, n : Int, i : Int) : Option((Int, Bool)) =
  if i < n && (bytes_index(b, i) == 101 || bytes_index(b, i) == 69) then
    let j =
      if (i + 1 < n
          && (bytes_index(b, i + 1) == 43 || bytes_index(b, i + 1) == 45)) then
        i + 2
      else
        i + 1
    if j < n && is_digit(bytes_index(b, j)) then
      Some((skip_digits(b, n, j), true))
    else
      None
  else
    Some((i, false))

defs.name: lex_number
defs.source:
fn lex_number(b : Bytes, n : Int, i0 : Int) : Option((Int, Bool)) =
  let i1 =
    if i0 < n && bytes_index(b, i0) == 45 then
      i0 + 1
    else
      i0
  match lex_int_part(b, n, i1) of
    None => None
    Some(i2) =>
      match lex_frac(b, n, i2) of
        None => None
        Some((i3, hf)) =>
          match lex_exp(b, n, i3) of
            None => None
            Some((i4, he)) => Some((i4, hf || he))

defs.name: classify_number
defs.source:
fn classify_number(
  lossy : Bool,
  lexeme : String,
  is_dec : Bool
) : Option(Json) =
  if is_dec then
    let f = parse_float(lexeme)
    if lossy || str_eq(show_float(f), lexeme) then
      Some(JFloat(f))
    else
      None
  else
    match parse_int(lexeme) of
      Some(n) =>
        if lossy || str_eq(show_int(n), lexeme) then
          Some(JInt(n))
        else
          None
      None =>
        if lossy then
          Some(JFloat(parse_float(lexeme)))
        else
          None

defs.name: parse_number
defs.ty: (Bool, Wire.Bytes, Int, Int) -> Result((Json.Json, Int), Json.JsonError)
defs.source:
fn parse_number(
  lossy : Bool,
  b : Bytes,
  n : Int,
  i : Int
) : Result((Json, Int), JsonError) =
  match lex_number(b, n, i) of
    None => Err(mk_err(b, n, i, "invalid number"))
    Some((end, is_dec)) =>
      -- A validated number lexeme is pure ASCII, so the conversion is total.
      let lexeme =
        match bytes_to_string(bytes_slice(b, i, end - i)) of
          Some(text) => text
          None => ""
      match classify_number(lossy, lexeme, is_dec) of
        Some(v) => Ok((v, end))
        None =>
          Err(
              mk_err(
                  b,
                  n,
                  i,
                  "number not exactly representable (use decode_lossy)",
                ),
            )

defs.name: parse_value
defs.ty: (Bool, Wire.Bytes, Int, Int, Int) -> Result((Json.Json, Int), Json.JsonError)
defs.source:
fn parse_value(
  lossy : Bool,
  b : Bytes,
  n : Int,
  i : Int,
  d : Int
) : Result((Json, Int), JsonError) =
  let j = skip_ws(b, n, i)
  if j >= n then
    Err(mk_err(b, n, j, "unexpected end of input"))
  else
    let c = bytes_index(b, j)
    if c == 123 then
      parse_object(lossy, b, n, j, d)
    elif c == 91 then
      parse_array(lossy, b, n, j, d)
    elif c == 34 then
      match parse_string(b, n, j) of
        Ok((str, k)) => Ok((JStr(str), k))
        Err(e) => Err(e)
    elif c == 45 || is_digit(c) then
      parse_number(lossy, b, n, j)
    elif lit_at(b, n, j, "true") then
      Ok((JBool(true), j + 4))
    elif lit_at(b, n, j, "false") then
      Ok((JBool(false), j + 5))
    elif lit_at(b, n, j, "null") then
      Ok((JNull, j + 4))
    else
      Err(mk_err(b, n, j, "unexpected character"))

defs.name: parse_array
defs.ty: (Bool, Wire.Bytes, Int, Int, Int) -> Result((Json.Json, Int), Json.JsonError)
defs.source:
fn parse_array(
  lossy : Bool,
  b : Bytes,
  n : Int,
  i : Int,
  d : Int
) : Result((Json, Int), JsonError) =
  if d + 1 > max_depth() then
    Err(mk_err(b, n, i, "maximum nesting depth exceeded"))
  else
    let j = skip_ws(b, n, i + 1)
    if j < n && bytes_index(b, j) == 93 then
      Ok((JArr(Nil), j + 1))
    else
      array_elems(lossy, b, n, i + 1, d + 1, Nil)

defs.name: array_elems
defs.ty: (Bool, Wire.Bytes, Int, Int, Int, List(Json.Json)) -> Result((Json.Json, Int), Json.JsonError)
defs.source:
fn array_elems(
  lossy : Bool,
  b : Bytes,
  n : Int,
  i : Int,
  d : Int,
  acc : List(Json)
) : Result((Json, Int), JsonError) =
  match parse_value(lossy, b, n, i, d) of
    Err(e) => Err(e)
    Ok((v, k)) =>
      let acc2 = Cons(v, acc)
      let j = skip_ws(b, n, k)
      if j >= n then
        Err(mk_err(b, n, j, "unterminated array"))
      else
        let c = bytes_index(b, j)
        if c == 93 then
          Ok((JArr(reverse(acc2)), j + 1))
        elif c == 44 then
          array_elems(lossy, b, n, j + 1, d, acc2)
        else
          Err(mk_err(b, n, j, "expected ',' or ']' in array"))

defs.name: parse_object
defs.ty: (Bool, Wire.Bytes, Int, Int, Int) -> Result((Json.Json, Int), Json.JsonError)
defs.source:
fn parse_object(
  lossy : Bool,
  b : Bytes,
  n : Int,
  i : Int,
  d : Int
) : Result((Json, Int), JsonError) =
  if d + 1 > max_depth() then
    Err(mk_err(b, n, i, "maximum nesting depth exceeded"))
  else
    let j = skip_ws(b, n, i + 1)
    if j < n && bytes_index(b, j) == 125 then
      Ok((JObj(Nil), j + 1))
    else
      object_members(lossy, b, n, i + 1, d + 1, Nil)

defs.name: object_members
defs.ty: (Bool, Wire.Bytes, Int, Int, Int, List((String, Json.Json))) -> Result((Json.Json, Int), Json.JsonError)
defs.source:
fn object_members(
  lossy : Bool,
  b : Bytes,
  n : Int,
  i : Int,
  d : Int,
  acc : List((String, Json))
) : Result((Json, Int), JsonError) =
  let j = skip_ws(b, n, i)
  if j >= n || bytes_index(b, j) /= 34 then
    Err(mk_err(b, n, j, "expected string key in object"))
  else
    match parse_string(b, n, j) of
      Err(e) => Err(e)
      Ok((key, k)) =>
        let k2 = skip_ws(b, n, k)
        if k2 >= n || bytes_index(b, k2) /= 58 then
          Err(mk_err(b, n, k2, "expected ':' after object key"))
        else
          match parse_value(lossy, b, n, k2 + 1, d) of
            Err(e) => Err(e)
            Ok((v, m)) =>
              let acc2 = Cons((key, v), acc)
              let m2 = skip_ws(b, n, m)
              if m2 >= n then
                Err(mk_err(b, n, m2, "unterminated object"))
              else
                let c = bytes_index(b, m2)
                if c == 125 then
                  Ok((JObj(reverse(acc2)), m2 + 1))
                elif c == 44 then
                  object_members(lossy, b, n, m2 + 1, d, acc2)
                else
                  Err(mk_err(b, n, m2, "expected ',' or '\}' in object"))

fn esc_char(c : Int) : String =
  if c == 34 then
    "\\\""
  elif c == 92 then
    "\\\\"
  elif c == 8 then
    "\\b"
  elif c == 12 then
    "\\f"
  elif c == 10 then

  elif c == 13 then

defs.source:
fn sort_pairs(xs : List((String, Json))) : List((String, Json)) =
  match xs of
    Nil => Nil
    Cons(_, Nil) => xs
    _ =>
      let (l, r) = split_alt(xs)
      merge_pairs(sort_pairs(l), sort_pairs(r))

defs.name: split_alt
defs.source:
fn split_alt(xs : List((String, Json))) : (List((String, Json)), List((String, Json))) =
  match xs of
    Nil => (Nil, Nil)
    Cons(a, Nil) => (Cons(a, Nil), Nil)
    Cons(a, Cons(b, rest)) =>
      let (l, r) = split_alt(rest)
      (Cons(a, l), Cons(b, r))

defs.name: merge_pairs
defs.source:
fn merge_pairs(
  a : List((String, Json)),
  b : List((String, Json))
) : List((String, Json)) =
  match (a, b) of
    (Nil, _) => b
    (_, Nil) => a
    (Cons(x, xs), Cons(y, ys)) =>
      match (x, y) of
        ((kx, _), (ky, _)) =>
          if str_cmp(kx, ky) <= 0 then
            Cons(x, merge_pairs(xs, b))
          else
            Cons(y, merge_pairs(a, ys))

fn encode(j : Json) : String =
  match j of
    JNull => "null"
    JBool(b) =>
      if b then
        "true"
      else
        "false"
    JInt(n) => show_int(n)
    JFloat(f) => encode_float(f)
    JStr(s) => encode_string(s)
    JArr(xs) => concat("[", concat(str_join(",", map(encode, xs)), "]"))
    JObj(kvs) =>
      concat(
          "\{",
          concat(str_join(",", map(encode_member, sort_pairs(kvs))), "\}"),
        )

defs.name: ToJson
defs.source:
class ToJson(a)
  to_json : (a) -> Json
defs.doc:
Convert a value to a `Json` tree.

`deriving (ToJson)` writes the instance structurally, for a type whose schema is its own declaration. One constructor becomes one object: a record constructor's keys are its declared field names, a positional one's are its argument positions (`_0`, `_1`), and a sum additionally names the variant it holds under the key `$`, which no field name can spell. A document therefore names the constructor it holds rather than an index that quietly changes meaning when a constructor is inserted; a single-constructor type has nothing to discriminate and carries no tag. Constructor and field order are the declaration's, so one value has one tree, and `encode` sorts keys, so it has one string. Derive it in a pair with `FromJson`: a type that encodes but cannot decode is a document nobody can read back.

This is not the wire codec. A `Wire.Serialize` byte format is frozen and versioned; a JSON document is read by something that was not compiled against this program, so the encoding is self-describing rather than compact, and nothing here promises stability across a change to the declaration.

```prism
to_json([1, 2, 3])
```

```output
Json.JArr([Json.JInt(1), Json.JInt(2), Json.JInt(3)])
```

defs.name: FromJson
defs.source:
class FromJson(a)
  from_json : (Json) -> a ! {Fail | e}
defs.doc:
Recover a value from a `Json` tree, failing (through `Fail`) on a structural mismatch. A decode of foreign data is one ordinary failure channel.

`deriving (FromJson)` reads back exactly what the derived `ToJson` wrote, by the same keys: `from_json(to_json(x))` is `x`. A tree that is not an object, a sum whose `$` names no constructor of the type, a missing key, and a field that will not itself decode all leave through the same `Fail`. That failure carries no payload, so it reports that the document did not fit and not where: `Fail` is a nullary operation, and reporting a path would mean a different effect on this class's signature and so on every hand-written instance too. Catch it with `optional`, `default`, or `succeeds`, as with any other `Fail`.

```prism
from_json(JInt(41)) + 1
```

```output
42
```

fn json_field(kvs : List((String, Json)), key : String) : Json ! {Fail | e} =
  match kvs of
    Nil => fail()
    Cons(kv, rest) =>
      match kv of
        (k, v) =>
          if k == key then
            v
          else
            json_field(rest, key)
defs.doc:
The member named `key` of an object's member list, or `fail()` when there is none. Members are kept in parse order and duplicates are preserved, so the first occurrence wins, which is what makes a decode a function of the document rather than of a hash order. `deriving (ToJson, FromJson)` reads every field through this, so a missing field and a mistyped one leave through the same channel.

fn json_rebuild(j : Json, cs : List(Json)) : Json =
  match j of
    JArr(items) =>
      if length(items) == length(cs) then
        JArr(cs)
      else
        j
    JObj(fields) =>
      match json_rekey(fields, cs) of
        Some(fs) => JObj(fs)
        None => j
    _ => j

fn json_rekey(
  fields : List((String, Json)),
  cs : List(Json)
) : Option(List((String, Json))) =

    (Nil, Nil) => Some(Nil)
    (Cons(kv, more), Cons(v, rest)) =>
      match json_rekey(more, rest) of
        None => None
        Some(tl) => Some(Cons((json_field_name(kv), v), tl))
    _ => None

defs.name: float_at
defs.source:
fn float_at(size : Int) =
  let pick = nat_below(9)
  if pick == 0 then
    0.0
  elif pick == 1 then
    1.0
  elif pick == 2 then
    0.0 - 1.0
  elif pick == 3 then
    1.0 / 0.0
  elif pick == 4 then
    (0.0 - 1.0) / 0.0
  elif pick == 5 then
    0.0 / 0.0
  else
    let m = size + 1
    to_float(small_signed(size)) / to_float(m)

defs.name: gen_float
defs.source: let gen_float : Gen(Float) = Gen(float_at)
defs.doc: Generator of `Float`, including the nasty values (`+/-0`, `+/-inf`, `NaN`).

defs.name: gen_char

fn rand_bytes(n : Int, buf : Buf) =
  if n <= 0 then

  else

defs.source:
let gen_string : Gen(String) =

defs.doc: Generator of a printable-ASCII `String`, length bounded by size.

defs.name: list_of
defs.source:
fn list_of(g : Gen(a), size : Int, n : Int) =
  if n <= 0 then
    Nil
  else
    Cons(gen_run(g, size), list_of(g, size, n - 1))

defs.name: gen_list

fn gen_list(g : Gen(a)) : Gen(List(a)) =

defs.doc:

defs.source:
fn gen_option(g : Gen(a)) : Gen(Option(a)) =

    if nat_below(4) == 0 then

    else

defs.name: Outcome
defs.source: type Outcome(a) = Passed(Int) | Failed(a, Int, U64, Int)
defs.doc: The result of a property run: `Passed(n)` after `n` cases held, or `Failed(value, index, seed, size)` with the first counterexample and the seed and size that reproduce it via `gen_at`.

fn seed_for(base : U64, i : Int) : U64 =
  sm_out(base + to_u64(i) * splitmix_gamma)

defs.name: check_go

defs.name: check_with

  check_go(cfg, gen, prop, 0)
defs.doc:
Run `prop` over `cfg.count` inputs from `gen`, returning the first counterexample or the count that passed. Deterministic in `cfg.seed`.

```prism

```

    Passed(_) => true
    Failed(_, _, _, _) => false

defs.name: show_outcome
defs.source:
fn show_outcome(name : String, o : Outcome(a)) : String given Show(a) =
  match o of
    Passed(n) => concat_all([name, ": OK, passed ", show(n), " tests."])
    Failed(x, i, sd, sz) =>
      concat_all([
          name,
          ": FAILED after ",
          show(i),
          " tests.\n  counterexample: ",
          show(x),
          "\n  reproduce: seed ",
          show(sd),
          " size ",
          show(sz),
        ])
defs.doc:
Render an outcome for `name` as one report line (pass) or a block naming the counterexample and the seed and size that reproduce it.

```prism

```

```output
positivity: FAILED after 12 tests.
  counterexample: 0
  reproduce: seed 42 size 5
```

defs.name: TraceEntry
defs.source:
type TraceEntry
  = TInt(Int)
  | TStr(String)
  | TBool(Bool)
  | TOut

defs.name: Trace
defs.source: alias Trace = List(TraceEntry)

defs.name: rec_int
defs.ty: forall e0 a. ((Int) -> (List(Replay@TraceEntry)) -> a ! {e0} ! {e0}, List(Replay@TraceEntry), Int) -> a ! {e0}
defs.source: fn rec_int(k, t, x) = k(x)(Cons(TInt(x), t))

defs.name: rec_str
defs.ty: forall e0 a. ((String) -> (List(Replay@TraceEntry)) -> a ! {e0} ! {e0}, List(Replay@TraceEntry), String) -> a ! {e0}
defs.source: fn rec_str(k, t, x) = k(x)(Cons(TStr(x), t))

defs.name: rec_bytes
defs.ty: forall e0 a. ((Buf) -> (List(Replay@TraceEntry)) -> a ! {e0} ! {e0}, List(Replay@TraceEntry), Buf) -> a ! {e0}
defs.source: fn rec_bytes(k, t, buf) = k(buf)(Cons(TStr(hex_encode(bytes_of_buf(buf))), t))

defs.name: rec_bool
defs.ty: forall e0 a. ((Bool) -> (List(Replay@TraceEntry)) -> a ! {e0} ! {e0}, List(Replay@TraceEntry), Bool) -> a ! {e0}
defs.source: fn rec_bool(k, t, x) = k(x)(Cons(TBool(x), t))

defs.name: record
defs.ty: forall e0 a. ((Unit) -> a ! {IO, e0}) -> (a, List(Replay@TraceEntry)) ! {IO, e0}
defs.source:
fn record(action) =
  let g =
    handle action(()) with
      con_read_int() resume k => \(t) -> rec_int(k, t, prim_read_int())
      con_read_line() resume k => \(t) -> rec_str(k, t, prim_read_line())
      fs_read_file(p) resume k => \(t) -> rec_str(k, t, prim_read_file(p))
      fs_read_bytes(p) resume k => \(t) -> rec_bytes(k, t, prim_read_bytes(p))
      fs_file_exists(p) resume k => \(t) -> rec_bool(k, t, prim_file_exists(p))
      rng_rand() resume k => \(t) -> rec_int(k, t, prim_rand())
      env_get(s) resume k => \(t) -> rec_str(k, t, prim_getenv(s))
      env_argc() resume k => \(t) -> rec_int(k, t, prim_args_count())
      env_arg(i) resume k => \(t) -> rec_str(k, t, prim_arg(i))
      return r => \(t) -> (r, reverse(t))
  g(Nil)
defs.doc:
Run `action` against the real world, logging every capability observation (console, file, random, and environment reads) into a trace. Returns `(result, trace)`; feed the trace to `replay` to reproduce the run without IO.

```prism,no_run
record(\(u) -> rng_rand() + rng_rand())
```

defs.name: rep_int
defs.ty: forall e0 a. ((Int) -> (List(Replay@TraceEntry)) -> a ! {Fail, e0} ! {Fail, e0}, List(Replay@TraceEntry)) -> a ! {Fail, e0}
defs.source:
fn rep_int(k, t) =
  match t of
    Cons(TInt(x), rest) => k(x)(rest)
    _ => fail()

defs.name: rep_str
defs.ty: forall e0 a. ((String) -> (List(Replay@TraceEntry)) -> a ! {Fail, e0} ! {Fail, e0}, List(Replay@TraceEntry)) -> a ! {Fail, e0}
defs.source:
fn rep_str(k, t) =
  match t of
    Cons(TStr(x), rest) => k(x)(rest)
    _ => fail()

defs.name: buf_of_hex
defs.source:
fn buf_of_hex(s) =
  match hex_decode(s) of
    Some(bs) => bytes_buf(bs)
    None => fail()

defs.name: rep_bytes
defs.ty: forall e0 a. ((Buf) -> (List(Replay@TraceEntry)) -> a ! {Fail, e0} ! {Fail, e0}, List(Replay@TraceEntry)) -> a ! {Fail, e0}
defs.source:
fn rep_bytes(k, t) =
  match t of
    Cons(TStr(s), rest) => k(buf_of_hex(s))(rest)
    _ => fail()

defs.name: rep_bool
defs.ty: forall e0 a. ((Bool) -> (List(Replay@TraceEntry)) -> a ! {Fail, e0} ! {Fail, e0}, List(Replay@TraceEntry)) -> a ! {Fail, e0}
defs.source:
fn rep_bool(k, t) =
  match t of
    Cons(TBool(x), rest) => k(x)(rest)
    _ => fail()

defs.name: replay
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (List(Replay@TraceEntry), (Unit) -> a ! {Fail, e0}) -> a ! {Fail, e0}
defs.source:
fn replay(trace, action) =
  let g =
    handle action(()) with
      con_read_int() resume k => \(t) -> rep_int(k, t)
      con_read_line() resume k => \(t) -> rep_str(k, t)
      fs_read_file(p) resume k => \(t) -> rep_str(k, t)
      fs_read_bytes(p) resume k => \(t) -> rep_bytes(k, t)
      fs_file_exists(p) resume k => \(t) -> rep_bool(k, t)
      rng_rand() resume k => \(t) -> rep_int(k, t)
      env_get(s) resume k => \(t) -> rep_str(k, t)
      env_argc() resume k => \(t) -> rep_int(k, t)
      env_arg(i) resume k => \(t) -> rep_str(k, t)
      out_print(x) resume k => \(t) -> k(())(t)
      out_println(x) resume k => \(t) -> k(())(t)
      return r => \(_t) -> r
  g(trace)
defs.doc:
Re-run `action` against a recorded `trace`, performing no real IO: each capability read is served from the trace and output is dropped, reproducing the original result. Fails if the trace does not match the action.

```prism,no_run
let (first, trace) = record(\(u) -> rng_rand())
replay(trace, \(u) -> rng_rand()) == first
```

defs.name: enc_field
defs.source:
fn enc_field(tag, payload) =
  concat(tag, concat(show_int(str_len(payload)), concat(":", payload)))

defs.name: enc_entry
defs.source:
fn enc_entry(e) =
  match e of
    TInt(n) => enc_field("I", show_int(n))
    TStr(s) => enc_field("S", s)
    TBool(b) => enc_field("B", if b then "1" else "0")
    TOut => enc_field("O", "")

defs.name: serialize
defs.source: fn serialize(trace) = str_join("", map(enc_entry, trace))
defs.doc:
Encode a trace to a self-delimiting string for durable storage, read back with `deserialize`.

```prism,no_run
let (r, trace) = record(\(u) -> rng_rand())
write_file("run.trace", serialize(trace))
```

defs.name: un_int
defs.source:
fn un_int(o) =
  match o of
    Some(x) => x
    None => 0

defs.name: de_entry
defs.source:
fn de_entry(tag, payload) =
  if str_eq(tag, "I") then
    TInt(un_int(parse_int(payload)))
  elif str_eq(tag, "B") then
    TBool(str_eq(payload, "1"))
  elif str_eq(tag, "O") then
    TOut
  else
    TStr(payload)

defs.name: de_go
deserialize
defs.source: fn deserialize(s) = de_go(s, 0, char_at(":", 0))
defs.doc:
Decode a trace produced by `serialize`; `deserialize(serialize(t))` is `t`.

The frames are self-delimiting (tag, length, `:`, payload), so the encoding round-trips through text:

```prism
serialize(deserialize("I2:42S3:abc"))
```

```output
I2:42S3:abc
```

defs.name: persist_entry
defs.source: fn persist_entry(path, e) = append_file(path, enc_entry(e))

defs.name: step_int
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (String, (Int) -> (List(Replay@TraceEntry)) -> a ! {Fail, IO, e0} ! {Fail, IO, e0}, List(Replay@TraceEntry), (Unit) -> Int ! {Fail, IO, e0}) -> a ! {Fail, IO, e0}
defs.source:
fn step_int(path, k, t, real) =
  match t of
    Cons(TInt(x), rest) => k(x)(rest)
    Cons(_, _) => fail()
    Nil =>
      let x = real(())
      persist_entry(path, TInt(x))
      k(x)(Nil)

defs.name: step_str
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (String, (String) -> (List(Replay@TraceEntry)) -> a ! {Fail, IO, e0} ! {Fail, IO, e0}, List(Replay@TraceEntry), (Unit) -> String ! {Fail, IO, e0}) -> a ! {Fail, IO, e0}
defs.source:
fn step_str(path, k, t, real) =
  match t of
    Cons(TStr(x), rest) => k(x)(rest)
    Cons(_, _) => fail()
    Nil =>
      let x = real(())
      persist_entry(path, TStr(x))
      k(x)(Nil)

defs.name: step_bytes
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (String, (Buf) -> (List(Replay@TraceEntry)) -> a ! {Fail, IO, e0} ! {Fail, IO, e0}, List(Replay@TraceEntry), (Unit) -> Buf ! {Fail, IO, e0}) -> a ! {Fail, IO, e0}
defs.source:
fn step_bytes(path, k, t, real) =
  match t of
    Cons(TStr(s), rest) => k(buf_of_hex(s))(rest)
    Cons(_, _) => fail()
    Nil =>
      let buf = real(())
      persist_entry(path, TStr(hex_encode(bytes_of_buf(buf))))
      k(buf)(Nil)

defs.name: step_bool
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (String, (Bool) -> (List(Replay@TraceEntry)) -> a ! {Fail, IO, e0} ! {Fail, IO, e0}, List(Replay@TraceEntry), (Unit) -> Bool ! {Fail, IO, e0}) -> a ! {Fail, IO, e0}
defs.source:
fn step_bool(path, k, t, real) =
  match t of
    Cons(TBool(x), rest) => k(x)(rest)
    Cons(_, _) => fail()
    Nil =>
      let x = real(())
      persist_entry(path, TBool(x))
      k(x)(Nil)

defs.name: out_step
defs.ty: forall e0 a b. (String, (Unit) -> (List(Replay@TraceEntry)) -> a ! {Fail, IO, e0} ! {Fail, IO, e0}, List(Replay@TraceEntry), (Unit) -> b ! {Fail, IO, e0}) -> a ! {Fail, IO, e0}
defs.source:
fn out_step(path, k, t, real) =
  match t of
    Cons(TOut, rest) => k(())(rest)
    Cons(_, _) => fail()
    Nil =>
      persist_entry(path, TOut)
      real(())
      k(())(Nil)

defs.name: durable
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (String, (Unit) -> a ! {Fail, IO, e0}) -> a ! {Fail, IO, e0}
defs.source:
fn durable(path, action) =
  let loaded =
    if prim_file_exists(path) then
      deserialize(prim_read_file(path))
    else
      Nil
  let g =
    handle action(()) with
      con_read_int() resume k =>
        \(t) -> step_int(path, k, t, \(_z) -> prim_read_int())
      con_read_line() resume k =>
        \(t) -> step_str(path, k, t, \(_z) -> prim_read_line())
      fs_read_file(p) resume k =>
        \(t) -> step_str(path, k, t, \(_z) -> prim_read_file(p))
      fs_read_bytes(p) resume k =>
        \(t) -> step_bytes(path, k, t, \(_z) -> prim_read_bytes(p))
      fs_file_exists(p) resume k =>
        \(t) -> step_bool(path, k, t, \(_z) -> prim_file_exists(p))
      rng_rand() resume k => \(t) -> step_int(path, k, t, \(_z) -> prim_rand())
      env_get(s) resume k =>
        \(t) -> step_str(path, k, t, \(_z) -> prim_getenv(s))
      env_argc() resume k =>
        \(t) -> step_int(path, k, t, \(_z) -> prim_args_count())
      env_arg(i) resume k => \(t) -> step_str(path, k, t, \(_z) -> prim_arg(i))
      out_print(x) resume k =>
        \(t) -> out_step(path, k, t, \(_z) -> prim_print(x))
      out_println(x) resume k =>
        \(t) -> out_step(path, k, t, \(_z) -> prim_println(x))
      return r => \(_t) -> r
  g(loaded)
defs.doc:
Durable record/replay against a persisted log at `path`: replay the recorded prefix with no real IO, then perform each new observation for real, appending a frame per observation so an interrupted run resumes where it left off, exactly once at the crash boundary.

```prism,no_run
durable("target/run.log", \(u) -> rng_rand() + rng_rand())
```

defs.name: Step
defs.source: type Step(a) = SDone | SMore(a, (Unit) -> Step(a))

defs.name: empty
defs.source: fn empty() : (Unit) -> Step(a) = \(u) -> SDone
defs.doc:
The empty sequence: yields nothing.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.to_list(Seq.empty())
```

```output
[]
```

defs.name: singleton
defs.source: fn singleton(x : a) : (Unit) -> Step(a) = \(u) -> SMore(x, \(v) -> SDone)
defs.doc:
The one-element sequence yielding `x`.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.to_list(Seq.singleton(42))
```

```output
[42]
```

defs.name: range
defs.source:
fn range(lo : Int, hi : Int) : (Unit) -> Step(Int) =
  \(u) -> if lo < hi then SMore(lo, range(lo + 1, hi)) else SDone
defs.doc:
The ascending integers in `[lo, hi)`. Self-recursive: the continuation is the next `range`, so no element is built until pulled.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.to_list(Seq.range(1, 5))
```

```output
[1, 2, 3, 4]
```

defs.name: from_list
defs.source:
fn from_list(xs : List(a)) : (Unit) -> Step(a) =
  \(u) -> match xs of { Nil => SDone, Cons(x, rest) => SMore(x, from_list(rest)) }
defs.doc:
The container boundary in: the elements of list `xs`, in order.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.to_list(Seq.from_list([1, 2, 3]))
```

```output
[1, 2, 3]
```

defs.name: iterate
defs.source:
fn iterate(x : a, f : (a) -> a) : (Unit) -> Step(a) =
  \(u) -> SMore(x, iterate(f(x), f))
defs.doc:
The infinite sequence `x, f(x), f(f(x)), ...`. Bound it with `take`.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.to_list(Seq.take(Seq.iterate(1, \(x) -> x * 2), 4))
```

```output
[1, 2, 4, 8]
```

defs.name: repeat
defs.source: fn repeat(x : a) : (Unit) -> Step(a) = \(u) -> SMore(x, repeat(x))
defs.doc:
The infinite sequence of `x` repeated. Bound it with `take`.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.to_list(Seq.take(Seq.repeat(7), 3))
```

```output
[7, 7, 7]
```

defs.name: unfold
defs.ty: forall a b. (a, (a) -> Option((b, a))) -> (Unit) -> Sequence.Step(b)
defs.source:
fn unfold(seed : s, step : (s) -> Option((a, s))) : (Unit) -> Step(a) =
  \(u) -> match step(seed) of { None => SDone, Some(pair) => match pair of { (x, seed2) => SMore(x, unfold(seed2, step)) } }
defs.doc:
The generator producer: yield `x` for each `Some((x, seed'))` that `step` returns from the running seed, stopping at `None`. Every finite producer is a special case; on pull `Step` a generator is just a fold over the seed, needing no coroutine or handler.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.to_list(Seq.unfold(1, \(n) -> if n <= 3 then Some((n, n + 1)) else None))
```

```output
[1, 2, 3]
```

defs.name: map
defs.ty: forall a b. ((Unit) -> Sequence.Step(a), (a) -> b) -> (Unit) -> Sequence.Step(b)
defs.source:
fn map(s : (Unit) -> Step(a), f : (a) -> b) : (Unit) -> Step(b) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => SMore(f(x), map(next, f)) }
defs.doc:
Apply `f` to every element. Type-changing: `Seq(a) -> Seq(b)`.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.to_list(Seq.map(Seq.range(1, 4), \(x) -> x * x))
```

```output
[1, 4, 9]
```

defs.name: filter
defs.source:
fn filter(s : (Unit) -> Step(a), p : (a) -> Bool) : (Unit) -> Step(a) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => if p(x) then SMore(x, filter(next, p)) else filter(next, p)(()) }
defs.doc:
Keep only the elements satisfying `p`.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.to_list(Seq.filter(Seq.range(1, 7), \(x) -> mod(x, 2) == 0))
```

```output
[2, 4, 6]
```

defs.name: filter_map
defs.ty: forall a b. ((Unit) -> Sequence.Step(a), (a) -> Option(b)) -> (Unit) -> Sequence.Step(b)
defs.source:
fn filter_map(s : (Unit) -> Step(a), f : (a) -> Option(b)) : (Unit) -> Step(b) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => match f(x) of { None => filter_map(next, f)(()), Some(y) => SMore(y, filter_map(next, f)) } }
defs.doc:
Map and filter in one pass: yield `y` for each `f(x) == Some(y)`, dropping the `None`s.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.to_list(Seq.filter_map(Seq.range(1, 5), \(x) -> if x > 2 then Some(x * 10) else None))
```

```output
[30, 40]
```

defs.name: append
defs.source:
fn append(s : (Unit) -> Step(a), t : (Unit) -> Step(a)) : (Unit) -> Step(a) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => t(()), SMore(x, next) => SMore(x, append(next, t)) }
defs.doc:
Concatenate two sequences: all of `s`, then all of `t`.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.to_list(Seq.append(Seq.range(1, 3), Seq.range(10, 12)))
```

```output
[1, 2, 10, 11]
```

defs.name: flat_map
defs.ty: forall a b. ((Unit) -> Sequence.Step(a), (a) -> (Unit) -> Sequence.Step(b)) -> (Unit) -> Sequence.Step(b)
defs.doc:
For each element `x`, splice in the sequence `f(x)`.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.to_list(Seq.flat_map(Seq.range(1, 4), \(x) -> Seq.range(0, x)))
```

```output
[0, 0, 1, 0, 1, 2]
```

defs.name: take
defs.source:
fn take(s : (Unit) -> Step(a), n : Int) : (Unit) -> Step(a) =
  \(u) -> if n <= 0 then SDone else match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => SMore(x, take(next, n - 1)) }
defs.doc:
The first `n` elements, stopping the producer once the budget is spent.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.to_list(Seq.take(Seq.range(1, 100), 3))
```

```output
[1, 2, 3]
```

defs.name: drop
defs.source:
fn drop(s : (Unit) -> Step(a), n : Int) : (Unit) -> Step(a) =
  \(u) -> if n <= 0 then s(()) else match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => drop(next, n - 1)(()) }
defs.doc:
Skip the first `n` elements, yielding the rest.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.to_list(Seq.drop(Seq.range(1, 6), 2))
```

```output
[3, 4, 5]
```

defs.name: take_while
defs.source:
fn take_while(s : (Unit) -> Step(a), p : (a) -> Bool) : (Unit) -> Step(a) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => if p(x) then SMore(x, take_while(next, p)) else SDone }
defs.doc:
The longest prefix whose elements satisfy `p`; stops at the first failure.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.to_list(Seq.take_while(Seq.range(1, 10), \(x) -> x < 4))
```

```output
[1, 2, 3]
```

defs.name: drop_while
defs.source:
fn drop_while(s : (Unit) -> Step(a), p : (a) -> Bool) : (Unit) -> Step(a) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => if p(x) then drop_while(next, p)(()) else SMore(x, next) }
defs.doc:
Drop the longest prefix satisfying `p`, yielding the rest.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.to_list(Seq.drop_while(Seq.range(1, 6), \(x) -> x < 3))
```

```output
[3, 4, 5]
```

defs.name: dedup
defs.source:
fn dedup(s) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => SMore(x, dedup_after(x, next)) }
defs.doc:
Drop consecutive duplicates, keeping the first of each run (needs `Eq(a)`). Left unsigned so the `Eq(a)` constraint is inferred from `==`.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.to_list(Seq.dedup(Seq.from_list([1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3])))
```

```output
[1, 2, 3]
```

defs.name: dedup_after
defs.source:
fn dedup_after(prev, s) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => if x == prev then dedup_after(prev, next)(()) else SMore(x, dedup_after(x, next)) }
defs.doc: Helper for `dedup`: drop elements equal to the just-emitted `prev`.

defs.name: enumerate
defs.source:
fn enumerate(s : (Unit) -> Step(a)) : (Unit) -> Step((Int, a)) =
  enumerate_from(s, 0)
defs.doc:
Pair each element with its zero-based index, yielding `(i, x)`.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.to_list(Seq.enumerate(Seq.from_list(["a", "b"])))
```

```output
[(0, a), (1, b)]
```

defs.name: enumerate_from
defs.ty: forall a. ((Unit) -> Sequence.Step(a), Int) -> (Unit) -> Sequence.Step((Int, a))
defs.source:
fn enumerate_from(s, i) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => SMore((i, x), enumerate_from(next, i + 1)) }
defs.doc: Helper for `enumerate`: index from `i`.

defs.name: scan
defs.ty: forall a b. ((Unit) -> Sequence.Step(a), b, (b, a) -> b) -> (Unit) -> Sequence.Step(b)
defs.source:
fn scan(s : (Unit) -> Step(a), z : b, f : (b, a) -> b) : (Unit) -> Step(b) =
  \(u) -> SMore(z, scan_go(s, z, f))
defs.doc:
The running left-fold, streamed: yield `z`, then each successive accumulator.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.to_list(Seq.scan(Seq.range(1, 4), 0, \(acc, x) -> acc + x))
```

```output
[0, 1, 3, 6]
```

defs.name: scan_go
defs.ty: forall a b. ((Unit) -> Sequence.Step(b), a, (a, b) -> a) -> (Unit) -> Sequence.Step(a)
defs.source:
fn scan_go(s, z, f) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => let z2 = f(z, x) in SMore(z2, scan_go(next, z2, f)) }
defs.doc: Helper for `scan`: yield the accumulator after each element.

defs.name: interleave
defs.doc:
Alternate elements of `s` and `t` (`s0, t0, s1, t1, ...`); when one runs out, yield the whole remainder of the other. Streamed, no materialization.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.to_list(Seq.interleave(Seq.range(1, 4), Seq.range(10, 12)))
```

```output
[1, 10, 2, 11, 3]
```

defs.name: zip
defs.ty: forall a b. ((Unit) -> Sequence.Step(a), (Unit) -> Sequence.Step(b)) -> (Unit) -> Sequence.Step((a, b))
defs.source:
fn zip(s : (Unit) -> Step(a), t : (Unit) -> Step(b)) : (Unit) -> Step((a, b)) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, sn) => match t(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(y, tn) => SMore((x, y), zip(sn, tn)) } }
defs.doc:
Pair two sequences element-wise, stopping at the shorter. Genuinely heterogeneous: `Seq(a)` and `Seq(b)` yield `Seq((a, b))`.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.to_list(Seq.zip(Seq.range(1, 4), Seq.from_list(["a", "b", "c"])))
```

```output
[(1, a), (2, b), (3, c)]
```

defs.name: zip_with
defs.ty: forall a b c. ((Unit) -> Sequence.Step(a), (Unit) -> Sequence.Step(b), (a, b) -> c) -> (Unit) -> Sequence.Step(c)
defs.doc:
Combine two sequences element-wise with `f`, stopping when either runs out. Heterogeneous in both operand types.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.to_list(Seq.zip_with(Seq.range(1, 4), Seq.range(10, 13), \(a, b) -> a + b))
```

```output
[11, 13, 15]
```

defs.name: chunk
defs.source:
fn chunk(s : (Unit) -> Step(a), n : Int) : (Unit) -> Step(List(a)) =
  \(u) -> match s(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => match chunk_grab(next, n - 1, Cons(x, Nil)) of { (group, rest) => SMore(group, chunk(rest, n)) } }
defs.doc:
Group elements into consecutive lists of length `n` (the final chunk may be shorter). Pulls one group at a time, holding only the current group.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.to_list(Seq.chunk(Seq.range(1, 6), 2))
```

```output
[[1, 2], [3, 4], [5]]
```

defs.name: chunk_grab
defs.ty: forall a. ((Unit) -> Sequence.Step(a), Int, List(a)) -> (List(a), (Unit) -> Sequence.Step(a))
defs.source:
fn chunk_grab(s, n, acc) =
  if n <= 0 then
    (reverse(acc), s)
  else
    match s(()) of
      SDone => (reverse(acc), empty())
      SMore(x, next) => chunk_grab(next, n - 1, Cons(x, acc))
defs.doc: Helper for `chunk`: grab up to `n` more elements into the reversed `acc`, returning the finished (forward-order) group and the remaining sequence.

defs.name: window
defs.source:
fn window(s : (Unit) -> Step(a), n : Int) : (Unit) -> Step(List(a)) =
  \(u) -> match grab_n(s, n, Nil) of { None => SDone, Some(pair) => match pair of { (buf, rest) => SMore(buf, window_slide(buf, rest)) } }
defs.doc:
Every contiguous length-`n` sliding window, in order. Fewer than `n` elements yields nothing. Holds one window (`n` elements) at a time.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.to_list(Seq.window(Seq.range(1, 5), 2))
```

```output
[[1, 2], [2, 3], [3, 4]]
```

defs.name: grab_n
defs.ty: forall a. ((Unit) -> Sequence.Step(a), Int, List(a)) -> Option((List(a), (Unit) -> Sequence.Step(a)))
defs.source:
fn grab_n(s, n, acc) =
  if n <= 0 then
    Some((reverse(acc), s))
  else
    match s(()) of
      SDone => None
      SMore(x, next) => grab_n(next, n - 1, Cons(x, acc))
defs.doc: Helper for `window`: pull exactly `n` elements, or `None` if fewer remain.

defs.name: window_slide
defs.source:
fn window_slide(buf, rest) =
  \(u) -> match rest(()) of { SDone => SDone, SMore(x, next) => let buf2 = app_list(tail(buf), Cons(x, Nil)) in SMore(buf2, window_slide(buf2, next)) }
defs.doc: Helper for `window`: slide by dropping the oldest element and appending the next one pulled from `rest`.

defs.name: app_list
defs.source:
fn app_list(xs, ys) =
  match xs of
    Nil => ys
    Cons(x, r) => Cons(x, app_list(r, ys))
defs.doc: Local list append (`append` names the sequence combinator above).

defs.name: fold
defs.ty: forall a b. ((Unit) -> Sequence.Step(b), a, (a, b) -> a) -> a
defs.source:
fn fold(s, z, f) =
  match s(()) of
    SDone => z
    SMore(x, next) => fold(next, f(z, x), f)
defs.doc:
Left-fold the sequence with `f` from initial accumulator `z`.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.fold(Seq.range(1, 5), 0, \(acc, x) -> acc + x)
```

```output
10
```

defs.name: for_each
defs.ty: forall e0 a. ((Unit) -> Sequence.Step(a), (a) -> Unit ! {e0}) -> Unit ! {e0}
defs.source:
fn for_each(s : (Unit) -> Step(a), f : (a) -> Unit ! {| e}) =
  match s(()) of
    SDone => ()
    SMore(x, next) =>
      f(x)
      for_each(next, f)
defs.doc:
Run `f` for its effects on each element, in order. Effect-polymorphic: `f` runs in the ambient row (no handler intervenes), so `for_each(s, \(x) -> println(x))` threads `IO` out. The explicit `{| e}` row matters: unsigned, the self-recursion would infer `f` as pure and reject an effectful body.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.for_each(Seq.range(1, 4), \(x) -> println(show(x)))
```

```output
1
2
3
```

defs.name: sum
defs.source: fn sum(s) = fold(s, 0, \(acc, x) -> acc + x)
defs.doc:
Sum a sequence of integers.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.sum(Seq.range(1, 5))
```

```output
10
```

defs.name: product
defs.source: fn product(s) = fold(s, 1, \(acc, x) -> acc * x)
defs.doc:
Product of a sequence of integers.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.product(Seq.range(1, 5))
```

```output
24
```

defs.name: count
defs.source: fn count(s) = fold(s, 0, \(acc, x) -> acc + 1)
defs.doc:
The number of elements.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.count(Seq.range(1, 100))
```

```output
99
```

defs.name: to_list
defs.source: fn to_list(s) = reverse(fold(s, Nil, \(acc, x) -> Cons(x, acc)))
defs.doc:
Collect the sequence into a list, in order. The container boundary out.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.to_list(Seq.map(Seq.range(1, 4), \(x) -> x + 100))
```

```output
[101, 102, 103]
```

defs.name: head
defs.source:
fn head(s) =
  match s(()) of
    SDone => None
    SMore(x, next) => Some(x)
defs.doc:
The first element, or `None` if the sequence is empty.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.head(Seq.range(5, 10))
```

```output
Some(5)
```

defs.name: find
defs.source:
fn find(s, p) =
  match s(()) of
    SDone => None
    SMore(x, next) =>
      if p(x) then
        Some(x)
      else
        find(next, p)
defs.doc:
The first element satisfying `p`, or `None`; stops the producer at the match.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.find(Seq.range(1, 100), \(x) -> x > 10)
```

```output
Some(11)
```

defs.name: any
defs.source:
fn any(s, p) =
  match find(s, p) of
    Some(u) => true
    None => false
defs.doc:
True when some element satisfies `p`; short-circuits.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.any(Seq.range(1, 5), \(x) -> x == 3)
```

```output
true
```

defs.name: all
defs.source:
fn all(s, p) =
  match find(s, \(x) -> not(p(x))) of
    Some(u) => false
    None => true
defs.doc:
True when every element satisfies `p`; short-circuits on the first failure.

```prism
# import Sequence as Seq
Seq.all(Seq.range(1, 5), \(x) -> x < 10)
```

```output
true
```

defs.name: from_bytes
defs.source: fn from_bytes(bs : Bytes) : (Unit) -> Step(Int) = from_bytes_at(bs, 0)
defs.doc: The bytes of `bs` as a sequence of ints in `0..255`, in order.

defs.name: from_bytes_at
defs.source:
fn from_bytes_at(bs, i) =
  \(u) -> if i < bytes_length(bs) then SMore(bytes_index(bs, i), from_bytes_at(bs, i + 1)) else SDone
defs.doc: Helper for `from_bytes`: yield from index `i`.

defs.name: to_bytes
defs.source: fn to_bytes(s) = fold(s, bytes_empty, \(acc, x) -> bytes_push(acc, x))
defs.doc: Collect a sequence of ints (each masked to a byte) into a `Bytes`. The Bytes container boundary out.

defs.name: teleport
defs.source: fn teleport(f : (() -> a) @ {once, portable}) : a = f()
defs.doc:
Run a portable, single-use closure as a mobile unit.

A closure over top-level code and scalar arguments satisfies the contract, and running it through `teleport` is indistinguishable from calling it:

```prism
teleport(\() -> 6 * 7)
```

```output
42
```

Capturing a local binding is refused at compile time: a local does not travel, so the closure could not move to a fresh runtime:

```prism,compile_fail
let n = 6
teleport(\() -> n * 7)
```

defs.name: Arbitrary
defs.source:
class Arbitrary(a)
  arbitrary : (Int) -> a ! {Random | e}
defs.doc: A structural generator, sized by a fuel budget. `deriving (Arbitrary)` spends the budget on depth: at each recursive constructor it draws its fields a size smaller, and once the budget runs out it restricts to non-recursive constructors, so generation always terminates.

defs.name: arb_gen
defs.source: fn arb_gen() : Gen(a) given Arbitrary(a) = Gen(\(size) -> arbitrary(size))
defs.doc:
The generator of an `Arbitrary` type, as a `Quickcheck.Gen` ready for `quickcheck`/`gen_at`.

```prism,no_run
# import Quickcheck (..)
fn prop(xs : List(Int)) : Bool = reverse(reverse(xs)) == xs

fn main() = println(passed(quickcheck(arb_gen(), prop)))
```

defs.name: arbitraryInt
defs.source:
instance arbitraryInt : Arbitrary(Int)
  fn arbitrary(size) = gen_run(gen_int, size)

defs.name: arbitraryI64
defs.source:
instance arbitraryI64 : Arbitrary(I64)
  fn arbitrary(size) = gen_run(gen_i64, size)

defs.name: arbitraryU64
defs.source:
instance arbitraryU64 : Arbitrary(U64)
  fn arbitrary(size) = gen_run(gen_u64, size)

defs.name: arbitraryBool
defs.source:
instance arbitraryBool : Arbitrary(Bool)
  fn arbitrary(size) = gen_run(gen_bool, size)

defs.name: arbitraryUnit
defs.source:
instance arbitraryUnit : Arbitrary(Unit)
  fn arbitrary(_size) = ()

defs.name: arbitraryChar
defs.source:
instance arbitraryChar : Arbitrary(Char)
  fn arbitrary(size) = gen_run(gen_char, size)

defs.name: arbitraryFloat
defs.source:
instance arbitraryFloat : Arbitrary(Float)
  fn arbitrary(size) = gen_run(gen_float, size)

defs.name: arbitraryString
defs.source:
instance arbitraryString : Arbitrary(String)
  fn arbitrary(size) = gen_run(gen_string, size)

defs.name: arbitraryOption
defs.source:
instance arbitraryOption : Arbitrary(Option(a)) given Arbitrary(a)
  fn arbitrary(size) = gen_run(gen_option(Gen(\(s) -> arbitrary(s))), size)

defs.name: arbitraryList
defs.source:
instance arbitraryList : Arbitrary(List(a)) given Arbitrary(a)
  fn arbitrary(size) = gen_run(gen_list(Gen(\(s) -> arbitrary(s))), size)

defs.name: nanos_per_sec
defs.source: fn nanos_per_sec() : Int = 1000000000
defs.doc:
Nanoseconds in one second (the `Duration` scale factor for `seconds`).

```prism
nanos_per_sec()
```

```output
1000000000
```

defs.name: nanos_per_milli
defs.source: fn nanos_per_milli() : Int = 1000000
defs.doc: Nanoseconds in one millisecond.

defs.name: nanos_per_micro
defs.source: fn nanos_per_micro() : Int = 1000
defs.doc: Nanoseconds in one microsecond.

defs.name: secs_per_day
defs.source: fn secs_per_day() : Int = 86400

defs.name: secs_per_hour
defs.source: fn secs_per_hour() : Int = 3600

defs.name: secs_per_min
defs.source: fn secs_per_min() : Int = 60

defs.name: Duration
defs.source: type Duration = Duration(Int)
defs.doc: A signed span of time, in nanoseconds.

defs.name: dur_nanos
defs.doc:
The span in whole nanoseconds.

```prism
dur_nanos(seconds(2))
```

```output
2000000000
```

defs.name: nanos
defs.source: fn nanos(n : Int) : Duration = Duration(n)
defs.doc: A duration of `n` nanoseconds.

defs.name: micros
defs.source: fn micros(n : Int) : Duration = Duration(n * nanos_per_micro())
defs.doc:
A duration of `n` microseconds.

```prism
dur_nanos(micros(3))
```

```output
3000
```

defs.name: millis
defs.source: fn millis(n : Int) : Duration = Duration(n * nanos_per_milli())
defs.doc: A duration of `n` milliseconds.

defs.name: seconds
defs.source: fn seconds(n : Int) : Duration = Duration(n * nanos_per_sec())
defs.doc:
A duration of `n` seconds.

```prism
dur_nanos(seconds(1))
```

```output
1000000000
```

defs.name: minutes
defs.source: fn minutes(n : Int) : Duration = Duration(n * nanos_per_sec() * secs_per_min())
defs.doc:
A duration of `n` minutes.

```prism
dur_as_secs(minutes(2))
```

```output
120
```

defs.name: hours
defs.source: fn hours(n : Int) : Duration = Duration(n * nanos_per_sec() * secs_per_hour())
defs.doc:
A duration of `n` hours.

```prism
dur_as_secs(hours(1))
```

```output
3600
```

defs.name: dur_as_secs
defs.source: fn dur_as_secs(d : Duration) : Int = dur_nanos(d) / nanos_per_sec()
defs.doc:
The whole-second part of a duration (truncated toward zero).

```prism
dur_as_secs(dur_add(seconds(90), millis(500)))
```

```output
90
```

defs.name: dur_as_millis
defs.source: fn dur_as_millis(d : Duration) : Int = dur_nanos(d) / nanos_per_milli()
defs.doc:
The whole-millisecond part of a duration (truncated toward zero).

```prism
dur_as_millis(seconds(2))
```

```output
2000
```

defs.name: dur_add
defs.source:
fn dur_add(a : Duration, b : Duration) : Duration =
  Duration(dur_nanos(a) + dur_nanos(b))
defs.doc:
Sum of two durations.

```prism
dur_nanos(dur_add(seconds(1), millis(500)))
```

```output
1500000000
```

defs.name: dur_sub
defs.source:
fn dur_sub(a : Duration, b : Duration) : Duration =
  Duration(dur_nanos(a) - dur_nanos(b))
defs.doc:
Difference of two durations (`a - b`).

```prism
dur_nanos(dur_sub(seconds(2), millis(500)))
```

```output
1500000000
```

defs.name: dur_scale
defs.source: fn dur_scale(a : Duration, k : Int) : Duration = Duration(dur_nanos(a) * k)
defs.doc:
A duration scaled by an integer factor.

```prism
dur_nanos(dur_scale(seconds(1), 3))
```

```output
3000000000
```

defs.name: dur_negate
defs.source: fn dur_negate(a : Duration) : Duration = Duration(0 - dur_nanos(a))
defs.doc:
A duration with the sign flipped.

```prism
dur_nanos(dur_negate(seconds(1)))
```

```output
-1000000000
```

defs.name: dur_cmp
defs.doc:
Ordering of two durations (`-1`, `0`, `1`).


defs.name: run_clock_real
defs.ty: forall e0 a. (() -> a ! {Concurrent.Clock, IO, e0}) -> a ! {IO, e0}
defs.source:
fn run_clock_real(action : () -> a ! {Clock | e}) : a =
  let g =
    handle action() with
      now() resume k => \(t) -> k(t)(t)
      sleep(d) resume k => \(t) -> k(())(t + d)
      wall_now() resume k => \(t) -> k(prim_wall_now())(t)
      mono_now() resume k => \(t) -> k(prim_mono_now())(t)
      return r => \(_t) -> r
  g(0)
defs.doc:
Run `action` against the real OS clock. `now`/`sleep` still thread a virtual counter (they are the scheduler's logical time), so this is a superset of `run_clock`: `wall_now` and `mono_now` read the real clock through the `prim_*` builtins, each a recorded observation, and everything else stays virtual.

```prism,no_run
run_clock_real(\() -> wall_unix_secs(wall_clock()))
```

defs.name: days_from_civil
defs.source:
fn days_from_civil(y : Int, m : Int, d : Int) : Int =
  let yy =
    if m <= 2 then
      y - 1
    else
      y
  let era = yy / 400
  let yoe = yy - era * 400
  let mp =
    if m > 2 then
      m - 3
    else
      m + 9
  let doy = (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + d - 1
  let doe = yoe * 365 + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100 + doy
  era * 146097 + doe - 719468

defs.name: civil_from_days
defs.source:
fn civil_from_days(z0 : Int) : (Int, Int, Int) =
  let z = z0 + 719468
  let era = z / 146097
  let doe = z - era * 146097
  let yoe = (doe - doe / 1460 + doe / 36524 - doe / 146096) / 365
  let y = yoe + era * 400
  let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100)
  let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153
  let d = doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1
  let m =
    if mp < 10 then
      mp + 3
    else
      mp - 9
  let year =
    if m <= 2 then
      y + 1
    else
      y
  (year, m, d)

defs.source:
fn parse_frac(s : String, i : Int) : (Int, Int) =
  if char_is(s, i, 46) then
    frac_go(s, i + 1, 0, 0)
  else
    (0, i)

defs.source:
fn frac_go(s : String, i : Int, seen : Int, acc : Int) : (Int, Int) =
  if i < str_len(s) && is_digit(char_at(s, i)) then
    let acc2 =
      if seen < 9 then
        acc * 10 + char_at(s, i) - 48
      else
        acc
    frac_go(s, i + 1, seen + 1, acc2)
  else
    (scale_frac(acc, min(seen, 9)), i)

defs.source:

  if d >= 9 then
    acc
  else

defs.name: parse_zone
defs.source:
fn parse_zone(s : String, i : Int) : Option(Int) =
  if char_is(s, i, 90) && i + 1 == str_len(s) then
    Some(0)
  elif ((char_is(s, i, 43) || char_is(s, i, 45))
      && i + 6 == str_len(s)
      && char_is(s, i + 3, 58)) then
    match (digits(s, i + 1, 2), digits(s, i + 4, 2)) of
      (Some(oh), Some(om)) =>
        let mag = oh * secs_per_hour() + om * secs_per_min()
        if char_is(s, i, 43) then
          Some(mag)
        else
          Some(0 - mag)
      _ => None
  else
    None

defs.source: fn in_range(x : Int, lo : Int, hi : Int) : Bool = x >= lo && x <= hi

defs.name: parse_rfc3339
defs.source:
fn parse_rfc3339(s : String) : Option(Wall) =
  if str_len(s) < 20 then
    None
  elif (not(char_is(s, 4, 45) && char_is(s, 7, 45) && char_is(s, 10, 84))) then
    None
  elif not(char_is(s, 13, 58) && char_is(s, 16, 58)) then
    None
  else
    match ((
          digits(s, 0, 4),
          digits(s, 5, 2),
          digits(s, 8, 2),
          digits(s, 11, 2),
          digits(s, 14, 2),
          digits(s, 17, 2),
        )) of
      (Some(y), Some(mo), Some(d), Some(hh), Some(mm), Some(ss)) =>
        if (in_range(mo, 1, 12)
            && in_range(d, 1, 31)
            && in_range(hh, 0, 23)
            && in_range(mm, 0, 59)
            && in_range(ss, 0, 60)) then
          let (sub, j) = parse_frac(s, 19)
          match parse_zone(s, j) of
            Some(offset) =>
              let days = days_from_civil(y, mo, d)
              let secs = days * secs_per_day()
                + hh * secs_per_hour()
                + mm * secs_per_min()
                + ss
                - offset
              Some(Wall(secs * nanos_per_sec() + sub))
            None => None
        else
          None
      _ => None
defs.doc:
Parse an RFC 3339 timestamp to a wall reading in UTC, or `None` if the string is not a well-formed `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.frac](Z|(+|-)HH:MM)`. The date/time separators are checked, field ranges are validated, an offset is folded into UTC, and any trailing input is rejected, so the parser is total: a malformed or overlong string is `None`, never a partial or wrapped value.

```prism
wall_unix_secs(unwrap_or(wall_of_nanos(0), parse_rfc3339("2000-01-01T00:00:00Z")))
```

```output
946684800
```

defs.doc: A compact, positional byte body: an unboxed byte buffer and a read cursor, `Bytes(buf, off)` denoting the bytes `buf[off ..]`. The concrete representation is owned by the codec; a derived instance only ever threads a `Bytes` through the builders below, never inspects it.

defs.doc: What a downgrade could not carry down: the names of the fields dropped when lowering a value to an older frozen version. A downgrade never silently discards, it reports every field it had to drop.

defs.name: Serialize
defs.doc:
The codec, derived structurally by `deriving (Serialize)`. `encode` writes a value's compact positional body; `decode` reads one back, returning the value alongside the bytes that follow it so a reader can thread a frame's fields in declaration order. Decode is total: it fails through `Fail` on a truncated or malformed body rather than panicking, so hostile input is one ordinary failure channel.

`decode(encode(x))` recovers the value (and the bytes that followed it):

```prism
(fst(decode(encode(42))) : Int)
```

```output

```

defs.name: Stable
defs.source:
class Stable(a)
  shape_digest_of : (a) -> String
defs.doc:
The structural witness that a type's format is frozen-serializable: a record is `Stable` when all its fields are, a sum when all its variants' arguments are. The derivability is the whole content of the proof: persisting a type with a non-stable component (a function, an effectful thunk) fails at the `deriving (Stable)` site, at compile time, naming the offending field.

The one method, `shape_digest_of`, is the type's contract digest: the shape digest of its frozen layout. A derived instance's body is that digest injected by the compiler from its single shape-digest computation, so `shape_digest_of` is a per-type constant no source can forge (`Stable` is derive-only; a hand-written instance is rejected). The argument is used only to resolve the instance by value; the digest does not depend on it. `wire_encode_stable`/`wire_decode_stable` read it, so ordinary code never hand-threads a digest string into the envelope.

fn get_uvarint_go(
  bs : Bytes,
  mult : Int,
  acc : Int,
  count : Int

  if count >= varint_max_bytes then
    fail()
  else
    match wire_uncons(bs) of
      (b, rest) =>
        let acc2 = acc + mod(b, varint_radix) * mult
        if b < varint_radix then
          (acc2, rest)
        else
          get_uvarint_go(rest, mult * varint_radix, acc2, count + 1)

fn keys_strictly_ascending(ks : List(k)) : Bool given Ord(k) =
  match ks of
    Nil => true
    Cons(_, Nil) => true
    Cons(a, Cons(b, r)) => cmp(a, b) < 0 && keys_strictly_ascending(Cons(b, r))

        (vs, r2) =>
          guard(keys_strictly_ascending(ks))

defs.name: wire_open
defs.source:
fn wire_open(bs : Bytes, kind : Int, digest : String) : Bytes =
  match get_frame_str(bs) of
    (scheme, r1) =>
      if scheme == wire_scheme_tag then
        match wire_get_tag(r1) of
          (k, r2) =>
            if k == kind then
              match get_frame_str(r2) of
                (d, r3) =>
                  if d == digest then
                    r3
                  else
                    fail()
            else
              fail()
      else
        fail()
defs.doc: Open a frame, checking the scheme, kind, and digest before the body and returning the body bytes that follow. Any header mismatch fails through `Fail`, so a stale layout is rejected on a cheap comparison, never by a corrupt field.

defs.name: wire_is_reference
defs.source:
fn wire_is_reference(bs : Bytes, kind : Int, digest : String) : Bool =
  wire_is_empty(wire_open(bs, kind, digest))
defs.doc: True when a well-formed frame for `kind`/`digest` carries no body (a pure reference). Fails if the header itself does not match.

defs.name: wire_open_value_any
defs.source:
fn wire_open_value_any(bs : Bytes) : (String, Bytes) =
  match get_frame_str(bs) of
    (scheme, r1) =>
      if scheme == wire_scheme_tag then
        match wire_get_tag(r1) of
          (k, r2) =>
            if k == wire_kind_value then
              match get_frame_str(r2) of
                (d, r3) => (d, r3)
            else
              fail()
      else
        fail()
defs.doc:
Open a `value`-kind frame without knowing its contract digest up front, returning that digest alongside the body bytes. It checks the scheme and the `value` kind before the digest. An empty body is legal and returned as-is: a record with no fields encodes to zero bytes, so emptiness cannot be read as "reference" here without an explicit marker in the frame. Trailing-byte discipline is left to the body decoder, exactly as `wire_open` leaves it. A version-dispatched reader uses the returned digest to pick which frozen rung the body decodes as.

```prism
fst(wire_open_value_any(wire_frame(wire_kind_value, "dig", wire_empty)))
```

```output
dig
```

defs.name: wire_encode_value_with_digest
defs.doc:
Encode a value as a `value`-kind frame carrying an explicitly supplied contract digest. This is the escape hatch: it trusts the caller's digest verbatim, so it is for code that already holds a compiler-computed digest (a `stable` block's generated frame helpers) or is exercising a hand-built frame in a test. Ordinary `Stable` code uses `wire_encode_stable`, which supplies the digest from the type.

```prism
(wire_decode_value_with_digest(wire_encode_value_with_digest("d", 42), "d") : Int)
```

```output
42
```

defs.name: wire_decode_value_with_digest
defs.source:
fn wire_decode_value_with_digest(
  bs : Bytes,
  digest : String
) : a given Serialize(a) =
  match decode(wire_open(bs, wire_kind_value, digest)) of
    (v, rest) =>
      if wire_is_empty(rest) then
        v
      else
        fail()
defs.doc: Decode a `value`-kind frame against an explicitly supplied contract digest: check the header, decode the body, and reject trailing bytes. A bodyless reference frame fails here, because a value cannot be materialized without its bytes. The digest-supplying counterpart to `wire_encode_value_with_digest`; ordinary `Stable` code uses `wire_decode_stable`.

defs.name: wire_encode_stable
defs.source:
fn wire_encode_stable(x : a) : Bytes given Stable(a), Serialize(a) =
  wire_encode_value_with_digest(shape_digest_of(x), x)
defs.doc: Encode a `Stable` value as a `value` frame under its own contract digest. The digest is `shape_digest_of`, a per-type constant the `deriving (Stable)` instance carries, so no digest string is hand-threaded. This is the ordinary encode for a frozen-serializable value.

defs.name: wire_decode_stable
defs.source:
fn wire_decode_stable(bs : Bytes) : a given Stable(a), Serialize(a) =
  match wire_open_value_any(bs) of
    (dig, body) =>
      match decode(body) of
        (v, rest) =>
          if wire_is_empty(rest) && dig == shape_digest_of(v) then
            v
          else
            fail()
defs.doc: Decode a `Stable` value from a `value` frame, checking the frame's digest against the type's own `shape_digest_of` and rejecting trailing bytes. The result type comes from the use site; an unannotated call is ambiguous and asks for an annotation. A wrong digest, a wrong kind, a truncated body, and trailing bytes are all decode failures through `Fail`. The frame is opened without assuming its digest, the body decoded as the annotated type, and only then is the frame's digest required to equal that type's own, so a frame minted for another shape is refused.

defs.name: Policy
defs.source: type Policy = Reject | LargestSafeSubset
defs.doc: How to reconcile a higher-version value that a reader cannot represent at its own version: `Reject` refuses it, `LargestSafeSubset` downgrades it and keeps the `Loss`. A version mismatch always has one of these defined outcomes, never undefined behavior.

defs.name: reconcile
defs.ty: forall a b. (Wire.Policy, (a) -> (b, Wire.Loss), a) -> (b, Wire.Loss) ! {Fail}
defs.source:
fn reconcile(p : Policy, down : (hi) -> (lo, Loss), x : hi) : (lo, Loss) =
  match p of
    Reject => fail()
    LargestSafeSubset => down(x)
defs.doc:
Apply a mismatch policy to a downgrade. `Reject` fails through `Fail`; `LargestSafeSubset` runs the downgrade and returns the lowered value with the fields it had to drop.

```prism
reconcile(LargestSafeSubset, \(x) -> (x - 1, no_loss), 5)
```

```output
(4, Wire.Loss([]))
```
